title: trunk red: retired-image-key gate flags the ::replace listener id in machine_after_delay_resolution_fence_cljs_test (from PR #9748)
description:
TRUNK IS RED on docs.yml since PR #9748 merged (main runs failing at ea7bb075d6, df6d1411cb, bcba9e61e5; measured 2026-09-13 ~02:40Z).

Failing step: `python scripts/check_retired_image_keys.py --verbose` in the `MkDocs build` job reports one live retired EP-0026 image-key spelling:

    live-retired::replace: implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_after_delay_resolution_fence_cljs_test.cljc:75
        ::replace

The token is NOT an image key. It is the listener id passed to `rf.trace.tooling/register-listener!` (line 75) and `unregister-listener!` (line 95) in the test PR #9748 added (commit 717ae20730, rf2-fzbj.1 / rf2-gwye.21). The gate matches the spelling regardless of role.

Fix: rename that listener keyword (both sites) to a spelling the gate does not match, then run the gate and the test namespace. Do NOT add a removed-context marker (the line does not discuss the retirement) and do NOT loosen the gate.

Every PR whose docs job arms will be red until this lands (PR #9754 already is), so it blocks merges.

Why the PR run did not catch it: on PR #9748 the docs workflow's `detect` job reported no docs surface and `MkDocs build` was SKIPPED, while the main-push path filter arms on `implementation/machines/**`. That PR-side gap is a separate bead (hot-zone `.github/workflows/docs.yml`).
notes:
Fixed by PR #9760 (commit 6ba1d7d679, branch worker/trunkfix-a).

The trace-listener id ::replace in
implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_after_delay_resolution_fence_cljs_test.cljc
was renamed at BOTH sites — register-listener! (line 75) and unregister-listener!
(line 95) — to ::swap-observer, which names what the listener does (destroys frame A,
publishes same-id B mid-delay). The gate's bare-:replace pattern is :replace(?!-)
followed by a symbol-char negative lookahead, and :replace-standard is a separate exact
pattern, so the new spelling matches neither. Two lines changed, nothing else: no
removed-context marker (the line does not discuss the EP-0026 retirement, so a marker
would be a false statement to the gate) and scripts/check_retired_image_keys.py and its
fixtures are untouched.

* Full CLJS lane: compile exit 0 (2002 files, 2001 compiled, 0 warnings); run exit 0,
  "Ran 12022 tests containing 59807 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors."
* Neighbouring ratchets, all exit 0: check_retired_composition_vocab,
  check_retired_spellings, check_keyword_catalogue_drift, check_require_alias_dialect,
  check_test_lane_bijection.

CI NOTE: on PR #9760 the docs workflow's MkDocs build is SKIPPED (confirmed on the
rollup), because detect classifies the changed-file list as non-docs — the same gap that
let PR #9748 ship this red. The gate next executes on the main push that merges #9760.

THE detect GAP, for the separate hot-zone bead: .github/workflows/docs.yml's detect job
lights docs_surface only when git diff --name-only origin/<base>...HEAD matches its own

even a PR editing that gate itself would skip MkDocs build. Every non-PR event lights
docs_surface unconditionally, which is why the main push ran the gate and went red.

title: mcp-conformance: Windows hermetic cleanup grades the npx wrapper, not the shadow-cljs JVM
description:
## Correctness finding

The live hermetic runner can emit its GREEN sentinel and exit 0 on Windows after only the direct `cross-spawn` wrapper exits, while the shadow-cljs JVM descendant remains alive.

`makeCleanup` grades shadow teardown solely from `hasShadowExited()` (`tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:367-414`). That predicate is driven solely by the `exit` event on the child returned by `crossSpawn(...)` (`:1013-1021`, wired at `:1041-1044`). On Windows, the exact installed cross-spawn 7.0.6 parsing path turns the trusted bare `C:\Program Files\nodejs\npx` into `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /d /s /c ...` targeting `npx.CMD`. The returned handle therefore represents the command wrapper, not the downstream shadow-cljs JVM. Node's official child-process documentation explicitly warns that killing a shell child does not terminate the child processes it launched.

The current unit model collapses those separate lifetimes into one EventEmitter: `makeFakeShadow().kill()` emits that same fake object's `exit` (`tools/mcp-conformance/test/runner-cleanup.test.cjs:61-71`). It proves direct-child timing and escalation, but cannot detect a wrapper that exits while a grandchild survives.

## Impact

This defeats the verifier's defining hermetic guarantee. A false-green run can leave the shadow/JVM/watch server holding the fixture's fixed port 8030 (`run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:65`) and runtime metadata, contaminating or wedging the next human/AI run or causing it to exercise stale state. This is a certification defect rather than cosmetic cleanup: `finalizeConformance` converts `report.clean` into the pass sentinel and exit 0 (`:420-440`, `:1361-1368`).

## Evidence and history

- Read-only execution of the exact installed cross-spawn parser yielded command `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe`, `/d /s /c` arguments, and `file=C:\Program Files\nodejs\npx.CMD` for the runner's spawn shape.
- Read-only local process-table inspection confirmed shadow's ordinary Node-to-Java descendant shape.
- Node's primary documentation covers both Windows `.cmd` shell handling and the fact that killing a shell does not terminate its child processes: https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html
- Cross-spawn's primary source/documentation confirms its `.cmd` shim handling: https://github.com/moxystudio/node-cross-spawn
- Commit `ba8c8a20d6` introduced dirty teardown grading specifically so a leaked shadow JVM/port-8030 owner cannot pass, but the implementation equates wrapper exit with JVM exit.
- The repository already has a scoped Windows process-tree precedent: `scripts/test-core-jvm-windows.ps1:163-171` uses `taskkill.exe /pid <owned-root> /T /F`; `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:697-762` documents and handles the native descendant tree.

## Bounded fix

Make Windows teardown own, terminate, and grade the process tree rooted at the exact PID spawned by this runner. Adapt the existing scoped `/T` pattern, or use a graceful shadow stop with that verified fallback, while the root relationship is still observable. Do not mark cleanup clean merely because the npx/cmd wrapper emitted `exit`. Keep current POSIX behavior unless an equivalent demonstrated defect requires a change.

Add a small regression fixture/test that separates wrapper exit from grandchild liveness. Prefer an outcome-focused local helper or test seam over a generic process-supervision abstraction.

## Posture fit

This is a narrow truthfulness and ergonomics repair using a process-tree pattern already proven in the repository. It makes the powerful one-command hermetic verifier trustworthy and removes expensive rerun contamination for programmers and their AI tools, without adding public API or framework machinery.

## Non-goals

- Dynamic or parallel port allocation.
- A generic cross-platform process supervisor.
- Global stale-process reaping or killing unrelated Java/Node processes.
- Redesigning the fixture or MCP wire contracts.
- Expanding the host matrix.

## Duplicate check

Focused `rg` searches over `.beads/issues.jsonl` for mcp-conformance combined with Windows, cleanup, teardown, orphan, JVM, 8030, npx, and server.pid, plus exact symptom phrases, found no issue owning this outcome. Related closed `rf2-j538f7.19`/commit `ba8c8a20d6` established the intended guarantee but did not handle descendants; closed `rf2-ahjbc` and `rf2-a9l6e` have different scopes. A tracker memory records prior observed Windows false-green leftovers, but this finding was independently established from the runner, dependency source, platform semantics, process hierarchy, tests, and history.

## Uncertainty

The live suite was not booted in the review worktree because that would require the prohibited dependency link/install and runtime mutations; no process was listening on 8030 during inspection. The exact cross-spawn transformation, direct-handle control flow, official Node semantics, repository process-tree precedent, and observed Node-to-Java hierarchy establish the mechanism. The implementer should choose the smallest graceful-stop/tree-kill detail and verify the outcome below.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A regression launches or faithfully models a Windows wrapper with a separately long-lived grandchild; wrapper exit alone cannot produce `shadow.clean === true` or the overall GREEN sentinel.
2. Normal cleanup and SIGTERM/SIGKILL/watchdog paths terminate the runner-owned shadow process tree within the existing bounds; unrelated Node/JVM processes are never targeted.
3. Cleanup returns dirty, exit 2, and no pass sentinel whenever owned-descendant teardown cannot be proven.
4. Two consecutive Windows hermetic-suite runs both pass from their own state; after each, no fixture-owned process/listener remains on port 8030 and the next run does not trust stale runtime metadata.
5. Existing browser cleanup, live-test inventory, trusted-executable checks, wire assertions, sentinels, and exit-code contracts remain green.
notes:
AUDIT PR #9213 (2026-09-05): REOPENED. The new creation-time ownership fence is not applied to the root PID. `ownedDescendants` unconditionally includes `rootPid` whenever that numeric PID appears in the live table (`if (byPid.has(rootPid)) owned.push(rootPid)`), even if that row's `createdMs` predates `spawnedAtMs`; `makeShadowTreeReaper` then calls `taskkill /pid <rootPid> /T /F`. Once the short-lived cmd/npx wrapper exits and Windows recycles its PID, cleanup can therefore kill an unrelated process and its descendants, directly violating AC2 and the PR's safety claim. Deterministic probe at merge 2c08156e85: table root `{pid:100,createdMs:1000}` plus child `{pid:200,createdMs:6000}`, `spawnedAtMs=5000` returned owned `[100,200]` and invoked treeKill(100). The added recycled-PID test covers only a stale child, not the root. Bound the root row by the same creation-time check (and handle a missing/invalid creation timestamp fail-closed), while retaining discovery of legitimate orphans whose dead parent PID remains in `ParentProcessId`; add a regression that proves a recycled root is never targeted. Focused all-status search found no more exact owner than rf2-kzbf.
AUDIT PR #9247 (2026-09-05): REOPENED. The reproduced dated-root case is repaired, but the new algorithm is not actually fail-closed for ambiguous lineage.

1. For an undated root row, classifyRootRow returns unprovable and makeShadowTreeReaper sets rootError, but ownedDescendants still walks from that PID. With root {pid:100, createdMs:0} and child {pid:200, ppid:100, createdMs:6000}, the child enters owned and line 454 tree-kills pid 200 before the function returns the dirty error. If the undated root is a stranger, that is the stranger's child. Reporting dirty after the kill does not satisfy AC2 or the source/PR claim that unprovable ownership is not killed. The added test gives the undated root no child, so it misses this path. The close reason acknowledges this residual but closes the safety criterion anyway.

2. When our wrapper has exited and a stranger subsequently reuses the number, spawns a child, and itself exits before enumeration, rootClass is absent and strangerCeilingMs is Infinity. That stranger's surviving child retains the recycled number as PPID, passes the spawn floor, enters owned, and is killed. A boolean rootExited cannot distinguish it from our orphan; an observed wrapper-exit time provides the natural upper bound because our direct child had to be created before the wrapper exited.

Bounded repair: when the current root is unprovable, kill nothing and return dirty. Bound orphan discovery with positive ownership evidence such as the observed wrapper-exit instant, and add table-model teeth for an undated root with a child plus an absent recycled root with a post-exit child. Then satisfy AC4 on Windows: neither test.yml nor expensive-tests.yml can do so today because both suite jobs run on ubuntu-latest, where makeShadowTreeReaper is inert; the PR explicitly did not run the required two consecutive Windows hermetic suites and port-8030 checks.
IMPLEMENTED (PR #9256, 2026-09-05). Both PR #9247 audit residuals repaired, each reproduced red first.

(1) Unprovable root: ownedDescendants now refuses the walk entirely when classifyRootRow returns 'unprovable', so no child of an undatable root is ever handed to treeKill. Previously owned=[200] for {root 100 createdMs 0, child 200 ppid 100 createdMs 6000} at spawnedAtMs 5000, and line 454 killed 200 BEFORE the dirty error returned.

(2) Absent recycled root: the runner now records shadowExitedAtMs alongside shadowExited and passes it as rootExitedAtMs. A direct child of our wrapper had to be created before the wrapper died, so the observed exit instant is a genuine ownership ceiling. New helper rootOwnershipEvidence derives both ceilings (dated stranger row, exit instant) plus the kill decision from ONE table read, and the reaper drives kill and grade from that same object. Where neither ceiling exists and rows do claim the vacated number: kill nothing, grade dirty. An undated DIRECT claimant on a vacated number is likewise left alone and named in the dirty report (a third hole of the same shape, not in the audit note). Ceilings bind the root's direct children only - a grandchild our own JVM forked after the wrapper died reaches us through a parent already proven ours. POSIX unchanged (reaper still the inert identity).

Regression: six table-model tests in test/runner-cleanup.test.cjs, landed in their own commit red against the merged implementation (node --test test/runner-cleanup.test.cjs -> exit 1, 5 fail / 32 pass of 37); exit 0, 37/37 after the fix. The sixth pins the other direction (an already-empty tree stays CLEAN) so the repair cannot buy safety with a false RED. The real-process Windows witness ran UNSKIPPED (Windows 11 dev machine) and still discovers, reaps and proves-dead its orphaned grandchild through the new bound; it now wires rootExitedAtMs exactly as main() does.

Gates: node --test test/runner-cleanup.test.cjs exit 0 (37 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped); npm run test:unit exit 0 (149 tests, 140 pass, 0 fail, 9 skipped), re-run green after rebase onto origin/main. The full live hermetic suite and scripts/test-fast-pr.sh were NOT run locally (five sibling workers live; a gate that heavy wedges rather than fails under concurrency) - CI owns the spine.

AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5 met. AC4 is NOT met and CANNOT be met by CI as it stands: both suite jobs declare runs-on ubuntu-latest (.github/workflows/test.yml mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair line 5508; .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml mcp-live line 349), where makeShadowTreeReaper returns the inert identity, so none of this code executes there. Closing AC4 needs a Windows runner leg in a hot-zone workflow file, outside this change's fence. Filed as rf2-hhw6 (discovered-from rf2-kzbf).

Premise check: cross-spawn 7.0.6's installed parser re-run read-only on this machine returns command=C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe, args=[/d,/s,/c,...], file=C:\Program Files\nodejs\npx.CMD for a bare npx - the bead's founding premise holds.
close_reason:
MERGED as PR #9256 (rebased onto main 2026-09-05T02:47:35Z, verified state=MERGED and the mayor checkout fast-forwarded to 04230d0d33 carrying both files). Merged on all five clauses: 87 checks, 0 non-terminal, 87 passed-or-skipped, all four workflow runs at the full head oid 5bb59ab3c3f26a7842545abc49152ce8b3cb8b82 completed, and 0 structural workflow lines landed on the trunk since the merge base.

WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED IS NOT WHAT THE DISPATCH BRIEF DESCRIBED, and the worker corrected me at source. The brief restated this bead's ORIGINAL scope (grade the process tree rather than the npx wrapper); that work had ALREADY landed via PRs #9213 and #9247. The bead had been reopened twice by audits, and the worker's bd history walk found the live instruction to be the PR #9247 AUDIT note (notes 1182->3080 chars at 2026-09-05T08:31:25, status closed->open one second earlier), with description, acceptance_criteria and title unchanged across all 343 snapshots — notes being the varying field and therefore its own control. It followed the item over the brief, which is correct.

THE REAL DEFECT, both arms reproduced red first: PR #9213 fenced the root ROW and left the ppid LINK unfenced. (1) An unprovable root still handed the walk its children, running treeKill(200) BEFORE returning its dirty error — reporting dirty after the kill is not fail-closed. (2) An absent root left the walk with no ceiling at all, so a stranger that took the recycled pid, forked, and exited before enumeration had its surviving child killed as ours. The fix derives both ceilings and the kill decision from one table read; a third hole of the same shape the audit did not name (an undated direct claimant) is left alone and named in the dirty report. POSIX untouched.

EVIDENCE: six table-model regressions committed FIRST in their own commit, red at exit 1 (5 fail / 32 pass of 37) against the merged implementation, green at exit 0 (37/37, 0 skipped) after. The tests model wrapper-exit and grandchild-liveness as SEPARATE rows, which is precisely the blind spot of the superseded test where one EventEmitter was both. npm run test:unit exit 0 (149 tests, 140 pass, 9 skipped), run three times including after rebase. Gate provenance confirmed: the red log names the worker's own worktree five times.

AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5 are met. AC4 IS NOT MET AND IS NOT CLOSABLE HERE — it asks for two consecutive WINDOWS hermetic-suite runs, and no gate in this repository can supply that: both suite jobs declare runs-on: ubuntu-latest (test.yml mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair line 5508; expensive-tests.yml mcp-live line 349), where makeShadowTreeReaper returns the inert identity, so none of this code path executes there. That repair needs a Windows runner leg in a hot-zone workflow file and is filed as rf2-hhw6 (P2, discovered-from this bead) with the measurement and scope. The worker stopped at the fence rather than editing, which is correct.

So this bead closes on its bounded repair; AC4 lives on rf2-hhw6.

title: EPIC: excise lease completely from re-frame2
description:
## Problem

Mike ruled on 2026-07-20 that the lease idea was a mistake and must be removed completely, not deprecated or preserved as a convenience. The repository-wide tracked inventory currently finds the concept or terminology in 3,582 lines across 309 files, spanning re-frame.ui, all React-shaped adapters, the observation port, Resources ownership, specs, EPs, docs, examples, skills, AI findings, conformance fixtures, Xray, Pair, Story, and tests.

A narrow deletion of re-frame.ui/lease would leave the same idea, vocabulary, public hooks, generated evidence, and AI guidance in many corners. That is explicitly unacceptable.

## Decision

- Delete every component/view-lifetime lease API and its runtime/compiler/tool machinery. Add no replacement helper, deprecation alias, compatibility shim, or retired-name error.
- Preserve valid resource management through explicit causal owners: routes, machines, SSR requests, and semantic app events. Preserve owner-driven GC, polling, cancellation, and release; remove the generic [:lease ...] owner kind and all lease terminology.
- Preserve the observation port's commit-time ref-count semantics, but rename its returned object and grammar to a neutral observation handle. This is a vocabulary/API cleanup, not a redesign.
- Remove the concept from all current and historical tracked authoring material, including specs, EPs, docs, examples, migrations, skills, evals, tools, and AI findings. Do not leave a supersession paragraph that continues teaching the rejected construct.
- Finish with an executable zero-residue guard over tracked product and authoring paths. The Beads database and Git history are the only exemptions because they are immutable/audit history and this removal program itself must name the decision.

## Staged delivery

1. Delete the public view-lifetime surfaces and their implementation/tool consumers.
2. Normalize surviving internals: observation handles and causal resource owners.
3. Purge all specification, documentation, example, skill, AI, and tool guidance residue.
4. Land a zero-baseline repository ratchet and integration proof.

Stages may use stacked PRs, but each merged PR must keep every public surface it touches truthful. No docs/code mismatch and no temporary compatibility layer.

## Acceptance

- No tracked product or authoring filename/content outside .beads contains the retired lexical concept in prose, identifiers, keywords, test names, fixture ids, schemas, manifests, or generated surfaces.
- re-frame.ui/lease, with-resource-lease, use-resource-lease, [:lease ...], ObservationLease, and every equivalent helper/descriptor/error/tool field are absent.
- Resource loading and lifecycle management continue through causal owners without component-presence ownership.
- The zero-residue check is part of normal CI and is proven capable of failing on prose, kebab/snake identifiers, camel-case identifiers, and filenames.
- Relevant UI, adapter, core, Resources, conformance, Xray, Pair, Story, docs, and skill gates pass with non-vacuous test selection.
acceptance_criteria: The rejected lease construct and lexical residue are absent from every tracked product/authoring surface outside .beads; causal resource ownership and observation handling remain correct; a zero-baseline CI ratchet prevents reintroduction.
notes:
STRUCTURE REVIEW ADDENDUM (2026-07-20, mayor):

Inventory verified against the tracked tree with the precise residue pattern `\b[Ll]eas(e|es|ed|ing)\b|Lease` (word-boundary — matches lease/leases/leased/leasing + camel Lease; does NOT match release/please). Census: ~307 files / ~3.4k lines, consistent with the description's 3,582/309 snapshot (drift = rf2-y4mgw + #6570 landing since). Naive substring 'lease' inflates to 744 files via release/please — S4's guard discrimination requirement is load-bearing, keep it.

Dispatch topology + hot-zone fences (per CLAUDE.md sequential-hot-file rule):
- S1 solo first (touches hot-zone spec/API.md, spec/004-Views.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn).
- S2A ∥ S2B is parallel-safe ONLY under the file fence recorded on each: S2A owns spec/006 + spec/009 (observation row) + spec/002-Frames; S2B owns spec/Conventions + spec/005 + 012/014/016 + conformance fixtures. Disjoint hot files.
- S3A ∥ S3B parallel-safe (docs/spec/examples vs ai/skills/tools — disjoint trees).
- S4 solo last, against the final merged tree.

rf2-7a3uc (blocks S3B) closed AND its PR #6570 MERGED 2026-07-20 — S3B has no remaining wait.
close_reason: LEASE EXCISION COMPLETE (S1-S4 + zero-residue ratchet); all 6 stage children + j97yg closed.

title: review(xray/static-catalogue): senior-developer findings, 8 ranked, 4 spec chapters drift, trunk 9555881fe3 (2026-09-17)
description:
# Senior review: xray-static-catalogue

PARTIAL (stopped by the coordinator to conserve budget; nothing was run): READ in full — every file in the slice: static/shell.cljs, schemas/panel.cljs, interceptors/panel.cljs, flows/panel.cljs, routes/panel.cljs, routes/row_expand.cljs, routes/browse_list.cljs, routes/simulate_url.cljs, routes/simulate_nav.cljs, shared/search_box.cljs, shared/catalogue.cljs, mode_pill.cljs, persistence.cljs, panels/image_view_reads.cljs, panels/routing_helpers.cljc, plus the framework side: implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/match.cljc and the match-url / route-table / slice-writer regions of registry.cljc and events.cljc, registrar.cljc's emit path, schemas/storage.cljc's reg-app-schema, trace_collector.cljs's gate. NOT READ — panels/routing.cljs (Dynamic lens) beyond its install!, the static test BODIES (deftest names and the pinned slot-shape / strip-origin assertions were read; nothing else), tools/xray/spec/013 and 018 (grepped only), and no clj-kondo / clojure -M:test run.

Reviewer persona: a senior engineer who has built registry browsers and schema explorers and judges them by one question: when the registry changes under the panel (hot reload, late registration, a frame torn down), does the panel show what is registered NOW, and can the user tell?

### 1. Simulate-URL strips an "origin" out of the QUERY, so a redirect-style URL simulates the wrong route  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness] [size: S]

- What: `strip-origin` treats the FIRST `://` anywhere in the string as a scheme marker, so `/login?next=https://app.example/cart` is reduced to `/cart` and the simulator crowns `:route/cart` the winner, where the framework's `match-url` (registry.cljc:1272-1277, query split off first) matches `/login`.

# Senior review: adapters

Reviewer persona: senior framework-bindings engineer (hook rules, context propagation, subscription lifetimes, StrictMode double-invocation, test flush semantics, bundle isolation)
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: `implementation/adapters/reagent/src` (243) + testbed/spec; `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src` in full (~4.9K: adapter 158, `reagent2/ratom.cljs` 555, `impl/component.cljs` 805, `impl/batching.cljs` 258, `impl/template.cljs` 1332, `dom/client.cljs` 313, `dom/server.cljs` 1109, core + macros + diag) + testbed/smoke; `implementation/adapters/uix/src` (326) + testbed/spec; `implementation/adapters/test-react/src` (630); `implementation/adapters/scripts/*.cjs` (~780); `implementation/adapters/README.md` §Adapters that ship today; `implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs` (376), `adapter/use_frame.cljs` (157), `substrate/spine.cljs` in full (4482), `views.cljs` (949), `views/provider.cljs` (350), `views/frame_boundary.cljs` (392), `subs/cache.cljc` 120-340, `subs.cljc` 590-620 / 1456-1520 / 1795-1920, `subs/tooling.cljc` 165-228. Tests skimmed across all three adapter `test/` dirs (~13K source lines read, tests skimmed).
Owning specs consulted: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` (§99-390 adapter contract, §848-1260 sub-cache / ref-counting / disposal, §1739-2012, §2121-2245), `spec/002-Frames.md` §frame-provider/frame-root (1384-1443) and §Shared React frame Context (1643-1732), `spec/Conventions.md` §adapter shipping convention (1820-1887), `spec/Ownership.md:43-46`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:202, 261-272, 298`, `spec/011-SSR.md:874-877`.

Sibling context (Reagent adapter: real unmount emits no `:rf.sub/dispose`; `:ref-count` is a render counter reported as a live reader count) is extended, not re-derived: reagent-slim SHARES both by the identical mechanism; UIx AVOIDS both. The three shipped adapters therefore disagree on what the sub-cache tooling snapshot means.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Ratom substrates retire sub-cache slots by watcher auto-dispose, bypassing the ref-count / `:rf.sub/dispose` path that Spec 006 and the tooling describe  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness]
- Where: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:590-619` (bump on every hit) and `:1808`; `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1456-1484` (on-dispose closure releases INPUT refs then `dissoc`s the slot with no decrement and no emit); `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs:314-320` (`-remove-watch` auto-dispose when the last watcher drops and `auto-run` is nil) and `:436-464` (`dispose!`); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3985-4240` (`make-ratom-spine`: the render-owned deref path never calls `unsubscribe`); contrast `spine.cljs:3068-3576` (`use-subscribe-2`, UIx: commit-owned `subscribe-fn` +1, cleanup `rf.subs/unsubscribe-if-reaction` -1).
- What: On Reagent AND reagent-slim a view's `@(subscribe q)` bumps `:ref-count` on every render and nothing ever decrements it; the slot is removed when the component's render Reaction drops its last watch (Reaction auto-dispose → compute-and-cache!'s on-dispose closure → silent `dissoc`), so `:ref-count` is a cumulative subscribe counter, the 1→0 edge of Spec 006 §1118-1126 never happens, and `emit-dispose!` (reached only from `dispose-entry-now!` / hot-reload / cache-clear / frame-destroy, `subs/cache.cljc:137-192`) never fires for the view's own slot on a real unmount — only its layer-2 INPUTS get an emit via `release-input-ref!`. On UIx the same view goes through `unsubscribe-if-reaction` and does emit with a live count.
- Evidence: read the three code paths end to end. Grep `emit-dispose!` in `subs/cache.cljc`: 5 sites, none reachable from the Reaction on-dispose closure (control: the definition at :137 is found). Grep `rf.subs/unsubscribe` + `unsubscribe-if-reaction` across `core/src` and the three adapters: the only render-path caller is the UIx hook cleanup in `use-subscribe-2`; the ratom spine has none (control: the UIx site is found by the same pattern; `core.cljc:1307` is the public re-export). `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:912` (`:ref-count n ;; how many readers currently hold a reference`), `:1140` ("When `ref-count` reaches 0 ... a `:rf.sub/dispose` trace event is emitted"), `subs/tooling.cljc:179` ("the live consumer ref-count for the entry"), and Xray reads it as such (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs`, 9 `:ref-count` hits). Spec 006:1259 does say "Reagent's Reaction handles ... ref-counting and disposal automatically", so the spec half-acknowledges a second mechanism but still promises the emit and the live count. `reagent/test/re_frame/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:647` pins "ref-count reflects two outstanding subscribes" using imperative `subscribe`, which is the one path where the count IS live.
- Action: decide: A — make the ratom render path a real reader: in `make-ratom-spine`'s derived-value deref, take the reference once per (owner reaction, slot) and register `unsubscribe-if-reaction` on the owner's on-dispose (mirrors what `use-subscribe-2` already does; then `:ref-count` is live and `:rf.sub/dispose :no-more-derefers` fires on unmount on all three adapters); or B — keep Reaction auto-dispose as the ratom lifetime, but have compute-and-cache!'s on-dispose closure call `emit-dispose!` (reason `:no-more-derefers`) before the `dissoc`, and rename/redocument the slot as `:subscribe-count` for ratom adapters in `tooling.cljc:179` and Spec 006 §912. A gives one truth across adapters; B is a morning and fixes the silent trace but leaves Xray showing a render counter as readers. Whichever is chosen, Spec 006 §1259 should say which of the two lifetimes governs a ratom adapter.

### 2. reagent-slim `render-to-static-markup` silently drops the whole subtree under `frame-provider`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs:1024-1030` (`:>`, `:r>`, `:f>` heads → `emit-react-component-placeholder`), `:888-892`, `:41-45` (the parity claim); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:99-100` (`frame-provider` IS `[:r> (.-Provider frame-context) #js {:value frame-kw} ...children]`; slim wires it at `reagent_slim.cljs:126`).
- What: The canonical slim mount `[rf/frame-provider {:frame f} [app]]` rendered through slim's own static walker emits `<!--reagent-react-component-->` and nothing else — no error, no warning, the children are never walked — and the comment justifying it ("matches `react-dom/server.renderToStaticMarkup` ... treats foreign-component subtrees as opaque") is false: react-dom/server renders through Context Providers and components.
- Evidence: `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/ssr_keyword_head_contract_cljs_test.cljs:79-83` renders `[rf/frame-provider {:frame test-frame} tree]` through stock Reagent's `rds/render-to-static-markup` and asserts `<card>revenue</card>` at :92 — real markup through the provider. `reagent-slim/test/reagent2/dom/server_cljs_test.cljs:307-314` pins the placeholder for `[:r> Foo]` (it pins the divergence, not the provider case). Grep `frame-provider` in `reagent-slim/test`: 14 hits across 6 DOM-test files, 0 in `test/reagent2/dom/*` where the static-markup tests live (control: same pattern finds the 6 files). `server_subscribe_ssr_cljs_test.cljs` avoids the trap by rendering `[counter-app]` bare under `with-frame`, which is also what the counter example's `bundle_isolation_fixture.cljs:52-58` does. Spec 011:874-877 places reagent-slim in the hiccup SSR tier, and `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:261` sells `render-to-static-markup` for HTML export.
- Action: decide: A — in `emit-hiccup-vector`, recognise a React context Provider head (`(.-$$typeof head)` is `Symbol.for("react.context")` on React 19, `"react.provider"` before) and walk its children (frame scoping under the static walker already comes from `with-frame`, so dropping the value is fine); or B — route a Provider head to the existing bad-element throw at `server.cljs:1047-1058` and document `with-frame` + no provider as the slim static shape. A is ~10 lines and removes a silent-empty export; either way delete the false parity sentence at :41-45.

### 3. No gate pins the unmount-driven lifecycle traces on the ratom adapters, so #1 and #4 are invisible  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: test-gap]
- Where: `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/sub_dispose_view_cljs_test.cljs` (every `:rf.sub/dispose` assertion is driven by explicit `rf/unsubscribe` or direct `rf.interop/dispose!`; its own comment at :325-330 records "no emit for the parent on this path"); `form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:125-131` (`with-let` `finally` → explicit `rf/unsubscribe`); `frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs:195-280` (scenario 1 pins exactly one `:rf.view/unmounted` on a real unmount, NOT under StrictMode) and `:575-636` (scenario 6, StrictMode, asserts render counts only); `reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_strict_mode_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (pins DOM re-render + watch-count baseline only).
- What: Spec 006 §1140 and Spec 009:261 promise `:rf.sub/dispose` per eviction, and Spec 009:298 promises `:rf.view/unmounted` per instance teardown, but no Reagent or slim test mounts a view, unmounts it for real, and asserts either trace, and no adapter test asserts `:rf.view/unmounted` under StrictMode — so both breakages in #1 and #4 pass every gate.
- Evidence: Grep `:rf.sub/dispose` across adapter tests: reagent 4 files (read; all explicit-unsubscribe driven), slim 0, uix 0 (control: pattern finds 9 hits in `standard_epochs_views_subs_lifecycle_cljs_test.cljs`). Grep `:rf.view/unmounted` across adapter tests: 5 reagent + 1 uix + 0 slim files; crossing with `StrictMode|strict-mode` per file leaves `frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (44 StrictMode hits, unmounted listener only in non-Strict scenario 1) and `uix_use_sub_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (1). The slim adapter's `reagent_slim_surface_parity_cljs_test.cljs` compares adapter-map shape, not trace behaviour.
- Action: one DOM test per ratom adapter: mount a subscribing reg-view, `unmount` under `flushSync`, await the macrotask window (the `await-teardown!` helper at `frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs:168-176` already exists), assert one `:rf.sub/dispose :no-more-derefers` for the view's own query and one `:rf.view/unmounted`; then the same body wrapped in `React.StrictMode`. Write them against the intended behaviour chosen in #1 — today they fail, which is the point.

### 4. Under StrictMode the Reagent-family `:rf.view/unmounted` fires during the mount replay and not at the real unmount  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:345-350` (`component-lifecycle-reaction` returns the cached `.-rfLifecycleReaction` with no disposed check); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:392-415` (`install-unmount-hook!`: emit registered once via `add-on-dispose!`) and `:513-532` (`maybe-arm-unmount!`); `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:469-493` (transient `componentWillUnmount` disposes the render Reaction, sets `cljsRemountReattach`); `reagent2/ratom.cljs:436-464` (`dispose!` nils `on-dispose` / `on-dispose-arr` before firing them); `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:52-70` (classic Reagent gets the same holder-clearing from `install-dispose-guard!`).
- What: StrictMode's transient will-unmount disposes the render Reaction → the lifecycle reaction loses its last watcher → auto-disposes → emits `:rf.view/unmounted` (while the instance is about to be remounted) and its on-dispose holders are cleared; the remount's render re-derefs the SAME cached, disposed reaction, so the genuine unmount later disposes a reaction with no callbacks and emits nothing — Xray sees the view torn down at mount time and never at teardown. UIx's sentinel `useEffect` (`spine.cljs:2278-2327`) emits at both the simulated and the real unmount, matching React's own StrictMode semantics.
- Evidence: traced by reading; both `dispose!` implementations clear the holders and the cache lookup at `provider.cljs:348` has no liveness test. Not run (no browser allowed). Confirm by wrapping `frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs` scenario 1 in `React.StrictMode`: expect the unmount count to be 1 BEFORE `.unmount` and 0 within the awaited window.
- Action: in `component-lifecycle-reaction`, also register an on-dispose that clears `(.-rfLifecycleReaction cmp)` (two lines at `provider.cljs:348`), so the next render re-arms a fresh reaction; this yields emit-at-replay + emit-at-real-unmount, the same shape UIx already has. Pair with the StrictMode test from #3.

### 5. Dev builds hand React a fresh keyword object as the frame-context value, forcing every consumer to re-render when the provider's parent does  [PLAUSIBLE] [severity: low] [kind: perf]
- Where: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:100`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:2038-2040`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs:364-366` (`value (:id opts)`), `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:76-102` — all pass the caller's keyword straight through as `#js {:value frame-kw}`.
- What: React propagates a context change on `Object.is` inequality; under `:none` a keyword literal is `new cljs.core.Keyword(...)` per evaluation, so a `frame-provider`/`frame-root` element re-created inside a re-rendering parent changes the context value every time and every `:contextType` class consumer (Reagent/slim `current-frame`) re-renders past its argv `shouldComponentUpdate` — dev-only, and it inflates `:rf.view/render` traces relative to `:advanced`, which is the number Xray users read.
- Evidence: compiled dev artefact `implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/node-test/dev/out/cljs-runtime/re_frame.views.frame_boundary.js` (main checkout, read-only): `new cljs.core.Keyword(` 32 occurrences, `cst$kw$` 0 (no constant hoisting). `frame-root-fc` already `=`-compares `opts` for the make-frame side (`frame_boundary.cljs:338-368`) and `use_frame.cljs` `=`-memoizes for hooks, so only the Provider value itself escapes the `=` discipline. The shipped testbeds build their provider once in `init` and do not hit it (`uix/testbed/.../core.cljs:56-61`), so the condition is real but not universal.
- Action: intern the value at the three element-building sites — e.g. `(:id (frame-registry frame-kw))` or a module-level `(memoize identity)`-style intern keyed by `=` — so the same frame yields the same object across renders. Skip if dev/prod render-count parity is not something Xray promises.

## Considered, left alone
- UIx `frame-provider` validates `:frame` twice (`uix.cljs:98` then `spine.cljs:2035`); harmless duplication, not worth a morning.
- `test-react` leaves `add-on-dispose!` unrouted and is IDeref-only; it is local-test-only with no Maven coordinate (README roster), and its tests know it.
- slim `flush-render!` (`dom/client.cljs`) flushes one component pass under `flushSync`; second-order cascades are documented and the DOM test pins the first-order commit; no user-visible hole found.
- UIx adapter `set!`s `uix.compiler.input/*use-reagent-input-enabled?*` at load (`uix.cljs:44`); global, but required for controlled inputs and recorded under rf2-heqwo.
- slim smoke lives at `testbed/smoke.cjs` outside `adapter-smoke-filter.cjs`'s `ADAPTERS` roster; by design per CLAUDE.md, not a coverage gap.

## Instruments and controls
- `git -C <worktree> rev-parse --short HEAD` → `d89a41e057`.
- Grep `emit-dispose!` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc` → 5 sites (definition :137 + `dispose-entry-now!`, hot-reload, cache-clear, frame-destroy); none from the Reaction on-dispose closure in `subs.cljc:1456-1484`.
- Grep `bump-ref-count-fn` in `subs.cljc` → definition :590 + call sites :1505, :1808, :2466; decrement only in `cache.cljc` `unsubscribe!` :194-254 / `unsubscribe-if-reaction!` :256-302.
- Grep `rf.subs/unsubscribe|unsubscribe-if-reaction` across `implementation/core/src` + `implementation/adapters/*/src` → UIx hook cleanup in `spine.cljs` `use-subscribe-2` and the `core.cljc:1307` re-export; 0 in `make-ratom-spine` / `make-derived-value-fn` (control: the UIx site is found).
- Grep `:rf.sub/dispose` in adapter tests → reagent 4 files (read: all explicit-unsubscribe driven), slim 0, uix 0 (control: 9 hits in `standard_epochs_views_subs_lifecycle_cljs_test.cljs`).
- Grep `:rf.view/unmounted` in adapter tests → 5 reagent + 1 uix + 0 slim; per-file `StrictMode|strict-mode` cross → `frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs` 44, `uix_use_sub_dom_cljs_test.cljs` 1, rest 0; scenarios read at :195-280 and :575-636.
- Grep `frame-provider` in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test` → 14 hits / 6 files, 0 under `test/reagent2/dom/` (control: the 6 files are found).
- Grep `render-to-static-markup` ∩ `provider|frame` in `implementation/adapters/reagent/test` → `ssr_keyword_head_contract_cljs_test.cljs:79-83` (renders through `frame-provider`, asserts `<card>revenue</card>` at :92); `ssr_streaming_example_cljs_test.cljs:80-86` likewise.
- Grep `:ref-count` in `tools/xray/src` → `reactive_panel_subs.cljs` 9, `reactive_panel.cljs` 1, `epoch/projection.cljc` 2 (consumers of `sub-cache-snapshot`).
- Compiled dev artefact search (main checkout, read-only): `re_frame.views.frame_boundary.js` under `implementation/.shadow-cljs/builds/node-test/dev/out/cljs-runtime/` → `new cljs.core.Keyword(` 32, `cst$kw$` 0.
- No `clojure -M:test`, no shadow-cljs, no browser run; every CONFIRMED finding is confirmed by reading the code paths end to end plus the greps above.

description:
# Senior review: machines

Reviewer persona: senior statechart runtime engineer (SCXML / XState-class), reading for correctness and spec-drift
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc (543) and machines/{transition (4320, full), parallel (1896, full), timer (1291, full), hydrate (334), timeout (473), choice (323), cofx_attach (1087), reply (669), data_validation (651), grammar (204), internal_events (183), ssr (130), result (234)} and lifecycle_fx/{update_snapshot (170), spawn (1902), registration (1480), finalize (836), destroy (884), join (859), validation (1903), resolver (264), spawn_error (154), teardown (137), exit_cascade (142), frame_destroy (294)}; ~21K of ~22.8K source lines (tooling, classification, traces, paths, path_walk, spawn_order, error_emit, resource_release skimmed by search only). Tests (167 files / 52K lines) skimmed by search for the pins named in the brief.
Owning specs consulted: spec/005-StateMachines.md (§Snapshot shape / §Reserved keys, §Guards / §Actions, §Action effect map, §Path conventions + §Snapshot-level escape hatch, §Drain semantics + gotchas, §Hierarchical, §Eventless `:always`, §Delayed `:after`, §Cross-region coordination), spec/CP-5-MachineGuide.md (§inline-fn escape hatch), spec/Managed-Effects.md (§Cancellation), spec/Ownership.md row 42

## Findings, ranked

### 1. `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` replaces `:data` wholesale and silently drops the framework's reserved `:rf/*` slots  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/update_snapshot.cljc:148 and :165
- What: the escape-hatch fx does a TOP-LEVEL `merge` of `:rf/patch` onto the snapshot, so the documented idiom `{:rf/patch {:data {:status :degraded}}}` REPLACES the actor's whole `:data` map — taking `:rf/after-epoch`, `:rf/after-epoch-by-region`, `:rf/self-id`, `:rf/parent-id`, `:rf/invoke-id`, `:rf/join-child` and `:rf/spawned` with it — whereas an action's `{:data ...}` return MERGES (transition.cljc:2075-2077), so the two write paths that the spec presents as equivalent behave differently on exactly the keys the programmer cannot see.
- Evidence: `merged (merge (get snapshots machine-id) clean-patch)` / `(update-in runtime-db (snapshot-path machine-id) merge clean-patch)`. Traced end to end: (a) `transition.cljc:951` reads the current epoch as `(or (get-in snapshot [:data :rf/after-epoch decl-path]) 0)` and every armed timer carries epoch >= 1 (`bump-after-epochs` is `(fnil inc 0)`, :3309-3313), so after the patch every live `:after` timer of that actor is stale-suppressed on arrival — a state's timeout silently never fires; (b) `finalize.cljc:389-390` reads `parent-id (:rf/parent-id child-data)`, so a spawned child that patches itself finishes as if it were a singleton and its parent's `:spawn :on-done` / join fold never runs. spec/005:869 says "`:rf/patch` is merged onto that snapshot", so the code matches the spec's letter, but 005:2470 says the `:rf/` namespace inside `:data` is "reserved for runtime-managed keys; user code does not write under it" — this fx makes user code erase them. Control: all 17 `:rf/patch` uses in implementation/ (7 files) write a partial `:data` map as if it merged; the five test files that exercise the fx (40 hits) contain 0 mentions of `rf/after-epoch|rf/parent-id|rf/invoke-id` and declare no `:after` / `:spawn`, against 41 test files carrying those needles tree-wide — the wipe is unpinned by construction.
- Action: make the `:data` leg merge — `(update merged :data merge (:data clean-patch))` in both the validated preview and the swap — and change spec/005:869 to say the patch's `:data` merges like an action's. If wholesale replacement is wanted for some reason, carry the reserved keys across the way `resolver/carry-actor-identity` does (resolver.cljc:125-147) plus the epoch maps. Decide: merge (zero-surprise, matches the action idiom) vs replace-with-carry (keeps "escape hatch = raw write").

### 2. `:entry` actions see the SOURCE `:state`, and `:always` guards/actions see `:event nil`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:2054-2079 (`collect-actions`), :3557 (`pick-always-transition`), :3969 (`drain-to-fixed-point`)
- What: `collect-actions` threads `snap` with `:state` unchanged while it runs exit → action → entry, so an `:entry` callback's ctx `:state` is the state being LEFT (the step map beside it already carries the correct `:state`, it is just not handed to the callback); and eventless selection passes `nil` as the event (`select-passing-candidate-indexed ... snapshot nil`, `apply-transition-once m snap nil ...`), so an `:always` guard/action/entry cannot see the event that triggered the macrostep — both XState v5 and SCXML `_event` expose it.
- Evidence: read the three sites; `callback-ctx` (:355-363) builds `:state (:state snapshot)` from whatever snapshot it is given. Spec §Path conventions table (005:852-854) lists `:state` and `:event` for `:entry`/`:exit`/guards without saying which state or that `:always` gets nil; §`:always` (005:1979-2105) never mentions the event. No test pins either: Grep `:event nil|event nil|nil event` over machines/test = 0 (control: `after-elapsed` = 90 hits / 25 files); Grep `entry.{0,80}:state` = 30 hits, all trace tags or spec keys, none asserting the ctx an `:entry` fn receives.
- Action: hand `collect-actions` the step's own `:state` (`(assoc snap :state state)` for the ctx of an `:entry`/`:exit` step — one line) and thread the macrostep's triggering event into the `:always` drain instead of `nil` (two call sites); then add one sentence to the 005:852 table saying what `:state` and `:event` are for lifecycle and eventless callbacks. Decide: match XState/SCXML (event visible) vs keep nil and document it — the former costs nothing and removes a "why is event nil" question the AI will ask.

### 3. Region `:entry`/`:exit` fired through a parallel-root `:on`/`:after` target lose `:all-state` / `:tags`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/parallel.cljc:1086-1091 (`apply-root-region-target`) vs :687-734 (`reduce-regions`)
- What: the root-target path builds `region-snap` as `{:state :data}` + counter/history only, so region callbacks run under a root-owned target get no cross-region keys, while the same callbacks run through the normal region reduce (`reduce-regions` threads `:all-state frozen-all-state :tags frozen-tags`) do.
- Evidence: read both constructors; `callback-ctx` (transition.cljc:359-360) adds `:all-state`/`:tags` only when the snapshot carries `:all-state`. spec/005:451: "For a guard / action running inside a parallel region, the context map additionally carries `:tags` ... and `:all-state`" — no carve-out for the root fallback.
- Action: thread the frozen `:all-state`/`:tags` into `region-snap` in `apply-root-region-target` (three lines), so the region ctx contract is one contract.

### 4. Raise-depth abort omits the visited `:path` the spec and the sibling always-depth abort carry  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:4054-4067 and parallel.cljc:1297-1305
- What: the `:rf.error/machine-raise-depth-exceeded` info map has `:actor-id :depth :frame :recovery` but no `:path`, while the always-depth abort includes `:path visited` (:3952-3958) and spec 005:1367 says "halt the cascade and surface the path" for the raise cycle too.
- Evidence: read both abort branches in `drain-to-fixed-point` and `drain-parent-queue`; the raise loop has the dequeued event ids in hand so the path is free.
- Action: add `:path` (the raised event ids in dequeue order) to the raise-depth abort info in both drains; the conformance and depth-abort tests assert only the error id, so nothing else moves.

### 5. Runtime engine errors are stamped `:where 'rf/reg-machine`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:198-207 (`machine-error`), used at :651-659 (`:rf.error/machine-bad-state-form`, "The snapshot is corrupt"), :214-227, :241-254 (unresolved guard/action at dispatch time)
- What: one helper hard-codes `'rf/reg-machine` as the user-facing call site, so a runtime failure while handling a dispatched event tells the programmer to look at registration.
- Evidence: read the helper and its three runtime call sites; the registration-time validators have their own `validation-error` with the same `:where`, which is right for them.
- Action: give `machine-error` a `:where` argument (or a runtime sibling defaulting to `'rf/dispatch`) and pass the right symbol at the runtime sites.

## Considered, left alone
- `#'var` / multimethod guards are rejected by `fn?` (`chase-ref` :178, `ref-resolves?` validation.cljc:165): a REPL nicety; re-frame apps re-register the machine, and the error names the fix.
- Nested raise handling restarts `always-depth` at 0 and drops the nested `::microsteps` from the `:rf.machine/transition` `:microsteps` tag (:4098-4101, :4164-4168): the bounds still compose exactly as 005:2059 states; only the trace count is low.
- `root-after-match` / `root-after-elapsed?` read a nil decl-path as the root timer via `(vec nil)` (:2265, :2322): only a hand-built event can carry nil there.
- Inline `:definition` spec maps (fns) ride runtime-db under `:rf/machine-type` and `:rf/prepared`: the spec sanctions the snapshot carrying the definition, and the SSR projector already elides `:data` only.
- An escape-hatch `:state` patch bypasses exit/entry, timer cancel/arm and history: that is what an escape hatch is — trust the programmer (finding 1 is about the keys the programmer cannot see, not this).

## Instruments and controls
- `git -C review-sep16 rev-parse --short HEAD` → d89a41e057.
- Grep `:rf/patch` over implementation/ → 17 hits / 7 files, every use a partial `:data` map; control: Grep `after-elapsed` over machines/test → 90 hits / 25 files.
- Grep `update-snapshot` over machines/test → 40 hits / 5 files; grep -c `rf/after-epoch|rf/parent-id|rf/invoke-id` in those 5 files → 0 each (also 0 `:after {` / `:spawn {` declarations); control: same needles across machines/test → 41 files.
- Grep `after-epoch-path` transition.cljc → :951 `(or (get-in ...) 0)`; Grep `rf/parent-id|rf/invoke-id` finalize.cljc → :389-390 read off child `:data`.
- Grep `rf/after-epoch` spec/005 → :2470 (reserved, user code does not write under it), :81, :1780; Read spec/005:846-875 (escape hatch: "merged onto that snapshot").
- Grep `all-state` spec/005 → :451 (region ctx keys); read parallel.cljc:687-734 and :1080-1118.

title: flows: fence direct-clear settle trace delivery to the captured frame owner
description:
Wrap the direct-clear settle pass in the existing exact-owner trace continuation scope, using the owner token it already receives. This closes one reproduced callback boundary without changing flow evaluation, direct-registration deferral, or the direct-clear commit boundary.

Ownership and revision
- Slice impl_flows; implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc, primarily settle-frame-flows! at lines 474-482; computed-trace production at lines 345-361. The caller is implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:933-967.
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 2aa96fa4d62f777e48a0ed1c859103aee07e65ed. Owned source paths are unchanged from the baseline.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Fresh independent finding under rf2-gwye. No remediation was performed or dispatched.

Confirmed behavior and cause
The direct clear's :rf.flow/cleared trace is wrapped in trace/call-with-continuation-predicate (registry.cljc:933-940). That scope ends BEFORE the separate settle! call at line 967. settle-frame-flows! runs run-flows-on-db with :exact-owner-token, which protects derivation/cache/output processing, but it supplies no trace continuation scope. Consequently the dependent's :rf.flow/computed emission captures the ordinary always-continue predicate. Exact-owner checks around evaluate-flow! cannot guard individual trace listeners when their delivery is deferred until the cold serialized region releases.

This differs from the ordinary event route, which inherits the router's exact-owner trace scope, and from the already-fenced direct register/replace/clear lifecycle emissions. The existing shared fan-out checks its captured predicate between listeners; it needs the caller to supply the actual owner. Relevant mechanism: implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:79-87 and snapshot-continuation at 109-131; trace/tooling.cljc's deferred-continue and deliver-to-tooling! capture that predicate for post-lock delivery.

Concrete public-operation reproducer
1. On frame :review.flow/subject, register producer :review.flow/producer with [:input] -> [:source], derive identity; register dependent :review.flow/dependent with [:source] -> [:derived], derive #(or % :absent).
2. Dispatch a seed event with {:db {:input 5}}. Confirm app-db {:input 5 :source 5 :derived 5}.
3. Register two trace listeners, destroyer first and observer second. Both select the dependent's :rf.flow/computed. The first calls destroy-frame! on the subject and then creates a same-id successor. The second records the event and frame/event-continuation-live? for the original owner token.
4. Call (rf/clear :flow :review.flow/producer {:frame :review.flow/subject}) directly, with no intervening dispatch.

Actual: the destroyer is called once and the observer receives the original dependent's computed event once, with :result :absent while event-continuation-live? for the original owner is FALSE. The successor ends with empty app-db, as expected. Precise timing matters: nested teardown emissions advance the outer fan-out during destroy-frame!, so the stale second delivery occurs after the old owner's destruction claim but BEFORE the successor is constructed. This report does not claim successor state was overwritten, or that the successor already existed at receipt.

Expected: the already-entered destroyer callback may finish, while every later callback in that computation's fan-out is suppressed once its captured owner is no longer live. This is the same exact-owner callback contract executable in flows_replace_clear_trace_incarnation_cljs_test.cljc:83-180 and :228-313 for the neighboring direct lifecycle emits. Listener order is used only to produce a deterministic witness; applications are not required to depend on that order.

Impact
An observer receives ordinary computed evidence for a frame after another listener has claimed its destruction. This makes the direct-clear compute stream disagree with the event and direct-lifecycle streams at the same supported callback boundary and can make tooling continue processing an obsolete frame. The confirmed impact is dev trace delivery; no application-state corruption or production failure is claimed.

Bounded repair
In settle-frame-flows!, wrap the out-of-drain pass (including its trace-producing evaluation/failure/schema-observation branches) in trace/call-with-continuation-predicate with #(frame/event-continuation-live? frame-id owner-token). Keep the existing exact-owner evaluator argument and exact db install. Use the shared AND-composing scope so any enclosing continuation remains respected. No new public hook, scheduler, event, per-flow owner registry, or transaction system is needed.

Acceptance
- Add a cross-host direct-clear regression shaped as the reproducer: first dependent-computed listener loses the owner; a subsequent listener receives zero such stale events.
- Include a live-owner control: one computed delivery, dependent updated to :absent, ordinary synchronous clear behavior preserved.
- Keep the existing direct-clear settle/failure, lifecycle trace incarnation, dispatch-settle ordering, and direct-registration deferral suites passing.
- Cover at least the computed trace at this boundary; put the shared scope around the entire settle pass so sibling skip/failure/schema emissions cannot escape the same owner accidentally.

Validation performed
- Fresh isolated JVM execution of 18 existing suites: 170 tests, 775 assertions, zero failures/errors, Java exit 0. Suites: flows-test, flows-settle-on-dispatch-test, flows-settle-ordering-test, flows-direct-clear-settle-cljs-test, flows-direct-clear-settle-failure-cljs-test, flows-direct-reg-deferral-cljs-test, flows-schema-validation-test, flows-destroy-frame-teardown-test, flows-first-registration-trace-incarnation-test, flows-first-registration-watch-incarnation-test, flows-replace-clear-trace-incarnation-cljs-test, flows-clear-reg-watch-incarnation-test, flows-lifecycle-drain-race-test, flows-path-focused-no-db-cljs-test, flows-runtime-partition-input-test, flows-rollback-dirty-check-test, flows-topo-test, flow-algebra-view-test (all re-frame namespaces).
- Fresh witness with three arms: live owner -> one observed computed event and {:input 5 :derived :absent}; destroy -> one stale second delivery with original owner false and final successor db {}; process-local repair control -> destroyer still called once, second observer receives zero events, final successor db {}. Java exit 0.
- The repair control used with-redefs around run-flows-on-db ONLY IN THE PROBE PROCESS to install the proposed trace scope. No source was modified.
- First probe attempt exited 1 because its extra assertion assumed the successor already existed during receipt. Its output disproved that timing assumption. Attempt 2 explicitly measures original-owner loss and passes; all claims above use attempt 2's narrower timing.
- Evidence files: ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_flows/impl_flows-focused-1.{clj,log,exit}; impl_flows-settle-trace-1.{clj,log,exit}; impl_flows-settle-trace-2.{clj,log,exit}. Every run printed gate root and asserted actual flows classloader source URLs under SOURCE_ROOT. Unpiped Java exit codes were captured independently. Cached Clojure 1.12.4/Malli 0.20.1; no dependency resolver/install, shared build, server, or CLJS compile was used.

History and limits
- Prior aggregate rf2-fzbj.17 is closed/no-action and remains so. Its bounded earlier review did not reproduce this direct-clear settle listener boundary. This is not a split of an old actionable finding.
- Current all-status title searches for flow and settle plus the open issue index found no identical dedicated open issue. rf2-g1zb is closed: its latest notes/close reason say dependent settling and the direct-call failure wording are fixed. rf2-f3yl is closed with an explicit normative decision to preserve direct-registration deferral; this issue does not reopen it. Latest three history entries for these records and rf2-fzbj.17 were checked newest-first.
- Source comments/test docstrings cite historical rf2-rxsldx for adjacent lifecycle-trace fencing; exact bd show returned no matching current record, so no current tracker status is inferred for that identifier.
- No CLJS execution, browser/advanced-elision/release build, full conformance corpus, or high-contention stress suite ran. Shared implementation and cross-host regression patterns were inspected; measured behavior is JVM/plain-atom only. No speculative failing-substrate or unrelated lifecycle hardening is included.

title: Convert Slim MetaFn callback props into stable JavaScript functions
description: Convert object-backed ClojureScript Fn callbacks into stable JavaScript-callable functions at reagent-slim's prop boundary. P2. This is the independently actionable split of rf2-fzbj.30 finding 2, revalidated on 2026-09-13. The inherited fence remains: remediation is held until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. This issue records review findings and does not authorize or dispatch implementation. Ownership and source Primary owner: adapter_reagent_slim, implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:606-649. Both explicit `(fn? prop-value) prop-value` arms at lines 619 and 637 pass object-backed Fn values through unchanged; the 3-argument DOM-aware form delegates to this conversion. The identity-only regression is implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/template_cljs_test.cljs:210-247. Baseline: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. Reviewed HEAD: 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. `git diff --name-only BASELINE -- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim` returned no paths: owned source is unchanged. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Concrete trigger ```clojure (def handler (with-meta (fn [_event] :clicked) {:probe true})) [:button {:on-click handler} "Click"] ;; Also affects callback props in [:> Foreign {:on-select handler}]. ``` Expected: the host receives a JavaScript function that forwards arguments and return values to handler. Repeated conversion of the same handler preserves the OUTPUT function's identity for memoization and callback refs. Actual: with-meta yields cljs.core/MetaFn, an object satisfying CLJS Fn. The converter returns that object unchanged. Its CLJS invocation protocol and .call helper work, but JavaScript's `handler(...)` syntax cannot invoke it. React DOM's listener boundary requires `typeof listener === 'function'`; foreign components invoking the callback also throw. Metadata attached to an otherwise valid callback therefore breaks event handling/interop. The tests reach the correct branch but assert exact input/output identity without testing native invocation, pinning a non-callable value. Suggested repair Keep ordinary JavaScript functions unchanged (they already leave via js-val?). For object-backed Fn values, provide a JS shim invoking the CLJS callable protocol and reuse that shim per input object so conversion preserves stable output identity. Keep the current named/map/collection conversion ordering. Update the misleading identity-only test/doc wording to require stable callable output, rather than identity with an object the host cannot invoke. Acceptance criteria - All three converter arities return `typeof function` for MetaFn and preserve the same output reference on repeated conversion of the same input. - Native JavaScript invocation forwards representative arguments and returns the callback result; include real React callback integration. - Use direct JS call syntax as the witness, not only CLJS invocation or `.call`: MetaFn has a .call method that conceals the defect. - Ordinary JavaScript callbacks retain input identity. Existing non-Fn IFn wrapping and named/map/collection conversion semantics remain intact. Validation and limits Executed `node C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/ai/surface-review-20260913/adapter_reagent_slim/review-adapter_reagent_slim-1.cjs`, exit 0, with same-stem .log and .exit receipts. SOURCE_ROOT and React 19.3.0 appear in the log. The probe proves MetaFn is fn? true but typeof object, that conversion preserves that object in all three arities, and that direct native invocation throws TypeError. A real React server render of a foreign function component calling props.onClick() throws `props.onClick is not a function`; the plain-function control renders `clicked`. Current source and cached source-map contents separately retain both pass-through fault branches. The witness loads only existing compiled namespace dependencies from implementation/out/node-test.js, excluding test namespaces and runner entrypoints. No compilation output is written. The DOM listener boundary was inspected, not browser-executed. No release/package build or full CLJS/browser suite was run. All synthetic instances are unmounted and the process exited. That historical correction and the published conversion ordering stand. notes:
REMEDIATED in PR #9757 (branch worker/slim-a), rebased base b7d9ce9169, together with its aggregate rf2-fzbj.30 finding 2. Re-verified at tip before fixing: the defect still held.

FIX: `reagent2/impl/template.cljs` — the two `(fn? prop-value) prop-value` arms and the `ifn?` arm beneath them collapse into ONE `ifn?` arm routed through a new private `js-callable`, a JS shim cached per input in a WeakMap. Every object-backed callable therefore converts to a real JS function, and repeated conversion of the same handler returns the SAME function, so memoisation and callback-ref identity hold. Plain JS functions are unchanged — they still leave earlier at `js-val?` by identity. Named/map/collection conversion ordering is untouched. Collapsing the pair also gives the non-Fn IFn case that same stable identity instead of allocating a fresh wrapper per render.

TESTS, RED before and green after. All three arities asserted `typeof function` with stable output identity; the invocation witness is a NATIVE call (`Reflect.apply`), never CLJS invocation or `.call`, both of which MetaFn implements and which concealed the defect in the old identity-only regression — that test is replaced rather than extended. Real React integration on two lanes: a `react-dom/server` render of a foreign component calling `props.onSelect(...)`, and in the browser a real click on a metadata-bearing `:on-click` plus a metadata-bearing callback `:ref`. (let [payload {:user (with-meta {:x 1} {:cache-id 7})}

```clojure
;; wire => {:rf.mcp/dedup-table {7 {:x 1}, de-dupe.cache/cache-0 {:user 7}}}
;; expanded => {:user 7}
```

Repair: thread the allocated cache id separately through the traversal, or use an invocation-private identity marker that proves tag ownership. Do not trust a static metadata key or merely a cache-N-looking value. Preserve the existing equality-based compression, public wrapper, allocator grammar and disabled/no-repeat behavior.

Acceptance: add a .cljc regression using this public-wrapper reproducer; assert unchanged value and no invented wrapper.
