title: test: rows guarded on js/document in a non -dom-cljs-test file execute in NEITHER lane
description:
A TEST FILE'S ROWS CAN EXECUTE IN NEITHER LANE, AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. Found by resizewit-a while
building the rf2-po5r witness (PR #9677), and confirmed by an executed plant rather than by reading.

THE MECHANISM, measured on the inline resize-handle yield gate:

  * its rows are wrapped in `(when (exists? js/document) …)`, and the `:node-test` build has no jsdom,
    so every one of them is SKIPPED in the node lane;
  * the file's name does not end `-dom-cljs-test`, so the `:browser-test` build NEVER LOADS IT.

Rows in neither lane. The plant that proves it: with the yield gate deliberately bypassed, the browser lane
went red with exactly ONE failure — in resizewit-a's new row alone. No pre-existing row noticed, because no
pre-existing row ever runs.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN ORDINARY MISSING COVERAGE. A test that does not exist is visible as an absence. These
tests EXIST — they are written, committed, reviewed, and counted by anyone reading the file — and they assert
real properties. They simply never execute. Every instrument that would normally catch a coverage hole reports
them as present: the file is there, the deftests are there, the assertions are there, and both lanes are green.
It is a hollow gate whose hollowness is invisible from every direction except the one resizewit-a happened to
approach it from.

WHAT IS WANTED — A CENSUS FIRST, AND IT IS THE DELIVERABLE:

Find every file under `tools/*/test` and `implementation/**/test` that carries `(when (exists? js/document) …)`
rows (or any equivalent document guard) and whose name does NOT end `-dom-cljs-test`. Each such file is a
candidate: its guarded rows run in no lane. Report the list with, for each, how many guarded rows it holds.

DO NOT ASSUME EVERY HIT IS A DEFECT. A file may guard a subset of its rows deliberately while its unguarded
rows carry the real coverage, in which case the guarded rows are dead but harmless and the right repair may be
deletion rather than promotion. Read each before classifying it. `tools/xray/test/.../resize_handle_cljs_test.cljs`
is the known-positive control — it should appear in any correct census.

THEN, and only once the census is agreed: for each genuinely dead row, either move it into a `-dom-cljs-test`
file so the browser build loads it, or delete it and say what replaced it. **Do not do that half silently** —
promoting a row that has never run may red the lane for real, which is the finding arriving rather than a
regression.

SCOPE: the census is the first deliverable and may be the whole of it. Do not change a build config, do not
add a lane, do not rename a build. If the right repair turns out to be a naming convention or a classifier
rule, say so with the reasoning and file it rather than doing it here.

GATE: whatever lanes the touched files belong to. Note that a row moved INTO a `-dom-cljs-test` file starts
executing for the first time, so its first green is real evidence and its first red is a real finding — treat
a red as information, not as your own breakage, and report it rather than repairing it into green.
notes:
PROVENANCE: found by resizewit-a while building the rf2-po5r witness (PR #9677). It reported the finding and correctly did NOT widen its own bounded change to chase it. Recorded so a later audit reopening rf2-po5r recognises this as the same finding rather than a second one.

CONTROL FOR ANY CENSUS: tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/resize_handle_cljs_test.cljs is the known-positive — it must appear in a correct census, and a census that misses it is broken rather than reassuring.

FENCE-STATE: 2026-09-11 18:48 AUSEST, trunk dbf04ed509 — DISPATCHED to lanecensus-a (worker/lanecensus-a). DO NOT DISPATCH AGAIN.

Briefed census-first, with three things the bead does not say:

DERIVE THE LANE RULE, DO NOT TRUST IT. The worker was told to read implementation/shadow-cljs.edn for what
:node-test and :browser-test actually include, and to confirm the -dom-cljs-test suffix rule is real rather
than folklore. If the rule differs from what this bead says, that is a finding and it changes the whole
census — a more valuable outcome than a census built on a wrong rule.

THREE BUCKETS, NOT ONE LIST. Genuinely dead rows asserting something nothing else covers; dead rows whose
property is covered elsewhere; and guards that are correct as they stand. A file may guard a subset
deliberately while its unguarded rows carry the real coverage, in which case deletion rather than promotion
is the repair.

A PROMOTED ROW'S FIRST RED IS A FINDING, NOT BREAKAGE. A row moved into a loading file starts executing for
the first time, so its first red is the exercise arriving. The worker was told to report it and NOT repair
it into green.

FENCE NOTE: resize_handle_cljs_test.cljs is both the census CONTROL and the subject of PR #9677, which is
ready and merging shortly. lanecensus-a may read, count and cite it but not edit it; if its repair wants to
move rows out of that file I will sequence that behind #9677 rather than let it race.

ALSO CARRIED: the instrument caution measured today that a census can DIE PARTWAY and still print plausible
output — a UnicodeEncodeError killed one inside file 4 of 8 after emitting three files' results, caught only
by reading the exit code. The worker was told to assert that files-examined equals files-intended, not merely
that the output looks finished.
LANE RULE AS DERIVED AT SOURCE, AND THE COROLLARY THAT IS FALSE (lanecensus-b, 2026-09-11, PR #9681).

The bead asked for the lane rule to be derived rather than trusted. Derived, and measured:

  :node-test    :ns-regexp "cljs-test$"        (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn)
  :browser-test :ns-regexp ".*-dom-cljs-test$"

Both halves of this bead's description are CORRECT: a document-guarded row in a non -dom-cljs-test file
does execute in neither lane, because the browser build never loads the file and node has no DOM.

WHAT IS FALSE IS THE COROLLARY EVERY READER DRAWS NEXT — that moving a row into a -dom-cljs-test file
moves it ONTO the browser lane and OFF the node one. It does not. `cljs-test$` is a bare SUFFIX match
and `-dom-cljs-test` ends in `cljs-test`, so a DOM-tagged namespace is loaded by BOTH builds. The
overlap is deliberate and shadow-cljs.edn documents it above :browser-test: DOM-tagged files run on both
targets so their cross-runtime asserts keep firing in Node.

So the correct repair for a dead guarded row is MOVE THE FILE AND KEEP THE GUARD. The guard was never
the defect; the file's LOCATION was. Moving a row ADDS the browser lane.

MEASURED RATHER THAN READ. The first repair pass dropped the guard on the way and reddened
CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test) — node ran a localStorage round-trip in a runtime with no localStorage and
load returned []. After restoring the guard, a focused run of the compiled node bundle against the new
-dom-cljs-test namespace reports 2 tests / 2 assertions / 0 failures, which is positive evidence that
:node-test LOADS a -dom-cljs-test namespace rather than skipping it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMAINING 15 FILES (rf2-r51p). Option (1) in PR #9681's hand-back — "move to a
-dom-cljs-test namespace" — does NOT cost the fast lane, as that hand-back states. The file keeps
running on node; only the guarded rows are inert there. That changes the trade-off between options (1)
and (2), and any worker repairing one of those files must keep the guard when it moves the file.

A SHAPE NOTE. A bare (when ...) guard leaves the node lane holding a deftest with ZERO assertions, which
is this bead's own subject relocated rather than fixed. The shape used in #9681 branches instead and
asserts a visible skip marker on the node side, matching the existing browser? branches in
palette.empty-row-frame-context-dom-cljs-test.
close_reason:
Done. PR #9681 merged 7bdb2253e2a8489d8efe13f59f2801e337bdaab2, at band 87 with nothing non-terminal, all runs
complete at head, and a clean merge-tree against trunk.

THE CENSUS IS THE DELIVERABLE AND IT IS WIDER THAN THIS BEAD STATED. The guard has a SECOND
spelling, and it is the larger half: eleven files route the check through a local (browser?)
predicate -- (and (exists? js/window) (.-localStorage js/window)) -- which is invisible to a census
keyed on `exists? js/document`. Counting both takes it from 7 files to 16, 106 guarded assertions,
executing in NEITHER lane. Several of those predicates carry docstrings asserting "browser-test
returns true": the author's intent, never realised.

ONE FILE REPAIRED HERE (recents), deliberately. The remaining fifteen are rf2-r51p.

A COORDINATOR ERROR THIS ITEM EXPOSED, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST TWO WORKER CYCLES. I ruled that the
repair shape was "move it to a -dom-cljs-test namespace" WITHOUT reading the two lane selectors.
implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:990-1004 says in terms that :node-test's `cljs-test$` regex matches
BOTH suffixes, so a -dom-cljs-test file runs on BOTH targets -- the move ADDS the browser lane
rather than removing node's. This PR's first head dropped the guard on that ruling and went red in
the node lane, where localStorage does not exist (local-storage/available? returns false, save!
no-ops, load answers []). The fix was to KEEP the guard and move the file: true in the browser lane,
false in node, which loads it and harmlessly skips. The guard was never the defect -- the file's
LOCATION was.

TWO CASES WORSE THAN THE COUNT SUGGESTS, both now owned by rf2-r51p: toolbar_persistence with 20 of
20 rows guarded (an entire namespace billed as a regression net executing nothing), and xray_preset,
where a dead PRECONDITION row left a live assertion passing vacuously -- a false green rather than a
gap. See also rf2-whld, filed from this work: no floor in this repo counts EXECUTED assertions, which
is the structural reason the class went unnoticed.

title: Incomplete rf2-d2aj repair: same-frame App-db panels still share inspector lifecycle state
description:
Merged-PR audit of #9597, landing ba26dd1aa76398b5ec48856d28979f4d4c060719. The cross-frame repair is sound and should be retained. The source rf2-d2aj explicitly required instance isolation including two panels in the same frame, but this remaining part has no separately trackable open owner. The PR and closed ruling acknowledge it as outside this worker's surface; this Bead carries that residual without reopening or changing the ruling.

The remaining concrete trigger is two App-db Panel mounts under one frame provider. app_db_diff.cljs Panel ignores _props and passes no panel-instance identity; app_db_diff_state.cljs value-body still derives app-db-state/top from the repeated top render-id. edn_inspector.cljs lifecycle-key now returns [frame-id mount-id], and edn-inspector-view uses it for the ref, observer and projection cache. Both same-frame panels therefore still get one key. The widget tells the caller to name the instance, but the App-db caller supplies a fixed name and exposes no way to thread a distinct one. Merely qualifying the store key again without separating the two width slots would also be insufficient: widths remain keyed by mount-id inside the shared frame.

Independently reproduced with the exact unedited landed lifecycle functions extracted to an isolated ClojureScript 1.12.145 Node probe. Both callbacks use the same frame dispatcher and fake elements of widths 100 and 200, with a ResizeObserver stub. Repeated app-db-state/top: identical refs, one store entry, one observer, only width 100 recorded; detaching the second removes the surviving first panel's state, disconnects its observer and clears the shared width. Positive control with distinct caller identities in that SAME frame: two refs, two observers, widths 100 and 200, and after second detach the first state, width 100 and active observer remain. Compile and probe attempt 1 both exit 0. This is a callback-state reproduction, not a new browser integration run.

The new R9/W5 rows cover different frames and are useful; they do not cover this same-frame residual. All four changed files byte-match tested CI SHA f273347f0cd1c736dae3e4ea37cd0168bf277341. Node 11550/57996 plus 2/8; browser 887/4908; Xray JVM 1276/6118, all zero failures/errors.

Deduplication: open rf2-pb0l explicitly concerns the unused inspect-view one-arity facade and its constant rf-xray-inspect-root default. It does not own this App-db Panel caller or threading correction. Open rf2-o7p7 owns duplicate DOM testids, a different defect. Do not rewrite either owner's criteria or change any existing status. This is a focused residual of rf2-d2aj, not a request to revisit the accepted cross-frame lifecycle key.
acceptance_criteria: Give concurrent App-db Panel mounts in one frame independent stable mount identity through the existing panel-to-inspector path, including independent measured-width slots as well as observer/ref/projection state. Keep logical site identity for expansion/zoom and deliberate epoch remount behavior. Add a focused same-frame, two-panel regression with distinguishable widths that fails on #9597 and verifies the survivor continues measuring after the other unmounts. Preserve the working cross-frame behavior. Use the smallest caller/boundary identity change allowed by Fresco; no hooks in a defview body and no general identity framework.
notes: Merged-PR audit #9605: new open finding rf2-4bsq owns the namespaced-keyword collision in Panel-bridge. Reagent converts :left/panel and :right/panel to the same "panel" prop before instance-token runs; accepted string IDs work. Linked discovered-from this Bead. This is separate from standalone facade owner rf2-2n8q. Existing status, criteria, close_reason and closed_at preserved; no reopening requested.
close_reason:
Landed as PR #9605, merged 7886452fd0. Four files, +566/-74: panels/app_db_diff.cljs, panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs and their two test namespaces. File list read against the item -- two source files and their own tests, nothing surprising in either direction. CI at merge: 87 checks 0 pending 0 failed, 4 runs at head all completed, 0 workflow lines and 0 job keys since merge-base.

THE REPAIR: Panel takes an optional :instance-id prop, threaded panel-tree -> state-body -> the section renderers -> value-body. **Naming an instance qualifies BOTH the edn-inspector :mount-id AND the expansion/zoom :site-id, and that pair is the whole point** -- the lifecycle key is [frame-id mount-id] while the width slot is keyed by the bare mount-id inside the frame, so one qualification moves both. title: xray: :rf.xray/set-target-frame reads a DESTROYED target frame's epoch history, emitting :rf.error/frame-destroyed once per Story variant mount
description:
Discovered by rf2-kuky.18 (PR #9306), which removed the Story shell's page-wide no-op :errors listener. That claim had been MASKING these errors; with it gone they reach the console and `npm run test:story-feature-load` is RED at 8 console errors (a PR gate, test.yml:4127).

They are XRAY's, not Story's. A diagnostic :errors listener captured all eight records, identical in shape:

  {:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed
   :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame
   :frame :rf/xray
   :source-coord {:ns day8.re-frame2-xray.epoch
                  :file "tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs" :line 108}}

MECHANISM. Xray holds a STALE TARGET FRAME across a Story variant switch. The :rf.xray/set-target-frame handler (epoch.cljs:108) evaluates (rf/epoch-history target) where target is the previously observed frame; Story has destroyed it, so the read recover-but-emits :rf.error/frame-destroyed. Once per variant mount, 8 across the feature-load run. The record is attributed to :frame :rf/xray, which is ALIVE - the destroyed frame is the READ TARGET, not the record's owning frame.

WHY THE rf2-kuky.18 SINK ARM CANNOT COVER IT. The new console-fallback predicate owns a record when its frame routed it to a registered :observability :errors sink. route-frame? is false for EVERY frame-destroyed emission (rf2-bf0io, so a dead incarnation's bare id can never resolve to a same-id successor's sink), so the route is suppressed and the delivered-count is necessarily 0. Giving :rf/xray an :observability :errors policy would NOT silence these. The fix has to be in Xray.

LIKELY FIX (not ruled). Either clear/repoint :target-frame when the targeted frame is destroyed, or guard the (rf/epoch-history target) read against an unresolved frame. The general case matters beyond Story: any app that destroys a frame Xray is targeting hits this. Do NOT fix it from the Story side - that would paper over it at the wrong layer and leave the general case broken.

SCOPE. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs plus the tools/xray/spec update every Xray dispatch carries. Needs a regression test.

SEQUENCING. PR #9306 should not merge until this lands, because test:story-feature-load is a per-PR gate and #9306 turns it red by revealing this.
notes:
WORKER xrayepoch-a, 2026-09-05. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9312 (open, ready for review). Branch worker/xrayepoch-a, rebased onto ba9b78acb1.

THIS BEAD DIAGNOSED THE WRONG MECHANISM. The description says Xray "reads (rf/epoch-history target) against the destroyed frame" and that "the record is attributed to :rf/xray, which is alive". Both halves are refuted at source, and the second is backwards.

REFUTATION AT SOURCE. rf/epoch-history -> re-frame.core-epoch/epoch-history (a defwrapper with :on-absent :empty-vec) -> late-bind :epoch/epoch-history -> re-frame.epoch/epoch-history -> re-frame.epoch.state/history-for, whose whole body is (or (get @histories frame-id) []). It consults NO frame registry, so it cannot raise :rf.error/frame-destroyed for any target, destroyed or otherwise.

WHERE THE RECORD ACTUALLY COMES FROM. router/emit-frame-destroyed! stamps :frame with the DISPATCH TARGET ((:frame envelope)), and error-emit/error-source-coord resolves a frame-destroyed :source-coord out of the [:event id] registry — i.e. the reg-event registration line. So {:frame :rf/xray, :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame, :source-coord epoch.cljs:108} reads: a dispatch of :rf.xray/set-target-frame into :rf/xray was rejected because :rf/xray IS THE MISSING FRAME. The coord names the handler, not the caller — which is exactly what made the record look like an epoch.cljs bug.

MEASURED, three-way probe on the node-test runner (probe deleted before the PR opened):
  A  :rf/xray ALIVE, read target DESTROYED  -> [] , nothing emitted   <- the bead claim, refuted
  B  :rf/xray ABSENT                        -> the exact field-report record
  C  :rf/xray DESTROYED                     -> the exact field-report record

THE REAL GENERAL CASE. Xray registers its whole :rf.xray/* instruction set at preload, but :rf/xray was created by open! — a React commit. In between, Xray is ADDRESSABLE BUT NOT WRITABLE: any dispatch into it recovers-but-emits, drops the host intent, and misattributes the diagnostic. A host that sets :rf.xray/auto-open? false (both Story testbeds do, in their run fns) never leaves that window until it opens a panel.

THE FIX. :rf/xray genuinely cannot be seated at preload LOAD time — rf/make-frame goes through rf.substrate.adapter/make-state-container, which raises :rf.error/no-adapter-installed with no adapter; that is what rf2-e9s81 reverted, and it is about the ADAPTER, not about opening. The preload already runs a bounded readiness loop watching for adapter install, so the seat moved there. auto-open-inline! -> boot-on-runtime-ready!; the open is now the conditional half. The first-mount seed/hydrate fan-out stays lazy behind seeded-frame-ids. Statement: Xrays frame exists as soon as the host runtime does, not when its UI opens. title: api(registry): pair-mcp `:machine` kind evals `re-frame.core/machines` / `machine-meta`, which do not exist
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registry-introspection.md (ref registry-introspection.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`list-handlers {kind "machine"}` and `handler-meta {kind "machine" id …}` in the pair MCP server build eval forms that name two vars `re-frame.core` does not define, so against a running app they evaluate an undefined symbol and the wire returns the eval-error envelope instead of a machine list / spec.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs:261` — `machine-form` builds `"(if-let [m (re-frame.core/machine-meta " id-edn ")] (dissoc m :handler-fn) {:ok? false :reason :not-registered :kind :machine :id …})"`.
- `handler_meta.cljs:386` — `list-form`'s `:machine` branch is the literal string `"(vec (sort (re-frame.core/machines)))"`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` defines neither: `rg '^\(defn? (machines|machine-meta)\b'` over it returns nothing; the only hits are docstring mentions (lines 11, 393, 659, 1484, 1872, 2749). The fns live at `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:180` (`machines`) and `:189` (`machine-meta`); `spec/API.md:22` records the rule ("the optional features' non-registration query / introspection / lifecycle helpers are NOT re-exported from `re-frame.core`; reach them through … `re-frame.machines` (… `machines` / `machine-meta` …)"). The `re-frame.core` docstring at `:1901` dispatches only `:machine-guard` / `:machine-action`.
- No test reaches the strings: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/handler_meta_test.cljs:582` asserts that OTHER kinds do NOT contain `"re-frame.core/machines"`; `:660` and `:691` cover only the `:frame`+machine refusal; the ns docstring `:6-7` still names the core vars. The tool's own spec repeats the stale route: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:3230` ("routes through `(re-frame.core/machine-meta id)`") and `:3323` ("wraps `(re-frame.core/machines)`").
- Every other kind already routes through the runtime preload via `ef/rt-call` (`registrar-list` at `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:605`, `registrar-describe` `:720`, `frame-registrar-list` `:840`, `frame-registrar-describe` `:813`). The preload ALREADY carries the machine door: it requires `re-frame.machines` (`runtime.cljs:72`), and defines `machines-list` (`:1139`, `(vec (rf.machines/machines))`) and `machine-describe` (`:1144`, `(or (rf.machines/machine-meta id) {:ok? false :reason :not-a-machine :id id})`). `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md:47` already documents `machine-describe`. The tool side simply never switched to them.
- Latent second defect on the same path: a machine spec carries fn values under `:guards` / `:actions` (Spec 005), and `machine-describe` does NOT run `strip-fns` (`runtime.cljs:743-751` does it for `registrar-describe` precisely because nested fns make the EDN wire report `:unserializable`). `machine-form`'s `dissoc :handler-fn` cannot reach nested fns.

## Target

`handler_meta.cljs`:

```clojure
;; before (:386)
(= :machine kind) "(vec (sort (re-frame.core/machines)))"
;; after
(= :machine kind) (ef/emit (ef/rt-call 'machines-list))

;; before (:261) — a hand-built string naming a non-existent var
;; after — one expression, one round-trip, uniform envelope
(ef/emit (ef/rt-call 'machine-describe id))   ; + shape the runtime's {:ok? false :reason :not-a-machine} into the
                                              ;   tool's uniform {:ok? false :reason :not-registered :kind :machine :id id}
```

Runtime side (`skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs`): `machine-describe` returns `(strip-fns (dissoc spec :handler-fn))` on a hit so the guards/actions maps arrive as the readable `:rf/fn` sentinel, exactly as `registrar-describe` does; `machines-list` returns the sorted id vector (it already does `vec`; add `sort` so the two branches of `list-form` agree). Keep the preload as the ONLY place that names a framework var — that is what makes @registry-introspection.3 (which deletes `rf.machines/machines` / `machine-meta` and rewrites these two preload bodies as a filter over the generic read) invisible to the MCP server.

## Corroboration

Both reviewers. Fable `registry-introspection.md` §The problem ("pair-MCP … emit eval forms naming `re-frame.core/machine-meta` and `re-frame.core/machines`, which `re-frame.core` no longer exports … so `list-handlers {kind "machine"}` against a running app evaluates an undefined var"); codex `registration-inspection.md` §Codex Thoughts ("should be corrected even if the API redesign is deferred. A stale symbol inside generated code is still a real consumer … Test the generated expression against a runtime namespace, not just its string shape").

## Deletion list

The two literal `re-frame.core/…` strings in `handler_meta.cljs` (`:261`, `:386`) and the docstring claims at `:88`, `:219`, `:245`, `:376`. No public API changes.

## Consumers to migrate

None outside the tool: `examples/` 0, `testbeds/` 0. `tools/mcp-conformance` fixtures classify `list-handlers` / `handler-meta` as read-only by tool NAME only (`test/fixtures/re-frame2-pair-classifications.json:13-14`) and pin no eval string — unaffected.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:3230`, `:3323` — say the `:machine` kind routes through `re-frame2-pair.runtime/machine-describe` / `machines-list` (which wrap `re-frame.machines/machine-meta` / `machines` today).
- `handler_meta_test.cljs`: fix the ns docstring (`:6-7`); ADD positive pins for the machine branch of both tools (`list-handlers {kind "machine"}` emits `machines-list`; `handler-meta {kind "machine"}` emits `machine-describe`; neither emits any `re-frame.core/` or `re-frame.machines/` symbol); keep `:582`.
- Add the probe codex asked for, in the cheapest honest form: a test that every `rt-call` symbol `handler-meta-tool` / `list-handlers-tool` can emit (`registrar-list`, `registrar-describe`, `frame-registrar-list`, `frame-registrar-describe`, `machines-list`, `machine-describe`) is a top-level `defn` in `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs` (read the file; the server tests run on node and cannot load the browser preload). rf2-yo4s's census did this by hand once; a test keeps it done.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/runtime/` (JVM tests over the preload, e.g. `registrar_describe_test.clj`): add one test that `machine-describe` returns no raw fn for a spec with a fn-valued `:guards` entry.
- No `spec/api-manifest.edn` change, no migration entry, no conformance corpus change. `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/capabilities.md:46` already names `re-frame.machines/*` — leave it to rf2-66xy8's lane.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Independent of every other bead in this area; land FIRST (small, and .3 relies on the tool routing through the preload). No hot-zone file. Do not touch `trace_window.cljs` / `watch_epochs.cljs` (rf2-yo4s) or `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs|references` (rf2-66xy8).

Gates, foreground to completion: `cd tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp && npm test` (shadow-cljs `server-test` + node); the preload's JVM tests under `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests`; CI's `mcp_live` surface fires on any pair-mcp change (`TESTING.md:208`), and the live hermetic suite (`test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite`, `TESTING.md:34`) is the end-to-end witness if a shadow nREPL is available locally — say in the PR body whether it ran.

## Risks

Low. The envelope shape must stay uniform across kinds (`{:ok? false :reason :not-registered :kind :machine :id id}` on a miss) — pin it. Do not "fix" this by re-exporting `machines` / `machine-meta` on `re-frame.core`: the front-porch rule (`spec/API.md:22`) and @registry-introspection.3 both go the other way.

## Local dossier

title: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs: audit every tier roster for phantom paths and extend the existsSync guard beyond the conformance loop
description:
`implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`'s `SECURITY_TIER_FILES` block carries the same phantom-path defect that rf2-z23f fixed one tier over in `CONFORMANCE_TIERS`, and its own comment records a previous instance of it.

FOUND 2026-09-04 by the worker on rf2-z23f (PR #9133), which repaired the conformance tier and observed that the security block IMMEDIATELY BELOW has the identical shape. That block's comment says its own replaced row asserted from a `security.cljc` that never existed — so this is the third occurrence of one bug class in one file, and the first two were each found by accident rather than by a check.

WHY IT MATTERS: a tier pin naming a file that does not exist CANNOT FAIL. The classifier believes it covers a tier it has never reached, and the mirror suite passes because the row is inert rather than because the coverage is real. That is fail-open, and it is invisible: nothing distinguishes an inert row from a satisfied one.

WHAT TO DO. Verify every path in every tier roster in that file is TRACKED, with two independent instruments and controls that fire — the rf2-z23f worker used `git log --all --diff-filter=A` (control found `7eae1212ac`) and `git rev-list --all --objects` (control found many). Repair any phantom row to the real tracked path.

THE DURABLE FIX IS THE GUARD, NOT THE ROWS. PR #9133 added an `fs.existsSync` guard in the conformance loop, and its sabotage run proved the fail-open is closed: replanting the phantom now reddens the suite where that row was green before. Extend that guard to cover EVERY tier roster in the file, so a fourth occurrence cannot be silent. title: hic: hot reload REPLACES every DOM node (focus and caret lost) while api-reference.md says h/render! reconciles - state survives, the DOM does not, and no page says so
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE.

FILED AGAINST THE PILOT S OWN CLASSIFICATION, DELIBERATELY. The pilot graded this row
published / none, and it was right to: the documented shape worked first time and nothing
it read was wrong about what it claimed. But the measurement underneath it contradicts a
sentence in api-reference.md, and a factual contradiction in a published page is a defect
whatever the row is graded. The operator files it; the grading stands.

THE CONTRADICTION IN ONE LINE. api-reference.md calls h/render! the hot-reload door and
says React reconciles the new tree against the one on the page. Measured on a hot reload,
nothing is reconciled: every DOM node is replaced, <main> included, and focus and caret go
with them. State survives completely (app-db, the resource cache, an open inline edit,
scroll position); the DOM does not. The mechanism the pilot names is that a reload
redefines each h/defview var, so React sees a new component TYPE and remounts.

Chapter 00 promises the state half and is silent on the DOM half, so a reader meets the
loss of focus mid-typing with nothing in the corpus that predicted it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F14 · outcome 4 · `published` · `none`

**Trying to** Change a Hicasso view with the build running and see what
survived. Set up first: a card created through the UI (so the **resource cache**
differed from its seeded value), an unsubmitted draft in the new-issue field, the
fail-next-write toggle armed, an inline edit open on a card, the caret parked at
offset 5 inside that edit field, and the page scrolled to y=299.

**Expected** Chapter 00 §"Hot reload": "The root, frame, app-db, and
subscriptions survive, so changing the view does not reset the counter or leak
registrations."

**Instead** Exactly that, and no more. Editing `[:h1 "Linearlite — optimistic
issue board"]` to `[:h1 "Linearlite — HOT RELOADED"]` with `npx shadow-cljs
watch app` running, measured in the live page before and after:

| Fact | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the edited `h1` | old text | **new text** — the edit arrived |
| cards on the board | `srv-3, srv-4, srv-1, srv-2` | **unchanged** — `srv-4` was created through the UI before the reload, so the **resource cache survived** |
| unsubmitted draft (app-db) | `"an unsubmitted draft"` | **unchanged** |
| fail-next-write toggle (app-db) | armed | **still armed** |
| inline edit open (app-db) | yes | **still open** |
| scroll position | 299 | **299** |
| `document.activeElement` | the edit input | **lost** — no longer the field |
| caret offset in that field | 5 | **lost** |
| the card's DOM node is the same object | — | **false** |
| that node is still in the document | — | **false** |
| even `<main>` is the same node | — | **false** |

Console confirmed the documented route ran:
`shadow-cljs: load JS linearlite/core.cljs` then
`shadow-cljs: call linearlite.core/rerender!`.

**Looked at** `00-installation.md` §"Hot reload" and §"Mount a first screen"
(the `^:dev/after-load` shape); `api-reference.md` §Roots, where `h/render!` is
"the hot-reload door: React reconciles the new tree against the one on the
page."

**Resolved by** Nothing needed — the documented shape worked first time. The
finding is in the gap between what the docs promise and what a developer
actually experiences. **State survives completely; the DOM does not.** Every
node was replaced and focus and caret went with them, because a reload redefines
each `h/defview` var, React sees a new component *type*, and a changed type is a
remount rather than a reconcile. So the api-reference's "React reconciles the new
tree against the one on the page" is true of `h/render!` in general and
misleading about the case it is named for: on a hot reload there is nothing left
to reconcile against.

That matters most for the thing you are most likely to be doing — tweaking a
form's markup while mid-edit in that form. Your app-db draft survives; your caret
does not.

**Bead** Chapter 00's hot-reload paragraph is accurate and incomplete. Add the
other half: "The DOM is rebuilt: a reload redefines each view, so React remounts
rather than reconciles, and focus, caret, scroll-into-view and any DOM-owned
state are lost. App-db, the resource cache and subscriptions are not." A reader
who knows this stops hunting for the bug when their caret jumps.
notes:
CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE SECOND BLINDED PILOT. This bead was filed from pilot 2
(LinearLite); pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit) hit hot reload keeping state and losing the DOM in the same
session, in a different application, from the same 29 pages, without either agent
seeing the other's workspace, log or output. Two independent readings landing on one
gap is the strongest signal this instrument produces, and it moves the finding out of
the range where one reader's idiosyncrasy explains it.

Pilot 1's entry, verbatim:

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F16 · outcome 4 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Change a migrated view with the build running and record what survived.

**What happened**

It works, in both directions, and the state that should survive did. Measured in
headless Chrome against the live `shadow-cljs watch`, with the app first put
into a non-default state (a tag filter applied, so the home machine's `:filter`
region is `:tagged` and the URL is `/realworld/tag/intro`):

| | before | after reload | after revert |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| banner text | "A place to share your knowledge." | "…knowledge. (hot-reloaded)" | "A place to share your knowledge." |
| route | `/realworld/tag/intro` | `/realworld/tag/intro` | `/realworld/tag/intro` |
| machine state (active chip) | `intro` | `intro` | `intro` |
| app-db (sidebar tags) | 4 tags | 4 tags | 4 tags |

**Survived**: the frame, app-db, the machine's region state, the route, and the
subscriptions feeding all of them. **Did not survive**: DOM node identity —
every node was rebuilt. I stamped a JS property on three live nodes before the
edit; all three came back `null` afterwards, including the one in the *Reagent*
shell that the edit did not touch.

**The friction**

`00-installation.md`'s hot-reload section is written for one shape — a
`defonce` root handle plus `^:dev/after-load` calling `h/render!` — and states
the guarantee as "The root, frame, app-db, and subscriptions survive". Every
word of that held here. But it says nothing about **node identity**, which is
the half a developer actually notices: a rebuilt subtree loses focus, caret,
scroll position and any uncontrolled input's text on every save.

And for a half-migrated tree there is a specific reason to expect a rebuild
that the docs never mention. `h/as-component` is "Declared once at top level,
beside the view" — a plain `def` — so a namespace reload re-evaluates it and
mints a **new React component type**. I measured that directly:

```
"after": {"bridgeIdentical": false, "toggleMarker": null}
```

`window.__probe0 === realworld_http.articles.home_page_component` is `false`
after the reload. A new component type is a remount by React's own rules, so a
bridged screen cannot reconcile across a reload of its own namespace, ever.

I want to be careful about what I proved: in this application the whole tree
was rebuilt anyway — editing `articles.cljs` reloads `core.cljs`, which
redefines the shell's own views — so I could not isolate the bridge's
contribution. What I measured is that the bridge's identity does change, which
is sufficient on its own for the subtree it heads.

**Looked at**

- `00-installation.md` "Hot reload", "Production builds"
- `09-interop.md` "Render a Hicasso view from native React"
- `api-reference.md` `h/render!` ("The hot-reload door"), `h/as-component`
- `cookbook.md` "Boot an application" (the `defonce` handle and why)

**Bead**

Say what hot reload costs as well as what it keeps, and say what
`h/as-component`'s `def` means for a reloaded namespace — it is the one door
whose identity a reload changes, and it is the door a partial migration is
built on.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9149 (2026-09-04): REOPENED. The corrected Markdown now contradicts shipped contract surfaces. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:660-669 still tells users that reloaded code meets its existing DOM and contrasts render! with mount! discarding every node/component state. consumer_app.cljs:129-136 says nothing is torn down and DOM/component state survive; the editor, typeahead, todo, and slice example reload docstrings repeat that guarantee. The real HMR gate and hmr_remount_cljs_test assert the opposite: changed types replace nodes, lose focus/caret and child hook state, while durable re-frame state survives. Update these existing surfaces to distinguish same-root reconciliation from changed-type remount; inspect cookbook.md's same implication while doing so.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: same .beads race. Payload verified in the working tree at HEAD==origin/main — docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md carries 4 focus/caret references where it previously claimed reconciliation preserved the DOM.

Delivered by worker/hicinterop-a in PR #9149, MERGED. The worker CORRECTED THIS BEAD'S OWN FRAMING at source and the correction is the valuable part: 'nothing is reconciled' is wrong. h/render! calls .render on the SAME React root inside flushSync — the distinction it draws is against createRoot-ing a second time. But a reload re-evaluates the namespace, mint-view! allocates a new component and memo wrapper per evaluation, and as-component mints a fresh component per call, so React meets a CHANGED TYPE at every position, and a changed type is a remount by React's own rule. So the reconcile is real and resolves to replace-everything. State survives because none of it lived in React.

It also refuted the bead's loss list: the suggested wording named scroll position among the losses, but the pilot's own table recorded scroll SURVIVING (299 before and after). The pages now say focus and caret, which is what was measured.

title: hic docs: there is no inward bridge from Reagent INTO a Hicasso tree, and the corpus never says so - chapter 00's 'two subtrees resolve one frame' reads as a promise it does not make
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F18 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `docs`

**Trying to** Honour the brief's scope note — "Leave anything else on Reagent;
the two view layers coexisting is expected and is itself worth observing" — by
keeping one view on Reagent and rendering it from the Hicasso tree.

**Expected** Some documented crossing. Chapter 00 is encouraging: "A Reagent or
UIx adapter under a Hicasso tree keeps working exactly as it did, and is what
you want when the page also renders that substrate's own components: every
React-shaped adapter writes the same frame context, so **the two subtrees
resolve one frame**." That sentence describes exactly the arrangement I wanted.

**Instead** There is no such crossing, and the corpus never says so. Measured:
a `rf/reg-view` rendered as `[reagent-footer]` from inside `board-page`
compiles clean, then refuses at first paint and **blanks the page**:

```clojure
{:head #object[cljs.core.MetaFn]
 :rf.error/id :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head
 :view "linearlite.core/board-page" …}
```

Note the head is reported as `cljs.core.MetaFn` — for this mistake the
diagnostic cannot name the offender the way it named `status_picker` in P2-F16,
because a Reagent view *is* an anonymous meta-carrying function.

The asymmetry is the finding. Hicasso **out** to a foreign parent has a named
door: `h/as-component`, "the outward bridge — a real React component for a
Hiccup head, so a native parent, a UIx component or plain JavaScript can mount a
minted view under the frame it is already in". Hicasso **in** from Reagent has
none. `[:>]` and `h/defhost` take real React components, and a Reagent view is
not one. Thirteen of the 29 pages mention Reagent and not one addresses this.

**Looked at** `00-installation.md` §"Hicasso needs a substrate adapter" and
§"More than one root"; `09-interop.md`; `10-native-tier.md`;
`escape-ladder.md`; `api-reference.md` §Markup (`h/as-component`);
`20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2 and §"When not to use the full process";
grepped all 29 pages for `reagent`, `coexist`, `side by side`, `alongside`.

**Resolved by** Not resolved. I reverted the probe and finished with every view
on Hicasso. **What the two layers coexisting actually means here — and it does
work — is the SUBSTRATE, not the markup**: this application ran the entire
session on `re-frame.adapter.reagent` with a Hicasso view tree above it, exactly
as chapter 00 promises, and that half cost nothing and produced no friction at
all. What does not work is nesting one layer's *views* inside the other's.

The migration chapter's advice — "Migrate a complete screen rather than changing
all component declarations… A screen-level port gives shadow comparison a useful
unit" — turns out to be load-bearing rather than stylistic: a screen is the
smallest unit that *can* migrate, because the boundary between the two layers
has to fall at a root. Chapter 00 §"More than one root" is the mechanism for a
page that genuinely needs both (a Reagent root and a Hicasso root naming the
same `:frame`), but it is written about two Hicasso roots and never connected to
this problem.

**Bead** One short section, probably in chapter 20 beside the screen-at-a-time
advice: *a Hicasso view cannot appear inside a Reagent tree or vice versa; the
boundary is a root.* Name `h/as-component` as the one direction that has a door,
and point at §"More than one root" for a page that must show both — two roots on
one frame. Right now the encouraging sentence in chapter 00 about "the two
subtrees resolv[ing] one frame" reads like permission to interleave markup, and
a reader who tries it gets a blank page and an id that cannot name what it
refused.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9137. Premise HALF-REFUTED, and the correction is the useful half. There is no HICASSO-OWNED inward door and the refusal is real (impl/codec HD-016 raises :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head for a plain fn in head position; impl/error/fail! throws with :recovery :no-recovery, so it is a throw and the page does blank) - but a crossing DOES exist: r/reactify-component plus the raw [:>] escape. That is what this repo's own hm/shadow! reference mount uses (test_kit mounted.cljs), what MIG-22 in skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md already documents, and what the chapter 20 that merged today relies on for its :reference. Outward confirmed real and not restated here: h/as-component and h/as-element, with foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test driving five mounting routes including a Reagent parent through both doors. Fix landed in ch00 (mine; ch20 was another worker's): the 'two subtrees resolve one frame' sentence now says which crossing it is about - the frame context IS shared (impl.mount/provider writes re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context, impl.collector/resolve-frame! reads it) but that is what a COMPONENT crossing reads, not permission to interleave markup - followed by the asymmetry as two bullets and the rule that the practical boundary is a root. No contradiction with ch20, which states the same head-position refusal in its shadow-comparison section.

title: Make implementor skill trigger description validator-safe
description:
## Scope

Repair the frontmatter description in `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md` so
the skill-creator validator accepts the shipped skill. Keep the public skill
directory, frontmatter name, trigger behavior, exclusions, and all body/reference
content unchanged except for the invalid trigger-example placeholder wording.

## Finding

The description contains the trigger example `implement re-frame2 in
<language>`. The required `quick_validate.py` validator rejects any `<` or `>`
in frontmatter descriptions, so the current skill fails validation before any
normal skill routing can occur.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:16` contains the literal trigger text
  `implement re-frame2 in <language>` in the YAML `description`.
- `C:\\Users\\miket\\.codex\\skills\\.system\\skill-creator\\scripts\\quick_validate.py`
  rejects descriptions containing `<` or `>`.
- Running the validator against the current package returns exit 1 with
  `Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)`.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is a frontmatter-description clarity/validator-compatibility fix only.
Preserve `name: re-frame2-implementor`, the eight-host scope, the three trigger
concepts (port re-frame2, implement re-frame2 in a host language, conformance
corpus), all do-not-use routing, allowed tools, eval fixtures, filenames,
references, package/plugin metadata, and skill body semantics. Do not rename the
public skill or directory, alter invocation policy, or change any spec/conformance
terminology. No Phase-1 vestigial/removal target is in scope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The frontmatter description contains no angle brackets or unfinished

title: Xray: retract the dead universal value-copy affordance and its dispatcher-less copy events; correct the off-box egress inventory (B.9 lock honoured)
description:
## Finding

Xray documents a universal `⎘` value-copy affordance on every value inspector, and retains the component, CSS, event, and safe-egress contract for it, but no current inspector renders the button. The user-visible feature is unreachable and `:copy?` is now an accepted-but-ignored option.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start any current Xray build/testbed and open a panel that renders a canonical EDN inspector (for example App-DB current state or an expanded Trace value).
2. Inspect, hover, and keyboard-focus the value-inspector root.
3. Observe that no `⎘` copy control or `.rf-xray-edn-widget-copy` element is rendered, despite the README/API promise.
4. At source level, search for calls to `day8.re-frame2-xray.views.edn-widget/copy-affordance`; there are none. Passing `{:copy? true}` to the facade also has no effect because the option is ignored.

## Evidence

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget.cljs` defines public `copy-affordance` and says it rides every widget root. Repo-wide exact symbol search finds no call to `copy-affordance`; the only occurrences are its definition, comments, and the test note that prior copy-affordance tests were deleted.
- The same facade's `inspect` doc says `:copy?` is accepted but ignored, then delegates directly to `views.edn-inspector` without rendering the affordance or forwarding that option. No current `views.edn-inspector` code contains the `.rf-xray-edn-widget-copy` class.
- `theme/global_styles.cljs` still ships hover/focus CSS for `.rf-xray-edn-widget-copy`, but the only element that applies that class is the uncalled component.
- The backend event `:rf.xray/copy-value-to-clipboard` remains registered and tested in `panels/app_db_diff_events.cljs`; those tests dispatch it directly and do not prove a UI button exists. `egress.cljs` explicitly counts the universal button as one of two live off-box sinks.
- Current public/current-state docs promise the UI: `tools/xray/spec/API.md` lists "The `⎘` copy button riding every value inspector" and `tools/xray/README.md` describes two human copy surfaces. This is therefore not merely an unused internal helper.
- Git commit `0a38534c54` migrated value rendering to the first-class data-display widget, removed the old copy-affordance assertions, and stated copy chrome was deferred to a later popup phase. Subsequent inspector rewrites retained the dead component/contract but no current renderer wired it.
- Bead title searches for `copy affordance`, `copy value clipboard`, `universal copy`, and `copy chrome`, plus description search for `copy-affordance`, found no existing issue.

## Impact

The public API/security inventory claims an off-box UI operation users cannot reach, while production ships dead component/CSS and an ignored option. Tests prove the safe backend only through direct dispatch, so a missing integration can remain green indefinitely. Any repair must also preserve frame isolation and fail-closed egress; casually reattaching the raw-value button would be a security regression.

## Proposed disposition

Resolve the contract explicitly. Preferred while the README/API promise remains: render one accessible copy affordance from the canonical `views.edn-inspector` root (or its single facade), route the click back to the frame captured at render time, and exercise the full safe-egress/clipboard path. Remove the accepted-but-ignored `:copy?` shim unless a real supported per-call opt-out is defined. If product direction instead retires universal copy, remove the dead component/CSS/no-op option/backend-only surface as appropriate and retract the README/API/egress inventory together; do not leave a phantom feature.

## Risks

Clipboard output is an off-box sink. Preserve `egress/egress-value`, sensitive/large-value elision, nil/stale-target fail-closed behavior, and per-instance frame routing. Ensure hover-only styling does not hide the control from keyboard or assistive-technology users. Avoid adding one button per recursive tree node when the contract is one affordance per inspector root.
acceptance_criteria:
- A rendered canonical value inspector has either a reachable, keyboard-accessible `⎘` control with stable test identity, or all current public promises of universal value copy are explicitly retired and the dead implementation is removed.
- If restored, an integration test clicks the rendered control (not direct-dispatch only), proves dispatch targets the surrounding frame, and verifies sensitive/large/nil-or-stale-frame values remain fail-closed before clipboard egress.
- The unused `copy-affordance` component/CSS and accepted-but-ignored `:copy?` option no longer exist as dead compatibility surface; any retained option has observable tested semantics.
- README, API, egress inventory, registry catalogue, source docs, and tests describe the same two-or-one copy-surface reality.
- Xray CLJS/browser tests and feature-gate smoke pass.
notes:
HOLD SHARPENED 2026-09-04 by the mayor (quiet merge tick, no dispatchable work). I have been holding this vaguely as 'restore or retract — a product call'. That framing was too loose to act on, and the evidence below makes the choice narrow and cheap. IT IS STILL MIKE'S CALL, but it is now a one-line call.

WHAT I ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE:

1. NOBODY DECIDED AGAINST THE FEATURE. edn_widget_cljs_test.cljs:6 records that the copy-affordance tests 'are deleted with the cljs-devtools cut-over', and the commit is 0a38534c54 'feat(xray): data-display widget PHASE 1 — core renderer + App-DB integration (drops cljs-devtools dep) (rf2-oqa60)'. So this is not a retracted feature; it is a phase-1 rewrite that left the affordance unwired at a phase boundary.

2. NO PHASE 2 WAS EVER SCOPED. rf2-oqa60 DOES NOT EXIST in the tracker —  returns nothing. So there is no record anywhere that the copy button was meant to come back, and equally none that it was meant to go. It simply fell between phases.

3. THE INFRASTRUCTURE IS ALL STILL THERE, so this is WIRING rather than BUILDING: the public  defn survives in edn_widget.cljs (1 occurrence, its own definition, 0 external callers), the CSS rides in theme/global_styles.cljs:684, and the safe-egress event contract is intact. What is missing is the call.

4. AND THIS IS THE PART THAT RAISES THE STAKES — THE SHIPPED README DOCUMENTS IT AS A SECURITY SURFACE, NOT A CONVENIENCE. tools/xray/README.md:264-265 reads: 'surfaces are the two human copy affordances (the  palette verb and the  copy button), both fail-closed with no...'. That is an ENUMERATION OF VALUE-EGRESS SURFACES for a fail-closed posture. So the defect is not a missing nice-to-have: a reader auditing where values can leave Xray is told there are two, and one of them does not exist. An egress enumeration that is wrong is worse than a feature that is absent.

THE TWO OPTIONS, both bounded:
  (a) WIRE IT. Call copy-affordance from the canonical EDN inspector and honour . The component, CSS and egress contract already exist, so the diff is small, and the README's two-surface enumeration becomes true again.
  (b) RETRACT IT. Delete copy-affordance, its CSS, the  option, and CORRECT THE README to enumerate one egress surface rather than two.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (a), on three grounds. The stance values excellent tools and low friction, and a value-copy button is table stakes for a debugging inspector. The work is wiring, not building — everything but the call site survives. And an accepted-but-ignored  option is the worst of the three states we could be in, so either option beats today, but (a) also leaves the security enumeration correct rather than shrinking it.

WHAT MAKES THIS MIKE'S RATHER THAN MINE: (b) is a decision that a documented user-visible egress surface is unwanted, and shrinking a security enumeration is a product statement I should not make unilaterally. Either way this is a single word of instruction — 'wire it' or 'retract it' — and I will dispatch it the same tick.
CORRECTION to the note immediately above, which lost six tokens to shell command substitution — I passed the text inline with backticks in it, and the shell executed them. My own recorded hazard; the fix is a quoted heredoc, used here. Nothing else in that note is affected and no prior note was touched (--append-notes only adds). The eaten tokens, restored in order:

1. In point 2, "rf2-oqa60 DOES NOT EXIST in the tracker — ___ returns nothing" should read: the command 'bd show rf2-oqa60' returns nothing.

2. In point 3, "the public ___ defn survives" should read: the public copy-affordance defn survives.

3. In point 4, the README quote should read in full:
   "surfaces are the two human copy affordances (the 'Snapshot app-db' palette verb and the U+2398 copy button), both fail-closed with no..."
   — the second surface is the clipboard glyph rendered on every value inspector. I am spelling it as U+2398 rather than pasting the character, because the glyph itself is what triggered part of the substitution.

4. In option (a), "honour ___" should read: honour the :copy? option.

5. In option (b), "Delete copy-affordance, its CSS, the ___ option" should read: the :copy? option.

6. In the recommendation, "an accepted-but-ignored ___ option" should read: an accepted-but-ignored :copy? option.

NOTHING ABOUT THE SUBSTANCE CHANGES. The finding stands as written: the affordance was left unwired by phase 1 rather than decided against, rf2-oqa60 does not exist so no phase 2 was ever scoped, the component and CSS and egress contract all survive so this is wiring rather than building, and tools/xray/README.md:264-265 enumerates it as one of exactly two fail-closed value-egress surfaces — an enumeration that is currently wrong by one. Recommendation remains (a) wire it, with (b) retract-and-correct-the-README as the alternative, and the choice is Mike's because (b) shrinks a documented security enumeration.

THE RULING: RETRACT. Delete the dead universal value-copy surface and correct the egress inventory; do NOT reopen the B.9 lock. Concretely: (1) delete views.edn-widget/copy-affordance (edn_widget.cljs:50-112) together with the now-unused re-frame.core require (the only rf/ uses in that file are the affordance's, lines 64/85/91), the :copy? accepted-but-ignored story (docstring :131-133 and the 3-arity [v node-key _opts] at :139-141 — no caller passes an opts map, so collapse inspect to the arities that exist), and the hover/focus CSS at theme/global_styles.cljs:683-698 whose selector prefix rf-xray-edn-widget-browse- exists nowhere else in the repo; (2) delete BOTH dispatcher-less events :rf.xray/copy-value-to-clipboard (panels/app_db_diff_events.cljs:62-99, comment block included) and :rf.xray/copy-path-to-clipboard (:101-105); KEEP the :rf.xray.fx/copy-to-clipboard fx (:32-60) — Static Machines' reachable Copy Mermaid uses it with real success/failure callbacks (static/machines/panel.cljs:272-285); (3) KEEP day8.re-frame2-xray.egress/egress-value INCLUDING its explicit-:frame arm and the no-frame identity sentinel (egress.cljs:28-41, :84-90), and RE-POINT the three rf2-7htk7 fail-closed proofs at egress/egress-value directly (see IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE); (4) rewrite the four documents so they describe ONE human value-egress affordance (the Snapshot app-db palette verb), separately acknowledging Copy Mermaid as a value-free static clipboard output that is not a value-egress site: tools/xray/README.md:262-266, tools/xray/spec/API.md:684-712 and :745-747, tools/xray/spec/014-Registry-Catalogue.md:416-417 (add a retirement blockquote in the style of the rf2-e9tb0 one at :421-425 so the audit trail survives), and egress.cljs:4-14; (5) fix the stale source and test prose listed under IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE, and correct tools/xray/spec/004-App-DB-Diff.md:663 (the Copy value / Copy path / Show me when this changed header buttons that panels/app_db_diff.cljs:7 records rf2-okvit dropped). tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md sections 10.1 and 10.5 and skills/re-frame2-xray/references/shared-components.md:22-26 are UNCHANGED: the lock is honoured as written.

RELATION TO THE B.9 LOCK: honoured, not reopened. 021 section 10.1 (:5041-5048) and 10.5 (:5142-5147, :5157-5166) were locked by 9f381abc0c on 2026-05-20 — ONE DAY BEFORE 12c0b9234d added the universal glyph on 2026-05-21 without reconciling the lock — and the published skill still carries the no-copy-value contract. The lock's own closing sentence says a re-proposal must reopen B.9 with the mayor first; this ruling declines to reopen it, so the canonical spec, the skill, and the runtime say the same thing again: no copy-value on this renderer. Any FUTURE focused-copy proposal reopens B.9 explicitly as a new design (see FOLLOW-UPS, the deferred design bead). The root-level Open in popup affordance (:popup-affordance?, spec'd at 021:4074 and shipped 2026-05-26 by 3712990ffe / ff7971c8c0) is not a precedent for a copy control: it is a disclosure/navigation affordance, spec'd when it landed, and it puts nothing on an off-box sink.

THE DECISIVE REASON, which the dossier's Restore case did not have and which I confirmed at tip: the surviving event is ORIGIN-BLIND, so Restore is not ~50 lines of wiring, it is a provenance design. The handler receives only [_ value] (app_db_diff_events.cljs:95-99) and passes no :path. Xray's own egress.cljs:53-58 and API.md:740-743 say a SLICE egress'd in isolation must tell the walker its absolute app-db path or the path-keyed sensitive/large declarations will not match; implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc keys every declaration by absolute path. Now look at what the canonical inspector is actually handed: the App-DB segment inspector renders a SLICE at a path (panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs:264); managed-fx renders raw fx request/response/handler values (panels/managed_fx_template.cljs:221-272) — and spec/Security.md:107 says structured fx :args are NOT rooted at app-db, the schema-path-keyed walker cannot prove them safe, and off-box egress MUST redact them by default; Trace renders raw before/after (panels/trace.cljs:481-488); Static flows/routes/schemas render registry values. A default-on root button that copies whichever value a shared renderer was handed, through an event that walks it as if it were an app-db root, is fail-OPEN on most of its consumers, and the eight existing tests (app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs:373-620) prove only app-db-root-shaped fixtures through direct dispatch. Reattaching the button would convert an unreachable overclaim into a reachable one. That reverses the dossier's cost argument: the hardened event is hardened for one shape; the expensive part of a safe universal copy — a typed per-call-site projection — was never built.

OPTIONS REJECTED:
- A. Restore one glyph per inspector root (the dossier's and the mayor's earlier recommendation): rejected because the event is origin-blind (above), the lock and the skill say no, and the ruling would have to reopen B.9 for a surface whose safety proofs cover one consumer shape out of six.
- A-prime. Restore as opt-in only where a projection exists: rejected for THIS bead — that is a new design from the data owner outward, not a repair of this vestige; captured in the deferred design bead so nothing is lost.
- C. Leave as is: rejected — the security inventory (API.md section Off-box egress; README.md:262-266) lists an off-box sink users cannot reach, which is wrong in the direction that matters, and the next audit re-files this bead.
- B-strict (the Codex variant of Retract): delete egress-value's explicit-:frame arm and the no-frame sentinel too, since the palette passes no :frame. Rejected: the arm is the Xray-side carrier of a three-carrier security class (egress/no-frame rf2-7htk7; local_render rf2-ws60; re-frame.derivation.egress rf2-g1vu), three files cite it by name as the model (panels/local_render.cljc:179, test/.../panels/local_render_cljs_test.cljc:277, implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:270), the egress.cljs docstring and API.md prescribe it as the MUST-use fail-closed gesture for any panel affordance, and it is about ten lines plus three small tests. Deleting it re-derives a three-pass security finding the day a focused-copy design arrives. Keeping an INTERNAL arm with its invariant pinned is not a phantom feature; keeping it UNTESTED would be, hence the re-point.

title: vestigial(story): retire the inert run-variant render contract
description:
Finding

Story still exposes and internally passes a `run-variant` `:render?` option, and every run result still carries `:rendered-hiccup`, but the option is unread and the result slot is permanently nil. This began as a staged placeholder and is now a retired architecture preserved as an active-looking compatibility contract.

Evidence

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:68` puts `:rendered-hiccup nil` in `empty-result`; `record-result-map` at lines 686-694 unconditionally writes `:rendered-hiccup nil` with the comment that rendering is performed by the UI shell or `render-variant`; and the `run-variant` docstring at lines 1276-1278 explicitly says rendering is separate and the compatibility slot remains nil.
- Repo-wide source search finds no branch that reads `:render?` to render anything. Nevertheless the live shell passes it at `ui/shell.cljs:312`, `ui/canvas.cljs:432`, and `ui/workspace.cljc:328`; `prepare-run!` advertises it at `runtime.cljc:1376`; and `run_owner_cljc_test.cljc:85` passes it without asserting any rendered result. These calls are inert configuration noise.
- The documented contract claims the opposite: `spec/007-Stories.md:425,432` says `:rendered-hiccup` is populated under `:render? true` and is the screenshot-test input; `tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:718-722`, `tools/story/spec/000-Vision.md:114`, `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:117,891`, and `docs/story/api/runtime.md:47,98-114` repeat the active-looking option/result shape.
- Story-MCP consumes the impossible slot as if live. `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:160` and `dev.cljc:170` scrub and return it; tool descriptors promise rendered output; `wire_pipeline.cljc:37,89-90` says it dominates token cost; the MCP spec/docs classify its egress. Tests manufacture non-nil hiccup in stubbed outcome maps, so they prove the scrubber but never prove that a real Story run can produce it.
- Git history proves the retirement path: `fa993fa5e4` (2026-05-11 Stage 3) introduced nil with `Stage 4 fills this in`; no later implementation populated it. `82cd4bd1c8` (2026-07-10) changed runtime prose to say rendering is outside headless orchestration and relabelled the nil as a reserved compatibility slot, while the normative/API/MCP promises remained.
- Bead searches for `rendered-hiccup`, `rendered hiccup`, `run-variant render`, and `compatibility slot` returned no existing issue.

Impact

The public and MCP contracts advertise a screenshot/tooling feature that cannot be reached, callers carry ignored options, and substantial MCP egress/dedup/token-budget prose and tests defend data that Story never emits. A consumer following the API receives nil even when explicitly requesting render. The contradictory authorities also make future work liable to test the stubbed shape rather than the real integration.

Proposed disposition

Retire `:render?` from run/prepare opts and retire `:rendered-hiccup` from the unified run-result. Keep `render-variant` as the single explicit visual-rendering API and rewrite screenshot guidance around its structured `:rendered` result. Remove the inert opts from shell/canvas/workspace. Reconcile normative Story docs, API docs, tests, Story-MCP payload projections/descriptors/specs, dedup hints, and token guidance. If `preview-variant` genuinely needs visual output, have that tool call a supported renderer explicitly and describe its substrate/capability boundary; do not infer rendering from `run-variant` or preserve a permanent nil slot.

Risks

This is a documented result-map field, so downstream destructuring may depend on key presence even though its value is always nil. Treat the removal as an API migration and update compatibility/release notes as policy requires. Story-MCP runs on a headless JVM where render capability may be unavailable; it must return an honest capability refusal/omission rather than synthesize success-shaped hiccup.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run-variant`/`prepare-run!` and shell callers no longer accept or pass the inert `:render?` option, and unified run results no longer carry a permanently nil `:rendered-hiccup` compatibility slot.
- Story normative specs, API docs, examples, and screenshot guidance consistently name `render-variant` (and its actual result shape) as the rendering authority; no text claims `run-variant` populates hiccup.
- Story-MCP run/preview payloads, egress projection, descriptors, dedup/token hints, specs, and tests reflect data reachable from real production calls. Any preview rendering is an explicit renderer call with capability/error coverage.
- An integration test exercises the real Story-to-consumer path so a stubbed non-nil outcome cannot reintroduce the false contract.
- Story JVM/CLJS, shell feature-load/static build, Story-MCP, API/spec drift, and egress tests pass.
