title: RULING: defhost :callbacks roster - infer the contract from the prop position instead of declaring it
description:
defhost makes the consumer declare :callbacks {:on-close :event, :render-row :render, :x :handler} and learn a 6-row table for what one h/event means by position (docs/core/hicasso/03-events-as-data.md:113-120). But impl/intent.cljs:1200-1210 ALREADY selects the contract by position for every native tag (on* = event, else render, :ref excluded), and lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1283-1296) shows :handler has no positive behaviour: h/event -> identity, plain fn -> identity, vector -> refused - and a vector at an undeclared on* host prop is already refused (codec.cljs:2884). :handler appears in zero consumer-shaped code (only host_hatch and intent_cljs_test). The one consumer-shaped declaration in the repo (test/.../examples/ledger/views.cljs:14-16) declares two entries. 11 refusal ids exist solely to validate the defhost declaration map (codec.cljs:1538-2053), ~15 to police this grammar overall. The stated reason for the roster (value-first foreign callbacks) is already caught at runtime by intent-needs-the-event (intent.cljs:107,726).

RECOMMENDATION: infer on* -> event, everything else -> render, exactly as native tags do; keep :slots (genuinely uninferable - a vector is legal data). Delete :callbacks, :handler and ~8 ids (unknown-callback-contract, host-structural-callback, host-callback-slot-collision, intent-at-a-non-event-contract, host-undeclared-callback, host-unclaimed-callback, plus simpler macro-tail guards). Effort: medium. If ruled yes, dispatch with the refusal-shrink task.
notes:
*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** Banner added 2026-08-29 14:38 AUSEST by the merge+dispatch tick (mayor session re-frame2-9a). Type is decision; the epic rf2-6c12m names it as one of five rulings that gate tasks. WHOEVER RULES STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT.
2026-08-29 14:40 AUSEST - Decision dossier for Mike at ai/decisions/rf2-6c12m.2.defhost-callbacks-roster.md (local-only, untracked): problem, options with consequences, recommendation, how to record the ruling.
RULING 2026-08-29 15:29:54 AUSEST (delegated review per Mike, 2026-08-29): Option B, 2 values - infer the callback contract from the prop position exactly as native tags already do (on* -> :event, anything else walked -> :render, :ref -> React's); keep :callbacks ONLY as an optional override taking :event or :render; delete :handler; keep :slots.
BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:29:54 AUSEST: ruled.

WHY B (decisive facts)
- The runtime already infers for every native tag: position-contract (impl/intent.cljs:1200-1210) = ref? -> :ref, event-prop? -> :event, else :render; event-prop? is one regex ^on-[a-z]|^on[A-Z] (intent.cljs:916-926). lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1255-1302) routes declared :event/:render to the SAME two wrappers the native walk uses (event-callback, render-callback).
- Every declaration in the repo and the guide infers identically. The only consumer-shaped one (test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ledger/views.cljs:14-16, :137-138: {:render-row :render :on-window :event}) is exactly what inference gives. Guide declarations :on-change/:on-close/:on-pick/:on-value-change -> event and :render-row/:item-content -> render also match; the only two that do not are the two the guide invents to illustrate the roster (:on-imperative :handler, :on-render-row :render).
- :handler has no behaviour: h/event -> identity, plain fn -> identity, vector/map -> refused. A plain function already crosses untouched at every position (intent.cljs:1220-1228; codec.cljs:2865, host-prop-value's fn? arm). Zero consumer-shaped uses, tests only. Its own docstring says a plain fn is the handler contract (intent.cljs:1279-1281). It adds vocabulary, not capability.
- The stated reason for "never infer" (a value-first foreign callback such as onChange(date), where [:x ::h/value] would read date.target) is caught at runtime regardless of any declaration: event-arg! raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event naming the position (intent.cljs:95-117, :710-738). The declaration never prevented the mistake; the runtime check does.
- [:>] gets inference for free: raw-element walks props through host-entry against an EMPTY declared roster (codec.cljs:3465), so today [:> X {:on-pick (h/event ...)}] is refused as unclaimed and [:> X {:on-pick [:x/y]}] as undeclared. Under B host-entry's :else arm infers, so [:>] and defhost share one classifier (the second reviewer's point).
- Both the dossier author and the second reviewer (Codex) recommend B with 2 values. The added review is a clear recommendation, not a partial opinion; I weighed it against the code and found nothing against it. It adds three implementation constraints adopted here: reuse the native classifier (no second one), apply the same default in defhost and the [:>] host walk, and a proportionate test bar (below).

WHY NOT A (infer, delete :callbacks): one paragraph smaller, but no first-class spelling for an on*-named prop whose RETURN the library consumes and which is interactive. Fluent UI DetailsList onRenderItem/onRenderCell/onRenderHeader return UI; Ant Design Table onFilter returns a boolean, onRow/onCell/onHeaderRow return props maps. The event wrapper always returns nil (intent.cljs:551-596), so an h/event there blanks the list or vetoes every row, silently. A plain function is the escape and suffices for predicates and props-returning callbacks, but a plain function gets no frame/dispatch rebinding (render-callback, intent.cljs:598-704), so an intent inside a row it returns raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary at click - loud, not silent, but under A the only fix is an adapter component. Under B it is one line, {:callbacks {:on-render-item :render}}, and the render wrapper supplies the owning frame. The override costs one taught paragraph and one 2-value check that folds into .11's single bad-declaration id. The roster never prevented this hard case either: declaring such a prop :event blanks it the same way (skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:160 already warns).

WHY NOT C (keep as is): the consumer keeps declaring what the library already knows; the guide keeps a rule that contradicts its own native-tag behaviour; 4 ids, 1 half-id, 1 roster and ~560 lines of validation and commentary police a grammar with no consumer.

THE RULE AFTER B (position table 6 rows -> 4)
1. on*-spelled prop (native tag, defhost, [:>]) -> :event: h/event takes the event wrapper; an intent vector or key-map lowers as at a native event position; a plain fn crosses untouched.
2. Any other walked prop -> :render: h/event takes the render wrapper (frame + dispatch rebound); a vector or map crosses AS DATA via host-prop-value/clj->js exactly as at a native tag (nobody writes {:on-render-item [:x/y]} on purpose; refusing it is a guard a trusted programmer never trips). Plain fn untouched.
3. Declared :slots position -> markup (as-element); an h/event there stays refused (a function as a ReactNode renders nothing, silently) - this is the surviving half of host-unclaimed-callback.
4. :ref -> React's (check-ref!).
Override: {:callbacks {<prop> :event|:render}}, written only where inference is wrong; a declared contract outranks the spelling. Any other value is a bad declaration.

BEFORE / AFTER
;; today
(h/defhost date-picker DatePicker {:callbacks {:on-change :event}})
(h/defhost rows vendor/virtual-rows {:callbacks {:render-row :render :on-window :event}})
(h/defhost picker Widget {:callbacks {:on-pick :event :on-imperative :handler :on-render-row :render}})
;; after
(h/defhost date-picker DatePicker)
(h/defhost rows vendor/virtual-rows)
(h/defhost fluent-list FluentList {:callbacks {:on-render-item :render}})   ; the hard case: on*-named render prop
;; call sites unchanged
[date-picker {:selected (h/sub [:task/due-date]) :on-change (h/event [date _] [:task/set-due date])}]
[:> DatePicker {:on-change (h/event [date _] [:task/set-due date])}]   ; legal now too

REFUSAL IDS
Retired outright (4):
- :rf.error/hicasso-host-undeclared-callback - codec.cljs:2870-2897 refuse-undeclared-host-event!, emitted :2884, call site :3093-3094.
- :rf.error/hicasso-intent-at-a-non-event-contract - intent.cljs:1230-1253 refuse-dispatching-carrier!, emitted :1237, arms :1291 and :1295.
- :rf.error/hicasso-host-structural-callback - codec.cljs:1849 (.11 already lists it for deletion).
- :rf.error/hicasso-host-callback-slot-collision - codec.cljs:1976.
Narrowed (1): :rf.error/hicasso-host-unclaimed-callback - codec.cljs:2899-2954, emitted :2937 - keeps ONLY the node-slot? true branch (h/event at a declared :slots position, call site :3079-3080); the "nothing claims it" false branch (:3105-3106) goes, because inference now claims every position.
Folded (1): :rf.error/hicasso-unknown-callback-contract - codec.cljs:1947-1948 at mint, intent.cljs:1297 in lower-declared-prop - now a 2-value check; fold into the single hicasso-bad-host-declaration id .11 proposes (the :reason string names the fault). If this lands before .11's collapse, keep it as the 2-value check and let .11 fold it.
Kept, reworded (4): host-bad-options, host-unknown-option, host-bad-slots, host-extra-form lose their ":handler" / "never inferred" wording.
Code that goes: the callback-contracts roster (codec.cljs:1328); the :callbacks arms of mint-host!'s declaration block (codec.cljs:1538-2053); refuse-undeclared-host-event!; the false branch of refuse-unclaimed-host-callback!; refuse-dispatching-carrier!; the :handler arm of lower-declared-prop (keep :event and :render arms; a non-callback value at :render routes through host-prop-value so a vector crosses as data); and the HD-011/HD-024 commentary at codec.cljs:1220-1234, intent.cljs:1230-1302 and hicasso.cljc:297-370 (~500 lines; rewrite as a few sentences stating the inferred rule and the override - .4 is the prose-ratio ruling, do not fight it).
host-entry (codec.cljs:3040-3111): the :else arm becomes event? -> intent/lower-prop (vector, map and h/event lowered, else untouched); non-event h/event -> render-callback; then host-prop-value. Reuse position-contract / lower-prop; do NOT add a second classifier, a warning, or a compatibility layer. Declared :slots and :ref keep precedence over inference; a :callbacks override keeps precedence over the spelling.
Every retired id must go from ALL gate-bound places (per .20's landing): src; spec/009-Instrumentation.md catalogue rows :2518-2556 (hot-zone, one-toucher); implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md register rows :108, :112, :113, :114, :116, :151; docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md sections :251-280 and :436-473. Otherwise the keyword-drift and register gates go red. .20 found the register gate's R3/R4 scan now prunes test/re_frame/bench, so bench donors still emitting the ids do not block.

DOCS TO CHANGE
- docs/core/hicasso/03-events-as-data.md:113-120 position table: 6 -> 4 rows; drop "as declared" and "undeclared refuses".
- docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md:62-100 (Callback contracts): replace "Hicasso never infers a contract from an on* name" with the inferred rule plus one paragraph on the override (Fluent onRender* / Ant onRow as the example); delete the :on-imperative :handler example.

- docs/core/hicasso/glossary.md:354-366 (:357).
- docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md:251-280 (intent-at-a-non-event-contract, unknown-callback-contract) and :436-473 (structural, slot-collision, undeclared, unclaimed - narrow the last).
- docs/core/hicasso/16-diagnostics.md:162 (unclaimed row - narrow); 20-migration-from-reagent.md:271 (undeclared row - delete or rewrite); escape-ladder.md:148 (the "explicit contract" checklist question - rewrite).
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:297 and :320-370 (defhost docstring).
- docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md: DATED ADDENDA (not rewrites; check_provenance_pins.py polices this tree) on HD-011 (:437-611) and HD-024 (:1916-2124; table :2052-2058, value-first law :2087-2099) recording: inference by position is HD-024's own law applied to hosts; the value-first guard was always runtime; :handler retired; the override kept for on*-named render props.
- skills/reagent-migration: SKILL.md:67, :88 (stop labelling every suggested declaration a guess), :160; references/catalog-judgment.md:249-272; references/procedure.md, references/catalog-reject.md, spec/inputs.md, README.md (each carries a defhost mention - re-read and align); evals/evals.json:95-98 (rewrite both expectations). Teach "infer the usual case; override the vendor exception". Skill content stays generic to any consumer app.

TESTS

The :handler hits in per_keystroke, view_alias_registry and reincarnation_routing tests are :handler-fn, unrelated.

title: [DISPATCHED - in flight] tools/xray/README.md:44 places the nav cluster on the events ribbon - the SIXTH and last live instance, and the one every spec-scoped census could not see
description:
`tools/xray/README.md:44` says the `[◀ ▶ ⏭]` nav cluster is on the **events ribbon**. It lives on the
**L1 chrome ribbon**. **This is the SIXTH and LAST live instance of a class that has now cost six
PRs**, and it is the one every previous census was structurally unable to see.

Found by `rf2-d7258`'s worker (PR #10116) and **re-derived at source by the mayor at trunk
`dba4d41f0d`**.

## THE LINE

`tools/xray/README.md:43-45`, quoted verbatim:

> Selecting an event in the L2 event list moves a single spine sub
> (`:rf.xray/focus`); every Dynamic tab is a lens on that one focused
> event. Time-travel is the spine itself — **the events-ribbon nav cluster**
> plus the event list are the scrubber; there is no bottom rail.

**It is PROSE, not in a fence** — verified by walking fence state, not assumed. It carries **0 markdown
link tokens** (file-wide 40).

## WHY EVERY EARLIER CENSUS MISSED IT — the transferable part

The five earlier instances were all under `tools/xray/spec/`, so every sweep for this class was scoped
there, **including the mayor's**. `tools/xray/README.md` sits one level up and was outside the search
root every time. **The pattern was right and the SCOPE was wrong**, which is the failure that returns a
confident zero.

Measured repo-wide by the mayor, uncapped, excluding the tracker export: the fixed string
`events-ribbon nav` reads **3** — `018:98` and `021:1284` (both being corrected by PR #10116) and this
one. **After #10116 merges this is the only live site left.** `rf2-d7258`'s worker swept 464 files
under `tools/xray` with fence-state tracking and then all **5254** tracked files for eight spellings,
finding exactly this; the only other hits are inside `.beads/issues.jsonl` quoting bead titles about
this very class.

## WHY IT IS FALSE

- **`018:206`** — the L1 chrome ribbon's LEFT cluster is *"`Event History` label · the `[◀ ▶ ⏭]` nav
  cluster · the `+ filter` button"*.
- **`018:227`** — the nav cluster and `+ filter` *"live UP on the chrome ribbon (bar-1)"*.
- **`018:1332`** — *"the nav cluster lives on the chrome ribbon — rf2-3f2di A5"*.
- **At source**: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs`'s `ribbon-tree` composes
  `ribbon-nav-cluster` in the **LEFT** cluster (`:1421`, *"promoted to bar-1"*), and
  `shell_cljs_test.cljs:460` pins the negative. **Resolve this yourself at your tip rather than taking
  the line numbers** — they are `rf2-d7258`'s, reported in good faith and not re-derived by the mayor.

## Scope

**That one phrase.** `events-ribbon nav cluster` → the chrome-ribbon spelling, matching how
`018:206`/`:227`/`:1332` and PR #10116's landed corrections say it.

**The sentence's argument is CORRECT and must survive** — time-travel *is* the spine, the nav cluster
plus the event list *are* the scrubber, and there is no bottom rail. **Only the ribbon it names is
wrong.** Do not rewrite the paragraph.

**OUT OF SCOPE, each a live temptation:**
- **Do not edit `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md` or `021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md`** — PR #10116
  owns both lines; if it has merged by the time you start, they are already correct and still not yours.
- **Do not "tidy" the README**, reflow it, or update anything you were not sent for.
- **Do not renumber or restructure any section.**

## THE GATE IS A DIFFERENT ONE FROM EVERY EARLIER INSTANCE IN THIS CLASS — measured

- **`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` DOES NOT COVER THIS PATH.** Its roots are `docs/`, `spec/`,
  `skills/`, `migration/` and **`tools/*/spec`** — and `tools/xray/README.md` is not under
  `tools/*/spec/`. It **exits 0 on a broken link here**. Do not nominate it.
- **`python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` IS the gate** — its surface is every `README.md` beside
  source code, and it models GitHub's `-N` duplicate-heading suffix where the docs gate models MkDocs'

title: Xray Epoch: :app-db schema-check link is plain text for any failure below the registered root (row drops :registered-path)
description:
## The defect

In the Xray Epoch panel, the `schema check` link on an `:app-db` schema-violation row renders as PLAIN TEXT whenever the failure sits BELOW the registered root, e.g. a `[:map [:age :int]]` schema registered at `[:user]` failing at `:age`. It resolves only when the failing leaf IS the registered path.

## Measured (found while working rf2-1t8fn, PR #10065, 2026-09-18)

- Per spec/010-Schemas.md §Validation (the `:where :app-db` paragraph), the trace's `:path` is the FAILING LEAF, and the registration anchor rides separately as `:registered-path`.
- `schema-violation-row` in `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc` copies `:path` and drops `:registered-path`. `git grep -c registered-path -- tools/xray/src` reads 0, against a control of 19 in `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc`.
- The view's `:app-db` arm (`violation-schema-coord` in `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`) calls `rf.schemas/app-schema-meta {:frame f :path path}`, which is an EXACT path lookup (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc`, `app-schema-meta`: `get-in` on the normalized concrete path).
- A probe driven through the live framework on the node lane (a temporary deftest, not committed) produced a nested row `:path [:probe/user :age]` whose link rendered `:span`, and a flat control `:path [:probe/flat]` whose link rendered `:button`.

## Likely fix (not done; out of rf2-1t8fn's fence)

Carry `:registered-path` on the projected row, and have the view's `:app-db` arm read `(or registered-path path)`. Pin it with a producer-driven nested violation, as rf2-1t8fn's test does for the flat case.

title: method: no dispatch-brief shape exists for a zero-worktree (research/verification) dispatch — assembler emits a confident brief naming a directory that is not there
description:
FOUND BY THE §5 METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-09-16, by checking a rule the mayor has been ENFORCING against what the tree actually does — which is the axis §5 says drift lives on. The mayor hit it the same hour, on a real dispatch.

## THE DISAGREEMENT — three artefacts, and two of them do not know the third's shape exists

`CLAUDE.md`'s dispatch-ledger contract explicitly recognises a dispatch with NO worktree — "a dispatch with NO worktree — a zero-edit research or verification bead — uses them too: `(none)`, the agentId, the timestamp, `(none)`, the beads". Measured token counts: `CLAUDE.md` carries `zero-edit` 1, `no worktree` 1, `research` 2.

`docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` carries **zero** of those and substitutes `<ASSIGNED_WORKTREE>` at 4 sites, including its whole "worktree boundary block" — a fenced section that tells the worker to run the worktree guard and to use absolute paths under its assigned tree.

`ai/assemble-brief.sh` REQUIRES a bare worktree name and derives `$PARENT/$WT`, so there is no spelling for "there is no worktree".

**So a dispatch shape the ledger contract names has no brief shape in the tool that builds briefs.** The mayor's fallback is to hand-write the brief — which is precisely the drift `assemble-brief.sh` was built to close. Its own header: "Drift this exists to close (2026-09-11): three briefs went out whose blocks were extracted to files correctly and then RETYPED into the prompt."

## THE MECHANICAL HALF — measured, and it fails in the reassuring direction

Given the ledger's own sentinel, the assembler does not refuse. Measured:

    sh ai/assemble-brief.sh '(none)' rf2-probe <task>
      -> EXIT 0
      -> "assembled: gate block 14037 chars, stance 5/5 verbatim, 0 placeholders left,
          worktree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/(none)"
      -> 24578 characters of brief, telling the worker THREE TIMES that its worktree is
         that path, including "run the guard at the top level of <path> and check it
         prints <path>".

**"0 placeholders left" is TRUE and completely beside the point** — every placeholder was substituted, with a value naming a directory that does not exist. That is the reassuring-direction failure this project catalogues: the success line is accurate about the question it answers and silent about the one that matters.

**AND THE CLASS IS LARGER THAN THE SENTINEL.** A merely mistyped worktree name behaves identically: `sedicrlf-typo99` -> exit 0, full brief, absent directory. So the defect is "derived worktree does not exist", not "(none) is special".

**ONE LIMIT, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because the first probe tripped on it**: Windows paths are case-insensitive, so a CASE-ONLY typo (`sedicrlf-n2q7X` for `...x`) resolves to the real directory and reads EXISTS. An existence check cannot catch that class and must not be described as catching it. The probe that found this was itself the bad one, and its control is what exposed it.

## WHAT HAS ALREADY BEEN DONE — the bounded half

`ai/assemble-brief.sh` now refuses when the derived worktree does not exist, citing this bead. That is deliberately the SMALL fix: it authors no worker-facing text, and it extends a refusal the file already performs for path-shaped input, for the reason the file already gives in its own comment — "A worker handed that path spends a cycle before its guard refuses, so refuse it here instead." The existence check simply keys that same principle on the worktree being real rather than on the argument's shape.

## WHAT IS NOT DONE, AND IT IS A DESIGN CALL RATHER THAN A FIX

**Should the method carry a SECOND dispatch shape?** Today the template describes exactly one: a worker that takes a worktree, edits tracked files, runs gates, and opens a PR. A zero-edit research or verification dispatch differs in more than the worktree — it has no branch, no PR, no gates to run, and its "quality gates" block is largely inapplicable, so the right brief is not the standard one minus a block.

Arguments for adding it: the shape RECURS (the ledger shows zero-worktree rows, and one accounting found roughly one row in eight in that position), and every occurrence is currently hand-written, so the verbatim blocks do not travel mechanically and the stance is at risk of paraphrase — the exact failure the assembler exists to prevent.

Arguments against: the project stance says not to over-engineer, and a second full block set is real surface to keep in step with the first. A cheaper option is a short "no-worktree boundary block" in the template that the assembler selects instead of the worktree one, leaving the preamble and stance handling untouched.

**DO NOT TREAT THE GUARD AS HAVING SETTLED THIS.** The guard makes the failure loud; it does not give the shape a brief. Per the method's own warning, a guard is not a rule that cannot fail.

## NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT

`docs/the-mayor-method/**` is the OS-neutral method tree and is NOT project-specific, so anything added there must hold for any project — the stance stays in `CLAUDE.md` and must not migrate into the template, which says so in terms. `ai/` is gitignored, so the assembler half needs no PR; the template half does.
notes:
FENCE (2026-09-16 22:58 AUSEST). Held by a live worker in C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/noworktree-b3k9m on branch worker/noworktree-b3k9m.
Do not dispatch a second worker onto this bead or that branch until it reports.
Re-dispatch release: a completion report, or a recorded death.
The worker holds docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md UNTIL ITS PR MERGES.

Both release conditions are stated deliberately and they are NOT the same event. A report discharges the re-dispatch fence and authorises reaping the worktree; only the PR MERGING frees the surface, because a worker that has reported still has an open change editing that file, and a second worker branched off trunk would not carry it. The operational test is two questions: "can you quote the sentence where this agent says it is done?" and "has the PR that edits this surface merged?"

THE MEASUREMENT THAT JUSTIFIED DISPATCHING, taken at tip rather than carried from the bead's description: **114 of 590 dispatch-ledger rows, 19%, are zero-worktree dispatches** — field 1 exactly `(none)`. Controls both ways over the same file: 475 rows carry an absolute worktree path, and exactly 1 row is neither (the `(no-worktree: zero-edit research bead)` improvisation CLAUDE.md already names). So nearly one dispatch in five uses a shape the brief assembler cannot produce, and every one of those ~114 briefs was hand-written. title: xray: two ^{:key} sites attach metadata to a CALL FORM, so React receives no key at all
description:
TWO `^{:key …}` SITES ATTACH THEIR METADATA TO A CALL FORM, SO REACT NEVER RECEIVES A KEY.
Live today under Reagent, and they would stay broken under Fresco for a different reason.

VERIFIED BY THE MAYOR AT TRUNK f025546df1 (fact) — the metadata and the form it attaches to:

  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_template.cljs:405-406
      ^{:key (str (:surface rec) "-" (:origin-event-id rec) "-" (:fx-id rec))}
      (record-panel dispatch rec))])))

  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace.cljs:824-825
      ^{:key "rows"}
      (flat-row-list rows expanded-ids)])]]))

**THE MECHANISM.** `^{:key x}` is READER metadata: it attaches to the form that follows it. Where
that form is a VECTOR LITERAL the metadata rides onto the vector the reader produces, which is the
value Reagent later inspects — that is why the idiom works everywhere else. Where the form is a
CALL, the metadata attaches to the LIST, the compiler evaluates that list, and **the returned value
carries none of it**. Nothing errors; the key is simply absent.

Measured by the static6-a worker on the third site of this shape, in `static/flows/panel.cljs`:
`Metadata seen: [nil nil nil]` before the repair, three distinct keys after. That one is FIXED and
merged; these two are the ones it found outside its slice and correctly left.

**BOTH FILES ARE STILL REAGENT** — `managed_fx_template.cljs` carries 1 `reg-view` and 0 `defview`,
`trace.cljs` 2 and 0 — so this is NOT a latent Fresco-migration problem waiting to happen. Reagent
reads metadata THEN props, and there is no metadata to read. React is getting no key from these
sites right now, and has not been.

**AND IT WILL NOT BE FIXED BY THE MIGRATION EITHER**, which is why it wants its own bead rather
than a note on rf2-k97c.3: Fresco's codec reads `:key` from the ATTRIBUTE MAP and reads Clojure
metadata NOWHERE, so a migration that faithfully preserves `^{:key …}` preserves a no-op.

=== THE REPAIR ===

Two shapes are available and the right one differs per site:

  (a) `(with-meta (f …) {:key …})` — keeps the key on the value the call returns. This is what the
      Flows repair used, and it is correct while the file stays on Reagent.
  (b) Move the key into the returned hiccup's ATTRIBUTE MAP. This is what the standing direction
      under rf2-k97c.3 asks for, because Reagent reads meta THEN props, so ONE attribute satisfies
      both substrates and the site needs no second edit when its panel migrates.

**PREFER (b) WHERE THE CALL'S RETURN IS A HICCUP VECTOR YOU CAN REACH.** It is the shape that
survives the migration. Use (a) only where the return is opaque at the call site, and say which you
chose per site and why.

**THE KEY EXPRESSION MUST NOT CHANGE.** `managed_fx_template.cljs`'s composes three fields of the
record; reproduce it exactly. A key that changes value between renders is worse than no key.

=== EVIDENCE, AND THE HOLLOW-GATE WARNING THAT GOES WITH IT ===

**A ROW THAT ASSERTS ON CLOJURE METADATA IS A HOLLOW GATE.** It passes while React receives
nothing — that is the exact failure this bead is about, one level up. Assert on what reaches the
RENDERER: read the key off the attribute map, or off the rendered element. The mechanical test is
*delete the signal, keep the fault*.

The static6-a worker's probe is the model: it printed the metadata actually seen at the call site
before and after, and the `[nil nil nil]` is what made the defect undeniable.

=== SCOPE ===

Those two sites. **Do not sweep the tree for more** — the static6-a worker already swept
`static/**` (11 sites, 10 on vector literals, 1 on a call form) and these two came out of that
sweep. If you want to know whether other sites exist elsewhere, that is a census with its own
prose-contamination hazard and it is a separate bead: this tree's comments AND docstrings discuss
`^{:key …}` at length, so strip string literals first, then `;` comments, then flatten, and take
the control through the identical pipeline. A raw grep over this tree overstates view-registration
counts by roughly 7x.

Neither file is hot zone. Neither is held by a live worker at filing time — re-derive that at

title: checkpoint: MEMORY RECONCILIATION FAILED banner blames a deletion when the unclassifiable row is a blank line
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 in the mayor checkout, during an ordinary merge+dispatch tick.

WHAT HAPPENED (fact, measured):
`sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` printed the full `***** MEMORY RECONCILIATION FAILED
(rf2-cve7) *****` banner:

    export  2278 rows = 1214 issues + 1063 memories
    HEAD    2277 rows = 1214 issues + 1063 memories
    1 row(s) in the fresh export are neither an issue nor a memory

The unclassifiable row was A TRAILING BLANK LINE, not a memory row and not a deletion.
Measured on the committed blob and the working file: `awk END{print NR}` = 2278,
`jq -c . | wc -l` = 2277, `grep -n -v '^{'` names line 2278 and it is empty, and the
last three bytes are `} \n \n`. The previous checkpoint's blob (HEAD~1) ends `0 } \n`
at NR 2277. So the export genuinely carried one extra, empty record and the guard
counted it correctly.

THE GUARD WAS RIGHT. It saw a row it could not classify and said so, as a WARNING
rather than a refusal, which is the designed behaviour. Nothing was lost: the memory
populations matched exactly (1063 = 1063), and `bd export --include-memories` run
immediately afterwards read 2277 rows with the populations summing exactly and no
blank line.

WHAT THE MESSAGE COST (this is the actionable part):
The banner's prose frames an unclassifiable row as a probable MEMORY DELETION -- it
names the 2026-09-08 event where 210 keys disappeared, and every one of its four
recovery paragraphs is about recovering deleted keys by `.key` lookup against a
spelled-out commit oid. An operator following it during a real incident spends the
whole message hunting for keys that were never missing, and the one cheap check that
settles it in two seconds -- read the file's LAST BYTES -- is not mentioned anywhere.
It took a `_type` census, a row-set `comm`, six repeat exports and a log read to
establish that nothing was wrong.

THE FIX IS ONE SENTENCE, in the branch that prints the count of unclassifiable rows:
say that a row which is neither an issue nor a memory may simply be a BLANK LINE, give
the check (`tail -c 3 <file> | od -c`, or `awk 'END{print NR}'` against
`jq -c . <file> | wc -l`), and say that a blank line is benign and self-heals on the
next checkpoint. Keep the deletion paragraphs for the case where the MEMORY COUNTS
actually differ -- which is the discriminator the message already has in hand and does
not use: here they were EQUAL, and equal memory counts rule out a memory deletion
outright.

CAUSE (INFERENCE, NOT REPRODUCED):
The blank line appeared on exactly ONE of SEVEN `bd export --include-memories`
invocations measured in this session. The one that produced it ran concurrently with
the out-of-repo merged-PR audit harness writing its `merged-pr-audit-pr-9596` memory
and advancing `merged-pr-audit-cursor` -- proved by row-set `comm` between two exports
minutes apart (exactly those two rows differ) and by `a0e4824332 chore(beads): audit
merged PR #9596` landing on top of the checkpoint commit `3a9cb87861`. A race between
`bd export` and a concurrent `bd remember` write is the natural reading, but it was
NOT reproduced and no attempt was made to reproduce it deliberately. Do not write the
race into the message as a fact; the message only needs to name a blank line as a
possibility and give the check.

SELF-HEALING, CONFIRMED: the harness's own next commit rewrote the file cleanly
(committed blob now NR 2278 ending `} \n`, no blank line), and `minimal_diff_rewrite`
would have dropped it anyway -- it builds `cnt[]` from the EXPORT, and a blank line
absent from the export has `cnt[""] = 0`, so HEAD's blank line is not re-emitted.

SCOPE: `scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` only, in the reconciliation warning's text. Do
not add a refusal, do not strip blank lines defensively as a side quest, and do not
touch the deletion-recovery paragraphs beyond gating them on the memory counts
actually differing.
notes:
=== SHARPENED AFTER READING `memory_facts`' OWN COMMENT (mayor, same tick) ===

THE FUNCTION ALREADY DRAWS THE DISTINCTION THIS BEAD IS ASKING FOR, AND THE MESSAGE
THEN THROWS IT AWAY. `memory_facts`' header comment says, in terms:

    "So the sum is kept (it catches a row of an unknown `_type`, which is cheap to
     notice and would otherwise be invisible) and the LOSS DETECTOR is the key-set
     comparison."

So the design has TWO detectors with TWO different meanings:

  * THE SUM      -> internal WELL-FORMEDNESS. Fires on a row of unknown `_type`.
                    Says nothing about loss; the comment states it is "SILENT ON BOTH
                    SIDES" of the 210-key event it was proposed for.
  * THE KEY SET  -> the actual LOSS DETECTOR. Counts are a floor with a hole in
                    them; the key set has none.

Both run. Both had already answered when the banner printed. The key-set arm found
NOTHING -- no missing key was listed, and the two memory counts read 1063 against 1063.
The sum arm found one row. And the message routed that well-formedness hit through the
full LOSS narrative: the `MEMORY RECONCILIATION FAILED` headline, the 210-key incident,
the spelled-out recovery oid, the `git log -S'"key":"..."'` hunt and the warning about
grepping for a key. Every word of that is correct FOR A LOSS, and none of it applies to
a blank line.

SO THE REPAIR IS NOT "ADD A SENTENCE" -- IT IS TO SPLIT THE OUTPUT ALONG THE SPLIT THE
FUNCTION ALREADY MAKES:

  * KEY SET SHORT (real loss)      -> print what it prints today, unchanged. Do not
                                      touch those paragraphs; they are load-bearing and
                                      they were written against a real incident.
  * SUM SHORT, KEY SET INTACT      -> print a SHORT, differently-headed note. Something
                                      of the order of: N row(s) in the export are
                                      neither an issue nor a memory; the memory key set
                                      reconciles, so this is NOT a deletion; the usual
                                      cause is a BLANK LINE, check with
                                      `tail -c 3 <file> | od -c` or by comparing
                                      `awk 'END{print NR}'` against `jq -c . | wc -l`;
                                      a blank line is benign and the next checkpoint
                                      drops it, because `minimal_diff_rewrite` builds
                                      `cnt[]` from the export and a blank line absent
                                      there has `cnt[""] = 0`.
  * BOTH SHORT                     -> the loss message wins; say the sum is off too.

That is the whole change, and it needs no new detector, no new state and no refusal --
the two answers are already computed a few lines apart.

KEEP THE HEADLINE HONEST. `MEMORY RECONCILIATION FAILED` on a blank line is the part
that does the damage: it is the string an operator greps for, remembers, and eventually
learns to skip. A guard that cries wolf on a benign formatting artefact is worth less
than one that stays quiet, and this one is guarding a real 210-key incident.

WHILE YOU ARE IN THERE, CHECK THE `.ps1` SIBLING. `scripts/beads-checkpoint.ps1` is the
Windows twin and the two are kept in step by hand. If it carries the same message shape,
it needs the same split; if it does not carry this guard at all, SAY SO in the PR body
rather than porting the whole guard as a side quest -- that is a separate decision and
not this bead's.

DO NOT "FIX" THE BLANK LINE ITSELF. Stripping blank lines defensively in the export path
is a different change with a different risk, and the observed one self-healed. If you
think it is worth doing, FILE IT; do not fold it in here.

=== VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION, ~14 MINUTES AFTER THE MERGE (mayor, fact) ===

The new message fired on a real checkpoint in the mayor checkout, on exactly the case it was
built for, and it behaved as designed. Verbatim head of what it printed:

    beads-checkpoint: unaccounted rows in the export — NOT a memory deletion.
      The loss detector is the KEY-SET comparison against HEAD, it ran, and it
      found nothing missing: every `bd remember` key HEAD carries is present in
      the fresh export. What fired is the other arm — the two populations do not
      account for every row of the file (rf2-cve7, rf2-q88t).

      export  2290 rows = 1223 issues + 1066 memories
      HEAD    2289 rows = 1223 issues + 1066 memories

Then the blank-line diagnosis, the two checks, and the statement that it is benign and does not
accumulate. Nothing refused; the checkpoint committed and exited 0.

**THE PRESCRIBED CHECKS WERE RUN AS A COLD OPERATOR WOULD RUN THEM, AND BOTH LANDED FIRST TIME:**

    grep -n -v '^{' .beads/issues.jsonl   ->  2290:            (the empty line, named)
    tail -c 3 .beads/issues.jsonl | od -c ->  }  \n  \n       (the doubled newline)
    awk 'END{print NR}' = 2290  against  jq -c . | wc -l = 2289

Diagnosed in seconds, from the message alone, with no reading of the script. That is the whole
deliverable and it is discharged by use rather than by argument.

**AND THE PHENOMENON RECURS, WHICH THE BEAD DID NOT ESTABLISH.** The original filing measured ONE
blank line in SEVEN exports and could not reproduce it. This is a second independent occurrence,
hours later, and it coincided with the merged-PR audit harness writing again — the same coincidence
as the first. That does not promote the race from inference to fact, and the message correctly
still does not assert it. What it does establish is that this is a RECURRING benign event rather
than a one-off, which is precisely the case where a thirty-line loss banner would have trained an
operator to skip the string it needs to read. The repair earned its place.

No action follows. Recorded so the next reader of this bead knows the fix was exercised against
live data and not only against the four synthetic quadrants.

title: ssr: :children and :dangerouslySetInnerHTML reach the wire as DOM attributes
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 by the rf2-gw87 worker, in the file it was fixing, and deliberately NOT folded in. That
restraint is correct and is the first thing to preserve: `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is a CONTENT CHANNEL, not
an identity slot, so it is a different mechanism from the structural-slot defect rf2-gw87 fixed and does not
belong in that roster entry without its own argument.

THE DEFECT, measured live: `attr-string {:children "v"}` emits ` children="v"`. Both `:children` and
`:dangerouslySetInnerHTML` reach the wire as DOM attributes. React's own serialiser emits neither.

WHY EACH IS ITS OWN QUESTION RATHER THAN ONE FIX:
  * `:children` is React's own children channel. A props map carrying it is asking for children, not for an
    attribute — so emitting one is straightforwardly wrong, and the open question is only whether SSR should
    also HONOUR it as children or merely drop it. Answer that explicitly; do not leave it implied by whatever
    the code happens to do.
  * `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is raw-HTML content. Emitting it as an attribute is wrong in the same shape,
    but DROPPING it silently loses content the author asked to render, which is a different and possibly
    worse failure than a stray attribute. Establish what the client does and what the other emitters here do
    before choosing. A server that silently drops content a browser would render is a new
    server-diverges-from-client hazard, and this artefact takes such divergences only deliberately.

WHERE THE FIX GOES, ALREADY ESTABLISHED BY rf2-gw87 AND NOT TO BE RE-DERIVED: `strip-prop?` in
`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`. That worker verified at source that
`emit/attr-string` is a re-export (emit.cljc:57) of `html-helpers/attr-string`, which calls `strip-prop?`,
and that `strip-prop?` is called from nowhere else — so one roster entry reaches FOUR surfaces: the body
emitter, the streaming walker, the head emitter, and the ssr-ring host shell's `<html>`/`<body>` attribute
bags. A local `dissoc` anywhere else would mint a second roster, which that file's own notes forbid.

SO THE EVIDENCE OBLIGATION IS THE SAME AS rf2-gw87's: because the whole argument for editing `strip-prop?` is
that it reaches all four, a change that demonstrates only one has not shown the thing that justified its own
location.

AND CHECK THE HEAD EMITTER AND THE HOST SHELL EXPLICITLY BEFORE WIDENING. rf2-gw87 found that the shared
roster genuinely does change head output — it had been emitting `<meta key="m1" name="a">`, `<link key="l1">`
and `<script key="s1">` — and that worker pinned the new behaviour as a recorded decision rather than letting
it happen silently. Do the same here: establish current behaviour on all four surfaces first, report it, and
pin whatever you change.

GATES that were the substance for rf2-gw87 and are the right starting set: the JVM SSR suite, `test:ssr-node`,
the JVM ssr-ring suite and the JVM security suite — the last two derived rather than guessed, because
`implementation/{ssr,ssr-ring,fresco}` require `html-helpers` in src and `implementation/security` does so in
test. Fresco's use is `.cljs` with no JVM lane, so the CLJS side of this `.cljc` is exercised in CI.

SEQUENCING: this touches the same file as rf2-gw87. Do not dispatch it until PR #9593 has merged.

title: gh statusCheckRollup reports a RUNNING check with conclusion "" not null, so a null-guarded filter reads it as a failure
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-10 on PR #9590, head 8233507d78ebaa409b2fd2c219c20ed399b851c7, while running the merge
criterion against a healthy draft.

THE INSTRUMENT. `gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup` reports a check that is STILL RUNNING as
`status: "IN_PROGRESS"` with `conclusion: ""` — AN EMPTY STRING, NOT NULL. Every guard everyone writes
tests for null.

SO THE OBVIOUS FILTER COUNTS EVERY RUNNING CHECK AS A FAILURE:

    select(.conclusion != null and .conclusion != "SUCCESS"
           and .conclusion != "SKIPPED" and .conclusion != "NEUTRAL")

`"" != null` is true, so a queued or in-progress check falls straight through into the failure bucket.

MEASURED, BOTH WAYS, ON ONE PR IN ONE MINUTE:
  * the null-guarded filter reported `bad=10` and NAMED TEN REAL JOBS — clj-kondo, Splint, Public-API
    manifest drift-check, three CLJS jobs, Story/Xray browser gates, JVM tools/mcp-base, Node
    re-frame2-pair-mcp, MCP conformance story-mcp. A completely plausible list for a broken change.
  * grouping the WHOLE rollup by `(status, conclusion)` shows the truth: 53 COMPLETED/SKIPPED,

title: CLAUDE.md: scope CRLF normalization recipe and repair its splitlines regex example
description:
Merged-PR audit #9552; landed be17ea7d157301f309e36bbbdedfb2bb2186acf8, CLAUDE.md:119, instrument item (e). The new paragraph describes a Python splitlines() census losing CR characters required by its regex, then says deleting CR from BOTH SIDES is the guard for every case. That repairs unequal literal strings, but cannot repair a regex whose escaped CR is part of the pattern's semantics.

Minimal measured counterexample (Python):
  import re
  raw = 'payload\r\n'
  pattern = r'payload\r$'
  line = raw.splitlines()[0]
The raw-line control re.search(pattern, raw.rstrip('\n')) matches. re.search(pattern, line) does not. Deleting actual U+000D from BOTH pattern and line still does not match: the raw regex string contains backslash+r, not a CR byte. Using r'payload$' against the normalized line matches. Audit byte-validation.json records all four results. A separate literal-string control changes 0 matches to 3 after CR normalization. The target-derived positive-control requirement is useful and must stay: it detects the failed regex recipe, but does not make that recipe sufficient.

Repair only the new guidance: distinguish literal-byte normalization from adapting a pattern to normalized data (or retaining endings when a regex deliberately matches them). Explain the correct pattern/data pairing for the named splitlines example; scope the universal one-line claim accordingly. Likewise say differing jq output conventions CAN break comparisons, rather than asserting any mixed jq/non-jq comparison necessarily fails, which conflicts with the existing clean single-value example immediately above. No new helper, gate, framework API, or backlog-cleanup task.

No exact existing owner found in full exported titles/descriptions/notes/close reasons for the new guard or splitlines/CR case. rf2-jwlh owns the earlier jq alternation diagnosis and fixed-string-file remedy, already fulfilled; this is a new recipe introduced by #9552. > **RULED 2026-09-09 — OPTION B: archive `.git/lost-found` off-box with `xz -9`, verify with controls, then `rm -rf`. The exact copy-pasteable procedure is in the NOTES on this bead. Mike executes; do not close until the archive path and size are recorded here.**
> **2026-09-13 — THE CURRENT RUNBOOK IS THE NOTE HEADED "== RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-09-13, dossier + Codex review) ==" at the END of the notes.** It confirms option B and supersedes the 2026-09-09 runbook in three places: the step-3 expectations (post-deletion `du -sh .git` is about 4.5G, not ~2.2 GB; 30-90 min, not ~30), an added member-name inventory check, and an added `sha256sum` line. Its section 5 corrects this bead's stale figures (the 9 files are 223,404 B, not 243,404) and section 6 is the loss statement. Read that note, not the older one, at the keyboard.
>
> **THE COMPOSITION BELOW WAS MISREAD FOR MONTHS AND THE TITLE CARRIED THE ERROR.** "4.75 GB whose 4,739 objects are GONE" reads as 4,739 objects of content. It is not. **2,839 of the 4,739 files (59.9%) are 41-byte TOMBSTONES whose entire content is a copy of their own hash** — `git fsck --lost-found` writes bodies only for BLOBS, so every one of the 2,306 "dangling commits" in here holds no commit content and never did. The 4.64 GiB is **1,900 content-bearing blobs, 1,891 of which are successive revisions of `.beads/issues.jsonl`** from an eleven-day window in May 2026, plus **9** source/doc files that each have a live, larger successor. Price the decision off that, not off the file count.
>
> **Two claims below are now SUPERSEDED, struck rather than deleted so the reasoning stays legible:**
> - ~~"What these 4,739 objects actually contain. Not audited."~~ — **audited; see the notes.**
> - ~~"Default is RETAIN."~~ — that was the rf2-gwxj standing position taken before the audit. **The audit is done and the ruling is B.** The retain-by-default gate has been discharged, not overridden.
>
> **What HELD exactly, re-verified at HEAD `71decabd3f`:** all 4,739 named objects are absent from this object store, controls at both ends of one `cat-file --batch-check` stream, no alternates and no promisor remote. **Deletion is irreversible.** That is why B and not A.

---

Discovered while ruling rf2-gwxj (the beads-store/flatten decision). **This is NOT a reclaim task — it is an operator call about 4.75 GB of material that cannot be regenerated.** Nothing here is dispatchable to a worker: `.git/lost-found` belongs to the primary checkout's object store and does not exist in a linked worktree.

## What it is

`.git/lost-found` in the mayor checkout `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2`, measured 2026-09-08 23:1x AUSEST:

- **4,982,432,111 bytes (4751.6 MB)** across **4,739 files** — `other/` 2,433 files / 4751.5 MB, `commit/` 2,306 files / 0.1 MB.
- Directory mtime **2026-05-16**; the enclosing `.git/lost-found` is 2026-05-12. Output of a `git fsck --lost-found` run from a recovery nearly four months ago.
- Context: `.git` is 8344.7 MB total, of which `.git/objects` is 3543.8 MB.

## The finding that makes this a decision rather than a chore

The rf2-gwxj dossier proposed deleting this as a safe, effectively reversible 4.7 GB win, reasoning that `git fsck --lost-found` would regenerate it. **That is false, and the correction came from the Codex review; I reproduced it independently and extended it.**

`fsck --lost-found` writes *copies* of DANGLING objects. It cannot regenerate an object that is no longer in the object store. Measured with `git cat-file --batch-check` over the filenames:

- `other/`: **2,433 of 2,433 missing** from the object store.
- `commit/`: **2,306 of 2,306 missing** (Codex tested only `other/`; this set was added while ruling rf2-gwxj).
- **All 4,739 entries name objects that no longer exist in `.git/objects`.**

**CONTROLS, run through the same pipeline** — without these the zeros would not be evidence:
- POSITIVE: `HEAD` (`8e53b1f68f9fe2d5111d937da80c9dad3e32e4ae`) returned `commit 255`.
- NEGATIVE: a fabricated 40-hex hash returned `missing`.
- PAYLOAD INTACTNESS: `other/000490f9446c76f9822679b2ddc15b8f46a987cb` is 1,852,733 bytes; non-writing `git hash-object --no-filters` reproduces its filename exactly, while `git cat-file -t` on that hash exits 128. So the file content is intact and the object is genuinely absent.

**Consequence: these 4,739 files are the ONLY surviving copies of their objects. Deleting them is irreversible and unregenerable, and a clean `git fsck` afterwards would coexist with the loss and prove nothing.**

## Why the objects are missing — the cause is known and consistent

rf2-ah6r (closed) was Mike's `git gc` on this checkout (174,378 loose objects, ~63 GiB of `.git` at the time; `.git` is 8.3 GB now, so it ran). **`git gc` prunes dangling objects from the object store but does not touch `.git/lost-found`**, which is an ordinary directory of file copies. That is exactly the sequence that leaves lost-found filenames naming objects the store no longer has. Measurement and history agree.

## What has NOT been established

- **What these 4,739 objects actually contain.** Not audited. Their human value is unknown.
- **Whether copies exist elsewhere** (another clone, a backup, the remote). Not reviewed.
- Age establishes staleness, not that the May recovery concluded successfully.

## The decision required

**Default is RETAIN** — that is the standing position from the rf2-gwxj ruling, and no storage pressure argues otherwise (411 GB free of 953 GB; `.beads` accrues ~55 MB/day).

If Mike wants the 4.75 GB back, the safe order is:

1. **Sample the contents first** to establish what class of objects these are (blobs of which paths, commits of which branches). `git hash-object` confirms a file's identity without writing; inflating a copy to inspect it is read-only.
2. **Archive off-box and VERIFY THE ARCHIVE** — byte totals and file counts, and spot-check that a restored file still hashes to its filename.
3. Only then delete, and record the archive location on this bead.

Do NOT delete on the strength of "it is stale" or "fsck will regenerate it". The second is measurably untrue.

## Neighbour

rf2-fmst (open) is the live `.git` hygiene lane (keeping loose objects packed after the rf2-ah6r gc). Related surface, independent decision — do not merge the two.

--- RULING 2026-09-09 13:25 AUSEST — DECISION LANDED. Mayor checkout, HEAD 71decabd3f. Two independent analyses (dossier + Codex review) weighed; dossier deleted. ---

# DECISION: OPTION B — ARCHIVE WITH `xz -9` OFF-BOX, VERIFY WITH CONTROLS, THEN `rm -rf .git/lost-found`.

Not A (delete bare), not C (keep). The composition finding below makes deletion **safe rather than
brave**; the archive makes it **reversible** for ~30 minutes of unattended CPU and a file measured in
tens of MB. Mike executes; nothing has been deleted, moved, archived or pruned by this ruling.

**Against Codex on timing, with Codex on procedure.** Codex recommended "keep now, B only if Mike
wants the space back." Declined: the material is now fully characterised, the trade is priced, and
`lost-found` is **69.2% of the 6.71 GB `.git`** (4,982,432,111 of 7,201,732,292 bytes — re-measured
today) inflating every `du` and every backup of this checkout. "No urgency" is an argument against
rushing, not against deciding. But **every one of Codex's procedural corrections is upheld and is in
the runbook below** — three of them would have broken or silently degraded the dossier's
copy-pasteable commands.

---

## 1. THE PROCEDURE — copy-pasteable, every command tested today

Run from the mayor checkout in **Git Bash**, fleet quiet. GNU tar 1.35 / XZ Utils 5.8.2, both at
`/mingw64/bin`.

**Destination.** The dossier's `/d/archive/` **DOES NOT EXIST** — `ls -d /d` exits 2, and
`Get-Volume` reports **C: is the only volume on this machine** (391.8 GiB free of 952.4). Codex is
right that "outside the repo", "another volume" and "off-box" are three different properties, and
here only the first two are even available locally. The one genuinely off-box target on this box is
**OneDrive** (`$OneDrive` = `C:\Users\miket\OneDrive`), which syncs to cloud. Substitute an external
disk if preferred. **Do not put it inside the repo tree** — that defeats the purpose.

```bash
cd /c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
DEST=/c/Users/miket/OneDrive/archive          # off-box via sync; change if you prefer
mkdir -p "$DEST"
ARCH="$DEST/re-frame2-lost-found-2026-05-16.tar.xz"

# ---- 0. Record the source inventory BEFORE touching anything ----
find .git/lost-found -type f -printf '%s\n' | awk '{s+=$1;n++} END{print "SRC files="n" bytes="s}'
#   expect: SRC files=4739 bytes=4982432111

# ---- 1. Build the archive. Nothing is deleted by this step. ----
#   XZ_OPT=-9 IS LOAD-BEARING — see the correction below. ~30 min unattended.
XZ_OPT=-9 tar -cJf "$ARCH" -C .git lost-found
echo "create_exit=$?"          # must be 0
ls -l "$ARCH"
```

**Two tar traps, both measured today, both fatal-or-silent as written in the dossier:**

- **A drive-letter path in `-f` is parsed by GNU tar as a remote `host:path`.**
  `tar -cJf "C:/Users/..." ...` dies with `tar (child): Cannot connect to C: resolve failed` /
  `tar: Child returned status 128`, **exit 2**. Use the POSIX `/c/...` form above, or add
  `--force-local`. Both verified working (exit 0).
- **`tar -cJf` compresses at xz preset 6, not 9** — Codex's catch, and it is the single most
  expensive error in the dossier's runbook. Bare `-J` uses xz's documented default preset 6 (8 MiB
  dictionary); the dossier's 0.97% ratio came from an explicit `xz -9` (64 MiB dictionary), which is
  what dedups across near-identical snapshots. **Measured today on the same 25-file /
  141,723,921-byte sample: preset 6 -> 7,162,276 B (5.05%); preset 9 -> 1,218,244 B (0.86%). 5.9x
  worse.** So the dossier's command would have produced an archive nearly six times larger than the
  size it advertised.
- **Do NOT bother tuning member order or thread count.** Measured, so it can stop being a question:
  hash order 1,218,900 B vs size-sorted 1,218,244 B (0.05% apart), and `-T1` 1,218,236 B vs `-T0`
  1,218,244 B. Immaterial. The preset is the only knob that matters.

```bash
# ---- 2. VERIFY. All three checks must pass BEFORE any removal. ----

# 2a. Compression integrity.
xz -t "$ARCH"; echo "xz_t_exit=$?"                      # must be 0

# 2b. Inventory reconciliation — catches files ABSENT from the archive,
#     which 2c structurally cannot (it iterates archive members only).
tar -tvJf "$ARCH" > /tmp/cq3x-inventory.txt; echo "list_exit=$?"    # must be 0
awk '$1 !~ /^d/ {n++; s+=$3} END{print "ARCH files="n" bytes="s}' /tmp/cq3x-inventory.txt
#   must equal step 0 exactly: files=4739 bytes=4982432111

# 2c. FULL byte comparison of every member against the still-present source.
#     Silent + exit 0 = every archived byte matches disk.
tar -dJf "$ARCH" -C .git
echo "diff_exit=$?"                                     # MUST be 0, and output MUST be empty
```

**Never write these as `… | tail` or `… | grep -c`** — a pipeline's exit status is its last
command's, so a fatal tar abort reports as success. Read each `echo "*_exit=$?"` line.

`tar -d` was exercised in **both directions** today: exit 0 and silent against the intact source;
exit 1 naming `Mod time differs` / `Size differs` on a tampered member and `Cannot stat` on a deleted
one. It is a real instrument, not a formality. Step 2b is not redundant with it — Codex is right that
`-d` cannot see a source file the archive never contained.

```bash
# ---- 3. ONLY after 2a, 2b and 2c all pass ----
rm -rf .git/lost-found          # this exact path, nothing broader inside .git
du -sh .git                     # expect ~2.2 GB, down from 6.71 GB
```

`git fsck --connectivity-only` afterwards proves the **repository** is sound; it says nothing
whatever about what was lost or what the archive holds. Do not read it as verification. Then record
the archive path and size on this bead and close it.

## 2. THE COMPOSITION FINDING — this is what makes the decision safe

**The bead's own title was wrong about this and has been corrected today.** "4.75 GB whose 4,739
objects are GONE" implies 4,739 objects each holding a share of 4.75 GB. They do not. Re-measured at
HEAD 71decabd3f with `find`, never `ls | wc -l` (which omits dotfiles):

| Class | Files | Bytes | % files | % bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **41-byte tombstones** (content = the file's own hash, nothing else) | **2,839** | 116,399 | **59.9%** | 0.002% |
| — of which dangling commits (`commit/`) | 2,306 | | | |
| — of which dangling trees/tags (`other/`) | 533 | | | |
| **Content-bearing blobs** (`other/`) | **1,900** | **4,982,315,712** | 40.1% | **99.998%** |
| — revisions of `.beads/issues.jsonl` | **1,891** | | | |
| — source / documentation files | **9** | 243,404 | | |
| **Total** | **4,739** | **4,982,432,111** | | |

All four figures reproduced today independently of the dossier: `find -type f` 4,739 files /
4,982,432,111 bytes; `find -size -42c -size +40c` 2,839; `commit/` 2,306 + `other/` 2,433 = 4,739;
and a first-line classifier over all 1,900 content-bearing blobs read **1,891 tracker snapshots plus
exactly 9 non-tracker files**. That classifier discriminates in both directions — it named all nine
(`re_frame/core.cljc`, `registrar.cljc`, `digest_parity_fixtures.cljc`, the pre-rename
`day8.re-frame2-causa.registry-cljs-test`, a `PANEL_HANDOFFS` spec.cjs, the Causa feature-matrix
README, the "read Clojure in 40 minutes" essay, a "Test Tiering Audit" working proposal, and
`ai/extended-context/README.md`) — so a blanket answer is ruled out.

**Three consequences, and they are the whole basis of the ruling:**

1. **`git fsck --lost-found` writes bodies only for BLOBS.** For commits, trees and tags it writes a
   name, not a body. So the "2,306 recovered dangling commits" recovered **nothing** — there is no
   commit content in this directory and there never was. That loss, whatever it was, happened at the
   September gc and no disposition here touches it.
2. **99.5% of the 4.64 GiB is one file's revision history** — 1,891 successive snapshots of
   `.beads/issues.jsonl` from an eleven-day window (2026-05-06 -> 05-16), of a tracker whose entire
   id space has since been retired: 2,509 bead ids in there, **zero** overlap with the current 1,127.
   `.beads/issues.jsonl` is by design a regenerated full-database export; per CLAUDE.md the Dolt
   database, not the export, is the source of truth.
3. **The information is near-fully duplicated on trunk.** 2,507 of the 2,509 ids appear in a single
   trunk commit (`7349c1be`). The 9 non-tracker blobs each have a live, larger successor in trunk,
   upstream, or the local `ai/` tree — every one is an earlier revision, not a lost artefact.

**CODEX WINS ON THE LOSS BOUND, AND THE CORRECTION IS UPHELD.** The dossier compared per-id **maximum
record LENGTHS** and concluded "7,289 bytes across 20 records is a CEILING on unique loss." That does
not follow: equal-length records can differ in content; a longer replacement can have discarded a
shorter note wholesale; two shorter historical states can each hold text the longest state lacks. So
**7,289 bytes is an illustration of the character of the unique material, not a bound on its size**,
and the dossier's "10.5 KB total" and "triage done" overstate the evidence. This is precisely why the
ruling is B and not A: an unbounded-but-small loss is exactly the case an archive is for. The
character of the material is nonetheless well established and worth keeping: merged-PR fix summaries
and design notes on beads that no longer exist. The exemplar is rf2-higwg — a 2,071-character PR
number 728 root-cause report surviving in `lost-found/other/dd7eac18b3…` and replaced on trunk by a
285-character reopening note. **That is the `bd update --notes` replace-instead-of-append hazard
caught in the wild on 2026-05-13** — the single most valuable object in this directory is a note
destroyed by that exact flag.

## 3. THE IRREVERSIBILITY EVIDENCE — holds exactly, with controls

Re-verified today at HEAD 71decabd3f, one `git --no-lazy-fetch cat-file --batch-check` stream,
4,743 names in:

```
71decabd3f8ef8e5224e6feeb6934cad5af26394 commit 255   <- POSITIVE control (HEAD), FIRST line
0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 missing      <- NEGATIVE control
deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef missing      <- NEGATIVE control
... all 4,739 lost-found filenames ...
71decabd3f8ef8e5224e6feeb6934cad5af26394 commit 255   <- POSITIVE control, LAST line
tally: 2 commit / 4,741 missing        (exit 0)
```

The instrument discriminates in both directions and at **both ends** of the stream, so a truncated
or short-circuited read is ruled out. `.git/objects/info/` holds no `alternates` file, and a
`git config --get-regexp` probe for `promisor` / `partialclonefilter` remotes exits 1 — no partial
clone, no lazy fetch, nothing deferred. **The named objects are genuinely absent from this object
store and `git fsck --lost-found` cannot regenerate any of them. Deletion is irreversible.** Blob
payloads are nonetheless byte-intact: non-writing `git hash-object --no-filters` reproduces the
filename for sampled blobs, while the same command on a tombstone yields a different hash entirely
(`commit/0008e0c231…` -> `e4514c945e…`). Scope, stated honestly: this establishes absence from **this
local store**, not from backups, other clones or the remote — neither analysis searched those.

**Codex correction accepted, materially inert:** the dossier's line 33 glosses "dangling" as
"unreachable from any branch, tag, stash or reflog." Dangling is narrower — tips not referenced by
another object — and `fsck --lost-found` disables reflog roots, so the presence of these files does
not evidence the reflog claim. It changes nothing about the disposition.

## 4. WHAT DID NOT MOVE, AND WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE

- **`.beads/backup/` (~2.7 GB of `.darc`) and `.beads/embeddeddolt/` (~1.4 GB) were NOT searched**
  for the unique records. The Dolt store predates the id-space reset and may well hold them; querying
  it means touching a database a live mayor loop owns. **Option B makes this moot** — do not spend
  the time.
- **No separate bead for "extract the 20 unique records first." Deliberate.** B archives the entire
  corpus, so extraction is redundant; and per section 2 the "20" is not a sound figure to build a
  bead on. If Mike ever chooses A over B instead, extraction becomes a mandatory step of **that**
  decision, not a bead of its own.
- **Whether the missing objects survive on `origin`.** Unverified and not to be relied on.
- **Which branches the 2,306 dangling commits belonged to.** Unknowable — hashes only, reflogs long
  expired, content pruned. Independent of this decision.
- **No full-corpus compression, archive, verification or deletion was performed here.** Everything
  above is read-only measurement. `.git/lost-found` is intact, byte for byte, as found.
- **Neighbour, not merged:** rf2-fmst is the live `.git` hygiene lane. `lost-found` is not part of
  the object store, so no `git gc` and no `git maintenance` task will ever touch it — it will not
  shrink on its own.
- **Split out today as rf2-bd5n:** `.git` also holds **51 `codex-pr-audit-*` directories totalling
  122,606,133 bytes (116.9 MB)**, a second non-object-store consumer inside `.git`. Not this decision.

**Priority held at P3.** The decision is now fully specified and safe to execute, but nothing forces
the timing: 391.8 GiB free of 952.4, and the directory is inert. P3 with a landed procedure is the
right resting state for an operator-gated act.

## MAYOR, 2026-09-09 17:5x AUSEST — two figures in this bead re-measured. The RULING is untouched.

Nothing below changes option B, the procedure, or the operator-executes disposition. This bead's own
statement that it is not dispatchable to a worker was re-read and stands: `.git/lost-found` belongs

**1. The timing premise HOLDS, so P3 is still the right resting state.** This bead argues nothing
forces the timing, citing 391.8 GiB free of 952.4. Re-measured just now: **399.9 GiB free** — very
slightly MORE headroom than when the ruling was written, not less. The directory is still inert and
still untouched by any `git gc` or `git maintenance` task, exactly as recorded.

**2. THE codex-pr-audit FIGURE IN THE "Split out today as rf2-bd5n" BULLET IS BADLY STALE — do not
quote it.** That bullet says 51 directories totalling 122,606,133 bytes (116.9 MB). Measured now:
**72 directories, 2206 MB.** The size is roughly nineteen times the quoted figure and the count has
moved 51 -> 61 -> 72 within today alone, because the out-of-repo merge-audit harness is still
running and writes a new directory per merged PR.

**The reason the size exploded is the thing a reader most needs, and it is a deletion hazard rather
than a bookkeeping one.** The bulk is NOT audit scratch: `.git/codex-pr-audit-9546` holds
`recovery-1|2|3`, which are full copies of the beads Dolt database with SHA-256 snapshot proofs —
roughly 1.9 GB, about 89% of the whole population, one of them written 13 minutes before it was
measured. **A rule of the form "delete `.git/codex-pr-audit-*`" run today would destroy live tracker
backups.** Excluding those, all the audit directories together are ~246 MB, which is the number the
retention question should actually be argued over.

That was established by a read-only investigation under rf2-bd5n, whose title now carries both the
warning and an explicit "counts move hourly: re-measure, do not quote". **Read rf2-bd5n for the
retention question; treat every count in the bullet above as a dated snapshot only.**

Recorded here rather than by editing the original bullet, so the reasoning that produced the split
stays legible — same convention this bead already uses for its two struck claims.

== RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-09-13, dossier + Codex review) ==
2026-09-13 14:17:07 AUSEST — mayor checkout, HEAD == origin/main `38e9282e64`. Decided by a delegated agent on Mike's
instruction of 2026-09-13. The dossier `ai/decisions/rf2-cq3x.lost-found-archive-or-delete.md` — primary
analysis plus the appended "Codex Recommendation" — was read in full and weighed; what follows is what
survives of both, so the dossier can go. Nothing was deleted, moved, archived or pruned; no `git gc`,
`prune`, `repack`, `fsck` or `maintenance` ran; no tracked file was edited; no bead was reopened.

## 1. DECISION

**OPTION B CONFIRMED, unchanged from 2026-09-09:** archive `.git/lost-found` with `XZ_OPT=-9` to
`C:\Users\miket\OneDrive\archive\re-frame2-lost-found-2026-05-16.tar.xz` (written as
`/c/Users/miket/OneDrive/archive/...` in the commands), verify with the controls in section 4, record
the archive's path, size and sha256 on this bead, then `rm -rf .git/lost-found`. **Keep the archive
indefinitely; no retention job.** Mike executes at any convenient moment — nothing forces the timing,
and the directory is inert until then.

## 2. REASONING, graded against the stance and Mike's words

This is a 4.98 GB inert directory: 1,891 superseded exports of one tracker file, 9 superseded source
revisions, and 2,839 41-byte names of objects whose content is already gone. Every measurement the
ruling rests on was re-read at source today and matched exactly (section 5). B is one `tar` line, four
verify lines and one `rm`; it is the smallest act that turns the only irreversible step here into a
reversible one, and it asks no further decision of anybody. C (delete outright) saves roughly an hour of
UNATTENDED CPU and loses the material in section 6 permanently. "Don't litigate the minutiae" is an
argument for finishing this, not for deliberating a retention period, a member order, or a cloud
round-trip — so none of those is prescribed.

**Where the primary and Codex AGREED:** B; OneDrive as the only genuinely off-box target on this
one-volume box; `xz -9` explicit; keep indefinitely; record actuals rather than estimates; retaining the
directory while the archive is pending is fine; no library feature, tool or recurring audit.

**Where they DIFFERED, and how each was resolved:**

(a) **The loss inventory.** Primary: what lost-found uniquely holds is under 15 KB of note text on 27
retired ids, 2 never-committed ids and 9 superseded files. Codex: that inventory omits the export's
MEMORY rows (`bd remember` records — `_type`/`key`/`value`, no issue id): 24 distinct key/value pairs in

title: skill(re-frame2): spawn.md still teaches 'that region halts' for a :final? parallel region — PR #9482 deleted that sentence from spec/005 as wrong, and the consumer-facing skill is now the only copy
description:
`skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/spawn.md:108` still teaches that a `:final?` leaf halts its parallel region. PR #9482 (merged 2026-09-08T06:28:04Z) deleted exactly that sentence from `spec/005-StateMachines.md` because it is WRONG, and the skill is now the only place in the repo still saying it.

THE LINE, verbatim:

    - **Parallel regions.** A leaf in one region may be `:final?`; that region halts. When
      **every** region's active leaf is `:final?` the parallel root fires its own `:on-done`
      if declared — **and the machine keeps running** — otherwise the whole-machine
      auto-destroy / spawning-parent cascade fires.

The second and third clauses are fine. The clause "that region halts" is the defect.

WHY IT IS WRONG. A `:final?` LEAF sources nothing — a transition declared on it is refused at registration — but the REGION does not halt: an ancestor `:on`, `:always`, `:after`, or a raise can still move it. rf2-hu69's investigation established this at source and PR #9482 landed the correction in the spec plus an 8-test / 17-assertion fixture. The skill was not updated in that PR.

MEASURED 2026-09-08 after #9482 merged:
    grep -n 'region halts' skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/spawn.md   -> line 108, present
    grep -c 'region halts' spec/005-StateMachines.md                             -> 0 (deleted by #9482)
This is direct positive evidence (the line was read, not inferred from an absence), so it needs no instrument control; the spec zero is corroborating and is explained by the merged PR rather than by a broken grep.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY DOC TYPO: `skills/` is CONSUMER-FACING. It ships as authoring guidance to people building on re-frame2, who have no reason to cross-check it against `spec/005`. A consumer who reads "that region halts" will believe a completed region can no longer be moved, and will therefore not write the ancestor-`:on` guard that the real semantics require. The spec and the skill now disagree, and the skill is the copy a consumer actually reads.

THE FIX: correct that clause to match the post-#9482 spec — a `:final?` leaf sources no transition, but its region remains movable by an ancestor `:on` / `:always` / `:after` / raise. Keep the rest of the bullet.

WHILE THERE, worth one check rather than assuming: sweep `skills/**` for any other statement of the same claim, and for anything else #9482 invalidated. Use `grep -F -f <patterns-file>` for the multi-needle sweep (a jq-built alternation carries CRLF on this box and matches only its last alternative), take the count separately from the listing, and give every zero a positive control on the same corpus with the same tool.

GATE: `skills/**` markdown is graded by `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` for link targets and anchors, NOT by `check_doc_slugs.py` (different roots) and NOT by `mkdocs build --strict` (outside `docs_dir`). This edit changes prose rather than links, so no gate actually inspects the corrected sentence — verify the claim by reading it against `spec/005` and say so in the PR body.

DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-hu69, whose dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-hu69.final-region-conflict.md, local-only) carries the full semantics analysis.
acceptance_criteria: spawn.md:108 matches post-#9482 spec/005 semantics; skills/** swept for the same claim; PR body states the verification was by hand because no gate inspects this prose.
