title: [tools/xray/panels] Empty infinite feeds are reported as having fresh data
description:
Snapshot: 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Relevant source unchanged at mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d.

Xray reports an infinite feed which has not loaded any pages as having usable data, and its route/resource graph can report it fresh during first-load. This is a narrow diagnostic error, not a resource-runtime failure.

Expected: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:750-766 defines an infinite resource as has-data only when its page vector is nonempty. empty-infinite-entry at 1103-1120 initializes :data []. Xray spec tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md:217-234 requires derived :has-data? and the infinite-feed facts; lines 272-283 require the live freshness rollup.

Actual: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources_helpers.cljc:573-581 accepts only data and uses some?. instance-row:638-645 passes the empty page vector, giving true. resource-liveness:858-882 then skips :loading because has-data is true and chooses :fresh when the initial entry is not stale. Its :status remains :loading and :page-count is 0, making the diagnostic contradict itself. Existing infinite fixtures at tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:412-480 cover feeds with pages, not the initial empty page vector.

Minimal executed reproduction (bb with tools/xray/src on classpath):
```clojure
(require '[day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.resources-helpers :as h])
(let [row (h/instance-row
           [[nil :feed {}]
            {:resource/id :feed :resource/key [nil :feed {}]
             :status :loading :infinite? true :data []
             :active-owners #{:view}}] 0)]
  (prn (select-keys row [:status :has-data? :page-count]))
  (prn (h/resource-liveness :feed [row]
         [{:resource-id :feed :terminal? false}])))
```
Observed {:status :loading, :has-data? true, :page-count 0}; rollup has :active-work 1, :freshness :fresh. Probe used the actual pure projection namespace and exited 0 in under a second; no browser/CLJS compilation, runtime fetch, or suite executed.

Smallest repair: let the projection's data-presence derivation see the infinite-entry fact and distinguish an empty page vector from accumulated pages. Keep scalar nil/non-nil semantics and existing redaction/elision preservation (the rf2-tgm1xu behavior described at resources_helpers.cljc:573-579); do not add a resource owner or fetch while inspecting.

Focused acceptance: raw empty infinite page vector => has-data false and first-load rollup :loading; a feed with one empty page `[[]]` => has-data true; ordinary resource data [] still => true; populated sensitive/elided payloads retain the existing data-presence fact. Current and closed searches for resource liveness, Xray infinite, infinite and tgm1xu plus resource-panel memory search found no duplicate; tgm1xu was not returned by tracker or checked-in historical row lookup, so its current source/test rule is preserved rather than reopened.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9378. Xray's Resources projection derived :has-data? with a bare (some? data), so an :infinite? feed still on its seeded-empty page vector [] read as having data and resource-liveness called a never-loaded feed :fresh while the same row carried :status :loading / :page-count 0. entry-has-data? now derives from the ENTRY, mirroring re-frame.resources.state/has-data? (EP-0021 R1): >=1 accumulated page. Scalar nil/non-nil unchanged; the page-vector branch is guarded on sequential? so an upstream :rf/redacted / :rf.size/large-elided sentinel keeps the rf2-tgm1xu some? reading. tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md now states the rule at the Xray surface. Failing-first: exit 1, 3 failures + 1 error (:has-data? true, :freshness :fresh); after the fix exit 0. Full tools/xray suite exit 0, 1276 tests / 6118 assertions.

title: [implementation/adapters/test-react] Normal unmount logs child-before-parent instead of React class lifecycle order
description:
Surface: implementation/adapters/test-react, local-test-only fixture. Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; source unchanged at mayor HEAD 37fe77aad297bda18684d1904e37f207ad72f795.

The simulator advertises React class-component lifecycle fidelity, but reverses the normal componentWillUnmount order. This is a narrow P3 simulator correctness defect, not a request for full React reconciliation/emulation.

Expected versus actual:
- A React parent class receives componentWillUnmount before its descendant classes. Verified against the actually installed react-dom 19.2.0 package's cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:14384-14398: the ClassComponent deletion branch calls safelyCallComponentWillUnmount on deletedFiber.stateNode, THEN recursivelyTraverseDeletionEffects on the children. Upstream source locus: ReactFiberCommitWork.js, commitDeletionEffectsOnFiber, ClassComponent case (React v19.2.0).
- test_react.cljc:183-185 invokes each child's unmount thunk BEFORE logging the parent's :will-unmount. Its source at 149-159 and README.md:99-115 explicitly claim this children-first order mirrors React. The normal nested lifecycle probe therefore emits child,parent, the opposite of the behavior it claims to simulate.
- test_react_cljs_test.cljc:241-283 pins child-before-parent; its deep-cascade test at 1068 onward pins grandchild,child,parent. These protect the false model, rather than establish React parity.

Executed minimal reproduction using actual current test-react/core namespaces in an isolated Babashka process (exit 0, no build/shared runtime state):

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.adapter.test-react :as tr]
         '[re-frame.substrate.adapter :as sa])
(sa/install-adapter! tr/adapter)
(let [child (atom nil)
      parent (tr/mount!
               {:rf/component
                (fn [_] (reset! child (tr/mount-child! [:div])))})]
  (tr/unmount! parent)
  (prn
    (->> (concat
           (map #(assoc % :who :parent) (tr/lifecycle-log parent))
           (map #(assoc % :who :child) (tr/lifecycle-log @child)))
         (filter #(= :will-unmount (:phase %)))
         (sort-by :seq)
         (mapv :who))))
(sa/dispose-adapter!)
;; Actual printed result: [:child :parent]. React-equivalent: [:parent :child].
```

Impact and limits: a test using this fixture to reason about ancestor/descendant teardown order is told the opposite ordering to React, so cleanup assumptions can be falsely accepted. No current downstream consumer or application break was demonstrated: repository searches agree with README and closed rf2-6r9j.85 that this fixture currently has only its own artefact's tests. Priority is deliberately P3. The real React comparison is inspected package source, not an executed DOM mount; no React/browser/CLJS compile/full suite was run.

Smallest repair: place the parent's normal :will-unmount log at React's pre-descendant position while still tearing down every descendant and preserving exactly-once/idempotent eviction. Correct the two existing order assertions and directly contradictory source/README statements. Keep initial failed-render rollback and simulator-only :forced-teardown semantics separate; no reason to expand this into a reconciliation or scheduler project.

Dedupe: targeted current/all-status Test-React search and memories plus the tracked historical issue corpus. Read rf2-6r9j.141 (private descendant-helper rename), .142 (inspection names) and .85 (local-test-only/no-consumer truth) fully; none records a deliberate alternative ownership-order ruling. The .141 instruction to preserve recursion order was the fence of a naming-only change, not evidence that React uses that order.
acceptance_criteria: Nested and deep normal unmount logs show parent before descendants, while every node still unmounts exactly once and repeated unmount stays inert. Update existing reversed assertions and contradictory README/source claims. Preserve failed-render and forced-teardown semantics as separate paths.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07 AUSEST — implemented on worker/adapters-b, PR #9361 (bead left OPEN for the mayor) ---

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST.

React parity claim: confirmed against the INSTALLED react-dom 19.2.0
(implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js).
`commitDeletionEffectsOnFiber`'s ClassComponent branch (`case 1`) calls
`safelyCallComponentWillUnmount` on the deleted fiber's stateNode and only THEN
`recursivelyTraverseDeletionEffects` over its children. Parent-before-children
confirmed; the bead's expected/actual pair holds exactly as filed.

"Source unchanged at mayor HEAD 37fe77aad2" — STILL HELD at my base 90e9b0008a:
`git diff 37fe77aad2 90e9b0008a -- implementation/adapters/test-react` is empty.

WHAT CHANGED (cite the construct, not the line — the citations had not drifted,
but the constructs are the durable reference):

- `unmount-thunk`: the `(log-phase! mount :will-unmount)` call moves ABOVE the
  `doseq` that invokes each child's unmount thunk. Nothing else in the thunk
  moved: the `mounted?` entry guard, the render-depth `rendering?` guard, the
  `reset!`s and the `active-mounts` eviction are untouched, so exactly-once and
  idempotent-eviction semantics are bit-for-bit what they were.
- The two assertions that pinned the false model are INVERTED to pin React
  parity: `child-mounts-recurse-through-their-own-lifecycle` now asserts
  `(< parent-unmount-seq child-unmount-seq)`, and
  `deep-cascade-tears-down-leaf-upward` is renamed
  `deep-cascade-tears-down-root-downward` asserting
  `(< parent-seq child-seq gc-seq)`.
- Contradictory prose corrected at every site a two-axis census found (the
  MountedComponent field comment, the `unmount-thunk` docstring, the inline
  cascade comment, the public `unmount!` docstring, README "Render bodies and
  recursive children", README "no real reconciliation" class-3 invariant list).
  README gains a *Teardown order* section stating the invariant and its React
  provenance.

FORCED TEARDOWN DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED, per the bead's own fence.
`force-teardown-descendants!` keeps its grandchildren-first drain and
`force-teardown-record!` is unchanged; the failed-initial-mount rollback and
failed-update paths are unchanged. What DID change there is one false claim: the
docstring said that order "mirror[ed] React's leaf-upward teardown". React has no
analogue of forced teardown and its normal deletion effect is parent-first, so
the docstring now says plainly that the grandchildren-first drain is a
simulator-only order and NOT a parity claim, and gives the real reason (an
ancestor should not be evicted while it still lists a descendant).

FAILING-TEST-FIRST EVIDENCE (both states quoted).
- Pre-fix, assertions inverted, source untouched: `clojure -M:test` in
  implementation/adapters/test-react exits 1 — 2 failures, 35 tests, 157
  assertions. The deep-cascade failure reads `actual: (not (< 12 11 10))`, i.e.
  observed grandchild=10, child=11, parent=12: the leaf-upward order the bead
  described, measured rather than inferred.
- Post-fix: same command exits 0 — 35 tests, 157 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors.
  Same test count both runs, so the same set ran.

LANE. `jvm-adapters-test-react` (the required test.yml job that runs
`clojure -M:test` against this artefact's `:test` alias). This adapter is
local-test-only, carries no Maven coordinate and is deliberately unsmoked, so its
evidence comes from its own unit tests rather than a smoke lane — which is where
the whole of its coverage lives, per the deps.edn header and rf2-6r9j.85.

BLAST RADIUS CHECKED. `git grep` for `adapter.test-react` outside its own tree
returns only the surface classifier, `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, the
late-bind directory and the hicasso migration codemod — none of which depends on
teardown ORDER. This confirms rf2-6r9j.85's "only its own artefact's tests".
close_reason: PR #9361 merged; verified HEAD == origin/main. The test-react simulator now logs componentWillUnmount in React class lifecycle order rather than child-before-parent. Scope was correctly held to what the bead asked: a narrow simulator ordering fix, NOT full React reconciliation/emulation, in a local-test-only fixture that has no Maven coordinate and is deliberately unsmoked. No worker report (fleet starved); close rests on the merged diff and a green rollup at band 87.

title: gate: nothing checks that a shipped skill instruction only references shipped sources
description:
Found while fixing rf2-sfvt (PR #9230).

## The gap

rf2-sfvt was a packaging defect: skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md instructed the agent to cite a spec/Tool-Pair.md row and consult a sibling tool catalogue, neither of which the published package ships. Its npm 'files' allow-list yields exactly seven files (SKILL.md, README.md, LICENSE, package.json, agents/openai.yaml, references/known-frictions.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json). The instruction therefore failed at the point of use, on a consumer machine, with no recovery available to the agent.

No gate caught it, and the closest-named one could not have.

scripts/check_skill_eval_packaging.py sounds directly on point but is narrower than its name: its whole subject is whether a skill's PROSE and its package.json 'files' array contradict each other about whether evals/ ships. It has no notion of an instruction referencing a source the package omits.

scripts/check_doc_slugs.py validates link targets and anchors under skills/, but only for links that RESOLVE IN THE REPO — and in the monorepo working tree the sibling and spec paths do resolve. Repo-resolvable is exactly the wrong test for a packaging defect: the defect is invisible from the tree and only appears in the tarball.

## Possible invariant

For each packaged skill, every source its SHIPPED files name as REQUIRED to perform the skill's work must itself be inside that skill's package (per package.json 'files'), or be explicitly marked conditional/optional in the prose.

The hard part is distinguishing a REQUIRED reference from a conditional or illustrative one; a naive version would fire on every legitimate 'if you have a checkout' branch and on cross-links that are deliberately informational. That may make a general gate more machinery than the class is worth — the design-level rule (pair-retro design L7 'no vendored peer copy'; the standing 'skill guidance must work on any consumer app' rule) may be the better enforcement point. Worth a judgement call before building anything.

## Scope note

Deliberately NOT done under rf2-sfvt: that bead's non-goals exclude a generic evaluation framework, and a repo-wide gate was outside its fence. Filed so the class is recorded rather than actioned by default.
notes:
WORKER FINDING 2026-09-05 (citool-a) — RECOMMEND CLOSE AS WON'T-BUILD. The title's premise no longer holds as stated, and the half that remains open is one the bead already predicted would not be worth mechanising. No gate was written. Nothing under skills/ or either link-checker was touched.

1. THE MECHANICAL HALF IS ALREADY GATED, and was built after this bead was filed. scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py (rf2-deo2zp, hardened by rf2-kgw8z "scope package-ref links by where they resolve, not how they spell" and rf2-pp72 "derive the skill-package scan surface from the files allow-list") enforces: for every packaged skill, every INTRA-package relative link from a shipped doc must resolve to a file the package.json files allow-list ships. It is ARMED in two places -- .github/workflows/test.yml (self-test + --verbose --ci steps) and scripts/test-fast-pr.sh -- so this is not a local-only checker. Measured on tip: --self-test exit 0 over 14 fixtures of which THREE must produce findings and do (bad_unshipped_link, bad_parent_reentry_unshipped, bad_patterns_doc_unshipped_link), and --verbose --ci exit 0 over the live corpus. It discriminates.

2. THE REMAINING HALF IS DELIBERATE, NOT A HOLE. That gate scopes OUT references that resolve OUTSIDE the package, and a self-test fixture named ok_parent_escape_out_of_scope PINS that exclusion -- so it is a recorded design decision rather than an oversight. This bead asks for the excluded half. MEASURED over all 9 packaged skills / 137 shipped markdown docs on tip: 428 markdown LINKS resolve outside their package, every one of them existing in the repo; and 743 path-shaped citations (backticked prose plus link targets) name a repo tree outside the package. A gate over that class fires on the entire corpus. It is the house convention -- these docs deliberately cross-link into the monorepo for a reader browsing GitHub -- not a defect population.

3. THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE IS PROSE, WHICH IS WHY NO MECHANICAL RULE SEPARATES THEM, and the rf2-sfvt fix itself demonstrates it. PR #9230 did NOT remove the spec/Tool-Pair.md citation from skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md; the citation is still there. What it added was a DECLARATION: "This package ships no tool catalogue and no copy of spec/Tool-Pair.md, so on the ordinary standalone path neither is in front of you", plus an authority ordering for what to cite instead. The reference is unchanged; its REQUIRED-ness is what moved. Also note the citations are backticked prose, not markdown links, so no link gate could ever have seen them.

4. THE DESIGN-LEVEL RULE THIS BEAD NOMINATES AS "the better enforcement point" IS ALREADY LIVE AND OBSERVED. skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md carries it three times unprompted: "The links are supporting references, not required reads" (SS Routing), "an optional supporting reference, not shipped in the package -- this filter decides without it", and "Not loaded during normal operation and not shipped in the package; reach it from a monorepo clone". The package-refs gate even has a marker fixture for it (ok_monorepo_only_marker / ok_parent_reentry_marked). So the invariant is enforced where the bead guessed it should be.

CONCLUSION. Per the project stance (pre-alpha, no over-engineering or gold plating, trust the programmer), building a gate that fires 428 times and cannot tell a required read from an optional one -- or maintaining a 428-entry allow-list to silence it -- costs more than the class it guards. The bead's own scope note anticipated this: "a naive version would fire on every legitimate 'if you have a checkout' branch... That may make a general gate more machinery than the class is worth... Worth a judgement call before building anything." This is that judgement call, made against measurement.

IF A CHEAPER SHAPE IS EVER WANTED, the one seam that would not need judgement is inverting the marker: require every packaged skill that cites an out-of-package tree to carry SOME not-shipped declaration in its own prose, checked once per package rather than once per citation. Nine packages, not 428 links. Not built here -- it is still a new gate over a class with no live defects, and it would need a maintainer ruling on the marker's exact spelling first.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS WON'T-BUILD — the premise does not hold, and the verification is the deliverable. NO gate was built and NEITHER link-checker was edited. Shipped alongside PR #9266 as a finding recorded on the bead.

THE GATE LARGELY EXISTS ALREADY. scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py (rf2-deo2zp, hardened by rf2-kgw8z and rf2-pp72) is armed in test.yml AND in the fast-PR spine, and it discriminates: 14 fixtures, 3 of which must fire and do.

THE HALF THIS BEAD ASKS FOR IS A DELIBERATE EXCLUSION, not an oversight — pinned by a fixture literally named ok_parent_escape_out_of_scope. And the cost of removing it was measured rather than estimated: across 9 packages and 137 shipped docs there are 428 escaping markdown links (all resolving in-repo) and 743 path-shaped citations, so a gate there fires on essentially the whole corpus. That is not a ratchet, it is a wall.

THE MOTIVATING DEFECT WAS A DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM THE ONE THE BEAD MODELS. rf2-sfvt was backticked PROSE, not a link, and PR #9230 fixed it by ADDING a declaration ('this package ships no copy of spec/Tool-Pair.md') while LEAVING THE CITATION IN PLACE. So the required-versus-optional distinction lives in prose, which no link gate can grade, and the design-level rule the bead nominates is already observed in practice — three unprompted instances in the improver's own SKILL.md.

WEIGHED AGAINST THE STANCE AND REFUSED ON IT: building a gate whose true-positive rate is near zero and whose alarm covers the whole corpus is the over-engineering the posture rejects, and 'don't litigate the minutiae' is what lets this bead die with its reasoning recorded rather than consuming a worker. If the underlying worry resurfaces, the live question is whether a package DECLARATION is missing — not whether a citation escapes.

title: CLAUDE.md: the framework-testbed spec.cjs sentence describes the pre-migration world

That one is done; this bead is only about CLAUDE.md.

CONSTRAINT: CLAUDE.md is checked in, so this needs a PR like any other change. It is NOT hot-zone but it IS the file every agent reads first, so the diff should be minimal and the former wording preserved per the spec/012-Routing.md amendment convention.

title: resources: rule invalid-params recovery — :fix-registration vs :fix-params
description:

A FIFTH is planner-reachable and carries the same token: `:rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered`.

TRACED AT SOURCE (each hop read, not inferred):
  resources/route.cljc:722  materialize-occurrences calls resolve-entry-scope (inside the planner try/catch at route.cljc:1117-1132 and the prefetch twin at 1518-1530)
  resources/route.cljc:507  resolve-entry-scope
  resources/route.cljc:531  -> scope-registry/resolve-from-db-reference, where = 'rf.resource/route-entry
  resources/scope_registry.cljc:616  resolve-from-db-reference
  resources/scope_registry.cljc:629  -> require-scope-resolver!
  resources/scope_registry.cljc:429  require-scope-resolver! throws :rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered
  resources/scope_registry.cljc:157  ...via a private registration-error helper hardcoding {:recovery :fix-registration}

scope_registry.cljc:681 already documents this arm in prose ('...:rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered (via resolve-from-db-reference)'), so the omission is in the 009 row rather than in the runtime.

FENCE NOTE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md is hot-zone and was changed by PR #9145 on 2026-09-04; sequence this rather than parallelising it.

SCOPE, on the stance: correct the count and add the fifth id to the Trigger column's registry-rejection list. Do NOT add :recovery to any *Tags schema — rf2-v1sg5 struck it from all six that had it and a re-declaration now REDS the conformance gate (measured; see rf2-c2q3).

SECONDARY, worth a ruling rather than a silent fix: resources/registry.cljc:701 builds :rf.error/resource-invalid-params through the same registration-error helper, so a params-SCHEMA conformance failure surfaces with :recovery :fix-registration and tells the author to fix their registration. plan-error's own default for that case (resources/route.cljc:983) is :fix-params. notes: AUDIT PR #9158 (2026-09-04): PRIMARY FIVE-REJECTION DOC FIX VERIFIED and remains done. REOPENED only for the explicit SECONDARY that this bead and the PR both say was left for a ruling, because closing the only owner loses that decision. Source at merge fa3d28e5aabb291de36a0b791abe072fd5979f43 confirms registry.cljc:701 wraps a use-time :params-schema conformance failure in registration-error => :fix-registration; route.cljc:983 otherwise defaults plan failures to :fix-params but preserves the nested token; 009:2042 tells the caller to correct params while labelling recovery :fix-registration. close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: the .beads checkout/checkpoint race, thirteenth instance today. Payload verified in the WORKING TREE at HEAD==origin/main, with a control that fired (4 hits for 'resource-route-plan'): spec/009-Instrumentation.md now carries 'all five' once, names :rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered twice, and the old 'all four registry rejections' phrasing returns ZERO.

THE PREMISE HELD, and the worker improved on my brief in a way worth recording. I told it to change 'all four' to five and name the fifth. THAT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A FALSE SENTENCE: the existing clause attributes the four to require-resource-spec! — 'that registry's own fail-closed rejections' — while the fifth comes from a DIFFERENT registry, scope-registry. Appending the bare id would have mis-attributed it. The worker named the scope registry explicitly in one clause instead; still 1 insertion / 1 deletion.

That is the same failure family as my rf2-c2q3 brief earlier the same day: A COUNT IS SCOPED BY ITS SENTENCE'S SUBJECT, and adding to the count without re-reading the subject makes the sentence false. Two instances, both caught by workers.

IT RE-DERIVED THE CHAIN RATHER THAN TRUSTING MY LINE NUMBERS, three of which were wrong: route.cljc:722 -> :507/:531 -> scope_registry.cljc:614 -> :429 (require-scope-resolver! throws) -> :149 (registration-error hardcodes {:recovery :fix-registration}). title: hic docs: chapter 15's ht/intents example compares the whole intent stream, which a route-link's navigate head (carrying a frame id) breaks
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation, and it is evidence about the surface rather than a ratified design -
a pilot proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own
rule. The log is at ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-linearlite.friction-log.md
(local-only) and in the pilot workspace.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F10 · outcome 1 · `inferred` · `tooling`

**Trying to** Assert on the intents a Hicasso view carries, using `ht/intents`
the way chapter 15's L2 example does: `(is (= [[:todo/toggle 7]] (ht/intents
tree)))` — an exact equality over the whole intent stream.

**Expected** A stream of application intents.

**Instead** Any tree containing an `h/route-link` also carries routing's own
click decision, and that decision embeds **the frame id**:

```clojure
[:re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate
 {:frame :re-frame.hicasso.test/probe-1
  :payload [:rf.route/url-requested {:url "/issues/srv-1" …}] …}]
```

Under `ht/tree` that frame id is a per-probe counter. My two probe tests
produced `probe-1` and `probe-2` **in deftest order**, so an exact-equality
assertion over an intent stream containing a link is stable only until somebody
adds a test above it. Chapter 07 shows this shape and says "It is not an
authoring spelling", and chapter 15 recommends the exact-equality assertion —
neither warns that the two combine into a positional dependency.

**Looked at** `15-testing.md` §L2 (the `ht/intents` example) and §"Prevent
vacuous tests with a sabotage twin"; `07-routing-and-navigation.md` §"Render an
application route link" (the generated-Hiccup fence); the printed trees from my
own probes.

**Resolved by** Not using `ht/intents` at all on any tree containing a link.
Every link assertion in `views_test.cljs` reads `:href` instead — the router
built it from `:to` + `:params`, which is the fact worth pinning, and it is
stable. Guessed, and I am confident it is right, but nothing told me.

**Bead** Chapter 15's `ht/intents` example is on a tree with no link in it. One
line under it — "a `route-link`'s navigation decision appears in this stream and
carries a frame id; assert its `:href`, or filter the stream, rather than
comparing it whole" — would close it. Alternatively `ht/intents` could omit
navigate heads, or the probe frame id could be constant.
close_reason: PR #9136. Premise HELD, verified at source AND by running. Source: impl/route_link.cljs mints :on-click as [intent/navigate-head {:frame frame-kw :payload payload :native? native? :veto on-click}] -- the ambient frame is embedded in the intent VECTOR; ht/intents collects (vals (:events n)) keeping vectors, so the navigate head IS in the stream. Under ht/tree the frame is (keyword "re-frame.hicasso.test" (str "probe-" (swap! !probe-seq inc))) off a defonce atom, so it is a global monotonic counter across the run -- exactly the positional dependency the pilot measured. Run: re-frame.hicasso.route-link-cljs-test, 17 tests / 40 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0; its 'the-click-decision-is-readable-off-the-tree' reads {:keys [frame payload native? veto]} off (second on-click) and its 'two-renders-of-one-link-are-equal-data' pins :href as '/profile/jane', routing's own synthesis -- which is why the chapter now recommends asserting :href for the link. Chapter 15 keeps the whole-stream equality in the todo example (that tree has no link) and adds a subsection giving the membership form (contains? (set (ht/intents tree)) ...) and the filtered-stream form for when order is the claim, plus a troubleshooting row. NOT actioned: the pilot's alternatives (ht/intents omitting navigate heads, or a constant probe frame id) are framework changes outside a docs bead -- file separately if wanted.

title: Name Hicasso tool projection joins by evidence role
description:
## Evidence
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/tool.cljs` performs privacy projection, grouping, joining, and cross-frame attribution in a single pipeline, but complex transforms use locals such as `n`, `m`, `e`, `bkey`, `fs`, `fid`, `sid`, `r`, and `k`.
- These scopes distinguish raw subscription keys from projected boundary keys, read-set entries from registrations, and frame ids from sub ids. The surrounding evidence contract makes those distinctions correctness-critical.
- The four public reader names and emitted schema keys were previously settled by the Hicasso naming ledger and are consumers' stable surface; they remain unchanged.

## Actionable insight
Rename private/local projection roles to explicit names such as `view-name`, `views-by-read-set`, `projected-boundary-key`, `entry`, `frame-id`, `sub-id`, `boundary-row`, and `candidate-key`. Keep the algorithms and public evidence vocabulary unchanged.

## Ambiguity cost
A reader currently has to infer whether `k` is a raw cell key, an exported boundary key, or a `[frame-id sub-id]` join key. Misreading those categories risks bypassing privacy projection or correlating evidence across the wrong frame.

## Risks / migration
Lexical-only change. Do not rename public reader vars, namespaces/files, evidence schema keys, wire values, sentinel strings, or private function vars referenced by tests. Preserve ordering and fail-closed projection behavior exactly.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Multi-stage tool projection/join locals identify the data role they carry.
2. Public reader names and emitted envelope/schema bytes remain unchanged.
3. Tool-focused tests, production-erasure checks as applicable, lint, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented and validated lexical role renames; focused Hicasso compile, kondo, invariants, node syntax, controlled browser, HMR, and diff gates pass.

title: Name SSR Ring streaming writer state and post-shell results explicitly
description:
## Finding

The streaming transport's long writer and handler flows use generic identifiers at precisely the places where stage distinction matters: out/s, rendered, phase, entry/id, tmpl-fn, projected, ph/tags, resp/resp2/err2, resp-map, err-resp, and rendered again after the shell phase. Readers must repeatedly reconstruct whether a value is an output stream, rendered-shell bundle, continuation, projected delta, post-shell accumulator, or projected error response.

## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:119-121: write-chunk! accepts out/s.
- streaming.clj:250-429: run-streaming-writer! carries generic rendered/phase/entry/id/tmpl-fn/projected/ph/tags over about 180 lines and six writer phases.
- streaming.clj:433-578: private response helpers use resp, err-resp, rendered, resp2, and resp-map for different representations.
- streaming.clj:716-795: the handler uses rendered and resp2/err2 across the precommit shell and post-shell flush.
- Phase tags, continuation ids, payload keys, and stream order are protocol/observability contracts documented by Spec 011 and tests. They remain unchanged.
- Phase-1 bead rf2-6r9j.42 owns removal of rendered[:hiccup]; this work must not rename or otherwise churn that deletion target.

## Recommendation

Rename only surviving private parameters/locals to output-stream/chunk, rendered-shell, writer-position, continuation/boundary-id, render-template, projected-delta, writer-phase/failure-tags, response/post-shell-response/post-shell-public-error, ring-response, and projected-error-response. Update private-helper tests that call through vars. Do not rename public functions, map keys, phase keywords, wire markers, or the :hiccup removal target.

## Risks / contracts

title: Make after-timer cancellation race helpers name their protocol
description:
## Locations and evidence

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc:351-475` implements a delicate reserve/announce/claim cancellation protocol with private names `*announcing*`, `announced!`, and `claim-emit-release!`. The dynamic var is specifically a set of attempt tokens; `announced!` completes an announcement-cell CAS; the claim helper claims a cancellation, emits/delegates its cancelled row, and releases resources. At `after-cancel-fx` line 1117, local `snap` is a vector snapshot of timer entries, while `snap` elsewhere in the same file means a machine snapshot. `successor-published?-fn` also binds generic `captured` for a frame incarnation token.

## Ambiguity cost

These names force readers of concurrency-sensitive code to reconstruct which object is announcing/claimed/released and make `snap` mean two incompatible values in one namespace. That raises review risk around a protocol whose ordering comments explicitly say branch order is load-bearing.

## Recommendation

Identifier-only rename: `*announcing*` -> `*announcing-attempt-tokens*`, `announced!` -> `finish-announcement!`, `claim-emit-release!` -> `claim-cancel-and-release!`, `captured` -> `captured-incarnation`, and the non-machine `snap` -> `timer-entry-snapshot`. Update timer source comments and the race-test docstring.

## Compatibility / migration risk

All renamed vars except the local are private; repository search shows only in-file calls plus explanatory test prose. Do not reorder expressions, change CAS operations, alter dynamic binding scope, or change trace/serialized keys. Concurrency behavior must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Test-React runtime: name descendant teardown by its real scope
description:
## Naming finding

`implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:204-237` names a recursive helper `roll-back-speculative-children!`, but that is only one of its two call contexts. It recursively force-tears down every descendant under the supplied mount.

The name was accurate when commit `488bf70df6` introduced it for failed initial-mount rollback. Six hours later commit `bd14ef705e` added `force-teardown-subtree!` for failed updates and reused the helper on an already-committed live root. In that path the descendants explicitly include pre-existing children as well as children speculatively mounted by the failed attempt (`:225-226`), so "roll back speculative children" understates both the operation (forced teardown) and population (all descendants).

## Ambiguity cost

This is teardown code whose correctness depends on draining pre-existing and newly-mounted descendants alike. A maintainer following the old name can reasonably narrow the walk to attempt-local children or assume it is unsafe to reuse for adapter disposal/future forced teardown, reintroducing the live-child leak the failed-update path exists to prevent. The surrounding docstring currently has to explain the contradiction.

## Proposed change

Rename the private helper to `force-teardown-descendants!`, update its recursive call, both callers, and source commentary. Keep `force-teardown-record!` for one record and `force-teardown-subtree!` for descendants plus root; the three names then express the actual hierarchy. This is private and has no repo consumer outside the source file.

## Compatibility / exclusions

Do not alter recursion order, lifecycle phases, the `:children` record field, render-error propagation, or public APIs. Do not touch the Phase-1 `log-phase!` extras arm (`rf2-6r9j.83`) or duplicate cache tests (`rf2-6r9j.81`), both already assigned their own removals. All-status searches for the old/new terms and Test-React teardown naming found no owning bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- The recursive descendant-only primitive is named `force-teardown-descendants!`; `roll-back-speculative-children!` has no source/test/doc occurrence.
- `force-teardown-subtree!` calls the descendant primitive before tearing down its root, and failed initial mount calls it only for the never-committed parent's descendants.
- Leaf-upward order, clearing/eviction, exactly-one `:forced-teardown` per mounted record, and original-exception propagation are unchanged.
- Focused Test-React JVM and CLJS suites pass, including failed-initial, failed-update, nested-subtree, and sibling-scope cases.
- No Phase-1 removal target is renamed or otherwise changed.
notes: Implemented the private force-teardown-descendants! rename across recursion, failed-initial rollback, failed-update subtree teardown, and commentary. Exact old-name search is empty. JVM: 35 tests/160 assertions, exit 0. CLJS: warning-free node-test compile plus 15 changed-contract tests/95 assertions, exits 0, covering failed-initial, failed-update, nested, sibling, and leaf-upward order. Pinned focused clj-kondo: exit 0.

title: mcp-conformance: prune eight unconsumed private CommonJS exports
description:

title: Remove seven dead helpers and imports from SSR tests
description:
## Finding

The SSR test slice retains two private helpers with no caller and five imports/refers with no symbol use or unique namespace-load role. They are mechanically dead test scaffolding, distinct from the deliberate side-effect/dynamic-resolution requires in the same suite.

## Evidence

A focused `clj-kondo --lint implementation/ssr/src implementation/ssr/test` pass plus exact per-file symbol searches reports:

- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_client_dom_cljs_test.cljs:117-119`: `final-payload-html` is defined but never called. A whole-repository exact-name search finds only this definition. `constants/payload-script-id` remains used by live assertions at lines 220 and 612, so removing the helper does not orphan that require.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_hydration_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:172-173`: `app-db-seed` is defined but never read; the fixture continues to spell the seed inline at lines 99, 225, and 446.
- The same lifecycle test requires `re-frame.frame :as frame` at line 57 but has no `frame/` read; `re-frame.core` already loads `re-frame.frame`.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj:155` requires `re-frame.substrate.adapter :as substrate-adapter` but has no qualified read. The suite initializes through `re-frame.ssr.test-fixture`, and its direct `re-frame.core` dependency already loads the adapter namespace.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_route_slice_projection_test.clj:37` requires `re-frame.core :as rf` but contains no `rf/` form. Its shared test fixture already loads the core facade.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_render_state_jvm_test.clj:20` refers `clojure.test/testing` but contains no `(testing ...)` form.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_streaming_hydration_egress_test.clj:21` requires `re-frame.frame :as frame` but contains no `frame/` read; its direct core dependency already loads the namespace.
- History searches show `final-payload-html` was introduced by `5a0232e9f2` and `app-db-seed` by `80faa4f2c2`; neither name has ever had a recorded caller.

This excludes `re-frame.ssr.head` in the conformance runner and `re-frame.ssr` in the head test: their aliases are statically unused, but requiring the namespaces publishes hooks/registrations used through `resolve` or teardown and is intentional. It also excludes imports/helpers used by only one reader-conditional host.

Duplicate searches for the helper names, "SSR unused test helpers", "unused SSR imports", "ssr conformance substrate adapter", "route slice projection core", "render state testing", and "streaming hydration egress frame" found no owning bead.

## Impact

The residue adds false fixture/dependency signals and seven avoidable linter findings, making real dead-code warnings harder to distinguish from noise. The unused seed constant is especially misleading because three live fixtures bypass it.

## Proposed disposition

Delete `final-payload-html`, `app-db-seed`, the four redundant namespace requires, and the unused `testing` refer. Leave the existing inline seed values and live test behavior unchanged. Preserve side-effect-only and dynamic-resolution requires, even when static lint cannot see their consumption.

## Risks

This must remain a mechanical cleanup: do not rewrite payload fixtures, alter test enrollment, remove hook-publishing namespace loads, or fold platform-specific helpers into this issue. Confirm each removed namespace is still loaded where needed through the existing direct dependency before accepting.
acceptance_criteria:
- The two unused helper definitions and five unused require/refer entries listed in the finding are absent.
- Exact-name/alias searches find no stale reference, and focused clj-kondo output no longer reports those seven locations.
- `re-frame.ssr.head` dynamic-resolution loading, `re-frame.ssr` registration loading, reader-conditional imports, and all live helper definitions remain intact.
- SSR JVM tests plus the Node and browser CLJS test builds still discover and pass the affected namespaces.
- Payload bytes, fixture seed maps, assertions, and runtime setup/teardown behavior are unchanged.

title: http source/tests: remove sixteen proven dead imports and bindings
description:
## Finding

The HTTP source/test slice retains sixteen statically proven dead imports, aliases, referred macros, or local destructurings after excluding reader-conditional and intentional load-time registrations.

## Evidence

A clean `clj-kondo --lint implementation/http/src implementation/http/test --cache false` plus exact-symbol searches identifies:

Production (4 findings):
- `reply.cljc:169`: explicitly destructured `origin-event` and `issuance` locals are unused; `:as ctx` is what `work-id` consumes, so the keys remain available without these local bindings.
- `transport.cljc:1248`: `request-id` is destructured in `maybe-retry!` but never referenced.
- `transport_jvm.cljc:40`: `java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture` is imported but never used or type-hinted in that adapter (the shared `transport.cljc` has its own live import/use).

Tests (12 findings):
- `http_jvm_headers_shape_test.clj:34`: unused `java.util.List` import.
- `http_managed_test.clj:18`: unused `re-frame.http.encoding` alias, plus unused `server` destructurings at lines 402, 426, 455, and 491 (`srv` is retained for teardown and `port` is the only key read).
- `http_privacy_integration_test.clj:20`: unused `re-frame.registrar` alias.
- `http_restore_quiesce_test.clj:28`: unused `re-frame.http.transport` alias; the namespace is already reached through the required `re-frame.http.managed` closure.
- `http_transport_security_test.clj:4,6`: unused `use-fixtures` refer and unused `re-frame.http.privacy` alias; transport already loads privacy.
- `http_url_percent_encoded_redaction_cljs_test.cljc:17-18`: unused `use-fixtures` refer on both CLJ and CLJS branches.

Exact searches find no symbol use in the owning files. History explains several leftovers (for example privacy integration/core registration tests and transport security changed while their old imports remained). Bead title/description searches for these imports and lint findings found no existing HTTP cleanup issue.

The audit deliberately excludes clj-kondo noise that is not dead: opposite-host adapter requires and `ctx`/`abort-signal` are reader-conditional; explicit `re-frame.http.managed` test requires trigger effect/hook registration; `with-new-frame [f ...]` establishes dynamic frame scope even where the local symbol is unread; test interleave and registry snapshots are documented diagnostics.

## Impact

These remnants imply dependencies/dataflow that do not exist and keep the HTTP lint baseline noisy, making a newly introduced unused binding easier to miss. The four stale server locals and duplicate imports also obscure what each test actually controls.

## Proposed disposition

Remove only the listed unused imports/requires/refers and narrow the listed destructuring forms. Do not mechanically delete load-bearing side-effect requires or cross-host bindings.

## Risks / retained contracts

title: Retire React 18 act fallbacks below the React 19 adapter floor
description:
## Scope

Retire the pre-React-19 act-resolution compatibility path discovered in the UIx adapter audit, across the one shared runtime and every live test harness that copied it. Preserve the public flush-views! entry points and their React-19 test behavior. This includes:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs (the resolver used by UIx, Hicasso, and stock Reagent's adapter-level flush);
- implementation/adapters/uix/src plus its five DOM harness copies;
- the three stock-Reagent DOM harness copies;
- the shared React-adapter suite, SSR hydration harness, two machines-viz harnesses, and Story harness;
- the stale reagent-slim resolver commentary and its inert (or (.-act react) nil) shape.

Root rendering, flush-render!, scheduler ordering, and support for React 18 applications are not being redesigned here.

## Vestigial finding

The repository now has an explicit React-19 floor, but the shared spine still probes react-dom/test-utils as a React-18 fallback, the UIx public helper promises both React 18 and 19, and fourteen live source/test files require react-dom/test-utils. That fallback predates the current floor and no longer provides a valid path on any supported build.

## Evidence and reachability proof

- docs/core/25-from-re-frame-v1.md:49 says every re-frame2 adapter targets React 19 and React 17/18 applications must bump.
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md:7-11 repeats that React-19 floor and specifically says UIx hits it.
- spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:286-290 and :1336-1338 define adapter flush-views! as a dev/test boundary around direct React 19 act.
- implementation/package.json:19-20 pins react and react-dom 19.2.0. tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:191 pins generated consumers to 19.2.0, with a lockstep test against package.json.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1717-1744 still documents users on React 18.x, probes React.act, then requires react-dom/test-utils. UIx repeats the React-18 promise at implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:173-181.
- The exact require appears in fourteen files: core spine; core react_shared_suite; five UIx DOM tests; three stock-Reagent DOM tests; one SSR DOM test; two machines-viz DOM tests; and one Story DOM test. Repository-wide rg found no other live require sites.
- Runtime proof against the installed lock: with the React 19.2 development build, typeof React.act is "function", so the fallback is unreachable. With NODE_ENV=production, typeof React.act is "undefined"; react-dom/test-utils exports a function, but implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-test-utils.production.js:14-22 shows it is only a deprecated forwarding wrapper. Invoking it prints the deprecation and throws TypeError: React.act is not a function. It therefore cannot rescue the supported production build either.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs:73-113 already says this artifact is React-19-only and probes only React.act, but still claims implementation tests use React 18.3, claims the shared fallback remains load-bearing, and spells the resolver as (or (.-act react) nil). implementation/package.json disproves the test-tree claim.
- git blame attributes the shared fallback to e0a659445d (2026-05-14), before the current dependency floor and template pin.

## Impact

The branch and its copies preserve a support promise the product explicitly rejects, add deprecated module edges to browser test bundles, and obscure the actual contract. In React 19 development they are dead. In React 19 production the apparent rescue is worse than a no-op: the deprecated wrapper calls a missing React.act and throws. The copied compatibility prose also makes future audits and dependency changes reason from an obsolete React-18 test matrix.

## Recommended disposition

Use React.act as the sole supported dev/test implementation. In shared code, retain the current unavailable-act no-op only where production elision/node safety requires it, but remove the react-dom/test-utils require. Simplify local test helpers to React.act, remove stale React-18 compatibility prose, and simplify reagent-slim's resolver to its one real expression. Do not rename or remove any public flush-views! function and do not change its nil return contract.

## Risks

Some downstream project may have relied on the undocumented implementation detail that this helper happened to work on React 18, despite the explicit React-19 migration gate. That unsupported compatibility is the only behavior removed. React's production bundle intentionally omits act, so the shared helper must keep its documented safe behavior there rather than unconditionally calling an absent export.
acceptance_criteria:
- No live source or test file requires react-dom/test-utils; a repository-wide exact search for js/require "react-dom/test-utils" returns zero.
- Current comments and docstrings no longer claim React-18 compatibility or an React-18.3 implementation test tree for the adapter test-flush path.
- UIx, Hicasso, stock Reagent, reagent-slim, SSR, machines-viz, and Story test helpers obtain act from React on the supported React-19 development/test build.
- Shared flush-views! keeps both arities and returns nil. On a supported development build its callback runs inside React.act; when act is absent in the production React bundle, the intended safe/no-op behavior remains and no deprecated forwarding wrapper is invoked.
- Simplify reagent2.dom.client/resolve-act to the single React-19 lookup and replace its obsolete asymmetry commentary with the current contract.
- Add or retain a non-vacuous focused proof that spies on React.act and observes the callback pass through it; removing/bypassing that call makes the proof fail.
- The existing UIx, Reagent, reagent-slim, shared React-adapter, SSR hydration, machines-viz DOM, and Story DOM suites remain green.
- Do not change public flush-views! names, arities, nil return value, flush-render!, root APIs, or scheduler ordering.

title: tools/xray(popout): a hard reload of the opener leaves the pop-out silently stale — no re-bootstrap, and opener-gone? does not fire
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 02:57 AUSEST by the xray-b worker while disposing rf2-9vm0. Filed rather than fixed: rf2-9vm0 was a spec-drift item and its mayor ruling explicitly says a real bug behind the drift is to be filed, not papered over with a normative-future marker.

THE SPEC SENTENCE. tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md, §Pop-out, last constraint bullet:

  'The pop-out can't survive a hard reload of the opener - atoms get
   garbage-collected. Pop-out re-bootstraps on opener reload by
   re-reading window.opener.xrayRuntime.'

Nothing sets or reads window.opener.xrayRuntime. Census at tip over tools/xray/src: 0 hits line-oriented AND 0 whitespace-collapsed, against an 'opener' control returning 79 and a 'popout' control returning 165. (The one near-miss, make-xray-runtime-fixture in test_support.cljs, is an unrelated test fixture.) That half is spec drift and rf2-9vm0 marks the HANDLE normative-future.

WHAT IS NOT DRIFT, AND IS WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS. The sentence also promises a RECOVERY BEHAVIOUR, and no other mechanism supplies it:

1. There is no re-bootstrap on opener reload. Nothing re-resolves the opener's runtime after a reload.
2. The opener-gone overlay does NOT cover this case. mount.cljs opener-gone? is
     (or (nil? opener) (.-closed opener))
   A SAME-ORIGIN HARD RELOAD of the opener leaves window.opener live (non-nil) and .closed false, so the 500ms watchdog never observes 'opener gone' and never reveals #rf-xray-popout-opener-gone-overlay. The overlay was built for the CLOSED / reference-nulled cases (rf2-h3ekl) and its own design comment names exactly those.

NET OBSERVABLE. After the user hard-reloads the app in the opener window, the pop-out keeps rendering against the PREVIOUS JS realm's atoms. Panels freeze on the old session's data with no UI signal of the cause - which is precisely the failure the rf2-h3ekl overlay was introduced to abolish, reached by a route the overlay's predicate does not detect. Worse than the closed-opener case it was modelled on, because a frozen-but-plausible panel invites the operator to trust stale values.

NOT REPRODUCED IN A BROWSER. This is read from source (mount.cljs popout!, opener-gone?, start-opener-gone-watchdog!, install-opener-gone-overlay!) plus the DOM semantics of window.opener across a same-origin reload. A browser reproduction should be the first step.

DISPOSITION IS OPEN and deliberately not pre-empted. At least three shapes: (a) widen opener-gone? to detect realm replacement (e.g. stamp a per-realm token on the opener and compare) and show the existing overlay - cheapest, honest, no new surface; (b) implement an actual re-bootstrap, which is what the spec sentence promises and what the window.opener.xrayRuntime handle was for; (c) rule the reload case out of scope pre-alpha and correct 011 to say the pop-out must be reopened by hand. Under the project stance (a) looks like the proportionate answer and (b) like the gold-plated one, but that is a call rather than a finding.

The 011 marker landed by rf2-9vm0 cites this bead so the spec does not claim a recovery that does not happen.
notes:
FIXED by PR #9056, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9056, branch worker/xrayleak-a.

BOTH SOURCE READINGS VERIFIED AT TIP. (1) No re-bootstrap: xrayRuntime census over tools/xray/src returns 0 line-oriented AND 0 whitespace-collapsed, against controls opener=79, popout=165, .-opener=1 flattened — matching the bead. (2) opener-gone? is verbatim (or (nil? opener) (.-closed opener)) inside a defensive try; a same-origin hard reload leaves window.opener non-nil (a WindowProxy survives navigation, now fronting the NEW realm) and .closed false, so the predicate reads 'opener fine' and the watchdog never reveals the overlay.

A THIRD READING, WHICH CHANGES THE DISPOSITION AND IS THE MAIN FINDING HERE. Shape (a) — widen opener-gone? and reveal the existing overlay — CANNOT WORK, because the watchdog does not survive the event it would be asked to detect. Everything Xray runs for the pop-out lives in the OPENER's JS realm: popout! is called from there, substrate-adapter/render paints the pop-out's DOM from there, popout-state is an opener-realm atom, and start-opener-gone-watchdog!'s js/setInterval registers its timer on the OPENER's window. A hard reload discards that realm and every timer, closure and atom it owned, so after the reload there is no tick left to evaluate any predicate however widened. Detecting it after the fact would require Xray code running in the POP-OUT's own realm, which today runs none (the pop-out document is opened blank and rendered into from the opener) — i.e. injecting a script element, real new surface. So the bead's menu of (a) cheap / (b) gold-plated was not the real choice.

WHAT SHIPPED — a fourth shape the bead did not enumerate, and the cheapest honest one: THE OPENER ANNOUNCES ITS OWN DEATH ON THE WAY OUT. At pagehide the opener's realm is still alive and still holds the direct DOM handle to the pop-out's overlay node (same-origin, no serialisation layer — the pop-out's whole posture), so revealing the overlay is the EXISTING show-opener-gone-overlay!, reached from a different edge. The mutation lands in the pop-out's document, which is not reloaded, so it persists after the opener realm is gone. This delivers what (a) wanted — reuse the built machinery, tell the truth, no new surface — and unlike (a) it works. pagehide also fires on navigation and close, so it backstops the cases the watchdog already covers; the watchdog stays for the closed / reference-nulled cases.

TWO DELIBERATE CONSTRAINTS, both load-bearing. pagehide ONLY, never unload/beforeunload: this listener goes on the DEVELOPER'S OWN APPLICATION WINDOW, and an unload handler makes a page ineligible for the back/forward cache in every major browser — a devtool must not degrade the navigation behaviour of the app it inspects in order to report on itself. And a persisted pagehide is IGNORED: that is a bfcache freeze a back-navigation can resume, bringing the opener realm and the pop-out's render tree back alive, so announcing there would cry wolf. Plus a window-identity guard mirroring register-popout-unload-cleanup!, and detachment in teardown-popout-state! so repeated open/close cycles in one opener realm do not accumulate handlers.

OVERLAY COPY CORRECTED. It said 'The host application window has been closed', which is FALSE for a reload — the window is still on screen, and a message contradicting what the user can see reads as a bug in Xray rather than an explanation. Now: 'was closed or reloaded ... close this window and open a fresh pop-out'. The copy was pinned by neither the spec nor any test.

TESTS: five new arms in mount_cljs_test.cljs pinning the premise (opener-gone? reads false across a reload), the reveal, the persisted guard, the identity guard, and teardown detachment. Proved to bite: renaming 'pagehide' to 'unload' in mount.cljs turned npm run test:cljs RED (captured exit 1, 3 failures naming the new tests) — a RENAME, not a move, so a substring-matching assertion would not have caught it; restore verified by blob-hash equality (f873ede26f).

011 NOW DESCRIBES WHAT SHIPS. tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md §Pop-out: the constraint bullet states the pop-out does not re-bootstrap and announces instead, names register-opener-reload-announcer!, and records the pagehide-only / bfcache reasoning; the status note records why widening the predicate was not the answer. THE rf2-9vm0 NORMATIVE-FUTURE MARKER ON THE window.opener.xrayRuntime HANDLE IS UNTOUCHED AND KEEPS ITS REFERENT — the handle sentence was deliberately left in the bullet rather than deleted, so that settled ruling is not orphaned. No heading was changed (headings are anchors).

GATES: as recorded on rf2-ws60 — all foreground, unfiltered, exit codes captured, re-run on the final rebased base. npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11203 tests / 55820 assertions) is the lane that covers mount.cljs; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 covers 011 and was proved to bite on a planted broken anchor (exit 1 naming file, line 427 and the anchor; restore blob-hash verified 0d97fa813a).
close_reason: Fixed by PR #9056. Both readings verified, plus a third that changed the disposition: widening opener-gone? could not work because the reload destroys the watchdog's timer (it lives in the opener's realm). Shipped the cheaper honest shape instead — the opener reveals the existing overlay at pagehide while it still holds the pop-out's DOM handle; pagehide-only to protect the host app's bfcache, persisted-pagehide ignored, identity-guarded, detached on teardown. Overlay copy corrected for the reload case. 011 now describes what ships; the rf2-9vm0 marker is untouched.

title: spec+EP: three more carriers still claim resolve-resource-scope emits :rf.resource/scope-resolved (rf2-rlrd remainder)
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-rlrd worker (cluster code-a). rf2-rlrd named TWO carriers and asked the worker to "assume there may be a third". There are THREE more, in FOUR sites, all OUTSIDE that worker fence (spec/** was held by a live worker; docs/EP/** was not in the fence either), so they are filed rather than fixed.

THE FALSE CLAIM. rf/resolve-resource-scope is a PURE read: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:587 has body (resolve-scope*-pure scope-id spec db (quote rf/resolve-resource-scope)), and resolve-scope*-pure (:530) is "PURE ... WITHOUT emitting any observability state (rf2-ru73k6 F3)". Its sibling resolve-scope* (:550) is the TRACED wrapper for CAUSAL boundaries (resource events, route entry, mutation settle) and is the only thing that emits :rf.resource/scope-resolved. FALSE. Note spec/016-Resources.md and spec/API.md are BOTH already correct, so Ownership.md contradicts its own siblings.

A JUDGMENT CALL FOR THE MAYOR, not a defect: EP-0016 is "Status: final" and its own header says "This EP is now the rationale record; where it and the spec differ, the spec governs." So its two sites are a design-time statement that the implementation later deliberately departed from (rf2-ru73k6 F3). Correcting a final EP in place may be the wrong move — a dated correction note, or leaving it entirely, may be right. The two spec/** sites carry no such caveat and are plainly stale.

CENSUS INSTRUMENT AND ITS CONTROL, so this is reproducible. Line-oriented git grep for the token scope-resolved gives 30 candidate files (excluding .beads/); narrowing to files that ALSO mention resolve-resource-scope gives 15. The claim itself is LINE-BROKEN in most carriers ("like every\n  resolution site it emits"), so a line-oriented search for the sentence finds nothing — flatten first: tr \n " " | tr -s " " then grep for "not a pure data helper" / "like every resolution site it emits". title: re-frame.hicasso.server/render is blind to sub exceptions on a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host: cold reads go through compute-sub, whose :rf.error/sub-exception is stamped :frame nil
notes:
CARRIED FORWARD FROM SLICE E (rf2-8arzr.5, now closed) BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. Filed so a measured finding does not die with the bead that found it.

THE FINDING, as slice E measured it: the per-frame `pending-error-trace?` buffer reads CLEAN on exactly the failure it was named for. Hicasso s cold reads go through pure `compute-sub`, and `compute-sub` s `:rf.error/sub-exception` is stamped `:frame nil` BY CONSTRUCTION -- it is a pure fn with no frame in scope to stamp. `re-frame.ssr.error-listener` buckets by frame address (`pending-error-traces` swap at error_listener.cljc:178, keyed by `frame/frame-address`), so a `:frame nil` record is not in any frame s bucket and a per-frame peek finds nothing.

WHAT SLICE E DID ABOUT IT: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (the new body-only entry, implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:331) watches the ALWAYS-ON error-emit stream instead of the per-frame buffer, so the new crossing path is not affected. That was the right local fix and it shipped.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` (server.cljs:145), the DOCUMENT door used by a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host, has the same blindness today and was not changed. A sub that throws during a Hicasso server render can therefore go unreported on that path.

NOT A DOCS PROBLEM -- CHECKED. Slice F was asked to verify whether any doc describes the blind instrument as though it worked, and none does. docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md s error content is declaration/boot errors (`:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy`, `:rf.error/hicasso-bad-host-declaration`, `:rf.error/ssr-missing-payload-policy`) and the `window is not defined` Render-assertion case; it makes no claim about sub-exception detection during a server render. spec/009:2125 s `pending-error-trace peek` sentence is about `:rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed`, a DIFFERENT path (error-view rendering under the Ring host) that IS frame-stamped and does work. So nothing needed correcting in prose, and slice F corrected nothing here.

SIZING NOTE for whoever takes it: the likely fix is the one slice E already made one file over -- move `render` s detection to the always-on error-emit stream the way `render-body` does -- so this is probably small and has a worked precedent in the same namespace. Worth confirming that `:frame nil` is the only leak before changing anything: `error_listener.cljc:85-100` carries a long comment about a related skip whose reasoning is adjacent and worth reading first.
MAYOR NOTE, 2026-09-03 00:3x AUSEST — THIS AND rf2-ypom ARE ONE DEFECT, REACHED FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, AND THEY ARE DISPATCHED TOGETHER. rf2-ct24 was carried forward from slice E; rf2-ypom was filed by the PR #8997 audit. Both name re-frame.hicasso.server/render (server.cljs:145) as blind to recovered sub errors, and both prescribe the same fix: give it the verdict render-body already has. Verified at source at 76ffd860b4 — render is at :145, render-body at :331, and the :errors listener is registered at :323 and unregistered at :413, entirely inside render-body's extent. render has no corresponding registration.

NEITHER IS CLOSED AS A DUPLICATE, because each carries measured evidence the other does not: rf2-ct24 has slice E's mechanism (compute-sub stamps :frame nil BY CONSTRUCTION, being a pure fn with no frame in scope, so error_listener.cljc's per-frame bucketing at ~:178 can never see it) plus the instruction to read error_listener.cljc:85-100 first; rf2-ypom has the acceptance criteria (a throwing sub through server/render must get :rf.error/ssr-render-failed, a non-throwing control must return the existing shape unchanged, and the listener and request frame must be released on success, on refusal, and on a direct render throw). One PR closes both with a cross-reference each way.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9035 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9035), the same PR that closes rf2-ypom — SAME DEFECT reached from two directions, cross-referenced both ways. This bead carried slice E's measured mechanism and the instruction to read error_listener.cljc:85-100 first; rf2-ypom carried the acceptance criteria. One fix, one PR.

THE FIX: re-frame.hicasso.server/render now watches the always-on :errors stream for its render extent and raises :rf.error/ssr-render-failed on any recovered record — the fix this bead's sizing note predicted, the one slice E had already made one file over. The doors share the lifecycle helpers but register under DIFFERENT ids (::render-recovered-error / ::render-body-recovered-error), because the shipped single id's justification rested on the sidecar isolate's one-render-at-a-time guarantee, which is render-body's premise and not render's.

THE BEAD'S QUESTION ANSWERED: ':frame nil is the only leak' — NO, and error_listener.cljc:85-100 is exactly where the adjacent reasoning starts. Those lines are the :rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed paragraph, the second member of non-projection-eligible-errors: a record that is well-formed AND frame-stamped and still never reaches the buffer, skipped so a re-buffered trace cannot flip a 4xx to a 5xx under a custom projector plus a future re-flush. Reading error-emit-projection-listener out, it buffers only when ALL THREE hold: (1) the category is outside that skip set; (2) (:frame record) is non-nil — the leak this bead names, which compute-sub produces by construction; (3) (error-projector/server-frame? frame-id), i.e. the frame's :platform is :server.

CONDITION 3 IS A SECOND LEAK ON THIS DOOR SPECIFICALLY, and it is the finding worth more than the fix: render does NOT set :platform :server on its per-request frame — only render-body does — so on render the buffer could not fill even for a correctly frame-stamped record. Leaks 2 and 3 each independently suffice. NOT repaired here: giving render a :platform would change client-only-fx gating for every existing caller, well outside a bounded correctness fix. Flagged for whoever wants it.

The fix is unaffected and better justified than argued: the always-on stream sits upstream of all three conditions. refuse-recovered-render-error!'s docstring previously asserted the false premise this bug is made of — that a JVM host is survivable because the same process holds the record — and now states the three measured conditions instead.

WITNESS: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_recovered_error_ssr_cljs_test.cljs (refusal, non-throwing control, release of frame AND listener on all three exits, and the two doors' ids read from INSIDE each render). One existing row changed — see rf2-ypom's close reason for the frame_doors_ssr ambient-read row and the deliberate bluntness of the verdict.

GATES on the rebased tree: hicasso node lane 1176 tests / 4386 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0; fast-PR spine captured exit 0.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): errors.md names two reasons nothing emits (:ns-not-loaded, :handler-error) and omits the eval-cljs failure family (:rf.error/eval-cljs-compile-error / -threw / -timeout / -rejected / -disabled)
description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md is the leaf SKILL.md:194 routes to for "Translate a structured `{:ok? false :reason ...}` to plain English; suggest the recovery". Two of the reasons it lists are emitted by nothing, and the failure family an agent hits most often in a pair session is absent from it entirely.

Phantom ids:
- errors.md:9 — "`:ns-not-loaded :missing :re-frame2` → re-frame2 isn't loaded; check the user's deps."
- errors.md:22 — "`:handler-error` inside an epoch → the user's handler threw; surface the `:rf.error/handler-exception` trace event ..."

Missing family — `eval-cljs` is the workhorse (SKILL.md:206) and its own failures are:
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-compile-error` (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_cljs.cljs:330)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-threw` (grep `:reason` over tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-timeout` (eval_cljs.cljs:190)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-rejected` (eval_cljs.cljs:183 — the nREPL session refused the form)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-disabled` (eval_cljs.cljs:255 — server launched with `--no-eval`)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-mailbox-missing` / `-await-wrap-failed` (eval_cljs.cljs:198,203 — the `await: true` path)

TRUTH AT TIP

`grep -rhoE ':reason :[a-zA-Z0-9./?-]+' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src skills/re-frame2-pair/preload | sort -u` (~100 distinct ids) contains neither `:ns-not-loaded` nor `:handler-error`; a wider `grep -rn ns-not-loaded tools/ implementation/ skills/re-frame2-pair/preload` finds nothing at all. The re-frame2-not-loaded case cannot surface as its own reason: the preload namespace requires re-frame.core, so an app without re-frame2 never installs the marker and `discover-app` reports the ladder's `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` (errors.md:19 already covers it). `:rf.error/handler-exception` (errors.md:22's own body) is the real trace op; `:handler-error` is not a `:reason` any tool returns. Across the whole skill only two of the eval-cljs ids appear anywhere (`-timeout` and `-rejected`, once each, in references/ops.md:83); `-compile-error`, `-threw`, `-disabled` are taught nowhere (`grep -rn 'eval-cljs-(compile-error|threw|disabled)' skills/re-frame2-pair` is empty).

IMPACT

The compile-error case is the one an agent trips on first (a typo in a form, an unresolved alias such as `story/` — stories.md:28 warns there is no alias), and `-disabled` is the one that needs a specific operator action (relaunch without `--no-eval`), yet the "translate the reason" leaf says nothing, so the agent falls back to guessing. The two phantom ids teach reasons the agent will never see, and `:ns-not-loaded` sends it to "check deps" for a condition the ladder already names precisely.

FIX SHAPE

One PR against skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md: (1) delete the `:ns-not-loaded` bullet (line 9) — or fold its recovery into the `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` rung; (2) rewrite line 22 to key on the trace op `:rf.error/handler-exception` rather than a fake `:reason`; (3) add one "`eval-cljs` failures" bullet group naming the five reasons above with the recovery each implies (compile-error → fix the form, fully-qualify the namespace; threw → the form ran and raised, read `:message`; timeout → raise `timeout-ms` or project the result smaller / use `await: true` for a Promise; rejected → session refused, re-run `discover-app`; disabled → operator relaunched with `--no-eval`, use the typed tools). Keep it to ~12 lines; errors.md is 8.9 KB and stays under the leaf ceiling.

GATE

No gate checks errors.md prose against the emitted reason set — verify by hand: every `:reason` id the new text names must appear in `grep -rhoE ':reason :[a-zA-Z0-9./?-]+' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src skills/re-frame2-pair/preload`. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (skills/ is in its roots) for any anchor touched.

title: test(ssr): four more fixtures nest :config so their frames are never platform-tagged
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-umi1w (PR #8934), which fixed the same defect in multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc and deliberately did NOT sweep the rest — a general audit was out of scope there.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): `rf/make-frame` opts are FLAT — `:platform` is a top-level record-config key, per make-frame's own docstring. These four sites pass `{:id fid :config {:platform :client}}`, which nests as `:config {:config {...}}`, so the frames are never platform-tagged at all:

  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc  (lines 89 and 298)
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs  (line 45)
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/multi_root_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs  (line 42)

Line numbers are as measured on 2026-09-01 and should be re-derived at tip.

WHY IT MATTERS: harmless TODAY only because the runtime falls back to the host-wide platform marker — `(or (-> rec :config :platform) (interop/active-platform))` — and that marker is already `:client` on CLJS. So each fixture gets the platform it meant by accident, and no assertion in these files discriminates a tagged frame from an untagged one.

THE FIX, mirroring rf2-umi1w: flatten the opts to `{:id fid :platform :client}`, and add ONE assertion per fixture reading the tag back through `rf/frame-meta`. That accessor is `(merge (:config f) (:lifecycle f) {:id (:id f)})` — it flattens the frame's OWN config and does NOT fall back to the host-wide marker, which is what makes it discriminating. Verified on rf2-umi1w: restoring the nesting turns such an assertion red with `actual: (not (= :client nil))`.

NOTE the two `_dom_cljs_test.cljs` files are browser-gated, not covered by the ssr JVM suite or the consolidated node-test — gate them accordingly.

PRECEDENT: machine_after_rearm_cljs_test.cljc and multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc both now use the flat form and carry a docstring warning about the trap.

SURFACE: test-only, implementation/ssr/test/.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8945 (2026-09-02) — REOPENED FOR THE UNGUARDED FOURTH CALL SITE.

The merged code correctly flattens all four `make-frame` opts maps. The new regression proof, however, reaches only three sites: each `the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged` test calls that file's `fresh-frame!` helper. The fourth corrected site is the direct teardown/rebuild call in `failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc` (`rf/make-frame {:id fid :platform :client}` inside `a-root-whose-seed-does-not-land-releases-its-claim`), which bypasses `fresh-frame!` and has no `frame-meta` assertion.

That gap is discriminating, not hypothetical. Returning only this rebuild to `{:config {:platform :client}}` leaves all three new tests green because they exercise the still-flat helpers. The rebuild test then checks only that hydration lands; the PR's own red-before established that the pre-existing behavioral tests pass when the tag is absent because runtime platform lookup falls back to the host marker. Thus the exact silent defect can recur at one of the four audited sites with the whole suite green, contrary to the close note's claim that one gate covers all four.

Completeness: four sites were fixed but only three are guarded. Correctness: the rebuilt frame can again carry `:platform nil` without a failure. Implementation quality: the repeated prose says the rebuilt frame "must carry" the tag, but the executable contract never reads it.

Minimal outcome: immediately assert the rebuilt frame's `rf/frame-meta` platform at that existing call site (or route both constructions through one equally small checked helper). No broader sweep, new fixture, or abstraction is needed.

Duplicate search: `rf2-33lfn` owns this exact four-site SSR fixture sweep, so it is reopened rather than duplicated.
close_reason:
Second pass (audit reopen of PR #8945). Addressed the UNGUARDED FOURTH CALL SITE: the direct teardown/rebuild (rf/make-frame {:id fid :platform :client}) inside a-root-whose-seed-does-not-land-releases-its-claim in failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc, which bypasses fresh-frame! and so was never reached by the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged. PR #8956 adds ONE assertion there reading the tag through rf/frame-meta (merge of :config/:lifecycle/:id — no fallback to the host-wide platform marker, which is what makes it discriminate).

Code premise re-verified at tip: all four opts maps are already flat; two sweeps (line-oriented AND whitespace-collapsed) over implementation/ssr/test/** found no surviving nested {:config {:platform ...}}. So the merged code was correct and only the proof fell short, exactly as the audit stated.

DISCRIMINATING CONTROL (the point of this bead, since a green run proves nothing here): reverting ONLY the fourth site to {:config {:platform :client}} and recompiling reds exactly one assertion -- the new one -- with 'expected: (= :client (:platform (rf/frame-meta fid))) / actual: (not (= :client nil))', while the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged and the other 14 tests stay GREEN. Test/assertion counts identical to the clean run (15 tests / 125 assertions), so the plant was scoped. That single result proves both that the new assertion bites and that the previous pass's proof did not reach this site.
