title: reg-interceptor registration coords never reach the interceptor-exception trace (Xray chip gap for the supported authoring form)
description: The Xray Epoch INTERCEPTOR (exception) row's jump-to-source chip reads :source-coord off the :rf.error/interceptor-exception trace tag; the router takes it from the interceptor map's :source-coord (interceptor.cljc error-record). reg-interceptor (the ONE supported authoring form, EP-0022) captures registration coords into the REGISTRY meta (interceptor_registry.cljc reg-interceptor* -> source-coords/merge-coords), but descriptor->interceptor lowers {:before/:after} descriptors through ->interceptor* WITHOUT threading those coords onto the built value — so an interceptor authored the supported way never gets the exception-row chip; only a VALUE registered at the migration boundary carrying its own :source-coord does. Until rf2-93sxp the ->interceptor macro was the de-facto route to a coord-carrying value (tests and the standard_epochs testbed used it); with the macro gone (PR #8791) those sites author with reg-interceptor descriptors and the testbed's exception-row chip degrades to plain text (the INTERCEPTORS registry-read step's chip is unaffected — spec 021:426 documents it off handler-meta). Candidate fix: descriptor->interceptor stamps :source-coord from the registration meta's coords (registry resolver, one site), making the chip work for the authoring form everywhere. Touches interceptor_registry.cljc + tests; check spec/009 and tools/xray/spec/021 wording. Named as within rf2-93sxp's non-goals ('no redesign of source-coordinate diagnostics'), hence this follow-up.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8817: resolve-ref threads the reg-interceptor registration meta's coords onto every resolved interceptor value as :source-coord (registration-coords helper; value's own coord wins; programmatic/framework/production paths stay coord-free), so a descriptor-authored interceptor's :rf.error/interceptor-exception trace now carries the registration coord the Xray exception-row chip reads. title: gates: a link gate cannot fail on a file with no links — 20 of 488 tracked doc pages, and the green is indistinguishable from a real pass
description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by the rf2-u9dj1 worker while editing `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md`, and filed SEPARATELY on purpose — that bead's own close reason argues that "a finding cited as support for another finding never gets its own item", and leaving this one inside it would demonstrate the mechanism rather than fix it.

## THE OBSERVABLE

A link gate returns GREEN on a file that contains no links. The gate is working; it simply has nothing to inspect. So nominating `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for an edit to such a file produces a pass that says nothing whatever about the edit, and would say the same on a change that broke the document entirely.

`docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` is the instance that surfaced it: measured at trunk, **0 markdown links and 0 fence markers**, against live controls taken in the same run — `CLAUDE.md` 20 links / 4 fences, `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` 1 link / 6 fences.

## THE CLASS, MEASURED — IT IS NOT ONE FILE

Over every tracked `.md` file under `docs/`, `spec/` and `migration/`:

    tracked .md files                 488
    carrying ZERO markdown links       20   (about 4%)

Among them: `docs/EP/EP-0024-*`, `EP-0026-*`, `EP-0028-*`, `docs/core/fresco/06-lists-and-collections.md`, `docs/core/fresco/08-async-resources.md`, and several under `docs/design/freehand/studio/`. So roughly one tracked doc page in twenty-five is a page where the link gate cannot fail, and two of those are teaching-corpus pages under `docs/core/` that get edited.

## WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY USELESS

It fails in the REASSURING direction for the exact act every dispatch performs: the brief nominates a gate, the worker runs it, it exits 0, and both parties record a green. Nothing on screen distinguishes "the gate checked your change and found it sound" from "the gate found nothing of the kind it checks". **A gate that cannot fail is indistinguishable from a gate that passed.**

And it defeats the project's standing remedy for wrong-gate nomination, which is "nominate by PATH, not by job name". The path IS right here — `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` genuinely is `check_doc_slugs.py`'s surface. What is wrong is the file's CONTENT, which no path rule can see.

## WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND WHY THE FIX MAY BE A GENERALISATION RATHER THAN AN ADDITION

CLAUDE.md already carries the closest thing, scoped to fenced blocks: "for an edit CONFINED to a fenced block — and whole pages qualify — neither gate is the gate: nominating one returns a green that inspected nothing you changed, so check the links by hand and say so."

**That sentence's REASONING already covers this case exactly** — "a green that inspected nothing you changed" is precisely the observable here. What does not carry is its SCOPE: it is written about content the extractor strips, and a reader editing a file with no fences at all has no reason to think it applies. The two cases are mirrors — there the content is invisible to the gate, here there is no content of the kind the gate checks.

**SO THE LIKELY-CORRECT FIX IS TO WIDEN THAT EXISTING SENTENCE, NOT TO ADD A FIFTH WRONG-GATE DOOR BESIDE THE FOUR ALREADY DOCUMENTED** (rf2-8pb5k, rf2-3r2t, rf2-zk50, rf2-sodfq). Something of the shape: before nominating a gate, check the file actually contains what that gate inspects; where it does not, say so and verify by hand. Whoever takes this should read that paragraph first and decide — widening it is cheaper and leaves one rule instead of two, and this bead should NOT be read as asking for a new bullet.

**THIS IS DELIBERATELY P4.** The project stance says not to gold-plate, CLAUDE.md's gate guidance is already long, and a reader who has internalised the fenced-block sentence would reach the right answer unaided. What earns it a filing at all is the measurement: 20 files, and the failure is silent.

## THE MODEL RESPONSE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS WHAT A WORKER SHOULD DO

The rf2-u9dj1 worker did not report the hollow green. It planted THREE faults at a line its own change added, each with the match count read BEFORE the plant so a no-op plant could not fake a pass: a broken link in prose (`check_doc_slugs.py` exit 1 at loops.md:202); the same plant against `mkdocs build --strict` (exit 1, aborted on one warning); and the same link INSIDE a fence (exit 1 on the fenced-doc-link assertion at loops.md:205). That third plant confirmed at source that this tree inverts the usual fence-stripping rule — a claim its brief had asserted rather than demonstrated. **Planting a fault is what converts an empty surface into a live gate**, and it is already the project's standing control; what this bead adds is knowing WHEN the plant is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces.

## NOT ESTABLISHED

  * Whether `check_doc_slugs.py` does anything independent of links on such a file — it validates link targets AND heading anchors, and whether the anchor half inspects headings that no link references was NOT tested. If it does, the green is less empty than stated here and the count of 20 overstates the exposure.
  * Whether the same holds for `check_readme_links.py --ci` on its own roster; only the docs-gate surface was measured.
  * Whether any of the 20 is actually edited often enough for this to have cost anything yet. No history was taken.
notes:
SURFACE FENCE, set 2026-09-17 by the mayor BEFORE dispatch. YOURS: CLAUDE.md ONLY. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md IS HELD by a concurrent worker on rf2-uxh3e and you must not edit it, nor any other file under docs/the-mayor-method/. If you conclude the fix belongs there instead, REPORT THAT AND STOP. Releases: the re-dispatch fence on your completion report; the surface fence only when your PR MERGES.

=== WORKER VERDICT 2026-09-17 (PR #9915, branch worker/vacuousgate-h7k2m) ===

OUTCOME: the widening was written. One sentence-pair added to CLAUDE.md's existing
fenced-block wrong-gate sentence. No new bullet, no fifth door, no new gate, no new
lettered instrument item, none of the 20 files edited, nothing under
docs/the-mayor-method/ touched (rf2-uxh3e's fence respected).

--- THE "NOT ESTABLISHED" #1 QUESTION, SETTLED AT SOURCE AND DEMONSTRATED ---

Question: does check_doc_slugs.py do anything independent of links on a link-free
file — specifically, does the anchor half inspect headings that no link references?
If it does, the count of 20 overstates the exposure.

ANSWER: it DOES inspect rendered ids that no link references — but only where a
MANIFEST reaches, and the manifest reaches NONE of the 20. THE FINDING DOES NOT
SHRINK AND 20 DOES NOT OVERSTATE.

Mechanism, read at source. The per-file loop (check(), the `for path in files:` loop)
is driven entirely by _extract_links(path). Zero links means the loop body never
executes for that file — that is the whole of the corpus-wide inspection. Four checks
run OUTSIDE that loop, and not one rescues a link-free page:

  _check_compat_anchors          HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS: 12 enumerated pages,
                                 37 anchors, all under docs/machines, docs/async,
                                 docs/api, docs/routing. Link-INDEPENDENT, genuinely.
  _check_compat_anchor_placement COMPAT_ANCHOR_PLACEMENT: exactly 1 rule, on
                                 docs/routing/concepts.md.
  _check_source_comment_links    scans tracked CLOJURE source, not markdown.
  _check_fenced_doc_links        needs FENCES; only docs/design/fresco and
                                 docs/the-mayor-method.

OVERLAP between the manifest's 12 pages and the 20 zero-link files: ZERO. So on a
link-free page every mechanism the gate has is inert at once.

The link-independent half is nonetheless REAL, and was demonstrated rather than
asserted: 29 of the manifest's 37 anchors are referenced by no markdown link and no
source comment. Renaming one of those (an explicit anchor id on
docs/machines/concepts.md, confirmed unreferenced) turned the gate RED at exit 1 with
MISSING COMPAT ANCHOR. Restored; default-form blob hash equals the committed blob.

--- THE DEMONSTRATION ON A LINK-FREE PAGE, BOTH WAYS ---

A probe page was created under docs/EP/ carrying zero links and a duplicate heading
slug — the ambiguous-fragment fault the manifest half reds on as DUPLICATE COMPAT

**What the two lines say today** (`tools/xray/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md`, trunk 4520025651; :42 is the first line of a three-line bullet, so :43-44 are shown with it):

42  - **`Xray`** — Latin for "cause." Single word. Picks up the
43    causality theme directly. The headline reads naturally:
44    "Xray shows the cascade your last click triggered."
...

`Xray` is not Latin for anything; *causa* is Latin for "cause". `Latin` occurs exactly twice under `tools/xray/` — these two lines (Grep, control: `x-ray` 2 hits in `tools/xray/spec`).

**Whose rationale it was.** The lock was written for the name **Causa**. Single word. Picks up the causality theme directly. ... "Causa shows the cascade your last click triggered."`, the Pick `**Causa.** Tagline: *the cascade you can see.*`, and the Why bullet `Latin root signals "cause" without saying it three times.` (`git show '731188b1fb^:tools/causa/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md'`, lines 23-62). Every word of today's Lock #1 is that text with the brand token swapped.

**When it went stale, and why nobody saw it.** Commit `731188b1fb`, 2026-05-24 16:29:56 +1000, "refactor(xray): rename Causa -> Xray across the repo (rf2-3pdp9) (#2067)", 792 files. The sweep was lexical by design; it could not see that two sentences' MEANING depended on the token it was swapping. Seven commits have touched the file since (last two are PR #9966's, 2026-09-18) and none touched Lock #1 — PR #9966's own line-number table reads `Lock #1 :42-44 / :57-59 delta 0`.

**The rename bead is not retrievable today.** `bd show rf2-3pdp9` answers `no issue found`, and a select on the identity field over `.beads/issues.jsonl` at HEAD returns nothing (control: `rf2-l3jfw` found, `open`). That sentence predates the rename — it entered at `84fabaa0dd` (2026-05-18) reading "Causa's claim is" — so the x-ray-vision lineage was already the tool's claim when the name was chosen. Whether it MOTIVATED the rename is not recorded anywhere; it is the nearest sourced tie.
- `tools/xray/spec/000-Vision.md:5-8`: "Xray shows you what happens when an event fires. ... the programmer points at one event and Xray unfolds the full cascade behind it" — the bead's "cascade behind a click" phrasing is this sentence.
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:39`: the "x-ray glasses with HUD" promise.
- `tools/xray/README.md:3-4`: "Xray, the re-frame2 devtools panel. The cascade you can see."

**What the PR proposed, verbatim** (PR #9966 body, "Held for Mike"):

- line 42: `` **`Xray`** — the medical imaging metaphor. Single word. Picks up the see-through-to-the-cause theme directly. ``
- line 58: `- The imaging metaphor signals "see the cause" without saying it.`

Two things to know about it. description:
RULED 2026-09-22 (delegated by Mike; the ruling note and the `## IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF` are in this bead's notes). Decision: option C plus `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` — arm `story_static_gate` wherever the existing `is_story_xray_runtime_path` predicate already opens the browser job (one line at `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:2318-2320`), plus a nested case for `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` inside the existing arm at `:1983`; the two npm manifests are declined. The FENCE at the end of this description asked for a ruling before any roster change; that ruling now exists, so its third bullet is DISCHARGED and the bead is dispatchable. The two hot-zone bullets stand. Everything below this line is the original description, unchanged.

---

**The `story_static_gate` surface cannot be armed by a change to Story or Xray SOURCE — only by a change to the two files that implement the gate itself.** So the PR-time gate that would catch a static-export break is, by construction, never scheduled on the changes capable of causing one. The nightly is the system of record, which makes the exposure up to 24 hours plus however long nobody looks.

## VERIFIED AT SOURCE, 2026-09-21 at trunk `16dde76093`

**Exactly TWO sites set `story_static_gate=true`** in `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh`: the `mark_all` branch (line 256), and one case arm (line 1981) whose own comment describes its roster as "two files in one tree" — `implementation/scripts/check-story-static.cjs` and `story-build.cjs`.

**The decisive measurement.** `58bd56635b` is the commit that made release-mode Xray impossible and thereby broke the static export (see rf2-cljo6, rf2-n7lql). Handing the classifier that commit's seven PATHS — never revisions, per CLAUDE.md item (v):

    story_xray_browser=true
    story_full_gate=false
    story_static_gate=false

Control, so a `false` means absence rather than a broken instrument: `implementation/scripts/check-story-static.cjs` alone arms `story_static_gate=true`.

So the regression **did** arm the PR-time browser gate, that gate **ran**, and it **passed** — because the crash lives in the static-export STEP, which executes only when `story_static_gate` arms. Arming the job is not arming the step.

## WHAT THIS REFUTES, AND IT IS THE CLASSIFIER'S OWN RECORDED REASONING

The arm's comment block at `:1966-1967` justifies the narrow roster:

> A break in one already reds a job that runs at PR time, so paying for the static gate on top buys no signal.

## The problem, carefully

**What the README says versus the file beside it.** `examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md` refers to the facade as `h` in 17 places — 14 `h/verb` references on 13 lines (`:34,36,42,68,73,76,77,92,109,123,124,128,137`) plus 3 auto-resolved `::h/value` markers (`:29,30,47`) — and never shows a `(:require …)` form that binds `h` (the only `:require` mentions are prose at `:19,147` and the JVM host's REPL snippet at `:283-284`). The file it describes, `examples/substrates/fresco/login/core.cljs`, binds `[re-frame.fresco :as rf.fresco]` at `:42` and uses that alias 39 times (34 var calls plus 5 `::rf.fresco/…` markers, e.g. `::rf.fresco/value` at `:126`). The README's boot fence is the sharpest instance: `:72-83` writes `(h/client-root)` at `:73` and `(h/render! …)` at `:76` while its own line `:75` writes `(rf/init! rf.fresco.substrate/adapter)` — two dialects in one eight-line block presented as the file's boot. The same `h/defview` / `h/sub` / `::h/value` spelling sits in the catalogue rows `examples/substrates/README.md:32` (2 refs) and `examples/README.md:162` (3 refs). Total: **22 alias references across 3 prose files.** (The bead's headline "19 occurrences" is a raw substring count; the raw count today is 20, of which 3 are the near-miss `:auth/…` — `f13de844d6`'s own commit message flags `:auth/locked` as exactly that — so 17 is the README figure that matters.)

**Why the headline snippet is a reader error, measured.** A 7-case reader probe (`clojure -M` from `implementation/fresco`, throwaway namespace, no re-frame loaded): with only `rf.fresco` bound, `::rf.fresco/value` reads as `:re-frame.fresco/value` and `::h/value` is `Invalid token`; with both bound, `::h/value` reads as the identical keyword (`=` true); the one-colon `:h/value` reads fine but is a DIFFERENT keyword, so "drop a colon" is not a repair; control: an unbound `::zz/value` fails the same way. So a programmer or AI who pastes `{:on-change [:auth.login/edit-field :email ::h/value]}` (README:29) into `core.cljs` gets a reader error, and the runtime is indifferent to which alias is used — the keyword is the same either way.

**Who is affected.** Only a reader crossing from the README (or a catalogue row) into `core.cljs`. The example compiles, the 58-build sweep and the SSR crossing test are unaffected, and examples are test-free by lock (rf2-8cevm). This is a teaching defect, not a behavioural one — the bead says so and I confirm it.

**What the spec already rules, and the bead did not weigh.** `spec/Conventions.md:198-218` §Require-alias dialect (hot-zone file, read-only here):
- `:200` — the canonical alias for a framework namespace `re-frame.<leaf>` is `rf.<leaf>`; `:216` — a bare leaf alias is reserved for application namespaces.

That clause is the bead's option C, already ruled and in the spec. It also dissolves the bead's central fear — "whichever way it goes, one side of the 21/0 split becomes the drift" — because the guide's `h` is per-page consistent and permitted, and a `rf.fresco` README beside a `rf.fresco` file is per-page consistent too. ### A. `rf.fresco` in the example tree — the README and the two catalogue rows follow the code (bead's A, scoped by Conventions :218)
- What changes: 22 references in 3 files — `examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md` (17: `h/…` → `rf.fresco/…`, `::h/value` → `::rf.fresco/value`), `examples/substrates/README.md:32` (2), `examples/README.md:162` (3). - What changes: `core.cljs:42` libspec plus 34 calls and 5 `::rf.fresco/` markers → `h`; README untouched except its `rf.fresco.substrate/adapter` line (which stays canonical, so the mixed fence persists unless `substrate` is also re-aliased — another `:216` deviation). Consistency would then ask the same of 98 test files, 50 tools files and 5 bench files, or accept `core.cljs` as the lone `h`-aliased tracked source in the tree.

### C. Both legitimate; the README may teach `h` only if it shows the ns form that binds it (bead's C)
- What changes: the general half is already the spec (`:218`) and needs no ruling. The local half: add `(:require [re-frame.fresco :as h] …)` to the README's boot fence and one sentence ("`core.cljs` binds `rf.fresco` because tracked source is ratcheted to `rf.<leaf>`; the guide's `h` is the same namespace"); catalogue rows unchanged or given the same clause.

An AI copying README→`core.cljs` still meets the mismatch; it just gets told about it.
- Cost: smallest by minutes (1 fence line + 1 sentence + maybe 2 catalogue clauses); 0 hot-zone.
- Risk: low, but it keeps the seam inside one directory and adds a paragraph explaining a seam that A simply removes.

### A-wide (NOT recommended; named because the bead prices it as A's "later, larger correction"): migrate the guide to `rf.fresco`
- 29 pages / 39 libspecs / 616 sites, `docs/api/re-frame.fresco.md` (27), 18 skill files, `implementation/fresco/spec` (19), 11 docstrings, the MIG-24 rule, and the charter/decisions/invariants design records; the guide-samples gate needs no change (alias-agnostic). Multiple worker-days, and rf2-lwx8's measurement says a fence-scoped prose rename creates seams rather than removing them. `:218`'s last sentence exists to refuse this. **A**, ruled with the explicit clause that it is Conventions `:218` applied to one directory and does not canonicalise `rf.fresco` for prose — the guide, the API page, the skills, the facade docstring and the design charter keep `h`.

title: Two dead producer links in the Fresco studio clock page — and the 'three producer trees' claim they support went stale in the same tree move
description:
Found by the rf2-2fhoj worker on 2026-09-22 while measuring the ungated non-`.md` link class at trunk
`99488a3c35`. Reported rather than repaired, because the repair is a PROSE adjudication and not a path fix.

## The defect

`docs/design/fresco/studio/the-clock-behind-the-published-rows.md` cites two producer files at paths that
do not exist:

* line 99 → `../../../../implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_harness.cljs`
* line 100 → `../../../../implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/fresco_narrow.cljs`

Both files exist, at `bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/p0_harness.cljs` and
`bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/fresco_narrow.cljs`. `p0_harness.cljs` genuinely did live at the cited
`implementation/core/test/...` path until `8a10915ed8` ("bench(hicasso): move the bench tree to
bench/hicasso and retire the freeze gate (rf2-6c12m.1, move only)") relocated it. `git log --all` finds no
commit in which `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/bench/fresco_narrow.cljs` ever existed.

These are the ONLY two broken links among the 426 non-`.md` relative links across every root the docs gate
scans (against 14,974 `.md` links, of which 0 are broken).

## WHY THIS IS NOT A PATH FIX — read before repairing

The table rows describe these two producers as **"in a different tree"** and **"in a third tree"**, and the
paragraph beneath them opens **"The roster is closed and the answer is uniform — across all three producer
trees."** After `8a10915ed8` every cited producer is in ONE tree (`bench/fresco/src/re_frame/bench/`, the
other rows one directory deeper at `.../bench/fresco/`). So the move invalidated the links AND the claim
built on them, in the same commit.

Repointing the two paths alone would leave the page internally contradictory — links saying one tree, prose
saying three. Whoever takes this must decide what the "three producer trees" sentence should now say, which
is a claim about the evidence corpus rather than a link repair. That is why rf2-2fhoj did not touch it.

## Why no gate caught it, and why none will

Doubly invisible, and each half is deliberate:

* `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates only targets whose path-part ends in `.md` (explicit guard, with a
  comment delegating other file types to mkdocs). A `.cljs` target is skipped. Measured both ways on one
  line of `docs/routing/examples.md` under rf2-2fhoj: a broken `.md` target reds the gate, a broken non-`.md`
  target on that same line does not.
* `mkdocs.yml`'s `exclude_docs` lists `design/fresco/`, so the strict build never renders this page at all.
* `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` does cover `docs/design/fresco/`, but it grades commit permalinks, not
  file links.

So this will not be caught mechanically whatever happens to rf2-2fhoj — that item's own recommendation is a
CLAUDE.md sentence rather than a new gate, on a measured yield of these two links.

## Scope

Two lines, plus whatever the "three producer trees" sentence becomes. `docs/design/fresco/**` is outside
`mkdocs build --strict` (see `exclude_docs`), so the gate for the edit is `check_provenance_pins.py` plus
`check_doc_slugs.py`; note the latter cannot fail on either link even after the repair, so verify the two
targets by hand and say so.

title: fix(gate): check_provenance_pins.py scopes a whole BLOCKQUOTE as one accompaniment scope - the rf2-xlsh fail-open, surviving in a callout
description:
`scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` scopes an entire BLOCKQUOTE as ONE accompaniment
scope, so a perturbed pin inside a `>` callout is absorbed by a sibling and the gate stays
GREEN. This is the rf2-xlsh fail-open surviving in the one container the fix's own helper
docstring says the corpus uses.

## The defect, read at source at trunk `5c81c60be3`

The scope counter in `_scan_page` has TWO boundary tests, and only ONE of them was taught to
see through a blockquote marker:

* line 671-673 — the PARAGRAPH boundary: `if not line.strip(): scope += 1`, reading the RAW
  line.
* line 682 — the TABLE-ROW boundary: `if _TABLE_ROW.match(_strip_quote(line)): scope += 1`,
  reading the QUOTE-STRIPPED line.

`_strip_quote` (line 486) drops `^\s*(?:>\s?)+`, and its own docstring reads *"Drop leading
blockquote markers; the corpus writes whole blob tables inside `>` callouts."*

Inside a blockquote a paragraph break is written as a lone `>`. Its `.strip()` is `">"` —
NON-EMPTY — so the paragraph test never fires and the scope never bumps. A multi-paragraph
blockquote is therefore ONE scope from its first line to the blank line that ends the whole
callout.

## Why that is a fail-open and not a curiosity

The accompaniment rule (docstring at line 1003-1018) passes a pin that is not landed when
ANOTHER pin in its own scope is. Collapse a callout into one scope and any single landed hash
in it answers for every other pin in it — which is, verbatim, the defect rf2-xlsh was filed to
close. The script's own header says so at lines 24-26:

> A TABLE ROW IS A BLOCK OF ITS OWN, because the paragraph-sized scope was a
> fail-open (rf2-xlsh).  A record table is one unbroken run of non-blank lines, so
> every row in it shared a single scope and any one landed hash answered for all

and line 1011 states the intended contract: *"A scope is a prose paragraph, or a SINGLE TABLE
ROW — not the whole table."* The blockquote case satisfies neither reading.

## It was MEASURED, not inferred

rf2-idq2w (merged as PR #10249) planted pins in
`docs/design/fresco/studio/the-clock-behind-the-published-rows.md` to prove the gate bites.
Perturbing ALL THREE gave exit 1 naming lines 162/169/174. Perturbing a SINGLE one left the
gate GREEN — absorbed. That worker recorded the diagnosis rather than fixing it, out of scope:

> A GATE DEFECT WAS FOUND AND REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED, and it is worth someone's
> attention: perturbing a SINGLE pin left `check_provenance_pins.py` GREEN — absorbed. A
> scope is a blank-line-separated paragraph, but a lone `>` does not strip to empty, so an
> entire blockquote counts as ONE scope. A one-pin plant inside a note is therefore a no-op
> that reads as coverage.

The second-order cost is the one worth naming: a one-pin plant is the NATURAL non-vacuity
control, so the next person proving this gate bites will get a green and read it as the gate
working.

## What is wanted

Make the paragraph boundary agree with the row boundary about what a blockquote is, so that a
`>`-only line ends a scope exactly as a bare blank line does. The repair is yours to choose;
what matters is that a pin in its own blockquote paragraph is judged on its own.

**Do not widen scope beyond this gate.** The corpus is not wrong and nothing under
`docs/design/fresco/` needs editing for this.

## THE STILL-FAILS CONTROLS — this is a gate change, so the risk is a DISARM

A change that makes a gate stop absorbing something must be shown not to have made it stop
enforcing things. State each of these with a captured exit code:

1. **The defect closes.** Perturb ONE pin inside a multi-pin blockquote on a real page and the
   gate goes RED naming that file and line. This is the measurement rf2-idq2w got green.
2. **Genuine accompaniment still passes.** A pin that is not landed but shares its scope with
   a landed one — in a PROSE paragraph and in a TABLE ROW — must still pass. The whole point
   of the accompaniment rule is that it is permissive within a scope.
3. **The rf2-xlsh row scope is untouched.** A landed hash in one table row must still NOT
   answer for a different row. Assert both rows, as the existing test at line ~1435 does.
4. **Non-vacuity at trunk.** The gate reads exit 0 over the real corpus before and after, and
   the pin census (`906/777` at the last measurement — re-measure, it moves) does not collapse.
5. **The counts.** Report the `--self-test`/fixture count before and after. A repair grows
   them; a disarm leaves them flat while a rejection message quietly stops firing.

## Gates

`scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` runs as its own job in `.github/workflows/docs.yml`,
graded on changed pages under `docs/design/fresco/`. Run the script's own `--self-test` and
say which form you used. `mkdocs build --strict` does NOT apply — `exclude_docs` lists
`design/fresco/`; verify that in the file rather than assuming it.

This file is Python, not a `.cljc`, so no reader-conditional lane question arises. Check
`git ls-files --eol` before editing and take CR / CRLF / bare-LF with Python on the bytes
afterwards; never `sed -i`.

**[MIKE — OPERATOR DECISION, ~2 MINUTES] Two worker branches carry unlanded commits that are
deliberately NOT going to land. Keep them as records, or delete them.** Filed 2026-09-20 by the mayor
during a §4 hygiene sweep, because this question has been surfaced in chat on several ticks and was
recorded nowhere — so every sweep rediscovers it cold and re-asks you.

**AFTER THIS SWEEP THESE ARE THE ONLY TWO WORKER BRANCHES ON THE REMOTE THAT ARE NOT LIVE WORK.**
Measured by asking the remote itself, not a cached view:
`git ls-remote --heads origin 'refs/heads/worker/*'` returns exactly **three** —
`worker/receipts-hic081`, `worker/xspike-a`, and `worker/xrpick-u40qy` (which is live: open PR #10113).

## The two

**1. `worker/xspike-a`** — tip `862e0d1d93`. Local and remote. **Its bead `rf2-k97c` has CLOSED**, so
nothing open owns it. This is the one previously raised in chat as "keep-or-delete now rf2-k97c has
closed".

**2. `worker/receipts-hic081`** — tip `ae14841ab3`. Local and remote. **`git cherry origin/main` reads
3 unlanded commits.** The tracker says the work it carries was **DECLINED**: `rf2-xcqk` closes with
*"DECLINED (2026-09-08): hicasso capability receipts are NOT built, in any form — only the d[esign]…"*,
and `rf2-3rq2` covers reversing the capability-receipts Adopt row in the Hicasso design lane. So its
diff is meant never to land — which is the definition of a retained record rather than residue.

## Why the mayor did NOT decide this

`docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` §4 Branches: delete only on **patch-equivalence** (*contained* is
proof); ***not contained* is the ABSENCE of proof, not proof of absence**, because patch identity covers
the diff's context lines. And it names this exact case — *"A branch with unlanded commits and no
proposed change may be a DELIBERATELY RETAINED RECORD — a spike, whose findings are promoted as prose
and whose diff is meant never to land."* The closing asymmetry is the reason this is yours:
**"mistaking a record for residue destroys it; mistaking residue for a record costs a branch nobody was
using."**

## What was done around them, so the contrast is visible

The same sweep deleted **3** local branches on proof — `worker/xrring-q9x6h`, `worker/xrstat-uwvpi`,
`worker/xrviews-m1qh0`, each pinned to the exact tip `git cherry` proved contained AND cross-checked
against the head oid verified at merge time (#10112 `dea0ecd656`, #10110 `c90a3f4850`, #10111
`20098a5b69`), with a skip-if-moved identity guard. **8 stale remote-tracking refs were pruned**: they
showed in `git branch -r` as a deletable backlog while the remote had already auto-deleted every one at
merge — a phantom list, in §4's phrase, reached by a different mechanism than the one it names.
**0 stashes.**

## If you rule DELETE

Both are safe to remove by the same identity-pinned route, remote first then local, skipping if the tip
has moved:

    git push origin --delete worker/<name>
    git branch -D worker/<name>

**If you rule KEEP**, say so in this bead's close reason naming both branches — a close reason is where
§4 says a retention ruling lives, and that is what stops the next sweep asking again.

**A third option, and it may be the right one**: keep `receipts-hic081` (a declined-work record whose
reasoning is genuinely only in the diff) and delete `xspike-a` (whose bead has closed). They need not
share a fate.

## Options

The bead offers KEEP, DELETE, and a split; TAG-AND-DELETE and PROMOTE-THEN-DELETE are the brief's additions and are labelled as such. Rule per branch; the letters are for ruling by.

### A. KEEP BOTH, unconditionally (re-affirm rf2-p0hx without its trigger)
- What changes: nothing on the remote. This bead closes with a close reason naming both branches as KEEP with no release condition; `ai/hygiene-keep.tsv` rows drop their "condition has fired" clauses.
- Consequences: zero for programmer, AI, tools, production, spec. The hygiene tick reads the ruling and stops. xspike-a's 899 lines of non-compiling apparatus stay as the only copy of Design A's binding and the probe kit.
- Cost: minutes, no files touched, no hot zone.
- Risk: none to the product. The one residual cost is that "keep an unbuildable throwaway forever because deleting is irreversible" is a rule that keeps every future spike branch too; rf2-icif already argued exactly that, and it is defensible.

### B. DELETE BOTH (identity-pinned, remote then local)
- What changes: for each branch, one lease-protected push then a guarded local delete, e.g. `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/worker/xspike-a:862e0d1d93d87aaae32f49e6e65925d60d90eb5b origin :refs/heads/worker/xspike-a`, verify absence against a control read that returns `main`, then `git branch -D worker/xspike-a` only if `git rev-parse worker/xspike-a` equals the tip (rf2-jojz's recorded method; the bead's plain `git push origin --delete` form is equivalent minus the lease).
- Consequences: `ls-remote --heads` reads one line. **For receipts-hic081 this contradicts five standing rulings and dangles a live citation in a tracked design doc** (`left-field-ideas.md:31` says the commits "are retained"), so B also requires a docs edit under `docs/design/fresco/` — which is gated by `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` and `check_doc_slugs.py`, not `mkdocs build --strict`.
- Cost: minutes for the deletes; plus one small docs PR for the citation.
- Risk: the asymmetry's bad half, twice. For receipts-hic081 the executable derivation and witness are the one asset the prose does not carry, and every prior review said the ref is free.

### C. SPLIT — DELETE xspike-a, KEEP receipts-hic081 (the bead's own third option)
- What changes: the B commands for xspike-a only. Close reason records both dispositions; hygiene-keep row for xspike-a is removed, the receipts row stays.
- Consequences: `ls-remote --heads` reads `main` + `receipts-hic081`. xspike-a's apparatus is gone; every conclusion it produced remains on rf2-k97c.1/.2 and in the epic's close reason. The tracked doc citation of receipts-hic081 stays true. No code, spec or tool changes.
- Cost: minutes; no files touched; no hot zone.
- Risk: if Design B ever has to be unwound to Design A, the binding would be re-derived from rf2-k97c.2's prose (which documents the fallback) rather than copied from `observe.cljs` — 99 lines of code against a renamed tree. That is the entire downside.

### D. TAG-AND-DELETE (either branch) — brief's option
- What changes: `git tag -a spike/<name> <tip>` then `git push origin refs/tags/spike/<name>` **by name**, then the B deletes.
- Consequences: same bytes preserved, same durability, invisible to the branch sweep; but it introduces a tag convention the repo does not use, makes the first-ever remote tag a spike rather than `v0.0.1.alpha`, and falsifies the "no tags on origin" line two design docs and the gated first-tag bead lean on. For receipts-hic081 it is standing-rejected (three rulings) and its re-opening is refused in rf2-xcqk (ix).
- Cost: minutes, plus corrections to `release-policy.md:93` and `decisions.md:33` if their evidence line is to stay true.
- Risk: the `--tags` trap: an habitual `git push --tags` from this checkout ships the two `safety/*` tags. Low, but it is the one way this option can do damage.

### E. PROMOTE-THEN-DELETE (either branch) — brief's option
- What changes, xspike-a: land the testbed on main as a real PR — a `shadow-cljs.edn` edit (hot-zone file) plus nine files that must pass the `cljs-examples-compile` sweep, which means a Fresco rename pass over `arm_b.cljs`/`hic.cljs` first; then delete the branch. What changes, receipts-hic081: nothing — the prose promotion is already done (three tracked files), the code is declined and cannot be promoted, so E reduces to B for it.
- Consequences: a maintained, gated, two-arm testbed for a decision that is closed.
- Cost: about a worker-morning for xspike-a, touching one hot-zone file; zero for receipts (already promoted).
- Risk: gold-plating a throwaway; the sweep would then carry a testbed whose only reader is history.

## Recommendation

**C: delete `worker/xspike-a`, keep `worker/receipts-hic081`.** They were never symmetric, and the split has a concrete discriminator rather than a mood: receipts-hic081 is *cited by name in a tracked design doc as the retained record* and holds executable code the prose deliberately does not, while xspike-a is cited by nothing outside hygiene beads, was labelled THROWAWAY by its author in every docstring and in its close reason, produced conclusions that are entirely on beads, no longer builds, and the one contingency that justified keeping it (Design B might founder) has been retired by Design B shipping and the epic closing. The stance says don't litigate the minutiae: the option that removes a subject from every future tick is DELETE for xspike-a, and the option that costs nothing and honours five prior rulings plus a live citation is KEEP for receipts-hic081. Both are minutes. D and E buy nothing the ruling itself doesn't, and each adds a convention or a gate for a closed question.
What would change my mind: for xspike-a, if you actually want `probe.cljs`'s instruments or `observe.cljs`'s Design-A binding as a starting point for something planned — then keep it as a branch (A), not a tag, because keeping costs nothing and the only argument for deletion is tidiness. For receipts-hic081, only an explicit wish to stop honouring the doc citation — in which case B with the one-line doc edit, never D.

## Review notes — core-instrumentation (2026-09-23 22:00:03 AUSEST)

**Tree:** `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23` at `034d0c8fc8`. Afterwards `git status --porcelain` on the tree reads 0 lines.

### Scope read

All 14 scope files were read in full, 9704 lines:
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/`: classification.cljc 1252, elision.cljc 1346, error_emit.cljc 1134, observability.cljc 604, performance.cljc 226, privacy.cljc 328, privacy/url.cljc 137, projection.cljc 798, recordable.cljc 187, reply.cljc 797, trace.cljc 938.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/`: cascade.cljc 265, projection.cljc 334, tooling.cljc 1358.

Supporting material, read in excerpts:
- router.cljc: 50-80, 1048-1140, 1300-1350, 1800-1835, 2490-2530, 2860-2910, 3060-3080.
- interceptor.cljc 137-285; std_interceptors.cljc 115-230; fx.cljc 1700-1745; late_bind.cljc 95-175.
- epoch/tool_pair.cljc 1714-1805 and 2230-2300; ssr/error_listener.cljc 405-500; fresco/server.cljs 190-310.
- pair-mcp get_path.cljs 1-140 and trace_window.cljs 60-175.
- elision_test.clj setup plus the nested-axis tests; trace_buffer_test.clj setup.
- Spec 015: §Direct reads, §No propagation, §Author guidance for the exception-path residual.
- EP-0025 §Egress rules; Spec 009 §Handler-scope Composition; Conventions §Event payloads and the `:rf.interceptor.delta/*` row.
- The prior review of this slice, rf2-pk4i6.11: description and close_reason, read via export JSON.

### Method

1. Read every scope file end to end, then traced each suspected escape from producer to consumer back to a public entry point: `rf/dispatch-sync`, `rf/project-egress`, and the MCP get-path eval form.
2. Confirmed every filed finding with a bounded JVM probe, 9 runs in all, each well under 5 minutes. The probes ran from the reviewer scratch dir with core, and epoch where needed, as `:local/root` deps. No probe wrote into the tree: every `.cpcache` landed in the scratch dir.
3. Took a control for every result: the same scenario without the triggering shape, or a sibling slot that is redacted.
4. Did the tracker checks with full-text search over a read-only `bd export`, redirected to a scratch file (control: `elide-wire-value` matched 25 beads), plus `bd search`. Closed beads were read through JSON.

Note: `implementation/core/.cpcache/` appeared in the frozen tree at 21:48:39. It holds a basis for core's bare `deps.edn`, which points to another process running `clojure` inside that directory. My probes ran from the scratch dir, and theirs wrote their own `.cpcache` at 21:49:33. It is ignored, and the tree's tracked files are clean.

### Findings

| bead | P | title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.4.1 | P1 | offset-rooted egress (get-path / project-egress :path) ignores ancestor sensitive declarations and ships the subtree raw |
| rf2-3x7nj.4.2 | P1 | :rf.event/after-deltas on :rf.event/run-end ships the whole app-db unredacted (every [:rf.interceptor/path ...] handler), including in the off-box epoch projection |
| rf2-3x7nj.4.3 | P2 | a path written and classified :sensitive in the SAME event ships raw in that event's :rf.event/db-pending trace (projection reads the pre-commit registry) |
| rf2-3x7nj.4.4 | P2 | privacy/redact-path throws 'Key must be integer' on a vector payload parent, escaping dispatch-sync from prepare-handler-ctx and losing the event |
| rf2-3x7nj.4.5 | P3 | always-on error record :event skips the event registration's :sensitive marks (dev trace and sink route redact, corpus record ships raw) |
| rf2-3x7nj.4.6 | P3 | elision walk-tree throws on a defrecord value (JVM) - every :db event fails on a classified frame, and a handler error with a record payload escapes dispatch-sync |
| rf2-3x7nj.4.7 | P4 | trace ring :run-order subvec spine retains every evicted dispatch-id (unbounded growth behind a 50-slot ring) |

All seven were executed with controls; each bead carries its own measurements.

### Considered and rejected

- **Nested large-over-sensitive.** The non-sensitive siblings ride raw and no size marker is emitted. This is deliberate (rf2-izlr7f) and pinned by the `elision_test.clj` nested-axis tests. It is a size question, not a privacy one.
- **Exception objects and `ex-data` on the sink route under non-public-error profiles.** They pass through unwalked. This is the Spec 015 §Author guidance exception-path residual, and is deliberate.
- **The process-default sink redacts `:exception` and `:tags` for frameless records.** Dismissed under rf2-pk4i6.11 #2.
- **`inherit-scope` does not carry `:sensitive?` into nested fx / sub / cofx scopes.** Innermost-wins is what Spec 009 §Handler-scope Composition specifies.
- **`compute-sensitive?` lets a caller-supplied `:sensitive? false` demote a sensitive scope.** No producer ever stamps false (grep over core src), so this is moot.
- **`trace.cljc` statically requires `trace.tooling` on CLJS.** The bundle-isolation gate pins it at var level. Emit is debug-gated, so nothing flows in production. It is a size question, not correctness.
- **A tooling.cljc section comment says CLJS does not defer.** The code does defer on CLJS (rf2-uoy6m), and the docstrings say so correctly. It is a stale comment that misleads nobody.
- **The CLJS DOM-node arm of `reply/host-handle?` uses `object?`, which is false for real DOM elements.** This is a defensive misuse check (trust the programmer).
- **`recordable` accepts defrecords, which do not round-trip through the EDN reader.** This is a dev-time advisory guard (trust the programmer).
- **`privacy/overlap-redaction-paths` does nothing when the sensitive declaration is an ANCESTOR of the handler's path slice.** That arm is a payload-mirrors-slice heuristic. It is left alone, and it is distinct from rf2-3x7nj.4.1, which is about direct reads.
- **The six-domino `:render` bucket keys on `:rf.view/render`.** That operation is emitted as the render-start marker (views.cljs:233), so this is correct.
- **`bundle-frame` falls back to `:rf/default` for a frameless event that carries a dispatch-id.** `stamp-frame` now tags every in-run event, so the fallback applies only when the ambient frame is unresolvable.
- **Generic `:exception-data` is redacted only for machines.** Only flows and machines emit `:exception-data` (grep), and both are covered.
- **`:rf.event/coeffects` could carry the app-db.** It cannot: `:db` is filtered out by `fx/framework-coeffect-keys`.
- **`trace-buffer` bundle mode ignores the flat-only filter keys.** That is documented as `(:flat-only)`.
- **`redact-url-carriers` does not reach userinfo or path-borne tokens.** That is a documented non-goal in the namespace docstring.
- **`warned-unschema'd` is never pruned.** Dismissed in the rf2-pk4i6.11 considered list.
- **The `validate-reply` non-map message embeds `pr-str reply`.** That happens only on a programmer-bug path.

### Could not verify

- **The CLJS side of every finding** was inspected only, since the brief forbids shadow-cljs. For rf2-3x7nj.4.6 specifically: records in cljs.core 1.12.145 do not implement `IEmptyableCollection`, so CLJS rebuilds a record as a plain map rather than throwing.
- **What the ASYNC `dispatch` drain does** with the throw escaping `prepare-handler-ctx` (rf2-3x7nj.4.4).
- **The MCP get-path round trip over nREPL** was not run. The probe ran the same `project-egress` call that the tool's eval form emits.
- **Trace emit sites in other artefacts** (routing, http, resources, flows) that might put app values in tags `project-trace-event` does not walk are outside this slice.

title: resources-mutations-ssr: :populates/:patches over an entry with a read in flight leave that read live - the pre-write reply overwrites the authoritative value and settles fresh
description:
## Defect

A mutation's authoritative `:populates` (or `:patches`) write over an entry that has a READ IN FLIGHT does not supersede that read. `populate-entry` / `patch-entry` set `:status :loaded`, fresh timestamps, the new `:data` and a bumped `:revision`. They leave the entry's `:current-work` / `:generation` pointing at the pending read.

That makes the entry incoherent: it reads settled while a read is live. The read's reply still passes the reply-handler gate, which checks frame + work-id + generation, never the revision. If the server answered that GET before it committed the write, the reply carries pre-write data and overwrites the populated value, stamped `:loaded` and fresh.

The populated key is exempt from the same mutation's invalidation (Rider 1), so nothing follows up. Every later `ensure` fresh-skips it, and the user's write appears to revert.

Spec 016 §Populate is an authoritative load calls populate "semantically equivalent to a successful resource load" that "may still be invalidated/refetched by LATER events". The earlier in-flight read is not a later event, but it wins.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_runtime.cljc:291-327` (`populate-entry`) and `:257-289` (`patch-entry`): both keep the base entry's `:current-work` / `:generation` / `:request-id` while setting `:status :loaded`.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:208-249` (`apply-populates`) and `:160-206` (`apply-patches`): called from `succeeded-handler` at `:1762-1763`. Neither touches the entry's live read.
- The read reply is accepted through `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/reply_handlers.cljc:63` (`live-slot-for-reply`). It matches on `:current-work` + `:generation`, both still intact.
- `mutation_events.cljc:811-829` (`plan->fx`): populated keys are exempt from this mutation's invalidation pass, so no refetch corrects them.

Public entry point: a `reg-mutation` with `:populates` or `:patches` targeting a key that a `:rf.resource/refetch`, a poll, a focus/reconnect revalidation, or any invalidation-driven refetch has in flight when the mutation's `:ok` reply lands.

## Failure scenario

1. An article detail is loaded as `v1` and owned by the view. A focus revalidation, a poll or an explicit refetch issues GET `/a/w`, and the entry goes to `:fetching`.
2. The user saves. The PUT's reply (`v2`) lands first, and `:populates` writes `v2`: `:loaded`, fresh, with `:current-work` still set.
3. The GET, which the server answered before it committed the PUT, lands with `v1`. It is accepted: the entry now reads `v1`, `:loaded`, `:invalidated-at nil`, not stale.
4. The article shows the pre-save text, and a re-ensure issues no request.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe against the frozen tree (plain-atom substrate, captured `:rf.http/managed`, classpath via `clojure -Spath`, run from the scratch directory).
- Control, with no read in flight: after the populate the entry is `v2`, `:loaded`, `current-work? false`, `stale? false`.
- Race, with a read in flight: status `:fetching`, `current-work? true`. After the populate: `v2`, `:loaded`, `current-work? true` (the incoherent state). After the old read lands: `v1`, `:loaded`, `invalidated-at nil`, `stale? false`. A second `ensure` issued no request.

Tracker: a full-text regex over a `bd export` (2158 issues) for `populat.{0,80}in.flight`, `in.flight.{0,80}populat` and `populat.{0,60}current-work` finds no bead on this. The only hits were unrelated: rf2-oflj7, rf2-7sx1, rf2-bd5n. rf2-3x7nj.10.1 is the query-half sibling class, where an INVALIDATION landing during an in-flight read is lost. Its proposed fix, an `:invalidated-at` vs `:started-at` comparison, does not reach this: a populate is not an invalidation, and it clears `:invalidated-at` itself.

## Smallest fix

Make a mutation's authoritative entry write supersede a live read. When `populate-entry` / `patch-entry` land on an entry whose `:current-work` is live, mark that work record superseded, as `refetch`'s force-new-generation path does per spec 016 §Race and in-flight semantics, and clear the entry's `:current-work`. The late reply is then stale-suppressed by the existing gate. Best-effort abort the request through the existing `abort-fx`.

The optimistic apply has the same shape. `apply-optimistic-patch` leaves a live read in place, and its reply overwrites the paint mid-flight. Consider giving it the same treatment. This is TanStack's documented "cancel outgoing refetches" step, done by the runtime.

Fence: `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc`, possibly `mutation_runtime.cljc`, and one test under `implementation/resources/test/`. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/resources`. The code is plain `.cljc`, so the JVM lane compiles it. The tests also run in CI's CLJS node lane (`npm run test:cljs`).

## Decision needed

No. The one design point, whether an optimistic apply should also supersede an in-flight read, is optional scope for the same fix.
notes:
== FIXED — PR #10284 (worker/resources-3x7nj), 2026-09-23 23:36:59 AUSEST ==

Reproduced at trunk efd5279cac before the fix, for both :populates and :patches. The sequence was: load v1, force a refetch, settle the write as v2, then land the late read with v1. The entry read v1 and :loaded, and the ledger row of the raced read still read :running.

Fix:
- mutation_runtime.cljc: populate-entry and patch-entry set :current-work nil. A settled entry owns no read, so the late reply fails the work-id gate and is stale-suppressed.
- mutation_events.cljc: a new supersede-reads-under-writes runs between apply-populates and apply-removes. It settles the superseded read's row terminal :suppressed {:reason :superseded :by <mutation work-id>}, and it returns [work-id transport] pairs. The succeeded-handler emits a :rf.resource/clear-work-handle fx plus a best-effort abort-fx for each pair, mirroring the refetch force-new supersede path.
- The optimistic apply was left untouched. That was the bead's optional point, and it is out of scope.

Regressions, in implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_populate_exact_target_cljs_test.cljc: populate-supersedes-a-read-in-flight and patch-supersedes-a-read-in-flight.
Control: with the two :current-work clears planted out, 4 failures, and the write reverts to v1. The restore was verified by blob hash.
Gates: resources JVM 900 tests / 7956 assertions green. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0. The CLJS node lane was left to CI.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH A LOOK (not a blocker; recorded here and in the PR report). A :reply-to continuation on the raced read is no longer delivered. Measured with a scratch JVM probe, a refetch carrying :reply-to then a populate settling v2 then the late read reply:
- pre-fix: the continuation fired once with the STALE v1, and the entry reverted to v1;
- post-fix: it fires 0 times, and the entry keeps v2.
This follows Spec 016 §Read completion continuations as written: "Where there is no successor to hand to ... the continuation is never delivered". The mutation :removes path already drops a removed key's in-flight read continuations the same way. If handing that continuation to the write is wanted instead (deliver an :ok carrying the populated value), that is a spec-level choice about :cache-hit? and :rf.reply/work-id on such a reply, and it belongs in a separate item.
== NOTE from the rf2-3x7nj.11.2 ruling (mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:35:15 AUSEST) ==

rf2-3x7nj.11.2 has been ruled B. When the runtime rolls back a key whose baseline came from an attempt whose reply it discarded or abandoned, it restores the snapshot, marks the key stale with entry-invalidate, and arms the exact refetch if the key is owned.

This affects ONLY this bead's OPTIONAL scope: "should an optimistic apply also supersede an in-flight read?" If an apply does that, each of its rollbacks restores a snapshot whose refresh was cancelled. Such a rollback needs the same restore-then-stale step, and rf2-3x7nj.11.2 builds it.

PR #10284, as read for that ruling, does not take the optional scope: its mutation_runtime.cljc hunks change only patch-entry and populate-entry, and apply-optimistic-patch is untouched. Keep the scope out of this PR, and if it is still wanted, take it up after 11.2 lands. The in-scope work, where a populate or patch supersedes an in-flight read, is unaffected.
Merged-PR audit #10284: claim incomplete for a pending infinite-feed refetch sweep. New open correction rf2-w5p2p: authoritative populate/patch cancels the current read but retains :refetch-sweep; a later load-more completion revives the abandoned page fetches. Public-event JVM probe confirms the orphan sweep and unsolicited page-1 request. See rf2-w5p2p for reproduction and acceptance criteria. Existing status, criteria and closure metadata preserved.
Merged-PR audit #10284 (686af153502461fd20f46fa4b66b63c9b2c79c3c; merged 2026-09-23T14:47:42Z). Completeness: Optimistic commit trace payload removes the inverse snapshot; projection fails closed on non-key compound disposition slots. Invalidated loaded infinite-feed ensure arms the configured sweep. Authoritative-write supersession is incomplete for infinite feeds: orphan :refetch-sweep survives and later load-more restarts abandoned legs; new open rf2-w5p2p records the correction. Correctness: Reviewed exact merge 686af153502461fd20f46fa4b66b63c9b2c79c3c. Read work-id is cleared, old reply suppression and terminal work record cleanup are correct; managed abort uses its independent frame-qualified request id. Confirmed the orphan sweep through public resource/mutation events: original late reply suppressed, but subsequent page-3 load-more schedules unsolicited page 1. rf2-w5p2p linked discovered-from rf2-3x7nj.11.3, forward pointer appended, literal-open and bd ready verified. Implementation quality: Focused merged-source JVM resource suites: 46 tests/266 assertions; epoch egress suite: 84 tests/666 assertions; zero failures/errors, exit 0. All runner roots and relevant merged resource paths verified. Targeted orphan-sweep probe: 1 test, 5 controls pass, 3 defect assertions fail, zero errors, exit 1. CI 58 SUCCESS/30 SKIPPED. Existing APIs remain compact; correction needs only cleanup and regression coverage, no API expansion. Scanned 103 open Beads and found no exact duplicate. Actionable findings: rf2-w5p2p. ### Method

2. Traced each tool from `tools/call` → `wire-pipeline/invoke-tool` → handler → egress → `edn-result` → dedup/cap → `write-frame!`.

### Findings

| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.34.1 | P3 | story-mcp: wire-safe projections admit java.time.Instant (`inst?`), which Cheshire cannot encode — a run over an app-db holding an Instant returns -32603 instead of its result |
| rf2-3x7nj.34.2 | P3 | story-mcp: agent-facing tool text contradicts the registry — `get-variant` claims `:extends` is applied at registration, and `get-story-instructions` lists `:expect` as a variant slot the closed schema refuses |

**Verdict truth (priority 1): story-mcp INHERITS rf2-3x7nj.30.1. Not refiled.**

`tool-run-variant` (`testing.cljc:45-201`) and `tool-preview-variant` (`dev.cljc:100-188`) forward `(:status outcome)` verbatim from `rf.story/run-variant` → `runtime/record-result-map`, the same fold. `preview-variant` is the tool the re-frame2 skill uses for headless runs, so it inherits as well.

EXECUTED through `invoke-tool`:

- a `[:dispatch [:p/set :n 1]] [:wait-until [:db [:n] 99]]` variant read `run-variant` `:status :pass` with 0 assertions, and `read-failures` read `:status :pass :total 0`;
- CONTROL: the same script with `[:assert [:rf.assert/path-equals [:n] 99]]` read `:status :fail` with 1 assertion.

story-mcp adds no status-losing mapping of its own:

- `error-outcome` / `deadline-outcome` mint `:status :error`. EXECUTED: `[:wait 3000]` under `:timeout-ms 200` gave `:status :error`, and `read-failures` then read `:status :error :total 1`, both at once and after 3.5 s.
- `no-adapter-error` refuses with `isError` before any run.

### Considered and rejected (one line each)

- **`read-failures` verdict recomputed after the sensitive drop could read `:pass` for a failed run.** Unreachable: Story never stamps `:sensitive? true` on an assertion record and redacts `:actual`/`:expected` in place instead (`assertions.cljc:428-504`). `API.md:599-603` documents the behaviour, and the contradicting `testing.cljc:324-328` docstring is drift on a dead path.
- **`read-failures` reports only the assertion-record aggregate (no agreement floor, no run-level `:cannot-run`), and a never-run variant reads vacuous `:pass`.** Documented in the descriptor, `testing.cljc:318-322` and `API.md:590-592`.
- **Narrative `:db-before`/`:db-after` and `:sub-runs` values ship raw.** EP-0025's ruled fail-open for re-keyed values (the 002-Tool-Registry.md:173 row names "a snapshot nested under `:db`", and rf2-gwye.60 restates it). Also empty unless `re-frame.epoch` is loaded, and story-mcp carries no epoch dependency.
- **`read-a11y-violations` ships non-live axe nodes raw.** Named, documented exception, and the JVM provider is always nil (capability-unavailable).
- **An overflowed `isError` result loses `:isError`** (`build-overflow-result` ignores the original, `wire_pipeline.cljc:117-119`). Needs an error payload over ~5k tokens, the marker is explicit, and pair-mcp does the same (`tools/cap.cljs:140-145`), so it is a shared convention and mcp-base's (rf2-3x7nj.35) call.
- **Overflow drops a run's `:status` and a list page's `:next-cursor`.** The marker says it truncated and names the retry (`max-tokens`); this is the intended cap design.
- **list-stories cursor not staled by `register-variant`.** The fingerprint covers story ids only, so pages stay aligned (same stories and offsets) and only `:variants` content refreshes. `API.md:226-229`'s example is harmless drift.
- **`:cell-overrides` allowlist missing inherited args.** `rf.story/resolve-args` is the facade over `plan/effective-args`, so it is extends- and compose-aware.
- **`:state/*` tags unfilterable in list-stories.** EXECUTED: they are registered and filter correctly.
- **Write path safety.** No filesystem write is reachable from any tool. Writes go only to the in-memory registry behind `--allow-writes`, with size, depth and width caps before any intern and the id grammar checked before intern. Overwriting or unregistering project variants is inside the operator's opt-in.
- **Protocol robustness.** Traced non-map, array and scalar frames, bad `params`/`arguments` containers, unknown and tool-invalid keys, negative `:max-tokens`, oversize frames, the pre-initialize gate and encode failures. Each answers a correlated error or `isError`, and the loop survives.
- **`unregister-variant` leaves the variant frame allocated.** Bounded by distinct ids, and consistent with every run leaving its frame live for `read-failures`.
- **A timed-out worker that ignores interrupts keeps running.** Needs an infinite-loop handler; `[:wait]` is interruptible, and the probe showed the interrupted run recording its error.
- **`002-Tool-Registry.md:113-117` says `read-failures`' `:elided-large` is "structurally always 0".** Story's own `:actual` projection can emit large-elided markers, so the count can be non-zero. The count is correct and the spec is stale in a harmless direction.
- **dedup equality merges `[1 2]` with `(1 2)`.** mcp-base's primitive, and invisible on the JSON slot.

### What I could not verify

- CLJS-only branches, which are unreachable from the shipped JVM server: the browser a11y and substrate providers, and the `#?(:cljs …)` arms.
- Real MCP-host behaviour with overflow or dedup-wrapped results.
- Whether rf2-3x7nj.34.1 bites an existing consumer app. It rests on reachability through ordinary JVM app code, not a known consumer.

title: xray-domain-panels-b: :info lifecycle traces (:rf.http/issued) are classed as issues, so every managed-HTTP epoch gets the L2 issue wash and a ribbon count and trips auto-open
description:
## Defect

Xray's issue classifier treats EVERY `:op-type :info` trace as an issue. `op-type->severity` maps `:info` to `:advisory`, and `issue-event?` is true for any non-nil severity. Spec 009 now uses `:info` for plain success-path lifecycle rows: `:rf.http/issued` (added 2026-09-23 under rf2-x8oz5), `:rf.http/replied`, and `:rf.http.interceptor/registered` and `/cleared`. Spec 009 also says issue filters must not include them. As a result, every healthy epoch that issues a managed-HTTP request gets:

- the L2 row's light-pink "this event had a problem" wash;
- a non-empty `:rf.xray/issues-ribbon` projection;
- for users who turned on auto-open-on-error, the watcher's empty-to-non-empty trigger, so Xray pops open.

The Epoch status colour for the same bundle correctly reads `:ok`, so the spine now shows an issue wash on a green event. The namespace's own docstring says success-path and lifecycle op-types are "Excluded by design" (`issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc:145-149`). The mapping predates `:info` being used for lifecycle rows, and rf2-x8oz5 chose `:info` without looking at this consumer.

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc:131-152`. `op-type->severity` has `:info :advisory` at line 140. `issue-event?` is at 143-152.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/l2_timeline.cljc:185-198`. `event-bundle-has-issue?` runs `issue-event?` over the bundle's `:other` bucket and drives the L2 `:bg-issue-row` wash.
- The `:rf.xray/issues-ribbon` sub (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:982-993`) feeds the auto-open watcher (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/effects.cljs:619-723`).
- Producer: `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:337`, which runs `(rf.trace/emit! :info :rf.http/issued ...)` inside the issuing fx handler's scope, so the row carries the issuing dispatch-id and lands in that bundle's `:other`. `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:557` also emits `:rf.http/replied` at `:info`.
- Public entry: any app that returns `{:fx [[:rf.http/managed {...}]]}` with Xray attached, in a dev build.

## Failure scenario

1. A todo app dispatches `[:todos/load]`, whose handler issues a managed GET.
2. The request is issued and the fx is handled. Nothing fails.
3. Xray paints the `[:todos/load]` L2 row with the pink issue wash, next to an `:ok` status colour.
4. `:rf.xray/issues-ribbon` reports 1 issue with severity `:advisory`.
5. With `:general :auto-open-on-error?` on, Xray opens itself on this healthy request. It does this again for every later HTTP-issuing epoch after an empty one.

In an HTTP-heavy app most rows get the wash, so the wash stops being a signal.

## Evidence

This was **executed** as a bounded JVM probe that loaded the real `.cljc` helpers through a `:local/root` on `tools/xray`. Output:

```
issue-event? :rf.http/issued -> true
issues-ribbon :issues count -> 1  severity -> [:advisory]  :empty-kind -> nil
L2 event-bundle-has-issue? (pink wash) -> true
Epoch status outcome for the same bundle -> :ok      (event_status_colour/event-bundle-outcome)
--- controls
issue-event? an :error -> true
issue-event? an :rf.fx success row -> false
L2 wash on a bundle with no :info row -> false
```

The probe used a hand-built bundle and record shaped like the projection. The claim that the real runtime lands `:rf.http/issued` in the issuing bundle's `:other` is **inspected**, not executed. It rests on:

- spec 009:2292: "emitted inside the issuing fx handler ... carries the issuing run's `:rf.trace/dispatch-id`";
- rf2-x8oz5's own description: "the row lands in the issuing bundle (in `:other`, as an `:info` row)".

Whether `:rf.http/replied`, emitted from the async transport callback, lands in any bundle was not verified.

The spec says `:info` is not an issue:

- spec/009-Instrumentation.md:304: "Tools that filter for issues subscribe to `:warning` / `:error`; tools that surface activity timelines subscribe to `:info` as well."
- 009:2292 catalogues `:rf.http/issued` as `:info`, "n/a — informational lifecycle trace".

A census of the implementation tree found `emit! :info` sites for `:rf.http/issued`, `/replied`, `/retry-attempt`, `/stale-suppressed`, `/aborted-on-actor-destroy`, `:rf.http.interceptor/registered` and `/cleared`, and `:rf.ssr/host-adopted`. As a control, the same pattern counted 36 `emit! :warning` sites.

`tools/xray/spec/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:269-272` describes the projection as "errors + warnings + advisories". That page is where Xray's prose disagrees with spec 009.

## Smallest fix

Drop `:info` from `op-type->severity`, so issues are `:error` and `:warning` only, as spec 009:304 says. Then fix the "advisories" wording in `tools/xray/spec/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:269-272` and in the `l2_timeline.cljc` docstring. Update any ribbon test that pins `:info` as advisory.

- Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc`, its test, `l2_timeline.cljc` (docstring only), and `tools/xray/spec/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md`.
- No hot-zone file.

The alternative in "Decision needed" would move the runtime rows off `:info` instead. That touches `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, which is HOT-ZONE.

## Gates

- The helpers are `.cljc` with no reader conditional at the changed lines, so the `tools/xray` JVM suite grades them: `clojure -M:test` from `tools/xray`, and `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh`.
- The ribbon and L2 cljs tests run in `npm run test:cljs` (node lane).
- For the spec 016 prose: `check_doc_slugs.py` does not reach `tools/*/spec` for prose, so check it by hand.

## Decision needed

Yes. Which side moves:

- **(a)** Xray drops `:info` from the issue set, as spec 009:304 already says. This is recommended, has no hot zone, and needs a spec 016 wording fix.
- **(b)** Xray keeps `:info` advisories but uses an allowlist of the `:info` operations that really are advisories, and every new `:info` op must be classified by hand.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 00:35:06 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.24.1.info-traces-are-not-issues.md. The ai/ tree is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot. The decisive findings are restated below.

Trunk read at 8f940c5d20, equal to origin/main. The probe ran at 8e65232c40; no cited file moved in between.

RECOMMENDATION: option (a). Xray drops :info from the issue set by deleting the `:info :advisory` arm at tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc:140, and "errors + warnings + advisories" in tools/xray/spec/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:269-272 becomes "errors + warnings". Option (b), an allowlist, would have no members. Option (c) has no lower severity to move to (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:951 names three tiers) and would touch hot-zone spec/009. No hot-zone file moves under (a).

DECISIVE FINDINGS
1. All the :info the runtime emits: 11 sites, 8 operations, by Grep over implementation/**/src (control: 44 `emit! :warning` sites in 31 files; tools/**/src has 0 :info emits).
   - :rf.http/issued (http/handlers.cljc:337)
   - :rf.http/replied (http/transport.cljc:557)
   - :rf.http/retry-attempt (transport.cljc:1107)
   - :rf.http/stale-suppressed (transport.cljc:622 and :705; http/registry.cljc:966)
   - :rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy (registry.cljc:908)
   - :rf.http.interceptor/registered and /cleared (http/middleware.cljc:199 and :226)
   - :rf.ssr/host-adopted (fresco/impl/codec.cljs:644)
   None is something a programmer wants flagged. A failed completion already emits emit-error! (transport.cljc:919). spec/009:304 names retry-attempt itself as its example of a non-issue: "Tools that filter for issues subscribe to :warning / :error".
2. Executed probe (real runtime on the plain-atom substrate, local HttpServer, real Xray helpers):
   - :rf.http/issued lands in the issuing bundle's :other.
   - For [:app/load]: L2 wash true today and false under (a); ribbon severity [:advisory]; the Epoch status colour for the same bundle reads :ok.
   - Controls: a :rf.error/handler-exception bundle washes true/true; a :rf.fx/skipped-on-platform (:warning) bundle washes true/true; a plain :db bundle reads false/false.
   - On the JVM, :rf.http/replied and :rf.http/retry-attempt land :ungrouped, outside any event row.
3. The "advisory" tier never held what Xray spec 021 §8.2 (:1649, :1674) designed it for. Skipped-on-platform and cofx-skipped are :warning (spec/009:2022-2023), and hydration mismatch goes through emit-error! (ssr/hydrate.cljc:709). So the tier held only lifecycle noise, and it renders nowhere: severity-colour and severity-badge-label have zero callers under tools/**/src.

rf2-x8oz5 and PR #10266 never considered this consumer: 0 hits for ribbon, wash, auto-open or issue-event in the bead's fields or the PR body, against 7 and 3 hits for handlers.cljc. No earlier ruling exists (export search over 2211 issues). No trunk fix since 034d0c8fc8.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 01:05:00 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option (a). Xray's issue classifier counts `:warning` and `:error` only; `:info` traces are activity, never issues. Delete the `:info :advisory` arm of `op-type->severity`, correct the prose that describes the issue set as "errors + warnings + advisories", and change nothing in the runtime or in spec/009. No hot-zone file moves.

WHY
- Spec 009 already says it. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:304 (verified at trunk a61f903c5c): "`:info` — informational advisories ... Tools that filter for issues subscribe to `:warning` / `:error`; tools that surface activity timelines subscribe to `:info` as well." The issue classifier's own docstring (`issue-event?`, issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc:143-152) already says "Excluded by design: every success-path / lifecycle op-type." The `:info -> :advisory` arm (line 140) is the one line disagreeing with both. git blame (Codex) puts that arm in cc26a05da50 (13 May); the per-issuance `:rf.http/issued` `:info` row arrived with d53fc33d93 (23 Sep, rf2-x8oz5), whose bead and PR #10266 never considered this consumer (0 hits for ribbon/wash/auto-open/issue-event in either). So the old arm was harmless until a success-path `:info` row started landing INSIDE an event bundle.
- The enumeration decides (b). Every `:info` op the runtime emits, re-counted at trunk a61f903c5c by multiline search `emit!\s+:info\b` over implementation/**/src: 11 live sites, 8 operations (one further hit is a docstring in epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1694, not an emit). Control: the same search for `emit!\s+:warning\b` reads 45 sites in 32 files; `emit-info!` / `:op-type :info` read 0; tools/**/src emits no `:info`.
    :rf.http/issued                    http/handlers.cljc:337      every managed request; lands in the issuing bundle (measured)
    :rf.http/replied                   http/transport.cljc:557     every completion; lands :ungrouped on the JVM (measured); a failed completion already emits emit-error!
    :rf.http/retry-attempt             http/transport.cljc:1107    the configured retry policy working; 009:304 names this very op as its example of a NON-issue; lands :ungrouped
    :rf.http/stale-suppressed          transport.cljc:622, :705; http/registry.cljc:966   correct-by-design silence (009:2296); lands in the superseding bundle (measured below)
    :rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy  http/registry.cljc:908      the `:rf.http/aborted` `:error` row fires beside it anyway (009:2294-2295)
    :rf.http.interceptor/registered    http/middleware.cljc:199    registration chatter
    :rf.http.interceptor/cleared       http/middleware.cljc:226    registration chatter
    :rf.ssr/host-adopted               fresco/impl/codec.cljs:644  success-path trace (009:2026)
  None is something a programmer wants flagged, so (b)'s allowlist would have zero members (or retry-attempt, which 009 names as a non-issue and which never reaches an event bundle, so allowlisting it could not reach the wash or the ribbon anyway). (b) is a mechanism with no members plus a standing per-op classification burden: rejected as gold-plating.
- (c) moves the side that is already correct. There is no severity below `:info` (009:951: `:severity` is "restricted to the three severity tiers" `:error`/`:warning`/`:info`), so (c) means re-typing lifecycle rows off the severity axis in HOT-ZONE spec/009, for all eight ops or none (stale-suppressed and aborted-on-actor-destroy also land in bundles), to work around one consumer reading the tier wrong — and it would change what pair-MCP's `:severity :info` filter returns. Rejected.
- The "advisory" tier never held what its design meant. Xray spec 021 §8.2-8.3 (:1649, :1674) designed it for fx skipped-on-platform, SSR hydration mismatch and cofx skipped; the runtime emits all of those above `:info` (`:rf.fx/skipped-on-platform` / `:rf.cofx/skipped-on-platform` are `:warning`, spec 009:2022-2023; hydration mismatch is an `:error` envelope on the hiccup tier and `:warning` on the adoption tier, spec 009:2024 — so it counts as an issue either way, and the dossier's "009 and hydrate.cljc disagree" side note is NOT a defect: 009:2024 documents the two tiers).
