title: xray-epoch-panel: SIDE EFFECTS ledger never paints ↺ overridden — an overridden fx reads ✓ as if the real handler ran (fx-effect-rows keys on :rf.fx/id, which override-applied never carries)
description:
## Defect

The Epoch panel's SIDE EFFECTS ledger promises `↺` for an overridden fx, but it can never produce it for a real trace. So an fx the test or story harness overrode shows `✓`, as if the real registered handler ran.

`fx-effect-rows` keeps only events whose `:rf.fx/id` tag is present. `:rf.fx/override-applied` is the only op mapped to `:overridden`, and the producer never puts `:rf.fx/id` on it. It carries `{:rf.fx/from X :rf.fx/to Y}`. So the override event is filtered out, and the row that survives is the following `:rf.fx/handled`, which maps to `:ok`.

For a keyword redirect, the ledger shows only the target id with `✓`, and the original fx-id the handler actually emitted disappears. The one test for this case (`side-effects-per-row-status-test`) passes only because its fixture puts `:rf.fx/id` on the override event, which the producer never does.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc`
  - `:2224-2257`: `fx-effect-rows`. It filters on `(some? fx-id)` where `fx-id (common/tag-of ev :rf.fx/id)`.
  - `:2020-2028`: `fx-outcome-op->status`, where `:rf.fx/override-applied :overridden`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/badge.cljc:501-518`: `fx-row-status-glyph`. `:overridden` gives `↺`, and the default is `✓`.
- Spec `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:3912`: "`✓` ran / `✗` threw / `↺` overridden / `–` skipped-on-platform".
- Producer, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc`:
  - `:1198-1203`: the redirect emits `override-applied {:rf.fx/from original :rf.fx/to target}`.
  - `:1587-1591`: the fn-value override emits `{:rf.fx/from original :rf.fx/to ::fn-value}`.
  - `:1261-1278`: `:rf.fx/handled` carries `:rf.fx/id`, plus `:rf.fx/from` on a redirect.
- Fixture drift: `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection_cljs_test.cljc:2690` has `(ev :rf.fx :rf.fx/override-applied {:rf.fx/id :metrics})`.

## Failure scenario

A test or story overrides `:http/post` with a stub fn (`:fx-overrides {:http/post (fn ...)}`). The handler emits `[:http/post {...}]`, and the stub runs instead of the real handler. The Epoch SIDE EFFECTS ledger reads `✓ :http/post`, which is identical to a real network call. A programmer checking whether the override took effect is told the real effect ran.

With a redirect (`{:http/post :http/fake}`), the ledger reads `✓ :http/fake`. The `:http/post` the handler returned is gone from the ledger.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe. It ran from the scratch dir against the frozen tree's `tools/xray` as a `:local/root`, with no writes into the tree (`probe1.clj` section P2):

```
-- baseline (no override)
   trace :rf.fx/handled #:rf.fx{:id :probe/fx}
   ledger rows: [{:fx-id :probe/fx, :status :ok}]
-- fn-value override
   trace :rf.fx/override-applied #:rf.fx{:from :probe/fx, :to :re-frame.fx/fn-value}
   trace :rf.fx/handled #:rf.fx{:id :probe/fx}
   ledger rows: [{:fx-id :probe/fx, :status :ok}]
-- keyword redirect
   trace :rf.fx/override-applied #:rf.fx{:from :probe/fx, :to :probe/other}
   trace :rf.fx/handled #:rf.fx{:id :probe/other, :from :probe/fx}
   ledger rows: [{:fx-id :probe/other, :status :ok}]
```

The control is the baseline. The overridden ledger is byte-identical to the unoverridden one, so the panel cannot tell them apart.

Tracker search for `override-applied` and `overridden`: no existing bead for the Epoch ledger.

Cross-slice: `panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:385` maps the same op to `:overridden` for the domain panels. It was not probed here and belongs to the domain-panels-a slice.

## Smallest fix

In `fx-effect-rows`, mark a row `:overridden` when its `:rf.fx/handled` carries `:rf.fx/from`, which covers the redirect case. For the fn-value case, mark it when a preceding `:rf.fx/override-applied` in the same epoch names that fx-id in `:rf.fx/from`. In both cases, key the row on the ORIGINAL id (`:rf.fx/from`) and show the target as detail.

Correct the fixture at `projection_cljs_test.cljc:2690` to the producer's real shape, so the test pins the real contract.

Fence:

- `panels/epoch/projection.cljc`
- `projection_cljs_test.cljc`

No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM lane from `tools/xray` (`clojure -M:test`), which runs `projection_cljs_test.cljc`. Also run the node lane `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

No.

== NOTE FROM THE rf2-3x7nj.23.5 RULING (mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 01:14:00 AUSEST) — same root cause, other panel; this bead's "Decision needed: No" stands ==

rf2-3x7nj.23.5 (Managed-Fx panel) was ruled OVERRIDDEN, with a correction this bead's fix should share so the two panels keep one vocabulary:
1. An override means the fx HANDLER was replaced (spec/002-Frames.md §`:fx-overrides`), not that nothing real ran: measured at trunk a61f903c5c, a fn-value override that delegates to the registered `:rf.http/managed` handler issues exactly one real request. So derive `↺` from override PROVENANCE only — an `:rf.fx/override-applied` row, or `:rf.fx/from` on the `:rf.fx/handled` row — and never from the absence of some other row.
2. A measured failure stays visible: if the replacement threw, the row reads `✗`, not `↺`. Do not let override-ness overwrite a failure status.
3. Key a keyword-redirect row on `:rf.fx/from` (the id the handler emitted) with the target as detail — as this bead already plans. For fn-value, match the override-applied row to its handled row by position over trace `:id` (it is emitted immediately before the fn fires; handled follows), not by `:time`.
4. Producer shape, verified at a61f903c5c: override-applied carries only `{:rf.fx/from :rf.fx/to}` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1230-1232 redirect, :1620-1621 fn-value, `:rf.fx/to :re-frame.fx/fn-value`); `:rf.fx/handled` carries `:rf.fx/id` (the TARGET on a redirect) plus `:rf.fx/from` on a redirect (:1298-1308). == WORKER RESULT (xray-3x7nj, 2026-09-24) — FIXED, draft PR #10299, commit af6d70f53c ==

title: ssr: render-to-string/render-shell emit hiccup prop names and values verbatim (read-only, tab-index, view-box, html-for, className; :type :button, :class [..]) where the client adapter paints the DOM attribute - React never repairs it
description:
## Defect The hiccup emitter behind `re-frame.ssr/render-to-string` and the streaming shell (`render-shell`) writes each attribute key's `name` VERBATIM as the HTML attribute name, and writes a non-string value through `str`. The client adapters that hydrate that markup do something different. Stock Reagent and reagent-slim convert the props first: kebab keys are camelCased, keyword values go through `name`, and class collections are joined. react-dom then writes the real DOM attribute. So for ordinary Reagent-tier hiccup, the server paints attributes the browser does not recognise: - `read-only`, `tab-index`, `view-box`, `html-for`, `col-span`, `content-editable`: kebab names, where the DOM wants `readonly`, `tabindex`, `viewBox`, `for`, `colspan`, `contenteditable`. - `className` and `htmlFor`: React spellings. HTML attribute names are case-insensitive, so `readOnly` and `tabIndex` happen to work, but these two do not. - `type=":checkbox"` for a keyword value. - `class="["a" nil "b"]"` for a class vector. React hydration neither patches nor reports an attribute-only divergence (Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection, *What React-native adoption does not catch*). The render-tree hash is taken over the tree, not the HTML, so it agrees. The wrong attributes therefore stay in the live DOM until that prop's value next changes, and none of the checks catches it. Some examples: - a `[:input {:read-only true}]` stays editable - a `[:button {:type :button}]` becomes a SUBMIT button, because an unrecognised `type` falls back to submit, so a Cancel button inside a form submits it - a `[:div {:class ["card" "active"]}]` is unstyled - an SVG `:view-box` never scales - a `[:label {:html-for "email"}]` is not associated with its input ## Where Cites are at `034d0c8fc8`, under `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/`. - `html_helpers.cljc:988-1107` `attr-string`. The `:else` branch at 1079-1103 emits `(validate-attr-name! k)` and then `(escape-attr rendered-val)`. `rendered-val` is `v` untouched for anything that is not a number or a style map, so a keyword prints as `:kw` and a collection prints as EDN. - `html_helpers.cljc:381-400` `validate-attr-name!` returns `(name k)` unchanged, so no name mapping happens anywhere on this path. - `html_helpers.cljc:877-880`, the `boolean-attr-class` docstring, records the behaviour: "the hiccup emitter writes author names verbatim; `re-frame.ssr.ui-tree` maps them through the React prop vocabulary". The same fn classifies names hyphen-collapsed (`:read-only` is recognised as the boolean `readonly`), yet the emitted name stays `read-only`. - `emit.cljc:200-211` `merge-class-attrs` joins the tag class and the user `:class` with `clojure.string/join`, which applies `str` to a vector or a keyword. - `emit.cljc:809, 825, 836, 851` in `render-to-string`, and `streaming.cljc:379, 389, 397, 408` in `walk-dom-tag` under `render-shell`. Both public emitters share the helpers above. - **Contrast in the same artefact.** `ui_tree.cljc:111-473` (`standard-names`, `dom-attr-aliases`, `react-prop-name`, `dom-attr-name`) and `ui_tree.cljc:598-610` (`coerce-value`, where a keyword becomes `name`) already carry this mapping for `emit-ui-tree`. reagent-slim's own static emitter maps too: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs:260` maps `:tab-index` to `tabindex`. - **The client side of the comparison** is `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs`: `dash-to-prop-name` (366-381), `cached-prop-name` (390) and `class-names` (674-701). ## Failure scenario A view renders `[:input {:type :checkbox :read-only true :tab-index 0}]` and `[:div {:class ["card" "active"]} …]`, server-rendered through `render-to-string` and hydrated with the Reagent or reagent-slim adapter. - **Server HTML:** `` and `
`. - **Browser:** the unknown `type` falls back to a text box, the input is editable, it is not focusable in tab order, and the div matches no CSS class. - **After hydration:** React's props already say `checkbox`, `readOnly`, `tabIndex 0` and `className "card active"`, so React writes nothing. The page stays wrong, `verify-hydration!` records a match, and no hydration warning fires. ## Evidence **Executed.** I ran two bounded JVM probes from `implementation/ssr` in the frozen tree, with output redirected to scratch. `git status --porcelain` read 0 lines before and after. `render-to-string` produced: | Input | Output | |---|---| | `[:input {:read-only true :max-length 10 :tab-index 0 :auto-complete "off"}]` | `` | | `[:td {:col-span 2} "x"]` | `x` | | `[:label {:html-for "email"} "Email"]` | `` | | `[:svg {:view-box "0 0 10 10"}]` | `` | | `[:input {:type :checkbox}]` | `` | | `[:div {:class :active} "x"]` | `class=":active"` | | `[:div {:class ["a" nil "b"]} "x"]` | `class="["a" nil "b"]"` | | `[:div.x {:class [:a :b]} "x"]` | `class="x [:a :b]"` | | `[:div {:className "card"} "x"]` | `className="card"` | | `[:label {:htmlFor "e"} "x"]` | `htmlFor="e"` | Controls: - **Other direction.** `emit-ui-tree` on the same author names gives ``, `` and `

title: story-execution: an unregistered decorator id (the spec's own :force-fx-stub spelling) still reads :pass while the real effect fires - decorator errors are not folded into :status
description:
## Defect

A variant whose decorator id is not registered still reads `:pass`, and the effect the decorator was meant to stub runs for real. `resolve-decorators` records the problem, `run-variant`'s result carries it, and the canvas shows a "Decorator errors:" block, but the run's `:status` ignores it. So a CI gate or an agent reading `:status` sees green on a variant whose stub never installed.

The spelling that triggers it is the one the specs teach: `[:force-fx-stub …]` in spec 005 and 001 (15 lines, filed as rf2-3x7nj.31.4). The registered id is namespaced, so every copied example lands in this state.

## Where (trunk, tools/story unchanged since 034d0c8fc8)

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/decorators.cljc:145` produces `{:rf.error :rf.error/decorator-unknown …}` for an unregistered id.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/decorators.cljc:215` is `resolve-decorators`, which returns it under `:errors` and installs nothing for that entry.
- The run-result fold in `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc` computes `:status` without reading those decorator errors. This is the same fold rf2-3x7nj.30.1 names for play-runner failures.

## Failure scenario

An author copies the spec's example `[:force-fx-stub :http/get {}]` onto a variant to freeze it mid-request. The stub does not install, the real `:http/get` handler fires, and `run-variant` returns `:status :pass`. Test mode, Run all and the story-mcp `run-variant` tool all report green.

## Evidence

EXECUTED by the rf2-3x7nj.31.4 dossier agent's bounded JVM probe on the mayor checkout at `ba2c41a767` (`scratchpad/decisions-sep23/rf2-3x7nj.31.x-probe.clj`, output `.out`):

    Q1  bare :force-fx-stub id              [status app-db real-calls] -> [:pass {:rf.story/lifecycle :ready, :status :pending} 1]
    Q1b resolve-decorators :errors for bare id                          -> [:rf.error/decorator-unknown]
    Q1c run-result mentions decorator-unknown?                          -> true
    Q2  canonical id + fn response          [status app-db real-calls] -> [:pass {:rf.story/lifecycle :ready, :status :pending} 0]

Q2 is the control: the registered id installs the stub (0 real calls). Q1 has the error present in the result and a `:pass` verdict with one real call.

## Smallest fix

Fold decorator-resolution errors into the run's `:status` as `:cannot-run`, since the variant's declared world could not be built, carrying the error. Do it in the same fold rf2-3x7nj.30.1 repairs, and land it with or after that fix, because both edit the same code. The canvas's existing error block stays as is.

## Gates

`tools/story` JVM suite (`clojure -M:test` from `tools/story`). Add a RED case: unregistered decorator id reads `:cannot-run`. Keep a control case: the registered id still reads `:pass` with 0 real calls. The fold is shared `.cljc`, so run `npm run test:cljs` too if the fold has a `#?(:cljs …)` branch.

## Decision needed

No. The rf2-3x7nj.31.4 dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.31.4.force-fx-stub-spec-absorb-or-deliver.md, local-only) identified this as a separate no-decision fix, independent of how 31.4 is ruled.
notes:
== POINTER from the rf2-3x7nj.31.4 ruling (mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 05:03:27 AUSEST) ==

rf2-3x7nj.31.4 was ruled A: correct the specs to the shipped absorb-and-log stub. That spec fix removes the commonest trigger for this bead, the specs' own bare `[:force-fx-stub ...]` spelling: 14 doc lines at trunk 7fc78b7b72. It does not remove the class: any typo'd or unregistered decorator id still installs nothing.

One design observation for whoever takes this bead, from Codex's independent review of 31.4 and checked against trunk 7fc78b7b72. It is not a ruling on this bead, whose own "Decision needed" is No. A verdict folded AFTER the run reports honestly, but the stubbed real effect has ALREADY fired by then. The 31.4 probe's bare-id case made 1 real call and read `:pass`. The decorator stack, with its `:errors`, is resolved in `runtime.cljc` `prepare-context` (`:decorator-stack (rf.story.decorators/resolve-decorator-refs (get-in plan [:world :decorators] []))`), which runs BEFORE `run-phase-0!` allocates the frame. The inline path resolves the same way in `prepare-inline-context`. So refusing there, when the stack carries an error, would stop the effect from running at all. Through `handle-run-error!` or the plan-error shape it would surface as a run-level result, the way an unknown composed fragment already fails before any frame exists (tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md §Inline plan: "the frame is never allocated"). Whether that result is `:cannot-run` (this bead's text) or `:error` (the fragment precedent) is this bead's call. A post-run fold alone would leave a real payment call fired from CI with an honest red beside it.
Merged-PR audit #10310 (2b16d6683ee3e3bded162c5f88a1b488d807596b; merged 2026-09-23T21:49:55Z). Completeness: Fresh reruns/replays, compiled play selection, failed-step folding across executed plays and decorator refusal are implemented. Canvas verdict integration was explicitly omitted by the fence; independently tracked in rf2-iftxj. Correctness: Reviewed runtime phase/refusal paths, assertion de-duplication, trigger rewiring and canvas generation guard. Accepted reported JVM 2058/7722 and five negative controls; CI 38 successful checks. Canvas gap confirmed by source and the implementer report, without a rerun. Implementation quality: One owner and retained run options reduce divergent behavior; avoid a second run or parallel status store when connecting the canvas to its new generation. Actionable findings: rf2-iftxj. Existing finding updates: none.

An unresolvable decorator ref now stops the run before any loader, setup step or script executes, as the 31.4 ruling note asked. The correct :rf.story/force-fx-stub still reads :pass with 0 real calls. Spec 017 gains a paragraph on the refusal. CONTROL: fix removed -> 8 failures.

title: machines-viz: Context-band redaction reads the retired [:schemas :data] bridge, so a machine's :sensitive [[:data ...]] slot renders raw into the chart and image exports
description:
## Defect

`MachineChart`'s Context band is documented to redact live machine `:data` by default before it reaches the DOM, and therefore before it reaches the SVG, PNG and clipboard exports. But the band's redaction still reads the RETIRED EP-0005 schema bridge. The only producer of its classification is `context-redaction/derive-classification`, which reads `:sensitive?` / `:large?` props off the machine's `[:schemas :data]` schema. API.md tells hosts to build `:context-band-sensitive` exactly that way.

Spec 015 and Spec 005 reversed that bridge (EP-0025). A machine's durable `:data` classification is now the projection-relative `:sensitive` / `:large` paths on the `reg-machine` spec (e.g. `{:sensitive [[:data :token]]}`). The `[:schemas :data]` props only drive validation-failure-trace redaction. So a machine that declares its secret slot the canonical way gets an empty classification from the documented recipe. A host that feeds live `:data`, a use API.md explicitly supports (`:context-band-inferred? false`), then renders the secret raw into the chart and into every image export. The redaction default the docs promise ("a host feeding live `:data` cannot leak a schema-marked secret/large slot into an egress artefact") is silently off for correctly-written machines.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/context_redaction.cljc:17-24`: the docstring states "machine `:data` sensitivity is **schema-first**".
- `context_redaction.cljc:77-95`: `derive-classification` reads `[:schemas :data]` props only. It has no production caller (grep: only `context_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`).
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/projection.cljc:1314-1328`: `xyflow-graph` redacts only the keys in `:context-band-sensitive`.
- `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:77`: "The host derives it from the machine's `[:schemas :data]` schema `:sensitive?` slot props". The same recipe appears at :674-675.
- The contract it contradicts: `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:152-195` (machine-owned durable classification; ":sensitive? / :large? per-slot props additionally drive **validation-failure-trace** redaction ... a *different* axis"), :365, :537 (conformance fixture: "the `[:schemas :data]` schema carries no classifying prop"), and `spec/005-StateMachines.md:4079-4081`.
- Entry point: `MachineChart` props `:context-band` / `:context-band-inferred? false` / `:context-band-sensitive`, then `export/chart-as-svg`, `chart-as-png!` and the `copy-*` fns, which clone that DOM.

## Failure scenario

Take the machine `{:initial :idle :sensitive [[:data :token]] :schemas {:data [:map [:token :string] [:user :string]]} :data {:token nil :user nil} :states {:idle {}}}`.

A host follows API.md. It feeds live `{:token "sk-live-SECRET-123" :user "ann"}` with `:context-band-inferred? false` and `:context-band-sensitive (:sensitive (derive-classification (get-in def [:schemas :data])))`.

`derive-classification` returns `{:sensitive #{} :large #{}}`, and the root-container band data is `[["token" "\"sk-live-SECRET-123\""] ["user" "\"ann\""]]`. That is the raw token, in the DOM and in any SVG/PNG export.

## Evidence

Executed: a bounded JVM probe (`p5.clj`, frozen tree, scratch `deps.edn`) drove `layout/project-definition` and `projection/xyflow-graph`, and printed exactly the band above. Control: the same slot marked the retired way, `[:token {:sensitive? true} :string]`, derives `#{:token}` and the band reads the redaction sentinel, so the instrument can see redaction when it happens.

Reachability, stated plainly: every in-tree host (Xray's `topology_view.cljs:301`, `machine_inspector.cljs:527`, `static/machines/sim.cljs:895`, `topology.cljs:122`) feeds the value-free static SHAPE, not live values. So no in-tree path leaks today. The exposure is any host using the documented live-data path, and that is why this is filed P2 rather than P1.

Tracker: no bead names `derive-classification`, `context-band-sensitive` or `context_redaction`.

## Smallest fix

Make `derive-classification` (or a sibling that takes the whole definition) read the machine's root `:sensitive` / `:large` paths. Each path's segment after `:data` is the band key, and a deeper path such as `[:data :payment :token]` should redact the whole top-level `:payment` value, because the band prints the value whole. Optionally keep the schema props as an extra input. Then correct API.md :77 / :674-675 and the ns docstring to name the `reg-machine` declaration as the source. Fence: `chart/context_redaction.cljc`, `spec/API.md`, `context_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`. No hot-zone file. Spec 015 and Spec 005 are right as written.

## Gates

`tools/machines-viz`: `clojure -M:test` (JVM; `chart/context_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`, `chart/context_redaction_wiring_cljs_test.cljc`).

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT 2026-09-24 (worker/mviz-3x7nj, PR #10312) — FIXED ==

Reproduced at trunk b3fb23a6c4: for the bead's machine (:sensitive [[:data :token]]), a host following the documented recipe got empty sets, and the band row for :token read the raw "sk-live-SECRET-123".

Built: context-redaction/derive-classification now takes the machine DEFINITION and reads its projection-relative :sensitive / :large paths. [:data k ...] names band key k: a deeper path such as [:data :payment :token] classifies the whole top-level :payment, because the band prints values whole. A bare [:data] names every key of the definition's own :data map (a key only the live value carries is unknown there). A path not rooted at :data is ignored. The [:schemas :data] :sensitive? / :large? props are no longer read at all (EP-0025; Spec 015 says they drive validation-failure-trace redaction only), so the private Malli-walk helpers went with them. API.md (:context-band-sensitive row, the egress-contract prose with a recipe snippet), the ns docstring, and comments in chart.cljs and export_dom_cljs_test.cljs name the declaration as the source. Sensitive-wins-over-large is unchanged, which also satisfies Spec 015's rule that a large subtree containing a sensitive descendant redacts rather than elides.

Regression: context_redaction_cljs_test (declared paths -> sets, deeper path -> top-level key, bare [:data] -> every :data key, schema props classify nothing, absent / non-:data -> empty) and context_redaction_wiring_cljs_test (the documented recipe end to end through project-definition + xyflow-graph: the secret appears in no band row, :token reads :rf/redacted, control: "ann" still renders). Red before the fix: 7 failures. Control: declared-path read disabled on the committed tree -> 7 failures; restored, blob hash equals HEAD.

Left alone: the machines-viz large marker's `:reason :schema` provenance label (core's own marker says :classification). It is out of this bead's scope, and nothing reads it for routing.

Merged-PR audit #10312 (c879b9cd171f975f3a19df4f1068804753a31b01; merged 2026-09-23T22:02:26Z). Completeness: SCXML own-format marker, spawn/on-error edges and Mermaid declarations meet the stated scope. Whole-data Context-band classification remains incomplete for keys introduced at runtime; separately tracked. Correctness: Read all changed production paths and declared regressions. Accepted author JVM 664/2940, CLJS 872/3926, negative controls and Mermaid parser proof. Static data-flow proof identifies live-only key disclosure; no broad rerun. Implementation quality: Changes are focused and dependency-light. Keep the correction small: apply whole-data classification to the actual band keys while preserving the explicit raw opt-in. Actionable findings: rf2-k7i6y. Existing finding updates: none.

A path like [:data :payment :token] redacts the whole top-level :payment. A bare [:data] path redacts every key in the definition's own :data; a key that appears only in live data is not covered. title: pair-mcp: on a default launch get-path cannot fetch an elision handle - the handle path returns the same marker and elision false is silently forced true, while descriptors and spec 009:3024 promise the fetch
description:
## Defect

On a default launch, with `--allow-sensitive-reads` OFF, no pair tool can return the content behind a `:rf.size/large-elided` marker, and the agent is told in three places that it can.

1. `get-path` forces `elision` to `true` unless `--allow-sensitive-reads` is set (`get_path.cljs:173-175`; the same pattern appears in `snapshot`, `read-sub`, `list-subscriptions`, `record`, `watch-until` and `dispatch-dry-run`). A caller's `elision false` is therefore dropped without any indication. The `get-path` descriptor and the shared `elision` knob both say "false overlays `include-large? true` ... so large slots ride verbatim" and never mention the gate. The tool spec says the same at `003-Tool-Catalogue.md:116-119`: "pass `elision false` to opt large content back in and receive the un-elided value".
2. Following the handle does not work either. The advertised route is "the agent re-fetches via `get-path` using the handle's path" (the knob text, and the snapshot descriptor's "drills into the handle via `get-path`"). Under the forced profile, a `get-path` on the handle's own path projects the value at that path, and the path matches the `:large` declaration. So it returns **the identical marker**, and the agent loops.
3. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3024 promises: "Passing the handle to the existing re-frame2-pair-mcp `get-path` tool fetches the literal elided value".

The forced elision itself is documented, in `003-Tool-Catalogue.md:735-737` ("2. Force `:elision true` on every call"), so this is a contract conflict rather than an accident. The tool spec contradicts itself (116-119 against 735-737). The descriptors the agent actually reads carry only the permissive half. The size axis is being gated behind a flag named for, and documented as, the *sensitive* axis, even though the same spec (003:765-770, EP-0015 fail-closed) says `elision false` alone never reveals a declared-sensitive slot.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`, under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/`:

- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_path.cljs:173-175` (the force) and `:201` (`egress-opts (elision/egress-opts-edn (not elision?) incl?)`), echoed as `:elision elision?` at `:295`/`:316`.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/raw_state.cljs:17` (ns docstring: "FORCES `:elision true` on every snapshot / get-path call").
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_knobs.cljs:86-108` (the `elision` knob text: "false overlays `include-large? true` ... so large slots ride verbatim", with no gate) and `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs:1012-1019` (the `get-path` description, which says the same and mentions the gate only for `include-sensitive`).
- `spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:116-119` against `:735-737`.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3024`.

Entry point: MCP `tools/call` `get-path {:path <handle path>}` or `get-path {:path ... :elision false}`.

## Failure scenario

1. The app declares `{:large [[:blob :payload]]}` and stores a 50 KB string there.
2. On a default launch the agent reads `get-path {:path "[:blob]"}` and gets `{:payload {:rf.size/large-elided {... :handle [:rf.elision/at [:blob :payload]]}}}`.
3. Following the descriptor, it calls `get-path {:path "[:blob :payload]"}` and gets the same marker back.
4. Following the descriptor again, it calls `get-path {:path "[:blob :payload]" :elision false}`. `elision` is forced to `true`, so it gets the same marker a third time. The echoed `:elision` slot reports `true`, but nothing says the argument was overridden or which launch flag would honour it.

## Evidence

**Executed**: a bounded JVM probe of the core projection that `get-path`'s eval form calls. It ran from the scratch dir against the frozen `implementation/core` as a `:local/root`, the tree's `git status` read 0 porcelain lines before and after, and no file was written into the tree. It used the `make-reset-runtime-fixture` / plain-atom adapter, frame `:p/main`, and `apply-classification-effects {:large [[:blob :payload]]}`.

- Parent read, `(rf/project-egress {:payload <50000 X>} {:path [:blob] :frame :p/main :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool})`, gives a marker with handle `[:rf.elision/at [:blob :payload]]`.
- Handle fetch with the default-launch opts (`egress-opts-edn false false` renders the bare off-box-tool profile): `(rf/project-egress <payload> {:path [:blob :payload] ... :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool})` gives `marker? true`, handle `[:rf.elision/at [:blob :payload]]`, and a body **equal** to the parent's marker (ignoring `:digest`).
- Control, the opts `elision false` would send if honoured (off-box-tool plus `:rf.egress/include-large? true`), gives a string of length **50000**.

**Inspected**: the force at `get_path.cljs:173-175`, and its six siblings, found by a Grep for `raw-state-allowed?` over the pair-mcp source. Seven tools bind `elision?` through it (get-path, snapshot, read-sub, list-subscriptions, record, watch-until, dispatch-dry-run). dispatch, trace-window and watch-epochs use the same predicate only for `include-sensitive`, so the Grep sees both kinds of site.

Tracker: the rf2-ealv5 dossier (notes, 2026-09-24) records this side effect in passing: "'elision false still fetches the raw value' holds only under --allow-sensitive-reads ... and the get-path descriptor does not say so, so a default-install agent has no structured route under the declaration". It then proposes "an optional separate ruling on un-gating the size override". rf2-ealv5 itself is about *descendant* reads under a `:large` declaration and is not refiled here. This bead is the separate ruling that the dossier names but no bead records. There is no other bead on the elision gate.

## Smallest fix

One of the following, per the decision below.

- (a) **Un-gate size.** Honour the caller's `elision` regardless of `--allow-sensitive-reads`. The walker keeps sensitive slots redacted whenever `include-sensitive` is false, so no privacy is lost. That is a seven-site change in the pair tools, plus the 003:735-737 item and the `raw_state.cljs` docstring. No hot-zone file.
- (b) **Keep the gate, tell the truth.** Add the gate to the `elision` knob text and the `get-path` description ("honoured only under `--allow-sensitive-reads`"), reconcile 003:116-119 with 735-737, and qualify spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3024 (**hot zone**) to say that a handle fetch returns the literal only when the server permits large reads. Optionally, have `get-path` add a structured `:hint` when it overrides a caller's `elision false`.

## Gates

`npm test` and `npm run check:descriptors` in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp`. `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the spec/009 edit under (b).

## Decision needed

Yes. Should `--allow-sensitive-reads` keep gating the SIZE axis? (a) Un-gate it, so `elision false` works on a default launch and sensitive slots still redact. (b) Keep the gate and correct the descriptors, 003 and spec/009:3024 to say that a handle fetch needs the flag.

title: xray-domain-panels-a: Machines focused-event chart never renders for a SPAWNED actor (attach-def looks up the <type>#<n> address, ignores :rf/machine-type)
description:
## Defect

The Machines tab's focused-event lens cannot draw the chart for any SPAWNED actor. That includes every `:rf.http/managed#<n>` wrapper actor a parent machine spawns (Spec 014 §Machine-shape wrapper). It shows "No introspectable definition — chart cannot render." and paints no fired or guard-blocked edges, even though the definition is fully introspectable.

The cause is the lookup key:

- `project-focused-event-transitions` attaches a definition with `(get defs (:machine-id base))`.
- `:machine-id` there is the transition's `:actor-id`, the live instance address, for example `:probe/child#1`.
- Xray's definitions map is keyed by REGISTERED machine ids only, so a spawned actor's address never matches.

The type is right there on the record. The runtime's transition trace carries `:before`/`:after` snapshots, and they hold `:rf/machine-type`, which is how the runtime itself resolves a spawned actor (`resolver/spec-from-snapshot`). Xray never reads it: `machine-type` appears 0 times anywhere under `tools/xray/src`.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- **The miss:** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:957-961`, `attach-def` in `project-focused-event-transitions` (`:876`).
- **Where the record's `:machine-id` comes from:** `machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:239-253`. `machine-id-of` prefers `:tags :actor-id`.
- **The definitions map, registered ids only:** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs:1005-1023` (`registered-machines-value`) and `:1039-1059` (`machine-definitions-value`).
- **The sub:** `machine_inspector.cljs:1190-1218`, `:rf.xray/machine-transitions-for-focused-event`. It feeds `definition` (nil) into `extract-fired-edge-ids` and `extract-guard-blocked-edge-ids`.
- **The view:** `machine_inspector.cljs:459-465` renders the "No introspectable definition" branch.
- **Runtime side:**
  - `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:805-816` emits the transition. Its comment says ":actor-id … a spawned actor's `<type>#<n>` … Reserved `:machine-id` names the registered TYPE only".
  - `lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc:66` is `spec-from-snapshot`.
  - `registration.cljc:1409-1416` says spawned actors are "materialised on demand … rather than held in a per-instance registrar entry".
- **Entry point:** Xray Machines tab. Focus any epoch in which a spawned actor transitioned.

## Failure scenario

1. `(rf/reg-machine :probe/child {:initial :idle :states {:idle {:on {:go :busy}} :busy {}}})`.
2. A parent whose `:running` state has `{:spawn {:machine-id :probe/child}}`.
3. Dispatch `[:probe/parent [:start]]`, then `[:probe/child#1 [:go]]`.
4. Focus that epoch in the Machines tab. The section for `:probe/child#1` shows the idle → busy transition text, but the chart slot reads "No introspectable definition — chart cannot render." and no edge is highlighted.

The same happens for every `:rf.http/managed#<n>` wrapper actor spawned by a parent machine (`{:spawn {:machine-id :rf.http/managed …}}`, `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/machine_wrapper.cljc:1-33`).

## Evidence

**Executed.** A bounded JVM probe (`probe_spawned.clj`, reviewer scratch dir) ran the real machines runtime (plain-atom substrate) with the frozen tree's `machine_inspector_helpers.cljc`. It built the definitions map exactly as `machine-definitions-value` does.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Live actors | `(:probe/parent :probe/child#1)`; the child snapshot's `:rf/machine-type` is `:probe/child` |
| Xray's definition keys | `(:probe/child :probe/parent :probe/solo)` |
| Focused event on the spawned actor | record `:machine-id :probe/child#1 :from :idle :to :busy`, `:definition present? false`, `(get-in rec [:after :rf/machine-type])` is `:probe/child` |
| Control: registered singleton `:probe/solo` | `:definition present? true` on both records |

**Census and control.** `rg -c machine-type tools/xray/src` returns nothing. The control `rg -c actor-id` on the same helper file reads 4.

**Inspected, not run:** the view branch at `machine_inspector.cljs:459-465` and the empty edge sets. That was CLJS-only and no CLJS run was allowed in this review.

**Tracker.** No bead covers it (export search on `attach-def`, `spawned`, `machine-type` together with the Xray machines surface). rf2-y8doi.1, the prior machines-panel review, does not raise it.

## Smallest fix

In `attach-def`, fall back to the actor's type when the address misses:

```
(or (get defs (:machine-id base))
    (let [t (:rf/machine-type (or (:after base) (:before base)))]
      (if (map? t) t (get defs t))))
```

A keyword type is looked up in `defs`. A map type is an inline definition, used as-is. A birth record (`:rf.machine/started`) has no `:after`; it can use its own `:state`/`:data` tags or skip, since it draws no edge.

The fired and guard-blocked edge extraction then works unchanged, because it already takes `definition` and `machine-id` separately.

**Fence:** `machine_inspector_helpers.cljc` and its test. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`machine_inspector_helpers.cljc` is graded by the tools/xray JVM suite (`clojure -M:test` from `tools/xray`) and by `npm run test:cljs` (`machine_inspector_helpers_cljs_test.cljc`). If the view is touched, `machine_inspector_view_cljs_test.cljs` is on the node lane only.

## Decision needed

No.

title: routing: {:url} / url-requested normalise a reference to the ADDRESS-BAR location (window.location), not app-relative path-form — under with-base-path or hash-url-strategy a relative or same-origin absolute URL commits not-found with a doubled base or the wrong route
description:
## Defect

`url/request-url->app-url` reduces an accepted `{:url …}` / `:rf.route/url-requested` string to `pathname + search + hash`, resolved against `window.location.href`. That is the ADDRESS-BAR location, not the APP-RELATIVE path-form the rest of the cascade expects. `match-url`, `route-url` and the nav fxs are path-form and base-agnostic, and only the strategy consult points ever see a base path or a `#/…` wrapper; `with-base-path`'s own docstring says so at `strategy.cljc:340-342`, and spec 012 line 1969 says "the router only ever sees app-relative URLs". Under the default history strategy with no base path the two forms coincide, which is the only case the rf2-fzbj.12 / rf2-gwye.26 repair considered ("using the ordinary history strategy"). Under `with-base-path` or `hash-url-strategy` they differ. The effective URL is then matched as if it were app-relative, and the push re-encodes it through the owner strategy. The result is a wrong route or a not-found, plus an address bar the spec says cannot happen (line 509: the reference is to "commit and push as the location the address bar will show").

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url.cljc:504-520`: `request-url->app-url`, whose CLJS branch is `(str (.-pathname parsed) (.-search parsed) (.-hash parsed))` and consults no strategy.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc:316-327`: the `{:url}` door. The effective URL feeds `url-resolution`, the not-found params and `:requested-url`.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/decisions.cljc:427`: the `:rf.route/url-requested` door.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:312-389`: `with-base-path` and `strip-base-path`, the ingress rule these doors never apply.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/nav_fx.cljc:253-259`: the push encodes the path-form URL through the owner strategy.

Public entry points: `[:rf.route/navigate {:url …}]` and `[:rf.route/url-requested {:url …}]`, the latter for app code handing it a string. `route-link` clicks are unaffected, because the link door passes its rooted path-form URL.

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-route :route/home {} "/")` and `(rf/reg-route :route/user {} "/users/:id")` are registered.

- With `(with-base-path history-url-strategy "/app")`, the user is on `https://host/app/users/42`.
  - `{:url "?tab=2"}` becomes `/app/users/42?tab=2`. `match-url` gives nil, so the navigation commits `:rf.route/not-found`, and the push encodes the requested URL as `/app/app/users/42?tab=2`. The intended result is `:route/user` with `{:id "42"}` and `?tab=2`.
  - `{:url "https://host/app/users/7"}`, a same-origin deep-link or redirect target, becomes `/app/users/7`, and the navigation commits not-found with the same doubled base.
- With `hash-url-strategy`, the user is on `https://host/#/users/42`.
  - `{:url "?tab=2"}` becomes `/?tab=2`, which commits `:route/home` with `{"tab" "2"}`, a different route.
  - `{:url "#section"}` becomes `/#section`, which commits `:route/home` with fragment `"section"`.
  - `{:url "https://host/#/users/7"}` becomes `/#/users/7`, which commits `:route/home` with fragment `"/users/7"`.

## Evidence

The CLJS branch itself was not executed, since no browser or shadow-cljs was allowed. The two halves were EXECUTED separately and composed.

1. `new URL(u, base)` in Node, which follows the same WHATWG URL algorithm the CLJS branch calls, gave `?tab=2` against `https://host/app/users/42` → `/app/users/42?tab=2`; `https://host/app/users/7` → `/app/users/7`; `?tab=2` against `https://host/#/users/42` → `/?tab=2`; `#section` → `/#section`; `https://host/#/users/7` → `/#/users/7`. The control was `?tab=2` against `https://host/users/42` (history, no base) → `/users/42?tab=2`.
2. A JVM probe loaded the frozen routing source and fed those strings to the path-form cascade.
   - `match-url "/app/users/42?tab=2"` → `nil`. The control `match-url "/users/42?tab=2"` → `:route/user {:id "42"} {"tab" "2"}`.
   - `(:encode (with-base-path history-url-strategy "/app"))` of `/app/users/42?tab=2` → `"/app/app/users/42?tab=2"`. The control, the same encode of `/users/42?tab=2`, → `"/app/users/42?tab=2"`.
   - `match-url "/?tab=2"` → `:route/home` with `{"tab" "2"}`, and `match-url "/#section"` → `:route/home` with fragment `"section"`.

Tests: the `request-url->app-url` rows in `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_history_cljs_test.cljs` (lines 284-358) run under the history strategy only. No test combines `{:url}` / `url-requested` with `with-base-path` or `hash-url-strategy`.

Tracker, full-text over a `bd export`: `request-url->app-url` hits only rf2-fzbj.12 / rf2-gwye.26 / .28 / .29 (history-only, fixed). rf2-exnw and rf2-gwye.29 fixed the LISTENER / decode ingress, not this door.

## Smallest fix

Reduce the resolved reference to app-relative form through the URL owner's strategy before `url-resolution`: strip the base for a path-form strategy (the existing `strip-base-path` rule), and unwrap the fragment for a fragment-form one. The simpler alternative for the relative forms (`?…`, `#…`, dot-segments) is to resolve against the current APP-RELATIVE URL (the slice `:url`) instead of `window.location.href`. That needs a pure href → app-relative leg beside the existing ingress rule.

The fence is `url.cljc`, `strategy.cljc`, `navigate.cljc`, `decisions.cljc`, the routing CLJS tests, and spec 012 line 509's sentence. There is no hot-zone file.

## Gates

The changed forms sit in a `#?(:cljs …)` branch of `url.cljc`, so ONLY the CLJS lane compiles and grades them: `npm run test:cljs`, which runs `routing_history_cljs_test.cljs` and `routing_url_strategy_cljs_test.cljs`. A JVM green is not evidence about this change.

## Decision needed

Yes, in two lines. Does `{:url}` take ADDRESS-BAR references, to be decoded through the owner strategy (base included, `#/…` unwrapped)? Or does it take APP-RELATIVE references, with relative forms resolving against the current app-relative URL? Either choice closes the defect; today it is neither.

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.12.2.url-reference-form.md. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot. The findings below stand on their own.
Read at trunk 51494841d9, which equalled origin/main. git diff 034d0c8fc8..51494841d9 -- implementation/routing spec is 0 lines, so every frozen-tree cite holds.

RECOMMENDATION: option 2, APP-RELATIVE. {:url} / url-requested speak the same path-form space as route-url, match-url and the route-link payload. A reference with no origin (?..., #..., dot-segments) resolves against the navigating frame's current app URL (the path-form URL of its slice, as scroll.cljc:182 route-slice-url already rebuilds it), not window.location.href. A reference WITH an origin is an address-bar URL and is decoded through the owner's existing ingress rule, the with-base-path strip-ingress at strategy.cljc:369-372 exposed as one optional extension key (sub-option 2b). 2a (the relative half only, plus one spec sentence) is a coherent smaller stop. Option 1 (address-bar references everywhere) is ruled out: it breaks rooted refs under hash, which is exactly what route-link dispatches (link.cljc:171-202, {:url path-url}), and it needs a new pure decode leg in the strategy contract.

DECISIVE FINDINGS (Node new URL composed with trunk JVM match-url and strategy :encode):
1. A rooted ref is ALREADY app-relative under every strategy today: {:url "/users/7"} commits user 7 in all four configurations (history, history+/app, hash, hash+/app). Every broken case is a relative or absolute ref, so option 2 changes only cells that are broken today.
2. Today, under with-base-path "/app" on /app/users/42, {:url "?tab=2"} reduces to /app/users/42?tab=2, which is NO-MATCH, so it commits not-found and pushes /app/app/users/42?tab=2. Under hash, "#section" reduces to /#section and commits :route/home with fragment "section". Under hash+/app, "#section" pushes /app#/app#section. Cause: url.cljc:504-520 resolves against window.location.href and consults no strategy, while spec 012:1951 says the strategy is consulted ONLY at the four consult points.
3. Trap for the fix: (fragment-form-strategy? (with-base-path hash-url-strategy "/app")) reads FALSE at trunk (the wrapped encode of "/" is /app#/). 2b must take the ingress form from the combinator and must not re-derive it from the outer strategy.

Spec conflict: 012:509 and :1192 (address-bar wording, written by the history-only rf2-fzbj.12 repair) against :1951, :1955 and :1969 (path-form cascade; "the router only ever sees app-relative URLs"). No earlier ruling exists. No hot-zone file. Lane: the change is in a #?(:cljs) branch of url.cljc, so ONLY npm run test:cljs grades it.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 00:18:04 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option 2, APP-RELATIVE. {:url ...} and :rf.route/url-requested speak the same path-form space as route-url, match-url and the route-link click payload. The rule has three parts:
- A reference WITHOUT an origin is an app reference. That covers rooted /x, ?query, #fragment, dot-segments and bare relative segments. It resolves against the NAVIGATING frame's current app URL.
- A same-origin reference WITH an origin (scheme or //authority) is a browser address. It is decoded by the URL owner's strategy :decode.
- To make that decode uniform, the strategy contract changes: :decode goes from (fn [] path), which reads window.location, to (fn [href] path). The href is the origin-relative browser address, pathname + search + hash.
The rule a programmer is told: no origin, it's an app path; an origin, it's a browser address.

WHY
- The two halves of spec 012 disagree, and the app-relative half is the architecture:
  - :1951: the strategy is consulted ONLY at its consult points, and everything else is path-form.
  - :1955: the route-link click "still dispatches the path-form :rf.route/url-requested".
  - :1969: "the router only ever sees app-relative URLs".
  - The SSR section says the same.
  - :509 (§Target form) and :1192 say the address-bar thing. They were written by the rf2-fzbj.12 repair, which scoped itself to "the ordinary history strategy". In that configuration the address bar and the app URL are the same string, which is how the conflict went unnoticed.
- Today's contract is already app-relative in practice, with a hole in it. A rooted reference resolves app-relatively under every strategy: new URL("/users/7", anything) has the pathname /users/7. route-link dispatches exactly that (link.cljc:171-202, [:rf.route/url-requested {:url path-url}]). Every broken case is a relative or origin-bearing reference. So option 2 changes only cells that are broken today. History without a base resolves identically, because there the address bar and the app URL coincide.
- Measured failures today. The dossier composed Node's WHATWG new URL with the trunk JVM match-url and each strategy's :encode. Codex independently compiled and ran the real CLJS request-url->app-url in Node with a supplied window.location. The two agree:
  - with-base-path "/app" on /app/users/42: {:url "?tab=2"} reduces to /app/users/42?tab=2, which is NO-MATCH, so it commits not-found and pushes /app/app/users/42?tab=2.
  - hash: "#section" reduces to /#section and commits :route/home with fragment "section". "?tab=2" commits :route/home with {"tab" "2"}. https://host/#/users/7 commits home with fragment "/users/7".
  - hash + /app: "#section" pushes /app#/app#section.
  - Control: /users/42?tab=2 is user 42 under all four configurations.
  The cause is at url.cljc:504-520: the CLJS branch resolves against (.-href (.-location js/window)), takes pathname + search + hash and consults no strategy. Its callers are navigate.cljc:317 ({:url}) and decisions.cljc:427 (url-requested). All three were verified at trunk 8e65232c40, with the routing tree unchanged since the review tree 034d0c8fc8.
- Option 1 (address-bar references everywhere) loses. Under hash, {:url "/users/7"} would mean https://host/users/7, which has no #/ fragment, so it decodes to / and lands on HOME. That breaks the one row that works everywhere today, and it is what route-link dispatches. Keeping route-link working would mean switching url-requested-payload and the :routing/link-model seam that Fresco's route-link consumes over to the ENCODED href. That contradicts :1955 and the SSR rule that "the navigation payload ... stays path-form". Option 1 also needs a new pure decode leg anyway.
- The dossier's "leave it, document that relative forms need the default strategy" records a defect instead of fixing it.

THE ABSOLUTE HALF: the dossier and Codex DIFFER here, and I adopt Codex's version.
- The dossier recommended 2b: expose with-base-path's strip-ingress as ONE OPTIONAL extension key, with a custom strategy that lacks it falling back to 2a (strip the origin and treat the path as app-relative). It named 2a, the relative half only plus a spec sentence, as a coherent smaller stop.
- Codex: do not add an optional key with a silent fallback. Make the existing decode operation accept browser-address input, and keep the window.location read at the browser boundary.
- What decides it:
  (a) A fallback gives custom strategies different semantics for the same supported input. validate-url-strategy! permitting extension keys does not make that behaviour a contract.
  (b) The contract change is SMALL. I took a census at trunk of zero-arity :decode implementers and call sites, over the whole repo and excluding HTTP's unrelated :decode:
    - src: strategy.cljc's two listener installers (:117, :202) and the with-base-path wrapper (:374); history.cljc's current-url (:84) and the initial-sync decode-url (:130/:164).
    - ONE in-tree custom strategy, the test helper decode-to-url-strategy (adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs:1700-1713), which ignores its input and keeps working.
    - About eleven test lines: nine in routing_url_strategy_cljs_test.cljs, and two in routing_url_strategy_test.clj (:334, :388).
    - spec/012-Routing.md:1934 and :1941.
    - Control: the same census finds :decode (fn [] path) in strategy.cljc's own namespace docstring, so the pattern is live.
  (c) It is the more elegant contract. :decode becomes PURE and host-agnostic, the exact inverse of :encode, so spec 012's round-trip law (:1945) becomes the pure law (decode (encode p)) = p. That law is testable on both hosts without a browser. history :decode becomes identity, mirroring its identity :encode, which is what :1962 already claims.
  (d) The project's own precedent avoided adding keys. fragment-form-strategy?'s docstring (strategy.cljc:283-310) chose derivation "with no sixth key added to the five-leg contract". 2b would add one.
- 2a loses because origin-bearing same-origin input is SUPPORTED and DOCUMENTED:
  - rf2-fzbj.12 added it deliberately for "deep-link handlers, server-redirect targets, programmatic redirects from a string" (:440).
  - Host anchor interceptors (:689) hand a.href, which the browser always makes absolute.
  - Under hash, 2a lands those on the WRONG ROUTE silently: https://host/#/users/7 becomes home with fragment "/users/7".
  - Leaving that input working under one strategy only would repeat rf2-fzbj.12's partial fix.
- Migration cost, stated honestly: a custom strategy's :decode must take one argument. In CLJS a legacy zero-arity fn called with one argument silently ignores it. It keeps working for the listener and the initial sync, but it would decode the CURRENT location instead of a passed absolute URL. This is pre-alpha, and the namespace itself says the shipped line "holds at two". Say it in the spec text and the changelog, and add no arity detection.

WHAT TO BUILD (trunk 8e65232c40)
1. The strategy contract (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc; spec/012-Routing.md §The strategy contract :1930-1945 and the SSR paragraph :1983):
   - :decode is (fn [href] path). href is an origin-relative address, pathname + search + hash, and :encode's own output is a valid input. Pure on both hosts.
   - history-decode = identity.
   - hash-decode = the part after the first '#'. An empty or missing fragment gives "/". It prefixes "/" exactly as today.
   - with-base-path's :decode = (fn [href] (strip-ingress ((:decode strategy) href))). strip-ingress stays chosen from the INNER strategy at wrap time, as today.
   - The listeners and the initial sync compute the href from window.location, (str pathname search hash), or "/" when there is no window. That preserves today's no-window behaviour.
   - history.cljc current-url becomes (history-decode <that href>).
   - Round-trip law: (decode (encode p)) = p.
   TRAP: never re-derive fragment-form from the OUTER strategy. At trunk, (fragment-form-strategy? (with-base-path hash-url-strategy "/app")) reads FALSE, because the wrapped (encode "/") is /app#/. Composing the wrapped :decode avoids the trap by construction.
   Measured strip-base-path behaviour, which should not move:
   - /app/users/7 -> /users/7
   - /app?tab=2 -> /?tab=2
   - /application -> unchanged
   - /users/7 -> unchanged
2. The reduction (url.cljc request-url->app-url, CLJS branch). Thread in the navigating frame's current app URL and the URL owner's strategy from both callers, navigate.cljc:317 and decisions.cljc:427. Both have rdb and frame in scope.
   - Keep the external-url? gate exactly as it is. Origin comparison against the document is legitimately address-bar semantics.
   - An in-app reference WITH an origin (scheme or //): parse it with js/URL against location.href. Take (str pathname search hash) and hand it to the URL OWNER's :decode, meaning url-strategy-for-frame-id of the URL owner, defaulting to history. The address bar belongs to the owner, including when a non-owner frame navigates.
   - A reference WITHOUT an origin: resolve it against the navigating frame's current app URL. The implementation can be js/URL of the reference against a synthetic base, (str "http://app.invalid" base-app-url), keeping pathname + search + hash. The base is:
     - (a) the CANONICAL reconstruction of the frame's current slice through route-url. That is the reconstruction route-slice-url (scroll.cljc:182) performs. Reuse it or lift it out, but do not make navigation depend on scroll-cache semantics.
     - (b) on a not-found slice, which route-url cannot rebuild (Codex measured route-slice-url returning nil for {:url "/missing/page?old=1"}), the slice's preserved requested app URL, (get-in current [:params :url]).
     - (c) "/" before any location exists.
   - A non-URL-bound frame (a story, a devcard, a test frame) therefore resolves ?tab=2 against its OWN route. Today it resolves against the host page's address bar, a quiet sibling defect this closes.
   - JVM: unchanged, identity. Its lexical gate classes origin-bearing and bare-relative references as external. Relative-reference resolution on the JVM is out of scope.
3. The consult-point text (spec 012 §The four consult points, :1949-1957). Keep the count at FOUR by widening point 4 to "ingress decode". The owner's :decode is then applied by the browser listener (each change and the initial sync) AND by the {:url} / url-requested doors to a same-origin reference that carries an origin. This matters because spec/API.md:293 (HOT-ZONE) describes with-base-path as acting "at all four egress/ingress consult points". Renumbering to five would make that row stale and force a hot-zone edit. Keeping four avoids it.
4. Spec 012 :509 (§Target form) and :1192 (url-requested) each get the rule in one sentence: no origin means an app reference resolved against the navigating frame's current app URL; an origin means a browser address decoded by the URL owner's strategy. Also state these explicitly:
   - {:url "/app/users/7"} under a /app base is an app path that does not exist, so it is not-found and the requested URL is kept. To pass a browser path, include the origin.
   - A host anchor interceptor must pass the anchor's resolved .href property (absolute), NOT getAttribute("href"). In a hash app the raw attribute "#/users/7" is an app-relative FRAGMENT reference: a fragment-only change on the current route, not "go to user 7".
   - Relative references resolve against the CANONICAL location, so a trailing-slash spelling is not honoured. Codex measured it: /users/42/ matches and reconstructs as /users/42, so a bare-relative "7" resolves to /users/7 rather than /users/42/7. This is a deliberate choice, made so route behaviour stays independent of deployment and host spelling. Document it; add no second history model.
   - An absolute same-origin URL outside a history+base mount, such as https://host/other, is returned unchanged by strip-base-path, matched as the app path /other, and is typically not-found. That is acceptable. Spend no rule on it.

REGRESSIONS (RED today, GREEN after the fix). These are CLJS rows in routing_history_cljs_test.cljs / routing_url_strategy_cljs_test.cljs, using the node lane's existing window stub. Run them through BOTH request doors.
- Under (with-base-path history-url-strategy "/app"), on /users/42: {:url "?tab=2"} commits user 42 with {"tab" "2"} and pushes /app/users/42?tab=2. RED today: not-found, pushing /app/app/users/42?tab=2.
- Under hash-url-strategy: {:url "#section"} is a fragment-only change on user 42. RED today: home with fragment "section".
- Under hash + /app: "#section" pushes /app#/users/42#section. RED today: /app#/app#section.
- Absolute: {:url (str origin "/app/users/7")} under the base, and {:url (str origin "/#/users/7")} under hash, both commit user 7. RED today: not-found and home respectively.
- A non-owner frame whose route differs from the host page: ?tab=2 resolves against the FRAME's route.
- Bases: a not-found slice, and no slice at all ("/").
- One custom strategy with its own :decode, proving the contract is uniform.
- Pure JVM rows, since decode is now host-agnostic: (decode (encode p)) = p for history, hash and both based forms. The existing JVM pins at routing_url_strategy_test.clj:334 and :388 move to the one-argument form.
- Controls that must stay green unchanged:
  - every rf2-fzbj.12 row at routing_history_cljs_test.cljs:306-358 (history, no base);
  - {:url "/users/7"} under all four configurations;
  - the off-origin refusal rows.
  The :284 rf2-aftbmz row and the :203-206 non-string row exercise the helper directly: their call shape changes with the signature, their expected strings do not.

LANE: the reduction sits in the #?(:cljs ...) branch of url.cljc, so ONLY npm run test:cljs grades it. A JVM green says nothing about it. The strategy.cljc decode change is .cljc outside reader conditionals (the listeners are CLJS-only), so the JVM lane grades that half: clojure -M:test from implementation/routing. Both lanes are needed. The shadow-cljs lane is machine-wide exclusive and needs the mayor's grant. No browser row is needed.

HOT ZONE: none, IF item 3 keeps the count at four. Otherwise spec/API.md:293 must move too, and the mayor must sequence it. The files are url.cljc, strategy.cljc, history.cljc, navigate.cljc (:317 only), decisions.cljc (:427), the routing tests, the one reagent realworld test helper (optional, since it keeps working) and spec/012.

INTERACTIONS
- rf2-3x7nj.12.1 edits navigate.cljc at the :query-merge fold (:421-424), not the {:url} branch. Sequence the two PRs or land them as one routing PR. title: mcp-base: diff-encode reports a vector->list/seq change as unchanged; decoded :db-after keeps the old kind
description:
## Defect

`diff-encode` decides "unchanged" with plain Clojure `=`, which holds a vector and a list/seq with the same elements equal. So when an event turns a vector into a seq without changing its elements (the classic re-frame `sort-by` / `filter` / `remove` / `map` regression), the encoder emits NO patch for that path. The decoder then rebuilds `:db-after` from `:db-before` and reports the OLD kind: the agent is told the slot is still a vector when app-db now holds a seq. The same shared codec's dedup half already treats this exact erasure as a defect and fixed it (rf2-gwye.32, `wire=` = `=` refined by `same-kinds?`); diff-encode was never given the same equivalence. `diff-encode.md` promises "lossless replay", and the epoch EDN text is where kind is visible (JSON flattens both to arrays).

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode.cljc:475` — `(= a b) acc` short-circuits every equal-but-differently-kinded pair to "no change".
- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode.cljc:455` — the same `(= av bv)` guard inside same-length vector recursion.
- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode.cljc:392` — `(find a k)` pairs a map key with an `=`-equal key of another kind (a vector key respelled as a list key is also silent). This is a smaller sub-case of the same defect.
- The equivalence that fixes it already exists, but it is private: `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc:444-473` (`same-kinds?` / `wire=`).

Public entry: `diff-encode-epochs` (`diff_encode.cljc:898`), in default `:diff` mode, reached from re-frame2-pair-mcp's `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljs:180`) and `snapshot`'s `:epochs` slice (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/snapshot_pipeline.cljs:241`). Pair reads app values as EDN (`nrepl.cljs:775` `edn/read-string`), so a seq arrives as a list and the kind difference reaches the encoder intact.

## Failure scenario

A handler does `(update db :items #(sort-by :id %))` on an already-sorted `:items` vector. `:db-after` now holds a seq, and later `conj` onto it prepends. An agent debugging "why do new items appear at the top?" reads `watch-epochs`:

- Full mode shows `:db-after {:items ({:id 1} {:id 2}) ...}`.
- Default diff mode ships `{:rf.mcp/diff-from :db-before, :sections []}`, which says nothing changed. The decoded `:db-after` has `:items [{:id 1} {:id 2}]`, a vector.

The one epoch the agent needs is the one reported as a no-op.

## Evidence

EXECUTED: a bounded JVM probe against the frozen `src` (run from the scratch dir with Clojure 1.12.0 and Malli 0.16.4). Output:

```
after-edn :items class           = clojure.lang.PersistentList vector? false
(= before after-edn)             = true
encoded :db-after                = {:rf.mcp/diff-from :db-before, :sections []}
decoded :items                   = [{:id 1} {:id 2}] vector? true
decoded pr-str == real pr-str?   = false
full-mode pr-str of :db-after    = {:items ({:id 1} {:id 2}), :n 1}
nested encoded sections          = []            ; [{:tags [:a :b]}] -> [{:tags (:a :b)}]
nested decoded tags vector?      = true
```

Control, both ways: with a real value change in the same slot (`[{:id 1} {:id 2}]` → `({:id 2} {:id 1})`), the encoder emits `[[:items] :assoc ({:id 2} {:id 1})]` and the decoded value is a list equal to the real one. So the probe can see a patch, and the zero above is the defect rather than a blind instrument.

The logic sits outside any reader conditional. CLJS `=` also equates `[1 2]` and `(1 2)`, so pair's CLJS build behaves the same. `diff_encode_test.clj` has no kind case (a search for `list|seq|kind` finds only section-kind and patch-list hits). Tracker: no earlier ruling. rf2-fzbj.9 / rf2-gwye.32 fixed this class in dedup only, and rf2-ntbd1 was only about where the codec lives.

## Smallest fix

Make the no-change test kind-aware, using the same equivalence dedup uses. Lift `same-kinds?` / `wire=` out of `dedup.cljc` into a shared place, or make them public. Then in `collect-patches-into`, treat `(= a b)` without same kinds as a whole-leaf `[path :assoc b]`, and apply the same rule in the vector-element guard. For the map-key sub-case, emit dissoc plus assoc when the paired key differs in kind. The extra walk only touches subtrees that are already `=`. Over pair's EDN transport the `=` walk already visits those subtrees in full, so the added cost is a constant factor on unchanged data.

Fence: `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode.cljc`, `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc` (only if the helper is shared from there), `tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode_test.clj`, and optionally one sentence in `tools/mcp-base/spec/diff-encode.md`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `tools/mcp-base` (JVM; `diff_encode_test`). The change is not inside a reader conditional, so the JVM lane grades it.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab` JVM suite (`wire_vocab_test.clj` drives `diff-encode-epochs`).
- Optional CLJS confirmation: `tools/mcp-base`'s `cljs_branches_cljs_test` (shadow-cljs lane, machine-wide exclusive).

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== FIX LANDED ON PR #10322 (worker mcp-3x7nj, 2026-09-24 09:50 AUSEST) ==

Verdict: FIXED. The premise held at trunk 23f1406306. Reproduced with a JVM probe: before `{:items [{:id 1} {:id 2}] :n 1}` and after `{:items ({:id 1} {:id 2}) :n 1}` encoded to `{:rf.mcp/diff-from :db-before, :sections []}`, and the decoded `:items` was `[{:id 1} {:id 2}]` (vector? true).

Fix:

- `diff_encode.cljc` requires dedup and uses `wire=` for the no-change test in both the top-level `collect-patches-into` arm and the same-length vector guard. An `=` pair of different kinds falls through to the structural arms, so the patch lands on the slot whose kind changed: `[[:rows 0 :tags] :assoc (:a :b)]`, not the whole of `:rows`.
- Map-key sub-case: when `find` pairs `k` with an `=` key of another kind, the encoder emits `[p :dissoc]` then `[p :assoc bv]`, both under b's own key. The two share one path, so the stable section sort keeps the `:dissoc` first. `assoc` alone would keep the old key object.
- `dedup.md` Scope lists `wire=`, and `diff-encode.md` gains one paragraph.

Regressions in `diff_encode_test.clj`:

- `collect-patches-lands-a-nested-kind-change-on-its-own-slot`
- `diff-encode-reports-a-map-key-respelled-in-another-kind`
- Control: `collect-patches-real-change-in-a-kind-changed-slot-still-patches`.

Every kind assertion checks `list?` / `vector?` explicitly, because `=` erases kind in the assertions too.

Control, shown red: with bare `=` planted back at all three sites, mcp-base `clojure -M:test` exited 1 with 8 failures across the three regression tests, at the same 295 tests / 1052 assertions as the green run. The change is not inside a reader conditional, so the JVM lane grades it. The optional CLJS confirmation was not run, because the lane was not granted.
Merged-PR audit #10322 (eec6b9a6c4a77a8ecf9ee3882f7c03b1eef374e3; merged 2026-09-24T00:03:11Z). Completeness: All four MCP findings are addressed in both consumers and the shared wire layer: over-cap failure flag, token units, sequential collection-kind changes including map keys, and an unencodable Instant marker preserving the verdict. Correctness: Checked both ResultIO adapters, token selector, wire equality recursion, ordered dissoc/assoc key replacement, and JVM/CLJS scalar predicate branches. Accepted mcp-base 295/1052, Story-MCP 308/1794, wire-vocab 92/1038, negative controls and CI pair 1236/4581 plus live overflow conformance. title: story-mcp: agent-facing tool text contradicts the registry — get-variant claims :extends is applied at registration, get-story-instructions lists :expect as a variant slot the closed schema refuses
description:
## Defect

Two pieces of agent-facing tool text, the prose an AI reads from `tools/list` and from `get-story-instructions`, state registry behaviour that the code contradicts. An agent that follows either one does the wrong thing.

1. `get-variant`'s descriptor says it returns "one variant's full body (the resolved EDN, with `:extends` already applied at registration time)". Its example 2 shows a child's body "merged from" its parent. The registrar does not do that. `reg-variant*` stores the raw body with `:extends` intact, and the plan compiler is the single merge authority at compile time (spec/017:1322-1325). `get-variant` returns that raw side-table body (`with-variant` → `rf.story/variant->edn`). For a child variant the agent sees only the child's own delta: no inherited `:args`, `:setup`, `:network` or `:decorators`. It is told this is the fully resolved body, so it reasons from "this variant has no args" when the run uses the parent's. `explain-variant` is the tool that returns the resolved view.
2. `get-story-instructions` lists `:expect` among the `reg-variant` body slots. `:expect` is a PLAN key (`[:expect :checks]` / `[:expect :assertions]`), not a variant slot. The variant body schema is closed, so a `register-variant` body written from the instructions with `:expect` is refused with `:rf.error/variant-shape`. The real slots, `:checks` and `:assertions`, are not in the list.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc:533` (descriptor sentence) and `:536` (example 2), for `tool-get-variant` at 119-124.
- `tools/story-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn`: the committed manifest carries the same description string, so it regenerates with the fix.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc:35`: the `reg-variant` slot line of `story-instructions-text`, served by `get-story-instructions` (84-98).
- Contract being contradicted:
  - `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:1322-1325` ("the registrar stores it raw with `:extends` intact, and the plan compiler is the single merge authority");
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc:810-1015`, the closed `:rf/variant` map, which has no `:expect` slot and does have `:checks` (907) and `:assertions` (908);
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:1198`, where `[:expect :checks]` lives on the plan.
- Story-MCP's own test already records the raw storage: `tools/story-mcp/test/re_frame/story_mcp/wire_encodability_test.clj:358-361`.

Public entry points: `tools/list` (descriptor text), `tools/call get-variant`, `tools/call get-story-instructions`, `tools/call register-variant`.

## Failure scenario

1. The author has `(reg-variant :story.cart/base {:args {:qty 7 :label "from-base"}})` and `(reg-variant :story.cart/child {:extends :story.cart/base})`. An agent calls `get-variant {"variant-id":"story.cart/child"}` and receives `{:doc "child" :extends :story.cart/base :source …}`, with no `:args`. Its tool description promised the resolved body, so it concludes the child renders with no args, or copies this body as a "complete" starting point. `explain-variant` on the same id reports `:effective-args {:qty 7 :label "from-base"}`.
2. The agent follows `get-story-instructions`, writes `register-variant {:body "{:doc \"x\" :expect {:checks [:check/a]}}"}`, and gets `isError true`, `Registration failed: … unknown variant slot(s) :expect`, `:explain-humanized {:expect ["disallowed key"]}`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as process-local JVM probes against the frozen tree (`java … clojure.main`, classpath from `clojure -Spath -A:test` in `tools/story-mcp`):

- (1) `get-variant` on the child returned body `{:doc "child", :extends :story.probe/base, :source {…}}`, with no `:args`. `explain-variant` on the same id returned `:effective-args {:qty 7, :label "from-base"}`. The live descriptor read `Return one variant's full body (the resolved EDN, with `:extends` already applied at registration time).`
- (2) The instructions string matches `reg-variant[^\n]*:expect`, and `register-variant` with an `:expect` body returned `isError=true`, `:rf.error :rf.error/variant-shape`, `:explain-humanized {:expect ["disallowed key"]}`. CONTROL: the same call with `{:doc "x" :args {:a 1}}` registered, `:registered? true`.
- Tracker: `get-variant`, `already applied`, `story-instructions-text` and `get-story-instructions` turn up no bead on either sentence.

## Smallest fix

1. Reword `get-variant`'s descriptor to "the registered body as authored (raw side-table value; `:extends` / `:compose` are NOT resolved here — call `explain-variant` for the resolved plan, `:effective-args` included)" and drop example 2. Regenerate `tool-descriptors.edn` (`cd tools/story-mcp && clojure -M:gen`).
2. In `story-instructions-text`, replace `:expect` with `:checks :assertions` on the `reg-variant` line.

While there, the same text says "Seven canonical tags ship pre-registered" when twelve do (the five `:state/*` tags are canonical too), and "NO closures, NO fns" when `[:assert-db path :pred f]` is a supported form. Both are cheap to correct in the same edit and not worth a bead of their own.

Fence: `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc`, `tools/story-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn` (generated). No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- `cd tools/story-mcp && clojure -M:gen --check` for the descriptor manifest drift gate (also `test.yml`).
- `clojure -M:test` for the suite. No test pins either sentence today. The pattern `already applied|:expect\b` finds 0 hits under `tools/story-mcp/test`. As a control, the same pattern finds the 4 source/manifest sites cited above (`docs.cljc:533,536`, `dev.cljc:35`, `tool-descriptors.edn:13`). The `\b` keeps `:expected` out.

JVM lane only.

## Decision needed

No.

title: xray edn-inspector: diff-mode zoom into a key added this epoch diffs against the whole before-root
description:
## Defect

In the Xray EDN inspector's DIFF mode, a zoom into a key that was ADDED this epoch compares the zoomed AFTER subtree against the WHOLE before-root. The before side's path resolution falls back to the whole value when the zoom path does not resolve in the before value. So the zoomed pane shows a large spurious diff where it should show a plain addition.

This is distinct from the `:added?` missing-sentinel case, which already renders correctly. Here the key is absent from a real before map.

## Where

## Correction

When the zoom path resolves in the after value but not in the before value, resolve the before side to the missing sentinel rather than to the whole before-root, so the zoomed subtree reads as added. That is the same rendering the `:added?` path already uses. The mirror case, a key removed this epoch and zoomed from the before side, should read as removed if the same fallback applies there; check it and cover it only if it shares the defect.

## Control

A diff-mode test that zooms into a key present in `after` and absent from `before` goes red with the fix removed, because it compares against the whole before-root. With the fix it renders the subtree as an addition. The existing 25.2 zoom tests stay green.
