title: story-authoring-data: a published static export compiles out :sub-overrides (goog.DEBUG gate), so pinned variants render real subscription values, and spec 013's stripped table omits it
description:
## Defect

A published Story static export (`shadow-cljs release`, `:closure-defines {re-frame.story.config/static-mode? true}`) compiles the whole `:sub-overrides` seam out. `goog.DEBUG` is false there, and both halves of the seam sit behind `rf.interop/debug-enabled?`:
- Story's React-context carriage (`sub-override-provider`);
- core's `subscribe` consult (`resolve-sub-override`).

Every variant whose shown state comes from `:sub-overrides` therefore renders its REAL subscription values in the published export, not the pinned ones. `:sub-overrides` is one of the three rungs of spec 017's fidelity ladder (`#{:real-setup :db-seed :sub-overrides}`). In practice the export shows the default or empty state under the variant's name: "error banner", "loading", and so on.

Spec 013's "What gets stripped" table is the page a publisher reads to learn what a static export loses, and it does not mention this. Its `goog.DEBUG` row names only "trace listener emit, source-coord DOM stamp". The only record is a docstring inside `sub_overrides.cljc`.

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/sub_overrides.cljc:239-254`: the docstring states "Dev/tool builds only: under `goog.DEBUG=false` (e.g. the `:advanced` static-export release) … the whole sub-override seam is compiled out". The body is `(if rf.interop/debug-enabled? [:r> (.-Provider …) …] child)`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1747-1749`: `(when (and rf.interop/debug-enabled? (not superseded?)) (resolve-sub-override frame-id query-v))`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:217`: `debug-enabled?` is `goog/DEBUG`.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:2090-2102`: `:story-static/counter-with-stories` defines only `static-mode? true`.
- Contract gap:
  - `tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md:344-356` (§What gets stripped, with no `:sub-overrides` row);
  - `:357+` (§Downstream pattern, which tells an app to publish its own export the same way).
- Public entry: `npm run story:build` / an app's own `:story-static/<app>` release build of any story set that uses `:sub-overrides`. In this repo `examples/core/login/stories.cljs` and `examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.cljs` author them.

## Failure scenario

An app declares:

```
(reg-variant :story.login/error {:sub-overrides {[:login/error] "Bad password"}})
```

Its view renders the error banner from `@(subscribe [:login/error])`. In the dev workshop the banner shows. In the published static export the provider is not mounted and `subscribe` never consults the override, so the variant titled "error" renders no banner.

The export's own smoke only checks the selected variant's title (spec 013 §smoke, step 4), so nothing catches it.

## Evidence

This is INSPECTED, not executed: confirming it would need a shadow-cljs release build, which the review wave forbids. Confidence comes from:
- both gates being plain `debug-enabled?` tests;
- `goog.DEBUG` being false under a shadow `release` unless a build overrides it, and the static build overriding only `static-mode?`;
- the implementing namespace's own docstring stating the compile-out explicitly.

The code is deliberate, since the seam is dev-only by core design. The defect is that the static-build contract hides it from the person publishing.

No tracker duplicate. `bd search` for sub-override together with static, release, debug-enabled or `goog.DEBUG` finds no bead on it. rf2-cljo6 (Xray absent from static exports, accepted) is the analogous ruling for Xray, and 013's stripped table does record that loss, in its rf2-n7lql / rf2-n440v rows.

## Smallest fix

Add a row to spec 013 §What gets stripped:

| `:sub-overrides` pins | `goog.DEBUG`-gated in core `subscribe` and in Story's provider; a static export renders real subscription values, so publish `:real-setup` / `:db-seed` variants or accept the gap |

Optionally, the static shell could badge a `:sub-overrides` variant as "pins unavailable in static export". It already knows `static-mode?` and the plan's `:fidelity` set.

Fence: `tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md`, plus optionally a canvas badge in the story UI slice. No hot-zone file is touched.

## Gates

- `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the spec page (links and anchors only). Check the new table row's column count by hand.
- If the optional badge is taken, it is CLJS UI code, graded only by `npm run test:cljs` / the browser lane.

## Decision needed

Yes, one choice. Should the static export (A) document the loss, as with rf2-cljo6's accepted Xray loss? Or should it (B) keep the seam alive, e.g. by building the static export with `goog.DEBUG` true or by giving Story its own non-`goog.DEBUG` override path? A is one table row. B changes the release posture of a published bundle.
notes:

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.31.5.static-export-drops-sub-overrides.md in the mayor checkout. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so that path is a convenience that can rot; the findings below stand on their own.

Read at trunk 805612eef6 (= local origin/main; HEAD 4fe0cbe915 is one beads-only checkpoint ahead). tools/story unchanged since 034d0c8fc8. The core gate this bead cites at subs.cljc:1747-1749 has MOVED to subs.cljc:1817-1818 (b896ae1ca8), with the same code.

RECOMMENDATION: A. Add one :sub-overrides row to tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md section What gets stripped (currently :344-355); do not keep the seam alive in release bundles. Precedent: rf2-cljo6 (Mike ruled A for the Xray static-export loss; "(B) is DECLINED ... needs a new bead and a demonstrated consumer, neither of which exists today").

Decisive findings, inline:
1. ZERO shipped stories use :sub-overrides. rg ":sub-overrides" over examples/, testbeds/, tools/story/testbeds/, tools/xray/testbeds/ gives 3 hits and ALL are prose saying the variant does NOT use them (examples/core/login/stories.cljs:211, examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.cljs:50 and :227). RULING: A. Document the loss where a publisher reads it. The `:sub-overrides` seam stays dev-only, as core designs it, and a published Story static export renders a pinned variant with its REAL subscription values. Two edits, docs only: one row in tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md §What gets stripped, and one sentence in the tutorial beside the pin snippet (docs/story/03-fidelity-ladder.md §Rung 3). Keeping the seam alive in release bundles (B) is DECLINED, not parked, on the same terms Mike set for Xray in rf2-cljo6: anyone reaching for it later needs a new bead and a demonstrated consumer.

Decision needed (the description's A-or-B question): answered, A. The dossier recommended A; Codex recommended a narrow B. How that was resolved is below. No hot-zone file is touched (B would have touched two).

--- WHY ---

1. There is no consumer. At trunk 7fc78b7b72, `git grep -n -F ":sub-overrides"` over examples/, testbeds/, tools/story/testbeds/ and tools/xray/testbeds/ returns 3 lines, and ALL THREE are prose saying the variant does NOT use pins: examples/core/login/stories.cljs:211, examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.cljs:50 and :227. The exposure is downstream publishers who follow the tutorial (docs/story/03-fidelity-ladder.md teaches pins as "the fastest design-state path") and then spec 013's Downstream pattern.
2. The precedent is Mike's, and its criterion fits. rf2-cljo6 (closed 2026-09-21) ruled a published static export may lose a dev-time capability, and set the bar for restoring one: "(B) is DECLINED, not parked ... Anyone reaching for it later needs a new bead and a demonstrated consumer, neither of which exists today." Neither exists here either.
3. B is a core contract change for zero users. The seam is dev-only BY DESIGN at every layer, verified at trunk: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/sub_overrides.cljc `override-provider` (:252, `(if rf.interop/debug-enabled? [:r> (.-Provider ...) ...] child)`, whose docstring states the compile-out); implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1817-1818 (`(when (and rf.interop/debug-enabled? (not superseded?)) (resolve-sub-override frame-id query-v))`; the bead's :1747-1749 cite has moved); implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/sub_override_context.cljs:55 (no context in production); implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:217 (`debug-enabled?` is `goog/DEBUG`). spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2013 titles the contract "The sub-override subscribe seam (debug-gated)", and implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:2090-2102 builds `:story-static/counter-with-stories` with only `re-frame.story.config/static-mode? true`, its comment reading "The published export is dev-tool-free". B means a new core-owned closure-define across core `subscribe` (the hottest read path), the adapter context, Story's provider, spec/006 (HOT ZONE) and implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (HOT ZONE), plus a step every downstream publisher must copy.
4. The ecosystem already treats pins as the rung to upgrade before evidence matters. The skills teach "A variant that pins subscription values with `:sub-overrides` shows a picture, not evidence", and `re-frame.story.ui.view-state/upgrade-snippet` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/view_state.cljc:410) writes the `:real-setup` form that replaces a pin. `:db-seed` and `:setup` are not debug-gated and survive a release build. So a publisher has a supported path, and the doc row can name it.

--- WHERE THE TWO RECOMMENDATIONS DIFFERED ---

Codex argued for a narrow B: a published playground should show the scenario the author selected, an "error" variant silently rendering idle breaks that, Storybook's mocking works in static builds, and cljo6 was about a missing TOOL rather than changed CONTENT. That is a fair product argument and it is recorded here. It does not carry the ruling, for three reasons: the stance ("not over-engineering or gold plating"), the absence of any consumer, and the cost landing on a core contract and two hot-zone files rather than on Story. Codex's own fallback is adopted in full: "If implementation is deferred, document the limitation in both Spec 013 and the fidelity tutorial now, but keep it recorded as a capability gap rather than silently redefining what a shared variant means." So the row states a LIMITATION of the export, not a new meaning for `:sub-overrides`, and the tutorial gets the sentence the dossier had marked optional.

1. tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md §What gets stripped: the table is 2 columns (`| Surface | Why |`) with 8 rows at trunk. Add one row. Suggested wording (the implementer may tighten it):

Publish `:setup` / `:db-seed` variants for states that must survive (`re-frame.story.ui.view-state/upgrade-snippet` writes the `:real-setup` form), or accept the gap |

2. docs/story/03-fidelity-ladder.md §Rung 3, after the pin snippet: one sentence saying pins are a dev-build feature, compiled out of a published static export, so a state you intend to publish should use `:db-seed` or real setup.
3. Optional, not required: the same clause in tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md §View-state subscription overrides (:736-746 already says "dev-only ... it DCEs in production"; naming the static export there is a courtesy).
4. NOT in scope: the sidebar fidelity chip (ui/sidebar.cljs:410-412 is not static-gated, so it still shows `:sub-overrides` in an export). It accurately describes the variant's declared rung; a "pins unavailable in static export" treatment is CLJS UI code for no consumer. File it only if a publisher asks.

Gates: `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers tools/*/spec and docs/ links and anchors. `mkdocs build --strict` (or `python -m mkdocs build --strict`) builds docs/story. Neither validates table shape or prose, so say in the PR body that the row's column count and wording were checked by hand.

--- IF B IS EVER TAKEN (carried from Codex so the analysis is not lost; not to be dispatched now) ---

- Never build the export with `goog.DEBUG` true. That undoes every release elision: trace emission, schema validation, source-coord stamps.
- Introduce ONE internal compile-time capability, owned BELOW Story (core must not depend on `re-frame.story.config`), that defaults to `goog.DEBUG` and that the Story export recipe selects. Apply it together to context creation, context read, Story's provider and core's consult. Ordinary app releases must still compile the seam away; keep an elision check for that.
- History: commit e7636a59 added the provider gate to fix a static-export crash after production context creation was removed. Removing that gate alone reintroduces the nil-context crash, and changing the context gate alone leaves the consult disabled. It is a coordinated change, not one conditional.

title: FALSE: Story share can label an ambient-args variant fully reproducible after silently losing its plan
description:
Discovered while auditing PR #10315 (43bf4ee37ce115e4cfae1382989dc8c5f9df00ab), source rf2-3x7nj.28.3. Its implementation notes explicitly leave ui/share.cljs current-share-report on the same bare-compile defect fixed for Docs. No exact open corrective Bead exists.

At tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs:283-292, current-share-report calls (variant-plan vid) with no :run-args and catches any failure as nil. A valid variant relying on required props supplied by its story therefore loses its plan for sharing. egress.cljc:175-218 derives function-valued network/subscription/setup/script downgrade reasons from that plan, and classify:262-269 starts at :full. With empty cell overrides and no import drops, the missing plan yields a falsely fully-reproducible report even when the real plan contains an existing partial/view-only reason.

Example: registered component with required :label; story :args {:label "Go"}; variant inherits the component/args and declares a function-valued network stub (already supported/classified by world-reasons). Running uses the ambient args and succeeds. Sharing drops the plan on missing :label, omitting :network-reply-fn and reporting :full instead of the classifier's :partial.

Correction: compile the selected cell with the appropriate existing run-arg layer helper, keeping its plan consistent with the shared cell. Preserve the existing classifier and best-effort treatment of genuinely uncompileable plans. Add a regression with an ambient-required prop and an existing plan-derived downgrade reason, plus a plain full-reproducibility control. No new sharing API or privacy gate is needed.

Evidence: source/data-flow review and the implementer's acknowledged uncorrected bare share compile. Accepted reported PR tests; no redundant suite rerun.
notes:
## FIXED: PR #10343 (worker story3-3x7nj, 2026-09-24 AUSEST)

- The bare compile threw `:rf.error/story-view-args-invalid`, the plan was dropped, and `egress/classify` read `:full`.
- Compiled as the cell, the same variant reads `:partial` with `[:network-reply-fn]`.

**Fix:**
- `ui/share/current-share-report` compiles through `re-frame.story.cell-plan/cell-plan` over the shell's `:active-modes` and this variant's `:cell-overrides`. Those are the inputs the Copy EDN snippet's `effective-args` already reads.
- This is the same shared helper as the rf2-yfwfa fix.
- The classifier is unchanged, and so is the best-effort nil on a plan that genuinely cannot compile.

**Regression:** `ui/share_egress_cljs_test.cljs` `report-keeps-the-plan-of-a-variant-that-leaves-a-prop-to-its-story` covers the ambient-required prop with the fn-valued stub, which must read `:partial [:network-reply-fn]`. Its control is a plain variant of the same story, which must read `:full` with no reasons.

**Control:** under a coordinator-granted local `npm run test:cljs`, planting the share compile back to a bare `variant-plan` turned both assertions red. The restore was verified by blob hash.

**Gates:** CI green on head 1ec5585e11 (CLJS :node-test 12752/64652).

Completeness: Both ambient-args audit findings are corrected through the existing run-arg layers, including global-args cache invalidation and active-mode/cell-override share inputs. Canvas-scoped DOM lookup and exported positional-selector hints cover 30.5. The already-fixed rerun verdict gets the requested fail/pass, in-flight and single-execution regression. All source Beads are already closed by their owners; no statuses changed. Correctness: Read every production change and traced cell-plan to the same run-arg-layers used by runtime, the invalid-prop recovery, and the actual persistent outer canvas hook (including sized viewports). title: examples-scripts: check-examples-assets focus-ring, cells-grid and responsive-shell contracts pass on a COMMENTED-OUT rule (raw-CSS regex; the file strips comments everywhere else)
description:
## Defect

Three of the shared-CSS "this rule must be present" contracts in `checkSharedTree` run their regex over the RAW stylesheet text. So a rule that has been commented out, which is inert in the browser, still satisfies them. The three contracts are:

- the keyboard focus ring (rf2-mon7tz);
- the 7GUIs cells-grid compact width (rf2-gv5xd);
- the inline-Xray shell's narrow-viewport stacking media query (rf2-y82dk9).

Deleting any of those rules turns the gate red. Commenting it out, the other common way to remove CSS, leaves the gate green while the page loses the accessibility or layout behaviour the gate was built to hold.

The same file already strips comments before every other CSS scan: `extractCssImports` and `extractCssUrls` (rf2-lvw3z9), HTML (rf2-j538f7.28), and the `og.svg` palette check. That shows this class was judged real and fixed elsewhere, but not here.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`, `examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs`:

- `:1822`: `/\.cells-grid\s+input\s*\{[^}]*width:\s*56px/m.test(structure)`, over the raw `structure` read at `:1807`.
- `:1837-1840`: `/@media[^{]*max-width[\s\S]*?\.rf2-testbed-shell\s*\{[^}]*flex-direction:\s*column/m.test(structure)`.
- `:1925-1927`: `/input:focus-visible[^{]*\{[^}]*box-shadow:[^}]*--ex-accent-deep/m.test(style)`, over the raw `style` read at `:1783`.
- The helper that should feed them is `stripCssComments`, at `:520-522`.

Reached from `scanAll` (`:1951-1958`), which the CLI and the always-run `test:scripts` LIVE cases call (`implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs:311-318` and the contract cases after it).

## Failure scenario

Someone wraps `input:focus-visible, textarea:focus-visible, select:focus-visible { … box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--ex-accent-deep); }` in `/* … */` in `examples/_shared/css/style.css`. Maybe they are debugging, or trying a different ring. Every example's form controls lose their keyboard focus indicator. `check-examples-assets` reads 0 errors and `test:scripts` stays green. The same holds for commenting out `.cells-grid input { width: 56px }` (the spreadsheet grid blows out) or the `@media (max-width: 900px)` shell block (the Xray shell overflows on narrow viewports).

## Evidence

EXECUTED with `probe-css-comments.cjs`. It is read-only: modified CSS text is injected through an in-memory io into the real `checkSharedTree`, and nothing is written.

| Case | Errors |
|---|---|
| BASELINE, real files | 0 |
| CONTROL: focus-visible rule DELETED | 1 |
| CONTROL: `.cells-grid input` rule DELETED | 1 |
| CONTROL: 900px stacking media query DELETED | 1 |
| focus-visible rule COMMENTED OUT | **0** |
| `.cells-grid input` rule COMMENTED OUT | **0** |
| 900px stacking media query COMMENTED OUT | **0** |

The rules were located by their exact text, so each edit touched only the intended rule.

Tracker: `focus-visible`, `cells-grid`, `commented-out` and `stripCssComments` each return 0 beads. The same instrument returns rf2-3p85d for `structure.css`, so it does find beads. The prior `_shared` review, rf2-c5hp1, records no ruling on this.

## Smallest fix

Evaluate the three presence regexes over `stripCssComments(structure)` and `stripCssComments(style)`. For symmetry, run the two absence checks (`:1811` global `input[type="text"]`, `:1938` amber ring) over the stripped text too; today a comment that merely names them false-reds.

Add three test cases to `check-examples-assets.test.cjs` in the probe's shape: a commented-out rule must read red.

Fence:
- `examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs`
- `implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs`

No hot-zone file. It can share a PR with the sibling page-local-staging finding.

## Gates

- `npm run test:scripts` from `implementation/` (node `--test`, no shadow-cljs).
- `node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs`, expected to stay 0 on the real tree.

The new red cases are the plant.

## Decision needed

No. The file already rules that commented-out CSS is inert (rf2-lvw3z9); this applies that ruling to the three remaining checks.

title: story play: canvas-scoped DOM resolution cannot reach portalled content (modals) — fall back to document for non-positional selectors
description:
## Defect

PR #10343 (rf2-3x7nj.30.5, merged at trunk f3675052af) scoped Story's play DOM resolution to the canvas root whenever the shell has mounted one (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/dom.cljc`). That was the review's fix: before it, a positional `tag:nth-of-type(N)` selector resolved document-wide and could hit the shell's own chrome.

The consequence, reported by the #10343 worker: inside the Story shell, a play step can no longer reach an element the view renders OUTSIDE the canvas. The usual case is a portal into `document.body`, which is how most modal, dialog, popover and toast components render.

- A recorded click on a modal's button produces a selector that resolves to nothing under the canvas, so the step fails in the shell. The same step still works headless, or wherever no canvas root is mounted.
- No variant in the tree has such a step today, but portalled dialogs are common, and recording one is exactly what an author will try.

## Ruling (mayor, under the stance; no operator decision needed)

- **Canvas first.** A selector resolves under the canvas root first, when one is mounted.
- **Fallback for stable selectors only.** If it matches NOTHING there, and the selector is NOT positional (`selector/positional?` from #10343 answers that), fall back to the whole document. Stable selectors are id, `data-testid`, role/aria and text.
- **Positional selectors never fall back.** They are the ambiguous kind #10343 fenced, and they already carry the TODO-harden hint.

This keeps #10343's protection exactly where it applied (positional selectors) and restores portal reach for the selectors authors should be writing anyway.

## Correction

Implement the fallback in `play/dom.cljc`'s resolver, reusing `selector/positional?`. Update the one sentence #10343 added to `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` about where selectors resolve.

Tests, beside #10343's `dom_canvas_scope_dom_cljs_test.cljs`:
- a stable selector for an element portalled into `document.body` resolves while a canvas root is mounted;
- a positional selector with no canvas match does NOT fall back;
- a stable selector that matches inside the canvas still prefers the canvas copy over an identical one in the shell chrome.

## Decision needed

No (ruled above).
notes: Merged-PR audit #10349 (52119f573f7cb71531ff38afabd74c722f1246db; merged 2026-09-24T04:02:47Z). Completeness: Portal DOM lookup now falls back to the document only after a canvas miss for a non-positional selector, while canvas matches retain priority. The prior timer-wait finding is corrected by accounting for replay time already emitted. All remaining uoeyl prose items 15, 16 and 18 are corrected. Owners already closed all three source Beads; no statuses changed. Correctness: Read all production and prose changes plus the translator controls. The 0/40/80 case now emits wait 80; emitted waits count toward the replay clock, ignored entries preserve its state, and ordinary gaps retain the threshold. Query and query-all share the same fallback rule. Accepted reported planted-fix CI six browser, three replay and four JVM failures followed by final browser 1142/6268, node 12762/65202 and Story JVM 2089/7869 green; 84 static checks passed. No tests rerun or actionable residual found. Implementation quality: A single covered-time accumulator fixes the bounded timing defect without a scheduler. DOM lookup reuses the existing positional predicate and preserves canvas priority, restoring portal use with no new public API. Prose accurately describes the shared plan fold and framework-base fixture reachability. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: examples-real-apps: realworld_resources editor entry clears the shared :editor/save instance, which ABORTS an in-flight save/delete and suppresses its :invalidates — contradicting the file's own 'the mutation runs to completion' and the pair's 'abort is not proof'
description:
## Defect

`realworld_resources`' article editor dispatches `[:rf.mutation/clear {:instance :editor/save}]` on EVERY editor entry. The shared `save-instance` also carries the DELETE. The file's own WRITE OWNERSHIP passage promises the opposite: "The mutation runs to completion wherever the reader goes" (`article_editor.cljs:386`).

`:rf.mutation/clear` does not merely forget the instance. `clear-handler` BEST-EFFORT ABORTS the in-flight attempt, marks its work row `:cancelled`, and drops the instance, so the late reply is stale-suppressed. A save or delete still in flight when the reader enters another editor therefore:

- has its HTTP request aborted. The server may already have performed the write. The http twin states this law outright: "an aborted request is no proof the server declined to perform the write" / "abort is not proof" (`realworld_http/profile.cljs:470-473`, `:492`);
- never runs its `:invalidates`, because the reply that would run them is suppressed. So the article lists, the session feed and the tag list keep serving the pre-write cache: a deleted article stays listed, and an edited title stays old.

Reads here are fresh for `stale-after-ms` 60000 (`resources.cljs:41-45`). A revisit inside that window is a cache HIT that shows the stale rows, and nothing marks them stale.

The comment's second paragraph (`:397-403`) presents that clearing as the benign half of the ownership story: "the runtime suppresses a late result for a cleared instance, so the new session starts with usable controls". It never mentions the abort or the lost invalidation. A reader copies "clear the shared instance on entry" as the pattern for starting a fresh form session over an in-flight write.

## Where

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/article_editor.cljs:279-290`: `:editor/initialise` clears `save-instance` at `:290`.
- `:292-326`: `:editor/load-article` clears it at `:316`.
- `:152-154`: `save-instance` is the single id `:editor/save`.
- `:496-508`: `:editor/delete` fires the delete under the same instance.
- `:241-257`: the delete's `:invalidates` covers `[:article slug]`, `[:article-list]`, `[:feed]` and `[:tags]`.
- `:384-403`: the WRITE OWNERSHIP passage.
- Runtime: `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1495-1583`, `clear-handler`. Its docstring says "Best-effort aborts any in-flight attempt for a cleared instance ... the reply handler's existence check suppresses it". The abort fx is at `:1579-1583`.

## Failure scenario

INSPECTED ONLY. The app is `.cljs`, and no browser or shadow-cljs is allowed in this review. Live-API mode, or any backend slower than a click:

1. Load `/` so the Global Feed list is cached (fresh for 60 s).
2. Open your own article alpha, then Edit (`/editor/alpha`). With the draft clean, click Delete Article. The DELETE is in flight under `:editor/save`.
3. Before it answers, click the header's New Article link (`core.cljs:109`). The draft is clean, so `:editor/can-leave?` lets the navigation through. `/editor` matches, and `:editor/initialise` dispatches `:rf.mutation/clear {:instance :editor/save}`.
4. `clear-handler` aborts the DELETE and drops the instance. If the server had already applied it, alpha is gone server-side.
5. Click Home. The `[:article-list]` entry is still fresh, so it is a cache hit that lists alpha. Clicking it reaches a 404 article page.

The same path through Publish on a dirty draft goes through the can-leave confirm. A reader who confirms has been told nothing about losing the save's invalidation or its request.

Control: the nav-token gate at `:479` already refuses a reply issued under an earlier navigation. So the clear is NOT needed to stop a late continuation acting on the new page. That is the half `:393-395` credits it with.

## Evidence

- Code read at the lines above.
- The abort is established from `clear-handler`'s body: it collects `in-flight` work ids and emits `abort-fx` for each.
- The `:invalidates` loss is read off the runtime. `succeeded-handler` (`mutation_events.cljc:1681`) looks up the live instance and, when it is nil because the instance was cleared, takes the STALE SUPPRESSION branch (`:1726`). That branch writes no durable state and runs no invalidation. Invalidation is step 2 of the live branch only. It also follows from the documented ordering. `:invalidates` runs on the ACCEPTED `:ok` reply, before the `:reply-to` continuation (`article_editor.cljs:36-40`: "AFTER `:invalidates` staled the lists"). A suppressed reply is not accepted.
- Tracker: rf2-gwye.39 ("bind editor write replies to their page") added the nav-token gate and left the entry clears in place. A full-text search finds no bead on entry-clear aborting an in-flight write.

## Smallest fix

Make the editor's write instance per-session: `[:editor/save nav-token]`, minted at submit and delete time from `current-nav-token`, and subscribed by the view under the current nav-token. Then:

- entry need not clear anything, so the old write runs to completion and runs its `:invalidates`;
- its continuation is refused by the existing nav-token gate;
- the refused branch clears its own settled instance, so rows do not accumulate.

Alternatively, keep the single id and clear it on entry ONLY when it is not pending. That preserves the write, but the view would then show the old write's pending state on the new page.

Either way, correct the WRITE OWNERSHIP paragraph at `:397-403` to say what `:rf.mutation/clear` does to an in-flight write. One file, `realworld_resources/article_editor.cljs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- `npm run test:cljs`. The resources app suite (`adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs`) loads the editor, and its existing editor tests must stay green.
- CI's `cljs-examples-compile`.

## Decision needed

Only which of the two fixes. The per-session instance is the one consistent with the passage's own "runs to completion" claim.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 04:37:24 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.42.5.editor-save-instance-per-session.md. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so that path is a convenience that can rot; the findings below stand on their own.

Read at trunk a7913dfad9 (= origin/main). article_editor.cljs is unchanged since 034d0c8fc8.

RECOMMENDATION: fix 1, the per-session instance [:editor/save <nav-token>]. Store the nav-token in the editor slice at entry, execute save and delete under it, and have the view subscribe to it. Drop both entry clears (article_editor.cljs:290, :316). :editor/replied clears its own instance, checking the nav-token BEFORE the status so that a refused :error is retired too. This is closer to an implementation choice than a ruling.

DECISIVE FINDINGS
1. Executed at trunk on the real mutation runtime (the resources_mutation_cljs_test harness, mutation :invalidates #{[:article slug] [:article-list]}):
   - Control, no clear: 0 aborts, invalidation ran, continuation fired 1.
   - AS SHIPPED, clear before the reply: 1 abort, NO invalidation, 1 stale-suppressed, continuation 0.
   - Per-session, no clear: 0 aborts, invalidation ran, and the new session's instance reads nil.
   - Clear-if-not-pending: the write is kept, but the new form reads :pending.
   Runtime: clear-handler mutation_events.cljc:1622-1735 emits the abort; the succeeded-handler stale branch :1878-1893 runs no invalidation.
2. Fix 2 (clear only when not pending) breaks an existing pin, editor-write-continuations-stay-with-the-page-that-issued-them (implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:1982-2003), which asserts "the new session's save control is not busy". The view disables all fields on busy? (:pending? save) (article_editor.cljs:573, :575).
3. Fix 1 is the pattern the same app already uses: the list delete runs under [:delete-article slug] and its own continuation clears it (views.cljs:210, :227-231). settings.cljs clears only from its continuation.

ALSO
- The WRITE OWNERSHIP claim is at :387, not :386.
- rf2-3x7nj.11.2 (closed) rolls back only OPTIMISTIC cleared writes, and the editor's save and delete are not optimistic, so it does not rescue this. rf2-3x7nj.11.3: the editor declares no :populates or :patches, so there is no interaction.
- Acceptance: retarget the :1982 control to the session instance and add an assertion that [:article-list] is stale after the late reply (RED today, GREEN after). The lane is npm run test:cljs plus cljs-examples-compile.
== RULING (mayor's ruling agent, 2026-09-24 13:17:33 AUSEST, under the project stance; dossier + Codex Recommendation weighed) ==

QUESTION: how should the realworld_resources article editor start a fresh form session without cancelling a save or delete still in flight under its shared :editor/save instance?

OPTIONS (sizes)
- Fix 1, a per-session write instance [:editor/save <nav-token>]. One example file (examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/article_editor.cljs) and one test block. Drops both entry clears. Recommended by the dossier and by Codex.
- Fix 2, keep the shared :editor/save id and clear it on entry only when it is not pending. The same file, with the entry handlers reading pending state. It also inverts a pinned test assertion.
- Neither touches a hot-zone file.

RULING: FIX 1, the per-session instance. The session identity is the navigation token, read where it already lives, not copied into the editor slice. Five parts:
1. The instance for save, delete and the form is [:editor/save nav-token]. Submit and delete read the token with (current-nav-token rt), which both already do for :reply-to. The view reads it through a new sub over the public [:rf/route] runtime sub.
2. Delete both entry clears (:editor/initialise and :editor/load-article).
3. In :editor/replied, ask the nav-token gate BEFORE the status.
   - Refused (issued under a navigation the reader has left), whatever the status: clear the reply's own :instance and stop.
   - Current page, :error: do nothing. The error stays on the instance for a retry.
   - Current page, :ok: clear the reply's :instance and navigate, as today.
4. An error that settles while the reader is still on the page and is then abandoned leaves its settled row. No code for that.
5. Rewrite the WRITE OWNERSHIP passage and the stale docstrings to match.

WHY, AND WHERE I AGREED OR DISAGREED
- Fix 1 over Fix 2: all three (bead, dossier, Codex) agree, and I agree on the evidence.
  - Clear is a CANCELLATION, not a forget. It aborts the request and stale-suppresses the late reply, so the write's :invalidates never run. The file's own claim, "The mutation runs to completion wherever the reader goes" (article_editor.cljs:387), requires that the entry does not clear a live write.
  - Fix 2 keeps the write alive but lets the new form read the old write's :pending?/:error?. The view disables every field on busy? (:573, :575), which breaks the pinned "the new session's save control is not busy" assertion.
  - Fix 2 also leaves a SECOND way to lose the same invalidation, which is Codex's point, confirmed at source. A re-execute under the same instance id mints a new work-id (mutation_events.cljc:1380-1386), and Spec 016 says a reply for a re-executed or cleared instance is stale-suppressed and fires no continuation (spec/016-Resources.md:928). So any second submit in the new session would supersede the old write and drop its :invalidates again.
- Session identity, where I DISAGREE with both the dossier and Codex. Both proposed storing the entry token in the editor slice. I rule the bead's own "smallest fix" spelling instead: derive the instance from the routing nav-token where it already lives.
  - The token is published in the committed route slice BEFORE :on-match is dispatched (routing/events.cljc commit-navigation :229-234 publishes it; the on-match fx follow at :344-345).
  - The public :rf/route runtime sub exposes :nav-token (routing.cljc:405-407). This app already derives page subs from route subs (views.cljs:93-95).
  - This way the instance id and the reply gate compare ONE value read from ONE place. The editor slice stays as its docstring describes it: "The submission lifecycle is deliberately not here" (article_editor.cljs:94-96). No entry handler needs a new coeffect read, and the view cannot show the previous session's instance for the tick between commit and :on-match.
  - The slice-copy version is not wrong. Every commit re-runs :on-match, so the copy equals the current token. It is simply one more moving part.
- Cleanup in :editor/replied, where I side with CODEX's spelling. Clear the reply's own :instance field rather than rebuilding [:editor/save nav-token]. continuation-reply puts :instance on every accepted reply, success and failure alike (mutation_events.cljc:1221-1249, :instance at :1246; used at :2128-2139 and :2401-2408). And it is exactly the app's own precedent: views.cljs :ui/article-deleted destructures {:keys [status instance]} and clears {:instance instance} (:227-233). The gate-before-status order is the dossier's and Codex's shared point, and settings.cljs already does it (the ownership check at :224-226 comes before the status check at :228).
- Residue from an abandoned error, where I side with the DOSSIER (no code) and take CODEX's correction of the wording.
  - Codex is right that it is "proportional to user actions, not a fixed bound". The dossier's "bounded" was loose: one settled :error row, plus its terminal ledger rows, per editor session that fails a write and is then abandoned.

Standing rule for the present-tense epic (the parent of this bead). **The rule is the epic's description plus its newest `== CALIBRATION` note; read both.** This bead is blocked on the pilot, because the rule's final wording comes out of the pilot's calibration.

## Why

Much of the history in the tree was written by agents following their own habits. There is no instruction anywhere asking for bead ids in comments. Without a standing rule, new work grows it back within weeks of the 76-child sweep finishing.

## The work

1. **Add the rule to `CLAUDE.md`.** Put it under §Conventions & Patterns, or a short §Comments section beside it.

2. **Update CLAUDE.md §Architecture Overview's paragraph** on donor references in `spec/`. Its sentence "the donor references that survive in prose are deliberate rather than residue awaiting deletion … never something to delete on sight" is superseded for history by this epic (Mike, 2026-09-24).

3. **Check whether `AGENTS.md` duplicates either passage.** If it does, keep the two in step.

- CLAUDE.md is `w/crlf`: after editing, take its item (e) three numbers with Python and require CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0.

## Fence

`CLAUDE.md`, and `AGENTS.md` only if step 3 finds a duplicate. Nothing else.

title: xstate-parity: an :initial that names no declared state (and a Level-1 snapshot :state that names none) is accepted silently and boots a phantom state; XState refuses both
description:
## Gap

XState v6 (6.0.0-alpha.59) refuses to run a machine whose `initial` names a state that is not declared: `createActor(...).start()` errors the actor with `Initial state not found on "#(machine)"`, and the pure `transition()` throws when the snapshot's state value names a state the machine does not have (`deterministic.test.ts` "should throw an error for transitions from invalid states" / "from invalid substates"; `invalid.test.ts` "should reject transitioning from bad state configs"). A phantom state cannot exist on either path.

re-frame2 accepts `{:initial :zzz :states {:a ...}}` at `reg-machine` / `make-machine-handler` (no `:rf.error/*`), boots the machine into the phantom state (`{:state :zzz}` for a flat machine, `{:state [:p :zzz]}` for a compound whose child `:initial` is undeclared), and from there every event is a benign `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op`: the machine looks alive and silently does nothing. The Level-1 pure call has the same hole: `(machine-transition def {:state :zzz ...} [:GO])` returns `{:status :ok :snapshot {:state :zzz} :fx []}` instead of throwing. The hot-reload reconciler DOES catch a vanished state (`:rf.error/machine-state-not-in-definition`, invariant 3) but only for an already-installed snapshot on re-registration, never at first boot and never on the pure surface. Every transition TARGET is validated at registration (`:rf.error/machine-unresolved-target`); the one state reference that is not a target, `:initial`, is the one left unchecked.

## XState evidence

Executed: `xs/E-7-validation.mjs` -> `xs/E-7-validation.out` — row `initial names missing state | START errors actor: Error: Initial state not found on "#(machine)"`; `invalid.test.ts:89-117` and `deterministic.test.ts:125-139` (fetched to `xs-tests/`) pin the pure-path throws. `xs/E-3-json.out` shows the JSON layer (`createMachineFromConfig`) does NOT check a bad `initial` at construction (`badInitial: no throw`) — the refusal is at start, as for authored machines.

## re-frame2 evidence

Executed at trunk fe8de195bd:
- `jvm/E/E1_graph.clj` -> `E1_graph.out`: `initial-missing-state | ACCEPTED` through `re-frame.machines/make-machine-handler` (37 other defects in the same run were REJECTED with their `:rf.error/machine-*` ids, so the validator was live).
- `jvm/E/E5_initial.clj` -> `E5_initial.out`: flat — `reg-machine: accepted`, `start: {:state :zzz, :data {}, :rf/spawn-counter {}}`, `GO: {:state :zzz ...}`, machine traces `[... :rf.machine/started :rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op ...]`, error traces: none about the state; compound — `start: {:state [:p :zzz] ...}`; Level-1 — `{:status :ok, :snapshot {:state :zzz, :data {}}, :fx []}`.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc` (1930 lines): the only `:initial` checks are presence — compound must declare it (line ~971, `:rf.error/machine-compound-state-missing-initial`) and each parallel region must declare a keyword (line ~513) — never membership of `:states`. `registration.cljc:295-320` reconciles `:state-not-in-definition` only against an EXISTING snapshot.
- spec/005-StateMachines.md:515 says "The snapshot's `:state` slot is already validated at registration time (a transition targeting an unknown state fails registration ...)"; :4257-4270 (Level 1) says programmer-input errors "throw the same `:rf.error/*` ex-info the registration validators throw" and lists "A snapshot whose `:state` is neither keyword nor path" — a keyword that names no state is not covered by either sentence.
- No test pins the case: `rg` over `implementation/machines/test` for an undeclared/unresolved `:initial` returns 0 files (control: `machine-unknown-node-key` is pinned by 2 files; `machine-unresolved-target` by many).
- Tracker: `bd search` for "initial state", "undeclared initial", "phantom state" — 0 each (control: "SCXML" 4).

## Why it matters

A typo in `:initial` (or in a compound's child `:initial`) is the single most common way to write a machine that does nothing, and re-frame2 reports it as a healthy machine ignoring events. An AI scaffolding a machine gets no signal at registration and no error at runtime; the only symptom is "my events are unhandled no-ops", which points at the transition table, not at `:initial`. On the pure Level-1 surface the same phantom lets a test "pass" against a state that does not exist. XState makes both cases impossible.

## Options

1. Registration: extend `validate-machine!` so every `:initial` (root, every compound node, every parallel region body) must resolve to a declared child; reject with `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-target` (it IS an unresolved state reference, and the id already carries "target"/"declared state" semantics) or a new sibling `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-initial`. Runtime-only; spec/005:515 gains one clause. Breaks no valid machine (a machine with an undeclared `:initial` never worked).
2. Additionally, Level-1: make `machine-transition` throw `:rf.error/machine-state-not-in-definition` (or reuse `:rf.error/machine-bad-target`) when the snapshot's `:state` resolves to no declared node, matching XState's pure-path throw. Spec/005 §Level 1 (:4270) gains the case in its "programmer-input errors throw" list. Slightly wider: a hydrated stale snapshot driven through the pure API would now throw instead of no-op — which is what §Snapshot shape invariant 3 already promises for the runtime path.
3. Do nothing and document the phantom. Not recommended: it contradicts spec/005:515's own promise.

## Recommendation

Option 1 now (one validator clause, one error id, one test), option 2 in the same PR if the pure-error-contract test (`machine_pure_error_contract_test.clj`) accommodates it cleanly — it is the same defect on the other surface and XState refuses both.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc` (registration check)
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` and/or `parallel.cljc` (option 2, pure-path throw)
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/` — new pins (registration + pure)
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (:515 and §Level 1 :4270) — HOT ZONE
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Error contract only if a NEW error id is introduced — HOT ZONE (prefer reusing an existing id to avoid touching it)

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines` (JVM); no `#?(:cljs ...)` branch expected, but if `validation.cljc`'s change touches one, `npm run test:cljs`; the conformance corpus is untouched unless a `machine-reg-error-*` fixture is added (`spec/conformance/fixtures/`, capability `:fsm/registration-validation`, 9 fixtures carry it today).

The probe interleaved its own markers: a `:probe/mark` fx placed AFTER the emitting fx in the same event, and markers around each direct call. Results:

Emitted INSIDE a drain. In every case below, the listener ran AFTER the drain: in-drain? false, after the next fx in the same event (whose own marker read in-drain? true), and before dispatch-sync returned.
- `:rf.machine.spawn/spawned` and `:rf.machine.lifecycle/spawned`, from a `:rf.machine/spawn` fx.
- `:rf.machine.timer/scheduled`, from an ordinary `:after` arm on a transition.
- `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled` and `/scheduled`, from the `:rf.machine/hydrate-rearm` fx (the `:emit-scheduled-trace? true` path).
- `:rf.error/machine-action-wrote-db`, from a `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` fx whose patch carries `:db`.
- `:rf.machine/done` and `:rf.machine/destroyed`, from finalize.
- `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled` and `:rf.machine/destroyed`, from an ordinary `[:rf.machine/destroy id]` fx on an actor holding an armed `:after`.
- `/cancelled` and `/scheduled`, from a dynamic-delay re-resolution whose source changed inside an fx.
- A bare `rf.trace/emit!` inside an fx.

Emitted OUTSIDE any drain. In every case below, the listener ran SYNCHRONOUSLY, between the markers around the call, on the emitting stack.
- `/cancelled` and `/scheduled`, from `re-frame.machines.hydrate/rearm-after-timers!` called directly.
- `:rf.machine.spawn/spawned` and `:rf.machine.lifecycle/spawned`, from `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.spawn/spawn-fx` called directly under `rf.frame/call-with-event-owner-token`. This is the harness the incarnation-fence tests use.
- `/cancelled` and `/scheduled`, from a dynamic-delay re-resolution whose source atom was `reset!` outside a drain. On CLJS the ratom flush drives this path.
- A bare `rf.trace/emit!`.

So both comment families are true, each for one path. The code matches spec/009 §Subscription / consumption: public emits raised outside a drain fan out synchronously, and drain-owned emits are delivered at the post-drain boundary, before the operation returns.
- The "post-drain / closed BY CONSTRUCTION" prose describes the IN-DRAIN path: `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc` in the `install-spawn!` docstring and its inner comment on `type-ref-fn`, and the comment before `type-ref-fn` in `spawn-fx*`.
- The "a listener can synchronously destroy A here" prose describes the OUT-OF-DRAIN path: direct calls of the public effect fns and seams, and a watcher-driven re-resolution. It sits in `spawn.cljc` after the `:rf.machine.spawn/spawned` emit, and in `timer.cljc` in the `schedule-after-timer!` docstring, the "The row's listener runs synchronously" comment and the "`rf.trace/emit!` invokes listeners SYNCHRONOUSLY" comment. `lifecycle_fx/update_snapshot.cljc` says the same of its `:db` hard-disallow trace. It then lists the `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled` traces and the `:rf.machine/destroyed` trace among the boundaries "any of which can synchronously destroy A and publish a same-id successor B". It also says "a listener that registers B's handler at `<id>` on that trace's own stack keeps it".
- The probe's destroy-fx case refutes that on the path the paragraph names. In the drain, both traces reach listeners only after the drain has finished.
- spec/009 §Subscription / consumption (lines 638-645) says the opposite: a listener's side effects "cannot influence the drain that produced the event".
- The paragraph's trace clauses hold only when the destroy effect is called directly outside a drain, which is how the fence tests drive it.

title: Xray cascade: a child state's entry/exit action rows take their label and source key from the transition's state, not the declaring state
description:
## What

Worker mengine-v3kl4 reported this after fixing rf2-wnyaf (PR #10427, merged at trunk 910f9a0498). That PR made the `:rf.machine/action-ran` trace carry `:decl-path`, plus `:region` inside a region, for ROOT and REGION-BODY actions. Xray's cascade rows and `format` now read those first, so a root's own entry/exit points at `[:entry]` / `[:exit]` labelled `:rf/root`.

The worker reports that a CHILD state's entry/exit action rows still take their label (and source key) from the surrounding transition's state, not from the state that declares the action. That is the same class of wrong information rf2-wnyaf fixed, one level down: a click-to-source link from a debugging tool pointing at the wrong node.

## Required correction

1. Reproduce first. Take a machine where a transition from `:a` enters `:b` and `:b.c`, each with its own inline `:entry`. See what label and source key Xray's cascade rows give each action.
2. If they are wrong, carry the declaring state's path in the same `:decl-path` field for every state-declared entry/exit action, and have Xray's existing `:decl-path`-first reading label from it.
   - Add no new trace event and no public API.
   - Named actions and transition actions keep their current behaviour.
3. Red first: the child entry rows must resolve to their own declaring state's `[... :entry]` source key.

If the premise does not hold at your trunk, a verified "the premise does not hold" with the evidence is a complete deliverable.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src` (the action-ran emit sites in transition.cljc / parallel.cljc) and `implementation/machines/test`;
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc` and `format.cljc`, and their tests;
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`'s `action-ran` row, if the field's meaning widens (HOT).

## Gates

- `cd implementation/machines && clojure -M:test` and `cd tools/xray && clojure -M:test`, each with the count delta you predicted and the one you got; red-first.
- clj-kondo, WITHOUT `--fail-level error`.
- CLJS lanes via CI.
- CLAUDE.md item (e)'s three numbers on every changed `w/crlf` file.

Reproduced at trunk 910f9a0498, producer-derived: a transition from :a into compound :b (initial :c) gave :b's inline :entry the source key [:states :b :states :c :entry] and label [:b :c] (the leaf's); :b's :exit on the way back likewise; the initial descent at birth had NO key or label; states inside a parallel region had no key and were labelled with the whole region map.

Engine: NOT at fault. run-action already stamps every :rf.machine/action-ran with the declaring node's own path: collect-actions passes each exit/entry step's :state, which is that node's own prefix (pinned by implementation/machines/test/re_frame/action_ran_decl_path_test.clj, e.g. [:o-in :initial-entry [:o] nil]). spec/005's action-ran bullet already defines :decl-path as the declaring node, so spec/009 needed no change. The mayor-relayed hint is confirmed: the gap was Xray reading :decl-path only when it was [].

Fix (tools/xray panels/epoch/format.cljc): lifecycle-source-key builds [:states <s>... :entry|:exit] from :decl-path for every declaring node, prefixed [:regions <region>] inside a region ([:entry]/[:exit] and [:regions <r> :entry] for roots as before); lifecycle-declaring-node labels the row with the declaring state (keyword at top level, path below, {<region> <state>} in a region; :rf/root / region name for roots). title: xstate-parity: root :spawn (a machine-lifetime child at invoke-id []) - complete path: birth spawn, carrier staleness on flat and parallel, :on-done/:on-error at decl-path [], teardown destroy; lifts rf2-2n6uv.5.1's root-:spawn refusal
description:
## What

Make a root-level `:spawn` (a machine-LIFETIME child, the XState root `invoke`) work completely, and lift the root-`:spawn` registration refusal that rf2-2n6uv.5.1 adds.

Ruled under rf2-2n6uv.5.1 (2026-09-24): the machine root honours `:entry` / `:exit` / `:tags` in that bead, and refuses root `:spawn` until THIS bead lands, because emitting a root spawn alone would ship a partially working feature. Read rf2-2n6uv.5.1's ruling note for the root semantics (birth before the initial cascade, teardown after the leaf exits, never on a transition).

## Why it is separate (verified at source, trunk d09325ddf5, implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc)

1. `spawn-carrier-stale-reason` (~:1359-1387): on a parallel snapshot (map `:state`) it reads `(first invoke-id)` as the REGION name. With invoke-id `[]` that is nil, so the carrier is judged `:rf.machine.spawn/state-exited`. An independent probe: flat `[]` accepted, parallel `[]` returns `:rf.machine.spawn/state-exited`, a real region-child path accepted (control).
2. `pick-spawn-error-transition` (~:1468-1471) requires a NON-EMPTY invoke-id (`(seq invoke-id)`), so a root `:spawn :on-error` never resolves from the spawn map.
3. Teardown destroy is built from the geometry's `:exited-pairs` (`build-destroy-fx`), and the root is never an exited pair, so nothing destroys a root child at machine teardown.
4. `run-spawn-phase` (~:3436-3464) reduces over `:entered-pairs`, which never contain the root, so nothing spawns it at birth either.

## Scope

- Spawn at birth under invoke-id `[]` (after root `:entry`, before the initial leaf cascade's spawns), flat and parallel; `[:rf/spawn-attempts []]` and the `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent-id> []]` registry slot.
- Carrier staleness: a root carrier is current while the machine lives (the attempt check still applies); fix the parallel-snapshot reading of `[]`.
- `:on-done` fold and `:on-error` transition resolved at decl-path `[]` (a keyword target at `[]` resolves to a top-level state, as `target-path` already does).
- Destroy the root child at machine teardown (finality and every destroy entry point), after root `:exit` reads its final snapshot, matching the existing `:exit`-then-destroy convention.
- SSR hydration behaves as for any other spawn (check; do not invent new behaviour).
- Remove the root-`:spawn` member from rf2-2n6uv.5.1's refusal set. Root `:spawn-all` stays refused.
- Records: spec/005 root paragraph and grammar row (HOT ZONE), docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md root row.

Do NOT build a second child-lifecycle subsystem, and do NOT prepend the root to `nodes-along-path` (depth-indexed; the geometry slices it by `lca-len`; SSR hydration consumes it).

## Acceptance

RED first, then green, flat AND parallel: a root child is live after start; it SURVIVES ordinary child transitions (XState 6.0.0-alpha.59 measured: root invoke survives a->b); its completion folds via `:on-done`; its failure fires the root `:on-error` transition; it is destroyed with its owner at finality and on explicit destroy. Controls: region-child and state-level spawns unchanged; rf2-2n6uv.5.1's root entry/exit/tags tests green. Fix-removed control quoted in the close reason.

Lanes: `clojure -M:test` in implementation/machines; `npm run test:cljs` (machine-wide shadow-cljs exclusive: needs the mayor's grant, or cite CI); `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`.

Sequencing: after rf2-2n6uv.5.1 has merged (it adds the refusal this removes) and after any concurrent transition.cljc work.

title: INCOMPLETE: Save Variant still reports inherited DB seeds as uncaptured
description:
Audit of PR #10443 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10443), merged tree 5285b28986b066a7982abf025f04ca195263b0f3. The direct declared :db-seed fix works, but the capture report still mistakes raw registration data for a resolved source body.

Evidence: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/save_variant.cljc:162-167 calls its input resolved, but merely gets the slot; save-current-as-variant! at :494-497 supplies registrar/handler-meta. registrar.cljc:188-191 returns the stored body, and :500-515 explicitly stores :extends intact with parents unmerged. plan.cljc:262 and :1474-1486 merge inherited :db-seed into the effective world, then :1735 emits it.

Example: register parent {:db-seed {[:count] 1}} and source {:extends :parent}. Saving source emits a child extending source, so the seed survives and runs, but capture-slices receives only {:extends :parent}, assigns :not-wired and says app-db state is not captured. The same raw-body boundary omits inherited :setup from its new carry-forward sentence. The new tests pass literal maps directly and cover no registered inheritance chain. This is a remaining reporting defect, not a claim that this PR introduced inheritance behavior or loses the actual seed.

Required correction: derive the capture report from the source's effective inherited declarations using the existing resolution/plan machinery (including composed inputs where applicable), keeping authored carry-forward distinct from live state capture. Add an end-to-end save/report case with an inherited seed, and a genuinely seedless control. Preserve the minimal eight-slice UI and do not add live capture merely to fix the report.
notes:
VERIFIED STILL PRESENT at 51fecf7fe9 (triage 2026-09-25 22:57 AUSEST, read-only; code read at trunk, nothing run). tools/story has NO commits between the audited tree 5285b28986 and trunk: `git log 5285b28986..origin/main -- tools/story` is empty, and 5285b28986 is an ancestor of trunk.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/save_variant.cljc:494-497 passes `(rf.story.registrar/handler-meta :variant target)` to capture-slices.
- registrar.cljc:188-191: handler-meta returns the stored body.
- reg-variant* (:496-515) writes that body "VERBATIM — :extends INTACT, parents UNmerged".
- capture-slices reads `declared-slot` straight off that raw body (save_variant.cljc:204-205, :db-seed and :setup), so a seed or setup inherited through :extends reads as nil. The :db-seed row then falls to `not-wired` (:240-241): "no :db-seed declared on the source — app-db state is not captured".
- The effective world DOES carry the inherited seed: plan.cljc:1485-1486 merges :db-seed across the frag layers, and :1735 emits it. So the report contradicts the saved variant's behaviour.
- The prose claims the input is resolved, which is also false: the declared-slot docstring (:162-165) says "resolved SOURCE variant body", and the call-site comment (:490-493) says "Read the resolved source body". Both describe the raw registration body.
- Tracked nowhere else: a keyword search of every non-closed bead for save_variant / Save Variant / db-seed / capture-slices hits only this record. rf2-vzlaq (closed) fixed the direct declared :db-seed case only.
Surface: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/save_variant.cljc (capture-slices' input and its call site), reusing the resolution in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc, plus a new end-to-end save/report test under tools/story/test/. No live worker's fence covers tools/story.
== RULING (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance)

Fix it by REUSING the plan compiler's :extends resolution. Do not add a second resolver.

- capture-slices reports what the saved variant will actually carry.
  - A :db-seed or :setup INHERITED through :extends is reported exactly as a declared one is: the DB seed row reads the resolved seed, and the setup sentence covers the inherited :setup.
  - Take the resolution from wherever plan.cljc already merges it (about :1485). Call that function or its data; never copy the merge logic.
- If plan.cljc's resolution is not callable from the save flow without restructuring, report that before building anything.
- Keep the declared-case behaviour that PR #10443 just shipped. Move the spec/019 DB seed row wording and save_variant_cljs_test with it, if their meaning changes.
- Add a regression for an inherited-only seed that is red before the fix.
== WORKER VERDICT (seedshot-u9tq5, 2026-09-25 23:51 AUSEST): FIXED in PR #10450 (branch worker/seedshot-u9tq5, rebased on trunk fe5dece989)

What changed:
- save_variant.cljc: save-current-as-variant! now hands capture-slices `carried-source-body`. That helper compiles the SAVED variant `{:extends source :args snapshot}` with `rf.story.plan/variant-plan` and puts that plan's `[:world :db-seed]` and `[:world :setup]` into the registered body. When the plan cannot compile it falls back to the registered body, the same best-effort shape as `plan/effective-args`. There is no second resolver, and plan.cljc is untouched.
- Why the saved variant's plan and not the source's: `:compose` is child-only in `compile-body` (the plan.cljc comment at the `:compose` resolution says "it is not inherited"). A fragment the source composes is therefore NOT carried by `{:extends source}`, and compiling the source's own plan would report it as carried. So the description's "including composed inputs where applicable" does not apply to what the saved variant carries. This is established by reading plan.cljc, not by measurement.
- Declared case unchanged: capture-slices' signature and its literal-map unit tests are untouched and green.
- tools/story/spec/019 DB seed row now says the seed the source "declares or inherits through its own :extends chain", and that a :setup "declared or inherited" is not a seed.
- Regression: story_save_variant_test.clj `save-current-as-variant!-reports-the-seed-and-setup-the-source-inherits`. It covers a declared seed, an inherited-only seed, an inherited :setup, and a chain with no seed and no setup (the control).

Measurements (tools/story `clojure -M:test`, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS -Xms64m -Xmx768m, exit codes captured to file):
- Baseline (fix, no new test): 2099 tests / 7957 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0.
- With the test: 2100 / 7968, 0 / 0, exit 0. That is exactly the predicted +1 test / +11 assertions.
- Sabotage (call site reverted to the raw `handler-meta` body): 2100 / 7968, 4 failures, exit 1. The 4 are exactly the 3 inherited-seed assertions and the 1 inherited-setup assertion; the declared and seedless blocks passed both ways. Restore verified by blob hash equal to the committed blob c824130371. (A first sabotage attempt died before its first test on native memory exhaustion and was not read as a result.)
- Final base after rebase: 2100 / 7968, 0 / 0, exit 0.
- clj-kondo plain: save_variant.cljc 0 errors / 1 warning, which is the pre-existing unused `re-frame.story.args` require also present at the merge base; test file 0 / 0.
- Reader conditionals: every changed form sits outside any reader conditional (shared code). The single conditional is the catch class `#?(:clj Exception :cljs :default)`, the same spelling as plan.cljc's effective-args. The CLJS side is graded by CI only.

Open, outside the ruling's scope (the ruling names :db-seed and :setup):
- The :sub-overrides, :network, :fx-overrides and :viewport rows still read the raw source body, so a value inherited through :extends reports as not-wired.
- :fx-overrides has a design fork: the plan's `[:world :frame :fx-overrides]` also folds in :network's managed-stub lowering.
- The saved variant `{:extends source}` does not carry the source's :compose fragments, so the save flow loses them. The report is now honest about that, but the loss itself is untouched.

It compiles the saved body {:extends source :args snapshot} with the existing plan compiler (rf.story.plan/variant-plan) rather than reading the raw source body. No second resolver was written.

title: Migration guide and conformance fixtures still describe the non-existent co-located :rf/reply HTTP default
description:
Found by rf2-feyyp (PR #10477), outside its fence and not edited there.

## Defect

Tracked files still describe a co-located `:rf/reply` default: omit every reply target and the reply comes back to the originating event with `:rf/reply` merged into its message. That default does not exist. `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc` `validate-reply-target!` refuses an unaddressed request at fx-call time with `:rf.error/http-no-reply-target`, and `encoding.cljc` `build-reply-event` dispatches nothing for a branch with no supplied target. Spec 014 §Reply addressing and §Unified one-handler form already state the real contract: `:reply-to`, or `:on-success` / `:on-failure`, with the envelope appended as the target event's last argument.

Sites at trunk 2e5cb8da8d:
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/http-fx-to-managed-http.md`: line 47, the mapping-table row calling the default "(default — co-located reply)" with `(if-let [reply (:rf/reply msg)] ...)`, and line 311, "Migrating to the co-located reply form".
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-managed-default-reply-addressing.edn`: the fixture id `:rf.http.managed/default-reply-addressing`, its header comment, `:fixture/doc`, the `:article/load-reply` registry doc and the handler comment all describe the merged-`:rf/reply` default. The handlers themselves already use `:on-success [:article/load-reply]`, so the fixture behaves correctly and only its prose and id are wrong. The comment also names a JVM smoke test, `re-frame.http-managed-test/canned-success-default-reply-addressing`. Check at source whether that test exists and what it asserts.
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-managed-get-success.edn` line 6: its comment names the envelope as `{:rf/reply {:status :ok :value <decoded>}}`.

## Fix

Correct the prose to the implemented contract. Rename or re-describe the fixture only if its id is not pinned elsewhere; check the conformance roster and any tests that name it first. `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` is a hot-zone file; the page named above is not it.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (spectruth10, PR #10479, commit "docs: describe managed HTTP's real reply addressing in the migration guide and fixtures")
The contract was settled at source. handlers.cljc `validate-reply-target!` throws :rf.error/http-no-reply-target when none of :reply-to / :on-success / :on-failure is present. encoding.cljc `build-reply-event` does `(conj value reply-payload)` for a supplied vector, returns nil for an explicit nil, and dispatches nothing for an unsupplied branch.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/http-fx-to-managed-http.md: four sites now describe the split :on-success/:on-failure form and the unified :reply-to form: the intro sentence (line 13, not on the bead's list), the :on-success row (line 47), the payload bullet (line 210, not on the bead's list) and the modernisation bullet (line 311). The row no longer says new code should prefer a co-located form; Spec 014 recommends the split form by default.
- The fixture was RENAMED: :rf.http.managed/default-reply-addressing is now :rf.http.managed/split-reply-addressing, and the file is now http-managed-split-reply-addressing.edn. The census found the old id and file name nowhere but the fixture itself, including the conformance README. The JVM and CLJS runners discover fixtures from the directory and hold no id lists. Measured: planting a mismatched :fixture/id left the JVM conformance run at exit 0, while planting a changed :final-app-db made it exit 1, naming the new id. The fixture's prose was rewritten. The JVM smoke test its comment named, re-frame.http-managed-test/canned-success-default-reply-addressing, DOES NOT EXIST. The comment now names the tests that do: canned-success-reply-to-addressing and no-reply-target-fails-loud.
- http-managed-get-success.edn line 6 was fixed. http-managed-on-success-explicit.edn (not on the bead's list, same fence) carried the same stale default wording in 4 places, and those were fixed too.
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/http-fx-to-managed-http.md is a router leaf with no stale text, so it was not edited. check_skill_migration_o1617_router_drift (which grades the corpus companion) passes.
- FOUND, OUTSIDE FENCE, NOT EDITED: the implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc comment above `reply-ctx` still says "the co-located `(:rf/reply msg)` merge carries the canonical map under `:rf/reply`".
Gates: the JVM conformance corpus (243 loaded, 240 run, all pass), check_conformance_fixture_edn, check_doc_slugs, mkdocs --strict and the skills drift checks all exit 0. A planted broken link in the migration row turned mkdocs --strict red, and the restore was verified by blob hash.

Nothing else pinned it: a whole-tree search found only the fixture, and a planted mismatched id left the conformance run at exit 0. The JVM smoke test the fixture's comment named (canned-success-default-reply-addressing) did not exist, so the comment now names two tests that do.

description:

From GitHub issue #10498 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** task (docs consistency) · **Priority:** P4 · **Size:** small

## Gap

At `92c6b29960`:
- **Part 3** (`docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md`, lines ~57-74 and ~232) builds a form slice with `:submitted`, "the last server-accepted draft, which a `dirty?` check compares against". This follows the core convention in `docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md`; `docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md` also uses `:submitted`.
- **Part 4** (`docs/resources/tutorial/04-mutations-and-invalidation.md`, lines ~228 and ~242) says "The editor's app-db slice is a form in Part 3's style … plus a `:baseline` (the article as loaded, or blank)". It uses `:baseline` for the same role.

So Part 4 claims to follow Part 3's style and then renames its key. A reader following along sees two conventions for one idea.

Where `:baseline` comes from: the shipped example uses it (`examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/article_editor.cljs`). The example has no `:submitted` anywhere; its auth forms (`auth.cljs`) keep only `:draft` and `:touched`. An earlier review note said both names mirror the example app. That was wrong: only `:baseline` does.

- **A (recommended): Part 4 uses `:submitted`**, matching Part 3 and the core form how-to. Optionally, also rename the example's `:baseline` so the tutorial and the example agree. That is a code change in `examples/`, so check the example still compiles (the `examples_compile` surface).
- **B:** keep `:baseline`, and add one sentence in Part 4 saying why this slice differs. For an editor, the baseline is the article as loaded rather than a submission's result.
- **C:** close with the reasoning recorded, if it is judged too minor.

## Acceptance (A or B)

- A reader sees one name for the concept, or an explicit reason for the second.
- The doc gates exit 0. If the example changes, the example compile sweep passes (`node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs`, which takes the shadow-cljs build lane).

title: A managed-HTTP interceptor failure on a SENSITIVE request still reaches the trace raw through core's :rf.error/fx-handler-exception row (message, :reason and the exception's ex-data)
description:
Found by rf2-sdeze's worker (PR #10606, merged at trunk b7c5b81bf8), outside that fence. It is a CLAIM; reproduce it first.

REPORTED: #10606 redacts the HTTP layer's own failure rows (`:rf.error/http-interceptor-bad-return`, `-interceptor-failed`, `-reply-tail-failed`) under the request's effective sensitivity. But when a `:before` interceptor fails on a request going through `:rf.http/managed`, core's fx boundary ALSO records `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception`, and that row carries three things raw:
- `:exception-message`;
- `:reason`;
- the exception object itself, whose ex-data holds `:returned`.

So the secret the HTTP rows now redact rides out beside them on the core row. Reproduce with the #10606 regression's setup: a sensitive request (`:sensitive? true`, an `Authorization` header), and a `:before` returning `[(get-in ctx [:request :headers "Authorization"])]` through `:rf.http/managed`. Probe the core row.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS: prefer the PRODUCER. The exception that escapes the managed-HTTP fx is thrown by `implementation/http`, which knows the request's effective sensitivity. Core's fx boundary cannot know it in general. So on a sensitive request, the HTTP layer should not let an exception carrying the returned value or its textual echo (message or ex-data) escape to core. For example, it could rethrow with the same error id and interceptor identity, and the data-bearing parts redacted by the same policy #10606 used.
- Do NOT add a general core redaction policy for fx exceptions. Whether core should classify ANY fx throw whose message quotes its arguments is a separate design question. If you find the producer route cannot close this, report that question instead of choosing.
- Keep the in-process value raw, keep the error ids stable, and keep a non-sensitive request's rows unchanged, as a control.

A regression goes red at base, the core row carrying the secret, and green with the fix. Surface: `implementation/http` first; core only to read.
close_reason:
Fixed at the producer in PR #10609 (the commit titled "fix(http): a sensitive request's chain error leaves the walk projected, so core's fx row cannot echo it").

REPRODUCED at trunk 74b664c493 (the #10606 base) on the JVM. The setup was a sensitive :rf.http/managed request carrying an Authorization header, with a :before that returns [(get-in ctx [:request :headers "Authorization"])] or throws a message quoting it. The keys of core's :rf.error/fx-handler-exception dev-trace row that carried the secret were (:exception :exception-message :reason). The keys of the always-on record that carried it were (:exception :reason). The exception's ex-data carried it in (:reason :returned) for a bad return and in (:cause :reason) for a throw. :rf.fx/args was already clean through :http/project-managed-fx-args. The reply-tail fence's always-on record for a failing :after carried the same raw exception, which is a sibling door closed by the same fix.

FIX: re-frame.http.middleware's run-chain* builds both chain errors through one raise-chain-error! under the effective sensitivity (sensitive-of acc, which covers a mark an earlier :before set). On a sensitive request the ex-data slots go through rf.http.privacy/redact-failure (url query values, string :cause, non-nil :returned), and :reason and the message are rendered from the projected slot. The thrown ex-info keeps its :rf.error/id and :interceptor-id / :id. The trace row is prepare-emit-failure over that ex-data, which replaces #10606's emit-chain-error! re-render. Core has no new redaction policy.

On "keep the in-process value raw": this is read as the request / ctx and the interceptor's own return, which are untouched. The only thing projected is the error that leaves the walk. That error has no in-process consumer: grep shows no reader of its :returned / :cause outside the HTTP tests, and every production caller hands it to core's fx boundary or to the reply-tail fence.

AFTER, measured with the same probe: every one of those key lists reads (). REGRESSIONS: http_interceptors_test sensitive-chain-error-reaches-core-fx-row-without-the-secret covers three cases: top-level sensitive bad return, a throw quoting the token, and an earlier :before marking the request sensitive. It asserts on both the dev-trace row and the always-on record. http_reply_tail_test's sensitive :after case now asserts on the reply-tail always-on record too. SABOTAGE: with the pre-fix middleware.cljc swapped back in, the two namespaces read 10 failures across 42 tests and 251 assertions. With the fix they read 0 at the same counts. The restore was verified by blob hash bb1837801c against the committed object. CONTROLS: non-sensitive-chain-error-reaches-core-fx-row-unchanged still shows :returned [url], the :reason echo, and the throw's raw :cause and :url, and the #10606 regressions stay green.

GATES on the final base: http 549 tests / 4314 assertions (base 547 / 4281). Consumers were identical at base and final: resources 926/8101, reply-conformance 31/571, ssr-ring 266/1380, core 2163/12193. All read 0 failures. CI settled on the PR head with 88 checks: 59 success, 29 skipped, none failed. The CLJS node lane ran 12533 tests / 66235 assertions with 0 failures.

SIBLING, not fixed because the bead keeps non-sensitive rows unchanged: on a request NOT marked sensitive whose URL carries a denylisted query param (?api_key=...), the chain error's ex-data :url is raw. So core's fx-handler-exception row (:exception, dev trace and always-on) carries the value, while the HTTP row redacts it and :rf.fx/args projects it to :rf/redacted. Measured by probe on the final tree.
