title: Held route sub prior values lose sensitivity after the route is re-registered
description:
Audit of PR #10602 (194eb336f78e5ac594caa2fbfb125ff774739a9e). The affected core/routing classification files are unchanged on origin/main 74b664c4939352592022254f19aa3ce06a7c9ab8.

The new prior-route-classification in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/sub_egress.cljc looks up the leaving route in the CURRENT registrar. That is not necessarily the declaration under which the memoized value was computed. Re-registering the same route without its sensitive declaration (for example during development reload) before navigating away makes the prior classified value raw again.

Bounded JVM reproduction against the exact merged sources:
1. Register :audit/secret {:sensitive [[:params :secret]]} at /secret/:secret and an unclassified :audit/plain route.
2. Visit /secret/audit-prior-route-private-953. Hold and dereference [:rf/route] and [:rf.route/params].
3. Re-register :audit/secret with {} at the same pattern.
4. Capture traces while navigating to /plain and dereferencing both held subs.

Measured: both held subs emit one :rf.sub/run, and both :rf.sub/prev-value slots contain the secret. The paired control omits step 3 and leaks neither value. Both arms confirm the original in-process value is raw and the destination is :audit/plain. Probe exit 0; ai/probe-10602-audit-sep23-monitor-2.log, source ai/probe-10602/probe.clj. The first probe attempt failed to compile because it took the subscribe macro as a function; the corrected second attempt is the evidence.

Keep the prior value governed by the classification captured when it was computed, including the params/query derived-sub case, rather than relying solely on the route's current registration. Keep in-process values raw and avoid leaving stale route claims in the live registry. Add the small held-sub regression through a real re-registration and navigation. This is distinct from the URL-string carrier finding rf2-2p7fo and from historical epoch-record egress.
acceptance_criteria: A held route projection and params/query leaves keep the original sensitive slots redacted in prior-value traces after the leaving route is re-registered; unchanged-registration and raw in-process controls pass.

FIXED in PR #10618 (branch worker/routeegress-li9em, commit "fix(routing): a held route sub's prior value keeps its route's declaration across a re-registration"), rebased onto trunk f4ab8797c7.

## Decisive measurement, inline

The bead's probe was rebuilt verbatim as a JVM regression in routing_sub_prev_value_classification_test. It registers :audit/secret {:sensitive [[:params :secret]]} at /secret/:secret and an unclassified :audit/plain. It visits /secret/audit-prior-route-private-953, holds and derefs [:rf/route] and [:rf.route/params], re-registers :audit/secret with {}, then navigates to /plain inside a trace capture. A paired control omits the re-registration.

title: epoch tool_pair: replace-frame-state-bad-keys docstring says a map of only unrelated keys gets :reason :no-recognized-keys, but the unknown-keys check runs first so {:unrelated 1} returns :unknown-keys

title: Trial: cut worker tool-call count (batch into scripts, scope per-batch runs, one blocking CI wait); measure, then amend the dispatch template if it pays
description:

This trial targets the remaining cost: the NUMBER of tool calls, since every call re-sends the worker's whole context.

Baselines from today's completion reports (subagent tokens / tool calls / wall time):
- prune-ssr7: 518K / 450 / 2h55m;
- toolstests-qwtkk: 532K / 485 / 2h05m;
- resegress-lafas: 452K / 140 / 46m;
- navinplace-961fz: 291K / 109 / 44m.

Rules under trial: from 17:35 AUSEST, sent to every live worker and written into every new brief as a "Working efficiently" section.
1. Batch a measurement, a plant-and-restore cycle or a commit group into one scripted call; prefer one scripted edit per file over one edit per form.
2. Measure a batch's delta on the namespaces it touched; run the whole suite only for the baseline, the final count and after a reaching rebase.
3. Wait on CI with one blocking watch call at a time, never a loop of short polls.
4. Keep the final report to the Done list.

Evaluate after the next 4 or more completions: compare tokens and calls per item against the baselines above, by kind (pruning against defect fixes). Check that nothing was missed: no CI red that a skipped per-batch full run would have caught. title: Claim incomplete: Xray's independent-scroll host breaks routing top and Back restoration
description:
Merged-PR audit #10616, merge 5c997a5e378c3e5c4ef5a7a5bb7d4157213e114d. The independent app/Xray scroll layout works, but its integration with the library's routing scroll behavior is incomplete.

Evidence: examples/_shared/css/structure.css:223-239, all 18 testbed hosts, and the recommended config.cljc host snippet now constrain the shell to 100vh and make #app overflow:auto. The app therefore scrolls in its element rather than window. At this same merge, implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/scroll.cljc:267-269 still captures window.scrollX/Y, and :top without a fragment plus :restore still call window.scrollTo at lines 443-448. Spec 012 promises route scroll-to-top and saved-position restoration, and installs manual history scroll restoration. No element-scroller selection exists on these paths.

Bounded Chromium DOM probe used the exact before/after deep_machine host CSS with tall app content, then executed the same DOM operations as the routing handlers. BEFORE: scrolling 400px gives windowY=400, capture=[0,400], top returns to 0, restore returns to 400. AFTER: app.scrollTop=400 while windowY=0, capture=[0,0], window.scrollTo(0,0) leaves app at 400; after moving app to 100, restoring the captured position leaves it at 100 rather than 400. Probe exit 0; local evidence ai/probe-10616-audit-sep23-monitor-2/probe.html and probe.log. This was a focused DOM boundary probe, not a rerun of the compiled routing suite. Existing reported splitter/overflow tests are accepted.

Impact: routed apps adopting the recommended Xray host layout can open a new page at the previous page's scroll depth and fail to restore Back/Forward positions. This affects the documented SPA integration, not only the testbeds.

Required correction: retain independent app/Xray scrolling while aligning routing's top/capture/restore behavior with the actual app scroll surface. Choose the smallest coherent layout or routing integration; avoid a tooling dependency in core. Add focused browser coverage for navigation to a tall page and Back restoration under the recommended host layout, with the ordinary window-scrolling layout as a control.

(A) LAYOUT: the window scrolls again for the app, and the inline Xray pane becomes position:fixed/sticky with its own overflow. Routing is untouched and no contract changes; the #10616 guarantees (Xray never shares a scrollbar, nothing inside Xray widens the page, the splitter resizes) are kept by sizing the app column to the viewport minus --rf-xray-inline-width. It touches the same 18 testbed hosts, examples structure.css, the config.cljc snippet and the Xray docs that #10616 did.
(B) ROUTING: scroll.cljc's capture, :top and :restore target a configurable scroll element (for example a selector or element option on the router) instead of window. This is a new Spec 012 contract surface that every host using an element scroller must configure.
The mayor's recommendation under the stance is (A): it is smaller, keeps the library free of a tooling-driven option, and fixes every routed app adopting the recommended snippet without configuration.

title: Replace recordable JWT coeffects in the RealWorld auth examples
description: The documentation review found a remaining source/example contradiction outside the requested docs trees. examples/real-apps/realworld_http/auth.cljs registers :auth.session/token with :recordable? true around line 99, and examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs registers :realworld-resources.session/token likewise around line 118. Both suppliers read raw JWTs from localStorage and describe retaining them in replay/epoch inputs. spec/Privacy.md and SECURITY.md exclude credentials from recordable coeffects. Core PR #10674 and the Resources documentation update use a storage-read effect and separately classified reply event instead. Reconcile the executable examples and their related tests without weakening the credential boundary; retain cold-boot deep-link ordering and guard delayed replies against later-session changes where needed.
acceptance_criteria: No JWT is supplied through a recordable coeffect in either RealWorld example; token-bearing events/effects and app-db projections are classified; unreadable storage falls back safely; existing auth/SSR/deep-link tests are adapted to the effect seam and pass; source commentary describes the shipped contract.
notes:
== RESULT (worker realworld-jwt-nahcr, 2026-10-02 00:10 AUSEST) ==
PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/10680, head a596c0f638af415982e75f8ff448819d74b69dd2, one commit on base 954e86a4fe.

Shape shipped in both RealWorld examples, mirroring docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md and docs/resources/tutorial/03-auth-and-forms.md:
- The recordable :auth.session/token and :realworld-resources.session/token coeffects are removed.
- :auth/initialise seeds an empty :auth slice, advances a top-level non-secret :auth-generation, and fires a client-only load fx (:auth.session/load / :realworld-resources.session/load).
- The fx reads localStorage["jwtToken"] inside try/catch, so missing, blocked or throwing storage reads as nil. It dispatches [:auth/session-read {:generation g :token t}] into its frame.
- :auth/session-read is :sensitive [[:token]]. It drops a stale generation, normalises a blank token to nil, writes [:auth :token], and nudges the machine with [:auth/restore bool] as before.
- :auth-generation advances on init, in store-session-db (every stored session) and in :auth/clear-session.

Delayed-reply guard: :auth/session-restored is dropped unless restoring-session? still holds. This is the window guard, not the tutorial's (:request-id correlation) generation check, because the demo backend's canned replies carry no :correlation (verified at implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc emit-canned-success!). A login success also exits :restoring, so the machine alone cannot reject a late restore reply. Login replies stay machine-serialised and unguarded.

Cold-boot ordering: the read is synchronous and its reply drains inside the :auth/initialise step, so the token is in app-db before the URL-bound frame's first URL sync. All five existing deep-link race arms pass through the real effect.

Site delta beyond the two named auth.cljs sites:
- prose in realworld_http core.cljs and ssr.cljc, and in realworld_resources core.cljs and schema.cljs
- realworld_cljs_test.cljs (6 cofx-stub sites, including the booting-frame! map step), realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs (8 sites), example_realworld_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs (1 site), example_realworld_resources_boot_seed (prose)

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc reg-cofx docstring example is filed as rf2-tz4bl.

title: mcp-conformance wire-vocab: production-mirroring fixtures are never compared with production
description:
Found while pruning tools/mcp-conformance (owner: rf2-3h7v2.16, PR #10710). Not fixed there: that PR adds no tests.

Two wire-vocab namespaces validate HAND-WRITTEN fixtures that their docstrings say mirror production, but nothing compares the fixtures with the production source:

- operating_frame_address_test.clj: `success-fixtures` / `failure-fixtures` "mirror the descriptor examples in descriptors_data.cljs verbatim". The emitter is CLJS and never runs on this JVM lane, and no test reads the descriptor examples, so a descriptor example that gains a realm slot or drops `:frames` leaves every test green.
- reply_envelope_test.clj: the http / resource / machine fixtures "mirror" the `trace/emit!` tag maps. Only key presence as data in at least one emit site is pinned (`reply-envelope-keys-are-emitted-as-data-in-the-production-sites`), so a key dropped from one family's emit stays green while any other of the four sites still carries it as data.

The pruning PR removed the tests that asserted the fixtures' own literal contents (they could not see production either), so coverage is unchanged; the gap predates it.

Possible fix, if wanted: a source pin per fixture (each fixture key present as data in its named emit site / descriptor example block), or drive the real emitters where they are JVM-reachable. Low priority; decide whether it is worth having.

title: re-frame-migration skill: React DOM removal timing and Reagent legacy-render diagnostics are wrong (floor-gate Check 3, M42) (gh-10785)
description:
GitHub issue #10785: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/10785 (opened 2026-10-03T05:47:28Z under mike-thompson-day8). The body below is the issue's, verbatim. Mike's standing rule (2026-10-03): the worker that does this bead also closes issue #10785 as its last act, with a comment naming the PR.

---

## Problem

At framework revision 412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23, the migration skill gives two incorrect diagnoses for legacy mounts:

- [floor-gate.md, Check 3](https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23/skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md#check-3--legacy-react-api-scan) puts removal of render/hydrate/unmountComponentAtNode in React 18.
- The same paragraph describes stock Reagent's surviving render var as a warning followed by a harmless return. [guided-handlers-state.md, M42](https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23/skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md#m-42--react-19-removed-reagent-surfaces-bridge-and-slim) repeats the no-op diagnosis.

An agent following this guidance can misclassify a real JavaScript exception and interpret missing framework diagnostics as expected harmless behavior.

## Evidence

[React's official upgrade guide](https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide#removed-reactdomrender) places deprecation in React 18 and removal in React 19; it covers hydrate and unmount similarly.

[Published Reagent 2.0.1 source](https://github.com/reagent-project/reagent/blob/f23875aac29679b9202809e14539523818cab50d/src/reagent/dom.cljs) checks whether the legacy function exists, logs a warning if absent, and then calls it unconditionally. Both render-comp and unmount-comp have this shape. Calling the absent function produces a JavaScript TypeError; the wrapper does not return early. This was verified against both the published jar and the official tag's source.

A narrow React 19.2.0 Node probe also confirmed that all three legacy DOM exports are undefined. No application smoke pass is claimed.

## Proposed correction

Update both skill passages to separate compile-time var availability from runtime call behavior. Use the accurate deprecation/removal versions and describe stock Reagent's warning followed by the missing-function call. Keep the existing M42 root-mount replacement and live-verification requirement.

Acceptance: neither passage promises a warning-only no-op, and React 18/19 timing agrees with the primary documentation.

Related closed #1377 covers prerequisite discovery rather than this diagnostic residual. Open and closed issue searches found no duplicate.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #10790 (GitHub issue #10785), commit "docs(skill): correct the React 19 legacy-mount diagnosis in floor-gate Check 3 and M-42". Check 3 now says ReactDOM.render/hydrate/unmountComponentAtNode were deprecated in React 18 and removed in React 19, per the React 19 upgrade guide: "ReactDOM.render was deprecated in March 2022 (v18.0.0). In React 19, we're removing ReactDOM.render". Check 3 and M-42 now keep compile-time Var resolution apart from runtime behaviour. Under React 19, stock Reagent's reagent.dom/render and unmount-component-at-node warn and then throw a TypeError. Source: Reagent tag v2.0.1 = commit f23875aac2, src/reagent/dom.cljs lines 11-21. render-comp runs (when-not (exists? react-dom/render) (js/console.warn ...)) and then calls (react-dom/render (comp) container ...) unconditionally. A probe of react-dom 19.3.0 threw "TypeError: d.render is not a function". M-42's adapter-owned client-root/render! rewrite is unchanged. M-42 has no explicit live-verification line, either at base or at the issue's revision 412f86be3d, so there was none to keep. No test pins these passages. check_doc_slugs went red on a planted anchor, the restore was verified by blob hash, and the gate is green; CI is green with 88 checks. Sibling carriers outside the fence (inventory-and-plan.md root-mount row; MIGRATION.md M-42) are filed as rf2-6yb5c.

title: Test-suite pruning, second pass: implementation/resources (child of rf2-zbnoc)
description:
Child of rf2-zbnoc (test-suite pruning, second pass). One artefact, one worktree, one PR: implementation/resources, ORDER item 9. Second-pass children merged so far: implementation/core (rf2-zbnoc.9-.13), machines (.14, #10781), fresco (.15, #10782), scripts (.16, #10783), tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp (.17, #10784) and implementation/adapters (.18, #10794).

Read rf2-zbnoc first. Its description has Mike's instructions verbatim (stages 1-4 in order, the always-keep list, VERIFY as you go) and HOW THIS PASS RUNS. Work to all of it. No production gate with an RF2_MIN_TESTS floor covers resources as far as the mayor can see; stage 1 confirms.

SURFACE, from the mayor's census at trunk 7860ee32e5 (CLAIMS; your stage-1 runner baseline is the authority): 70 test files under implementation/resources/test/, 896 deftest forms. 68 are .cljc *_cljs_test namespaces. The JVM lane (clojure -M:test in implementation/resources, the "JVM resources (clojure -M:test)" CI job) runs those, and so does CI's shared :node-test build. Two are CLJS-only .cljs files: resources_http_completed_at_clock_cljs_test.cljs and resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs. Because nearly all of it is .cljc, the JVM lane measures most of a batch for free, with no lane. CLJS-only reader branches (#?(:cljs ...)) and the two .cljs files need the shadow-cljs lane (AGENTS.md "Which Gate Covers Which Edit": JVM lanes read a :cljs branch but never compile it).

PRIOR ART: the first pass was rf2-98kzs.8, PR #10628, which removed 63 tests, folded 28 into 10 tables and renamed 12. JVM went 935/8216 -> 854/8037, and CI :node-test moved by the same -81/-179. It planted 12 source faults. Its defects bead, rf2-n4dy4 (PR #10637), then fixed six groups: a timer reschedule-cancel gap (positive-rearm-cancels-the-prior-host-handle added), assertions that could not fail, and untested branches. JVM went to 857/8039. Read both close reasons and both PR bodies for the removal ledger and the kept-uncertain list. A keep recorded there stands unless a plant settles it. Do not remove a test rf2-n4dy4 added to close a gap unless a plant shows a retained test catches the same fault.

LANE PLAN: do all reading and every JVM measurement first, by absolute path, with no lane. Then batch the CLJS work (the two .cljs files, any :cljs-branch edit, and a scoped :node-test head/base pair over the changed namespaces) into one lane window at the end, using the scoped model rf2-zbnoc.18 used: compile-node-test.cjs with --config-merge, base copies from the merge base in a separate bundle from head, and each namespace run alone with --test=<ns>.

KEEP BY RULE: tests pinning docs, spec wording or conformance (readiness_projector_conformance, the ep0037 integrated proof, replay determinism); gate and ratchet self-tests; tests of documented error ids (rf2-98kzs.3 ruling); tests cited by name or file name outside their file; egress and redaction tests (the *_egress_* and invalid_params_redaction files pin what may leave the frame); regression tests for real past bugs, unless a retained test demonstrably catches the same failure.

LESSONS FROM rf2-zbnoc.18 (adapters worker, written for this child):
- Plant a fault in production code to test any "covered elsewhere" claim. Its P1 refuted a cover that read as airtight, and the removed test went back.
- For counts, compile separate head and base bundles of just the changed namespaces with compile-node-test.cjs --config-merge. Build the base from merge-base copies of those test files, restore and confirm a clean tree, and run each namespace alone with --test=<ns>.
- Lint the touched files at base and at head with the CI-pinned clj-kondo 2026.04.15, not a local 2025 build, and compare findings with line numbers stripped. That is how its unused `testing` import was caught.
- Leaf assertions beside an exact-vector or whole-map equality are cheap, safe trims. Keep the ones whose message diagnoses a different failure.

LESSONS FROM rf2-zbnoc.9-.17: predict from per-test counter rows, because helper assertions count; a counter entry point must collect test data in its own namespace or later tests go uncounted; runtime set! on single-arity fns works as a dev-mode CLJS plant; search for a test FILE's name as well as its test names before deleting it; catch-all fixtures cannot check "no side effect before refusal"; run git diff --check after every batch; a scoped compile can warn on code the branch never touched, so compare warnings against the base copy; the Bash tool halves runs of backslashes, so write scripts with the Write tool; search departed names three ways (fixed-string, whitespace-collapsed, comment-stripped); run bd from the worktree root; pass origin/main to scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh and scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh.

title: remove-worker-worktree: CANARY is a count+sentinel signature; make it the path/kind manifest loops.md § 4 now requires
description:

That PR makes docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md § 4 Removing say the decisive preservation control is a MANIFEST (relative path and entry kind per entry, links recorded without traversal, content hashes only where byte preservation is claimed), with counts and clocks kept only as diagnostics that never outvote a differing manifest.

The tool the mayor actually runs does not produce one. scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh prints CANARY_BEFORE= / CANARY_AFTER= lines whose signature is '<immediate-entries>/<recursive-files>/<sentinels-present>' (find -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 | wc -l, find -type f | wc -l, and the .bin and shadow-cljs/package.json sentinels); scripts/remove-worker-worktree.ps1's Get-NodeModulesSignature returns the same three values. Measured by the u0yhg worker at trunk f530d4b5d2. So after #10900 the method's decisive check is one no tool supplies, and the mayor's reap verdict rests on what the method now calls a diagnostic.

Ask: make each script's canary a manifest under one enumeration policy (recursive, hidden entries kept, links recorded as links and not followed): a sorted list of relative path plus entry kind, reduced to a digest for the CANARY line, with the counts kept beside it as diagnostics. Fail loudly when the before and after digests differ, and refuse rather than pass when a scan did not complete. Content hashes are not needed (the claim is membership, not bytes). Keep the .sh and .ps1 in step, keep the unlink-first ordering, and keep the existing CANARY_BEFORE= / CANARY_AFTER= line prefixes so callers comparing them still work. Measure the wall-time cost on the real mayor node_modules and say it; if a full manifest is too slow to run on every removal, report that with the number rather than shipping a slow guard.

notes:
== RESULT (worker, 2026-10-05) — PR #10904, one commit 822c08daec

scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh and .ps1: each CANARY_BEFORE= / CANARY_AFTER= line keeps its prefix and one-line-per-real-node_modules shape and now reads `<path> manifest=<sha256> counts=<entries>/<files>/<sentinels>` (or MISSING / INCOMPLETE). Manifest = one `<kind> <relative/path>` line per entry, kind d/f/l/o, recursive, hidden kept, links recorded as `l` and never followed, sorted bytewise (ordinal in .ps1), SHA-256 over UTF-8 with a newline per line; no content hashes. Counts are read off the same manifest (diagnostics only). A moved manifest prints CANARY_FAILED plus the first 5 entries lost/gained and exits 1. An incomplete scan prints CANARY_INCOMPLETE=<path> <reason>: on the BEFORE scan the run refuses (exit 1) before any disarm/removal; on the AFTER scan it exits 1 with no verdict. Unlink-first order, exit codes and other lines unchanged. sh uses GNU find -printf, falling back to batched -exec printf per kind (byte-identical, ~5x slower). .ps1 uses an explicit EnumerateFileSystemInfos walk that never descends a reparse point (the old Get-ChildItem -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue silently read 6/3/2 on an unlistable 6/6/2 tree).

title: SSR settle keeps only the last buffered error: a handler 500 then a route 404 renders the partial app as a 404
description:
## Bug

When a request buffers more than one error, SSR settlement projects only the last one. A handler exception (500) followed by a route miss (404) settles at 404 with a 404 public error, so the host takes the 4xx arm and renders the app's own body and hydration payload over the partially updated app-db: the "quiet lie" the 5xx arm exists to prevent. Separately, three of the four response readers consume the error buffer, so a midpoint `get-response` (the reader its docstring calls canonical) steals the classification and the host's later result-bearing settle sees no public error.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc:240-243` (trunk 475bdcaacf) — `apply-error-projection!` 1-arity: `(last (consume-pending-traces! frame-id))`, documented at `:222-224` as "project the LAST trace (last-write-wins, mirroring the multi-status policy)". Earlier buffered traces are discarded unprojected.
- `:480-508` — `flush-response-result!` drains once; `:510-523` `flush-response!` and `:525-541` `get-response` delegate to it, so each consumes the buffer. Only `peek-response` (`:467-478`) is pure. `get-response`'s docstring calls it "the canonical host-adapter alias for the drain-then-read sequence".
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc:189-235` — the default projector maps a handler exception to 500 and `:rf.error/no-such-handler` `:kind :route` to 404.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:331-352` — the bundled handler classifies on `:public-error` from `flush-response-result!`: redirect, else projected 5xx → error page, else (4xx or nil) `build-full-response` renders the root view and payload.
- Repro, *probed* (JVM, `implementation/ssr` with routing on the classpath; identical results under `-Dre-frame.debug=false`):
  ```clojure
  (rf/init! rf.ssr/adapter)
  (rf/reg-route :route/home {} "/")
  (rf/reg-route :rf.route/not-found {} "/not-found")
  (rf/reg-event :p/boom (fn [_ _] (throw (ex-info "handler failed" {}))))
  (def f (rf.frame/make-anon-frame-record!
           {:platform :server
            :ssr {:public-error-id :rf.ssr/default-error-projector :dev-error-detail? false}}))
  (try (rf/dispatch-sync [:p/boom] {:frame f}) (catch Throwable _))
  (rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/handle-url-change "/no-such-page"] {:frame f})
  (rf.ssr/flush-response-result! f)   ; read :status of :response and of :public-error
  ```
  Observed, one fresh frame per row, in the order named:
  ```
  handler throw only        {:status 500, :public-error-status 500}
  route miss only           {:status 404, :public-error-status 404}
  throw, then route miss    {:status 404, :public-error-status 404}   ; app body rendered
  route miss, then throw    {:status 500, :public-error-status 500}
  throw; get-response midway => 500; host settle afterwards {:status 500, :public-error-status nil}
  ```
  The last case puts the request on the app arm under a 500 (`:public-error nil` is treated as "no projection"), shipping app HTML for a server fault.
- Contract: `spec/011-SSR.md:1396-1407` §Drain-time error classification — a projected 5xx before commit means app-db is in an arbitrary partial state, and the adapter "discards the root body and hydration payload". The spec's last-write-wins rule (`:1087`, §Multiple-status policy) is about `:rf.server/set-status` intentions, not buffered failures.

## Expected

Any buffered server fault in a request settles to the error arm, whatever 4xx follows it, and reading the response never changes the later settlement.

## Fix direction

- Project every buffered trace and keep the highest status, last-wins among equals. Dev's double buffering of the same failure on two axes (the comment at `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:407-418` relies on last-wins) stays benign under max.
- Keep `peek-response` and one result-bearing settle (`flush-response-result!`). Either make `get-response` / `flush-response!` pure reads, or delete them while the API is pre-alpha (the Opus review's preference). Application `:rf.server/set-status` writes stay last-write-wins.

## Acceptance

- Regression test: handler exception then route miss settles at 500 with a 500 public error, and the Ring handler serves the error arm with no `__rf_payload` (fails today: 404, app body).
- A `peek-response` or `get-response` between drain and settle leaves the settle's `:public-error` intact (fails today for `get-response`).
- The existing two-frame and redirect-precedence tests (`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_flush_response_result_test.clj`) stay green in both postures: the implementation/ssr JVM lane and `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh`.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (SSR rendering §1), adopted into Opus's cross-review (ssr decision 13, Action 3). Probed during bead drafting.
- Related: rf2-6c25z (open, SSR prune follow-ups) touches a neighbouring comment in `ssr.cljc:407-414`; coordinate if both are in flight.
- Hot zones: `spec/API.md:407` names `get-response` / `peek-response` / `flush-response!` as implementation-tier internals, so deleting names touches `spec/API.md` and `spec/api-manifest*.edn`. Making them pure does not. `spec/011-SSR.md` (not a hot zone) needs §Drain-time error classification to state the max rule.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/ssr.md` decision 13, insight 3, Action 3; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/27-ssr-rendering.md` §1.

Not deleted, per the mayor's choice, so spec/API.md and its manifest sidecars are untouched. Application :rf.server/set-status writes keep last-write-wins.

title: Fresco staged-read snapshot can tie across a same-id frame reincarnation, leaving the old tenant's value painted
description:
## Bug

Fresco judges a staged read (a key read at render that has no cell yet) by a sum of counters, `commit-basis`, rather than by frame identity. In the following case the sum is equal at render and at commit:
- frame A is destroyed between a boundary's render and its commit;
- a successor B is made under the same id and reaches A's install count;
- no other cell anywhere flushes in the gap.

React's post-subscribe check then sees no change, and the boundary keeps showing A's value until its key is next written. On a tenant or session switch, that is the previous tenant's data on screen. The source and its own test concede the gap.

## Evidence

Trunk 475bdcaacf. Paths are under `implementation/`.

- `fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/generation.cljs:50-72`: `commit-basis` is `generation + frame-commit-epoch + registry-epoch`. The docstring concedes: "a frame holding no other cell ties either way".
- `fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/collector.cljs:786-810`: `make-snapshot` adds the live `commit-basis` for each key that has no cell. That is the number React re-reads.
- `fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/collector.cljs:414-436`: a cell created at commit is stamped with the current `commit-basis`, which is B's.
- `core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1853-1861` and `:4265-4273`: `frame-commit-epoch` counts installs per id, and `dissoc-frame!` clears it on destroy, so "a fresh same-id incarnation restarts at 0 — the incarnation change is what the port's `current?` / frame-identity checks detect, not the counter value." Fresco has no such identity check for staged keys.
- `fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/staged_reincarnation_basis_cljs_test.cljs:35-46`: the test pins the case where another held cell bumps the generation, and states the open half: "A frame holding NO other cell at the reincarnation has nothing to rewire, so no flush bumps the generation and the basis ties with or without the term".

Sequence (*read*; the source and test above concede the tie; not run):
1. A boundary renders a cold key `[:who]` on frame `:f`, incarnation A, which has install count N. It paints "A", and React records basis(A) = g + N + r.
2. Before the boundary's passive subscribe runs, `(rf/destroy-frame! :f)`, then `(rf/make-frame {:id :f})`. B is seeded with N installs, for example the one seed dispatch A also had.
3. Nothing else flushes, so `g` and `r` are unchanged.
4. Commit: the new cell is stamped g + N + r, and React's re-read compares equal numbers. No re-render is scheduled, and "A" stays painted.

Contract contrast: Spec 006 invariant 5, "Moved evidence corrects before paint" (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1072-1076`), requires a same-id frame reincarnation to be caught by the `:node-key` axis "when version + epochs coincide". Fresco's own rule says every operation is pinned to the incarnation it was minted under (`docs/design/fresco/product/invariants.md`, §The callback and frame-incarnation rule).

## Expected

A staged key's snapshot differs across a same-id reincarnation, so React re-renders the boundary against B before paint, whether or not other cells exist.

## Fix direction

Make the staged term incarnation-aware while keeping it a cached number (`getSnapshot` must not allocate). Either:
- do not restart `frame-commit-epoch` at 0 for a same-id successor (continue from the predecessor's last value, or from a global install counter); or
- add a lifecycle revision to `commit-basis` that advances on every `make-frame` and `destroy-frame!`.

Core already exposes `frame-incarnation-token` (`core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1405`) if an identity comparison at commit is preferred.

## Acceptance

- At the commit seam (`render-body` / `commit-boundary!` / `snapshot-of`, as in `staged_reincarnation_basis_cljs_test.cljs`): with zero other cells, equal install counts and different values, the post-subscribe snapshot differs from the render snapshot. This fails on today's code.
- Control: a quiet gap with no reincarnation leaves the snapshot equal and schedules no re-render.
- Cover one Fresco body and one `native/use-sub` one-key entry.
- The existing reincarnation, generation-fence and HMR registry rows stay green.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (report 23, §2; corroborated from core in report 03), adopted by the Opus fresco cross-review (decision 13, action 2a).
- Related: rf2-mn2ht.42 (route-link) is the other exception to Fresco's incarnation rule. rf2-6c12m.19 (closed) proved the generation term load-bearing and recorded this no-other-cell half as not its to close.
- Hot zones: none, unless the fix changes `frame-commit-epoch`'s documented semantics in `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/fresco.md` decision 13; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/23-fresco-react-runtime.md` §2.

Do not dispatch a second worker onto it until that worker reports.

title: Security.md trust-boundary matrix cites nonexistent fixtures, tests and namespaces and omits implementation/security/
description:
## Bug

The "Conformance / test coverage" and "Implementation hook" columns of `spec/Security.md`'s trust-boundary matrix cite things that do not exist: conformance fixtures, test files and namespaces. The matrix also never mentions `implementation/security/`, which is the reference implementation's adversarial security tier. Security.md says other-language ports read it as their contract, and the coverage column exists to give a port "a known-good harness target". So a port or AI pair following these citations finds nothing, and could conclude the defences are untested.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42). Every claim below was *read*, and each path's existence was checked.

- **`:266`, Editor URI template row.**
  - The hook `re-frame.dev.editor-template/*` names a namespace that exists nowhere. A repo-wide search for `re-frame.dev.editor-template|re-frame.dev.path-policy|re_frame/dev/` hits only Security.md `:266-267`.
  - The test `implementation/core/test/re_frame/dev/editor_template_test.cljc` is missing.
  - The "editor-scheme-reject fixture in conformance corpus" does not exist: none of the 243 fixtures mentions `javascript:`, `vbscript` or an editor scheme.
  - The real hook is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/editor_uri.cljc`, and the real test is `implementation/core/test/re_frame/source_coords_editor_uri_test.clj`.
- **`:267`, File-path boundary row.**
  - The hook "`re-frame.dev.path-policy/*` companion in CLJS reference" names a namespace that does not exist.
  - The row says "no shared framework helper", yet a shared helper exists: `implementation/scripts/_path-policy.cjs`, tested by `_path-policy.test.cjs`.
  - The helper's approved roots are `implementation/out` for outputs and `examples/`, `tools/` and `implementation/` for index-HTML sources. The row says "`implementation/` + `examples/` prefix list".
  - The cited "conformance harness's writing-tool isolation check" does not exist.
- **`:268`, SSR trusted-shell row.** The cited "SSR conformance fixture for `:rf.error/ssr-trusted-shell-opt-invalid`" does not exist. The real test is `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:356`.
- **`:269`, SSR response-shape row.** The cited "`:rf.error/safe-redirect-*` conformance fixtures" and "`:rf.error/header-invalid-value` / `:rf.error/redirect-invalid-location` fixtures" number 0. The real reference tests are `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_end_to_end_test.clj:339-344` (the CR/LF/NUL redirect gate) and `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_safe_redirect_production_test.clj`.
- **`:270`, HTTP decode row.** The cited "HTTP decode conformance fixtures (`:reason :too-many-keys`, `:reason :truncated-escape`, `:reason :invalid-escape`)" number 0. The real tests are `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_json_test.clj:19-23` and `http_decode_test.clj:45`.
- **The security tier is missing.** Security.md contains 0 mentions of `implementation/security/`. That directory holds the seeded hostile-input tier: XSS escaping, egress and schema redaction, fail-closed and fail-open classification, and generator parity across JVM and JS.
- **The search could find fixtures.** The same search finds `routing-query-keyword-discipline.edn`, which row `:271` cites correctly, and the unrelated `ssr-redirect.edn`. So the zero counts above mean the fixtures are absent, not that the search missed them.
- **Contract.** `spec/Security.md:4` says ports "read this doc as contract". The matrix's reading note (`:275`) says the coverage column "names the test or fixture that asserts the default holds (so a port has a known-good harness target)".

## Expected

Every hook and coverage cell in the matrix names something that exists. Where a defence has reference tests but no portable fixture, the cell says so. The matrix names `implementation/security/` as the reference's adversarial tier.

## Fix direction

- Correct the five rows to the real files listed above, marking those defences as "reference tests; no portable fixture".
- Fix the two phantom hooks, and the File-path row's helper and roots wording.
- Add one sentence near the matrix naming `implementation/security/`.
- Lifting the named hostile cases into portable Mode-B fixtures is a separate, larger change and is not required here.

## Acceptance

- Every path in the hook and coverage columns exists, and every fixture cited is findable in `spec/conformance/fixtures/`. Check this by hand or with a throwaway script. These are code spans, not links, so no link gate sees them; say so in the PR body.
- `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` stay green.

## Notes

- **Origin:** Opus conformance-security review (Insight 4, action 5a). Sol (surface 32, insight 5) independently found that the matrix's claimed fixtures are absent.
- **Related:** rf2-obdl (closed) fixed a different Security.md defect, the decisions log's Bead column.
- **Hot-zone files:** none. `spec/Security.md` is not on the list.
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/conformance-security.md` Insight 4; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/32-conformance-security.md` §5.

A throwaway checker parsed all 15 rows (8 cells each, so the table shape is checked too) and resolved each code span as a path, a glob or a namespace. Before the edit it found 6 missing spans; after it, 63 of 63 resolve and 0 are missing. The fixture prose left is the routing row's routing-query-keyword-discipline.edn, which exists. These are code spans, so no link gate sees them.

title: Spec 009 recommends the event-emit listener for off-box APM, but its :event ignores reg-event :sensitive
description:
## Bug

Spec 009 still recommends the always-on event-emit listener as the door for off-box APM forwarding (Datadog, Honeycomb, New Relic), and calls its record "post-elision" and "designed for direct hosted-backend forwarding". But the record's `:event` is walked only against the frame's durable path registry. A payload classified at registration, `(rf/reg-event :auth/login {:sensitive [[:password]]} …)`, reaches every event-emit listener raw, although the dev trace redacts it.

The ruling under the closed bead rf2-kuky.22 made this registry implementation tier, with no public verb, so no in-tree consumer ships it off-box today. A reader who follows 009's use-case table would.

## Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/event_emit.cljc:114-156` — `dispatch-on-event!` projects only `(rf.elision/elide-wire-value event {:frame frame})` (`:142`), which reads the durable `[:rf.runtime/elision]` registry. It never consults the handler's registration classification.
- Spec 009 says the opposite in two places:
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1335` — the use-case table row "Off-box APM forwarder … — ship event throughput + latency to a hosted backend, including in production" answers "#3 event-emit listener + #4 error-emit listener".
  - `:1372` — "#3 event-emit listener | YES — tight record shape, post-elision, exception-isolated. Designed for direct hosted-backend forwarding".
- The same spec, and the API page, say this registry is not a door:
  - 009 `:685` — "Independent corpus observation regardless of a frame's policy is therefore **not a public primitive**";
  - `spec/API.md:627` — "It carries **no public registration verb**: an application declares a `:handled-events` sink instead";
  - `spec/API.md:645`.
- `spec/API.md:621` says the walker makes "schema-marked `:sensitive?` paths land as `:rf/redacted`". Neither schema marks nor registration marks reach this walker: schema props do not classify durable paths (Spec 015 §Schemas describe shape), and the walker reads only the durable registry.
- In-tree listeners are all on-box: the Fresco test kit's intent capture (`implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test.cljs:633`), a Story console demo, and tests.

Repro (*probed* at trunk on the JVM, from `implementation/core`):

```clojure
(rf/reg-event :auth/login {:sensitive [[:password]]} (fn [_ _] {}))
(ee/register-event-listener! ::cap #(swap! recs conj %))
(rf/dispatch-sync [:auth/login {:user "alice" :password "SECRET"}])
;; event-emit record :event                → [:auth/login {:user "alice", :password "SECRET"}]
;; dev trace :rf.event/dispatched, run-start, run-end → :password :rf/redacted
```

Contract: Spec 015 §Registration-owned transient classification (`spec/015-Data-Classification.md:95-112`) says event payload paths are classified by the event's registration and redacted at egress. 009's table presents this route as a production egress.

## Expected

Spec 009 never directs an off-box shipper to a route that ignores registration-owned classification. Any record that is called "post-elision" honours `reg-event :sensitive`.

## Fix direction

- Point 009's use-case table (`:1335`, `:1372`) at the frame-owned `:observability :handled-events` sink. That route applies registration-aware projection and omits event args off-box by default.
- Correct API.md's "schema-marked `:sensitive?`" sentence (`:621`) to say what the walker actually reads.
- Optionally, and Mike's call:
  - either project the record's `:event` through the registration-aware event projector the trace uses, so the implementation tier is never a weaker view;
  - or retire the event-emit registry in favour of the sink route plus scoped capture, as the Opus observability review proposes (its Action 2).

## Acceptance

- `check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` pass on the edited spec pages. A by-hand read confirms no 009 or API.md sentence recommends the event-emit registry for off-box forwarding.
- If the projector option is taken: a JVM regression shows the probe above delivering `[:auth/login {:user "alice" :password :rf/redacted}]` to an event-emit listener (fails today), with an unmarked sibling unchanged.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (08 §3, 07 §2), read; probed at trunk for this draft.
- Related: closed rf2-kuky.22 (the one-production-door ruling that made the registry implementation tier); rf2-mn2ht.53 (graph export ignores a sub's own declaration, the same class).
- Hot-zone files: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` and `spec/API.md` are both hot. An API.md prose edit moves no public name, so the manifests stay untouched.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-observability.md` §10 and Action 2; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/08-core-privacy-projection.md` §3; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/07-core-observability.md` §2.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:46:19 AUSEST at HEAD 200a67df2d) ==

DECISION: Option 1 plus the full doc fix. `re-frame.event-emit/dispatch-on-event!` projects the record's `:event` through the event registration's `:sensitive` / `:large` pass, run in the owning frame's resolution scope, and then through the durable wire walk. That is the composition error-emit and the sink route already run, and it should come from ONE shared helper rather than a third private copy. The registry stays (implementation tier, per rf2-kuky.22). Spec 009 and API.md stop pointing off-box shippers at the registry and describe the projection as it actually is. Security.md, implementation/SECURITY.md and the skills already promise this projection; after the fix they are true.

WHY:
- A programmer declares `:sensitive` once, at registration. The framework should honour that declaration on every route it controls. Today event-emit is the only always-on route that skips it. The dev trace, the error-emit record (sibling registry, same dispatch) and both sink profiles all redact, even the most permissive one, `:rf.egress/local-raw`. So the event-emit record is weaker than every other view, and a dispatch that throws is redacted on the error-emit record but raw on the event-emit record.
- The fix is about ten lines that copy a composition already shipped in error-emit (`error_emit.cljc:626-636`), plus one test. It moves no public name, and its production cost is effectively zero: the record is built only when a listener exists (`event_emit.cljc:133` short-circuits on an empty registry).
- Three existing normative or teaching sentences become true without edits: Security.md :93 ("Each path must default-project") and :258 ("the always-on substrates project before fan-out"), implementation/SECURITY.md :36 ("the same projection-before-egress obligation"), and the privacy skill :128 ("the event-emit record ... ships `:password` → `:rf/redacted`"). The alternative is turning them into confessions.
- This closes the class the same way rf2-mn2ht.53 closed it for graph egress: reuse the existing projector, resolve in the owner's generation, and keep one code path so the routes cannot drift.

REJECTED:
- Option 2 (retire the event-emit registry; sink route plus a new scoped-capture seam). Nothing about this bug requires it. It reverses rf2-kuky.22's "stay" clause. It needs a new capture mechanism for the shipped Fresco test kit (`capture-intents`, the mounted driver's `open-log!`) and for `with-emit-recorder! {:stream :events}`, because the sink cannot substitute: it requires frame policy and omits `:event` off-box. It touches many hot-zone files. The Opus review's Action 2 also retires the error-emit half (about 100 test files, SSR's load-time listener, the console-fallback rule), which is a separate decision. Option 1 does not foreclose Option 2. No bead is filed for it: rf2-kuky.22 deliberately kept the registries and no defect asks to revisit that.
- Option 3 (doc fix only). It would leave a framework observer shipping a declared secret raw, and make the privacy matrix document a leak that a ten-line change closes. Every future reader, AI pairs included, would have to know to avoid `re-frame.event-emit`. That is the opposite of low hidden context and of trusting the programmer's declaration.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- Dossier author: Option 1 plus the doc fix, with a shared helper. Codex: the same ("keep the implementation registry, apply the existing event-classification projector before its wire walker, and correct the production-monitoring documentation"). The bead carried no recommendation of its own. I agree with both.
- One wording disagreement, settled for Codex. The dossier's follow-up text said API.md :620 should be "corrected to say the walker reads registration marks plus the durable registry". Codex: "Describe the registration pass and durable walker separately; the walker itself does not read registration marks." Codex is right at HEAD. `re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value` reads only the frame's durable `[:rf.runtime/elision]` registry; the registration pass is a separate step (`:classification/redact-event-by-registration`) that runs BEFORE the walker. The prose must name two steps, not attribute the registration marks to the walker.
- Test shape, settled by combining both. The dossier asked for a JVM regression. Codex asked for a shared JVM/CLJS test that also checks the handler still receives the raw value, plus an image-local arm resolving through the record's owner. I adopt Codex's fuller shape. The image-local arm is the one that tells a correct owner-scoped call from a naive `(redact event)` call, which would pass the basic case.
- Facts: there is no factual disagreement. Both reviews probed the same defect independently, and I re-probed at HEAD (below).

EVIDENCE (HEAD 200a67df2d; no cited source file changed between the dossier's read at 3ae452324e and HEAD, except classification.cljc, which gained `project-sub-value` from rf2-mn2ht.53 and leaves the event path untouched):
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/event_emit.cljc:142` — the record's only privacy step is `(rf.elision/elide-wire-value event {:frame frame})`. The ns docstring (:73-77) says the same: "the record's `:event` runs through `re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value` against the frame's `[:rf.runtime/elision]` registry". The fn docstring (:118-135) promises "sensitive paths → `:rf/redacted`".
- `error_emit.cljc:455-468`, private `redact-event-by-registration [event frame-id]`: the late-bound `:classification/redact-event-by-registration` hook inside `:live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution` for `frame-id`. Applied at :634-636 as `(-> (redact-event-by-registration event frame-id) (rf.elision/elide-wire-value {:frame frame-id}))`. Its comment at :627-632 describes this bead's defect exactly: "without them this record would ship a declared-sensitive arg RAW while both sibling channels redacted it."
- `projection.cljc:281-323` holds a second private copy (`redact-event-by-registration [event elision-opts]`, identical semantics including the nil-owner case) and `project-event-slot [event elision-opts]` = registration pass, then `walk-slot` (= `elide-wire-value v elision-opts`).
- `classification.cljc:449-490` — `redact-event-by-registration` is the single event-vector chokepoint: static registration `:sensitive` / `:large`, plus the dynamic per-event-id layer (`:rf.mutation/execute`, `:rf.route/handle-url-change` / `:navigate` / `:url-requested`). Its docstring says it is "ALWAYS-ON (NOT gated on `interop/debug-enabled?`)". It is published at :1545. So the fix inherits the mutation and route projections as well as the password case.
- `router.cljc:2922-2952` — the router calls the event-emit registry and the `:observability/route-handled-event` sink route as two SIBLING fan-outs. The sink does not ride event-emit.
- Probe (this ruling), JVM, `cd implementation/core && clojure -M -i <scratch>/probe.clj`, exit 0, run at 9b51da3393. No source file on the event path changed between 9b51da3393 and 200a67df2d: the range touched resources/http, fresco roots, 009/016 prose, and `event_emit_cljs_test.cljc`, which gained an unrelated outcome test (`listener-reports-a-throwing-effect-as-ok-beside-its-error-record`). Setup: plain-atom adapter, `:rf/default`, `(rf/reg-event :auth/login {:sensitive [[:password]]} …)`, unmarked control `:auth/hello`, a marked `:auth/login-boom` that throws, and one event-emit listener plus one error-emit listener:
    == handler received :password "SECRET"
    == event-emit listener :event (HEAD)
       [:auth/login {:user "alice", :password "SECRET"}] outcome :ok
       [:auth/hello {:user "bob", :password "PLAIN"}] outcome :ok
       [:auth/login-boom {:user "carol", :password "SECRET2"}] outcome :error
    == error-emit listener :event (HEAD)
       :rf.error/handler-exception [:auth/login-boom {:user "carol", :password :rf/redacted}]
    == OPTION 1 composition: registration pass in owner scope, then durable walk
       [:auth/login {:user "alice", :password :rf/redacted}]
       [:auth/hello {:user "bob", :password "PLAIN"}]
  The last block is exactly what a listener receives under this ruling. The unmarked control is unchanged, and the handler still sees the real value, so the correction belongs at observation, not execution.
- The dossier author's wider probe (same HEAD family, exit 0) also showed: the default off-box `:handled-events` sink record omits `:event` entirely (`{:event-id :auth/login, :frame :rf/default, :correlation {:dispatch-id 1}, :status :ok, :kind :rf.observe/handled-event, :elapsed-ms 8}`); the `:rf.egress/local-raw` sink and the dev trace `:rf.event/v` both carry `:password :rf/redacted`. Codex reproduced the defect and the composition independently (`clojure -M -` from stdin, exit 0), and again under `-J-Dre-frame.debug=false` (exit 0, `:debug-enabled false`).
- Prior ruling, rf2-kuky.22 (closed 2026-09-06), close reason verbatim: "RULED: A — one production observation door: frame :observability + configure! {:observability …} process default via register-observability-sink!; :events/:errors leave register-listener! (vocabulary #{:trace :epoch}); error-emit/event-emit stay ^:no-doc implementation registries; Q4 ruled: unresolved-owner records route to the process default, fail-closed, never re-resolved, carried through the producer seam; follow-ups rf2-kuky.65 (A0 attribution) → rf2-kuky.67 (A1 default+frameless) → rf2-kuky.69 (A2 retirement), fixed order; notes on rf2-xpd8, rf2-kuky.21, rf2-kuky.20". Its ruling note: "independent corpus observation regardless of a frame's policy is WITHDRAWN as a PUBLIC primitive. It remains for the framework (the implementation registries) and for tests (a `re-frame.test-support` capture bracket)." Its non-goals: "Do not merge the sink with the raw streams (raw vs projected is load-bearing EP-0015 architecture); `re-frame.error-emit` / `re-frame.event-emit` stay as the substrate's fan-out." This ruling is consistent with it: the tier stays and only the record gets safer. Note that "raw" never meant "ignores registration marks". Event-emit already runs the durable walk and the router's db-focus redaction pass (`rf.privacy/redact-event`, `router.cljc:2517-2519`), so it is half-projected today. The error-emit sibling, the other "raw stream", already runs the registration pass.
(RULING continued, part 2 of 2)
IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
- Code (isolated; parallel-safe):
  - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/event_emit.cljc` `dispatch-on-event!`: replace the bare walk at :142 with registration pass (owner scope = the record's `frame`) → `elide-wire-value {:frame frame}`. Keep everything else as it is: the `continuation-live?` checks around each step, the try/catch re-throw shape, `:rf.trace/no-emit?` suppression, the empty-registry short-circuit, and listener isolation.
  - ONE shared helper. error_emit.cljc:455 and projection.cljc:281 are two private copies of the same frame-scoped wrapper; do not add a third. Hoist one and switch error-emit to it as well. A natural placement is to make `re-frame.projection`'s composition public (e.g. `project-event-slot` called with `{:frame frame-id}`, which is exactly registration pass then walk). `re-frame.projection` requires only elision / error / late-bind, so event_emit and error_emit can require it without a cycle (checked at HEAD: frame.cljc requires error / interop / late-bind / adapter / trace, and nothing below projection reaches the emitters). Placement is the implementer's call. The constraints: neither emitter may statically require `re-frame.classification` (they reach it through the late-bind hook, and an unbound hook stays inert / pass-through), and a nil owner keeps today's semantics (redact in ambient scope; the walker then fails closed on `{:frame nil}`). Keep error-emit's existing skip for `raw-identity-event?` / nil event (:632).
  - Docstrings: the event_emit ns docstring (:73-77) and the `dispatch-on-event!` docstring (:118-135) name the two steps. error_emit's helper docstring is updated if the helper moves.
- Failing-first test: add arms to `implementation/core/test/re_frame/event_emit_cljs_test.cljc` (runs on the JVM in both postures and on Node; reuse its `reset-runtime` fixture and `record-events!`):
  (a) `(rf/reg-event :auth/login {:sensitive [[:password]]} …)` dispatched with `{:user "alice" :password "SECRET"}` → the listener's `:event` = `[:auth/login {:user "alice" :password :rf/redacted}]`;
  (b) an unmarked sibling's payload arrives unchanged;
  (c) the handler itself received `"SECRET"`;
  (d) an image-local declaration: copy `install-login-frame!` from `implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_projection_owner_scope_cljs_test.cljc`, dispatch into that frame, and assert redaction, which proves the pass resolves in the record owner's generation, not the ambient one.
  Red at base (a and d fail), green with the fix, red again with only the src reverted. Report exit codes. Keep the existing outcome tests in `event_emit_cljs_test.cljc` green, and the advanced-build witness (`event_emit_elision_prod_test.cljs:22-30`); neither tests this guarantee today.
- Consumers whose comments become false (tools/ and fresco test kit; isolated):
  - `tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/elision_demo.cljs`: the "What to look for" bullet (:59-63, "it shows the original event vector, because the registration classification redacts on the trace surface, not in the implementation-tier event-emit record"), the `log-record!` comment (:238-243, "redacted on the trace surface, not here"), and check the header block (:210-230) still reads true.
  - `tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/core.cljs:107-111` ("The `:auth/sign-in` password shows raw there …").
  - `implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test.cljs` `capture-intents` docstring (:600-630) and `docs/core/fresco/api-reference.md:397`: add one sentence saying that an event whose registration declares `:sensitive` paths is captured with those paths as `:rf/redacted`, as on every other observation surface. The mounted driver's `open-log!` reads the same port. `ht/intents` (what the tree OFFERS) stays raw, so a test comparing offered and captured intents for a classified event must write `:rf/redacted` in the captured expectation. That is intended (it matches production), and the census found no test doing it.
- Doc fix (HOT-ZONE: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` and `spec/API.md`; sequence alone, never in parallel with another worker on either file). Prose only; no public name moves, so `spec/api-manifest*.edn` are untouched. Line numbers are at HEAD 200a67df2d:
  - 009 :1335 (use-case table, "Off-box APM forwarder"): answer the frame-owned `:observability :handled-events` sink (+ `:errors` sink), declared on the frame or once per process via `(rf/configure! {:observability …})` and wired with `register-observability-sink!`, not "#3 event-emit listener + #4 error-emit listener". Drop "already post-elision, already wire-shaped" as a reason to pick the registry.
  - 009 :1372 (off-box egress contract, "#3 event-emit listener | YES … Designed for direct hosted-backend forwarding"): the registry is implementation tier and not an application door (consistent with 009 :685 and API.md :626). Its privacy cell names both steps: registration marks first, then the durable walk.
  - 009 :1320 (row "3. Handled-event sink"): it gives the sink the registry's record shape `{:event :event-id :frame :time :outcome :elapsed-ms}`. The real `:rf.observe/handled-event` record is `{:kind :frame :event-id :status :elapsed-ms :effects :correlation}`: `projection.cljc:338-339` `handled-event-summary-keys`. It has no `:time`, it uses `:status` rather than `:outcome`, and `:event` is present only when the entry opts sensitive content back in (`include-event-args?`, :341-346; `project-handled-event`, :348-357), and then projected.
  - 009 :1222 (#1 "The handled-event observation surface … runs through a small always-on event-emit substrate"): the router fans out to the registry and the sink route as SIBLINGS (`router.cljc:2922-2952`); the sink does not run through event-emit. The record shape quoted in that paragraph is the registry's, not the sink's.
  - 009 :2763 ("The two always-on substrate boundaries (event-emit, error-emit) … rely on the per-path elision wire-walker, which reads the per-frame … registry"): add the registration pass that both substrates run before the walker.
  - API.md :620 (§Event-emit: "the `:event` slot is passed through the size-elision wire-boundary walker once before fan-out, so schema-marked `:sensitive?` paths land as `:rf/redacted`"): two steps. First the event registration's `:sensitive` / `:large` paths (and the dynamic mutation / route layer); then the walker against the frame's durable classification. Schema `:sensitive?` props do not reach this walker.
  - API.md :624 ("Sensitive data marking is path-based … There is no handler-meta `:sensitive?` annotation."): keep the boolean-`:sensitive?` point, and add that registration `:sensitive [paths]` IS honoured on this record.

title: hicasso: attack the interpreter-walk mount cost — the located deficit is 100% script, +1.06ms where uix pays +0.38ms on byte-identical DOM
description:
THE OPTIMISATION LANE'S PRIMARY TARGET, opened under the operator's 2026-08-02 directive ('keep going on the actual implementation, the optimisation can happen in parallel').

WHERE THE DEFICIT LIVES, from three independent measurements that agree:
  - rf2-0qj9w located it: the candidate pays +1.06 ms over its own floor where uix-subs — same spine, same adapter, same 300 reads, BYTE-IDENTICAL DOM — pays +0.38 ms. The runtime hiccup codec walking 901 elements.
  - rf2-emvod/rf2-yd52q: taskNet reads every gated pair 0.98-1.08 — the gap is ENTIRELY script, zero frame.
  - rf2-2rtt6.56 (census rows): typical census shape 1.16-1.22x vs UIx (instrument-limited at the 1.10 line); worst case 1.3053x on the ONE-BOUNDARY 1,202-element page — the pure interpreter-walk shape. The deficit scales with elements-per-boundary, not boundaries.
  - rf2-2rtt6.31 (HD-008 re-take): donor arms show the same ~10-13% interpreter cost over UIx at their shapes.

SO THE TARGET IS THE PER-ELEMENT COST OF THE HICCUP WALK: parse/classify/convert per element per mount. The one-boundary page (1,202 elements, one commit) is the acceptance shape — it currently FAILS the 1.10x line at 1.3053x [1.1044-1.4660] with an 18.7% margin clearing a 6.7% band; the census feed is the guard shape (it must not regress from 1.1646x).

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, to be costed not assumed — and the PRIOR-ART DIRECTIVE applies in full (mine Freehand, re-frame.ui, Replicant, Reagent, UIx; cite taken/declined):
  1. CACHE THE STATIC SKELETON: most census markup is static per view; Replicant and every compiled substrate exploit this. re-frame.ui's compiler shows what static extraction buys; the question is what a RUNTIME can cache keyed on the hiccup's identity without a compiler (fences: no compiler, no analyzer — but a value-keyed cache at the codec is neither).
  2. CHEAPEN THE PER-ELEMENT PATH: prop-map conversion, keyword->string, intent classification — profile first, the walk has never been profiled element-by-element.

title: Examples review: runner and shared assets, examples/scripts and _shared and the two READMEs (5 findings: dev:example stages the plain index.html for both Story-showcase builds so stories.index.html is served by nothing; the README's advanced note is false for three dev-http builds; TESTING.md describes a two-adapter smoke roster the tree outgrew)
description:
Filed from the review wave under epic rf2-fn0kx (report runner.md). The report below is the reviewer's, verbatim.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## Worker rules

- Every path:line below was read at the FROZEN review tree named in the report header. Re-verify each cite at the current trunk before editing; the review wave's earlier beads found premises that had moved.
- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.
- Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing.
- The shadow-cljs build lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor: ask before any build, and prefer static checks and the JVM lanes.
- Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Skills gates live in scripts/check_skill_*.py; run the ones that name your surface and say which.
- No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes.

---

# Senior review: examples runner and shared assets (examples/scripts, examples/_shared, examples/README.md, examples/TESTING.md)

Reviewer persona: senior build/tooling engineer reading the connective tissue every example depends on: the dev runner, staging, asset manifest, the two static gates, the Story launchers, and the three pages that describe them.
Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca
Scope read: all 13 `examples/scripts/*.cjs` in full (~5,460 lines); `examples/README.md` (165), `examples/TESTING.md` (164), `examples/_shared/README.md` (67); `_shared/css/*` (imports + media queries); the four `<base>`-bearing host pages plus both `stories.index.html` pages and their sibling `index.html`; `implementation/scripts/_navigation-ceiling-policy.test.cjs` (531); the `:examples/*` and `:dev-http` regions of `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` (~500 lines); `implementation/package.json` scripts; exports of `implementation/scripts/lib/local-browser-harness.cjs`; the job headers in `.github/workflows/test.yml` and `expensive-tests.yml` that run the example gates.
Surfaces the examples teach, consulted: CLAUDE.md §Build & Test (test-free lock rf2-8cevm, derived compile sweep, adapter-smoke roster); `implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs` (warning-fails logic); `implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs`; `implementation/adapters/TESTING.md`; `examples/core/login/README.md` and `examples/patterns/nine_states/README.md` (the run commands the top README defers to).
Checks run: `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` (58 builds: 44 `examples/*` + 14 `testbeds/*`, exit 0); `node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs` (33 host pages, exit 0); `node examples/scripts/check-reagent-slim-boundary.cjs` (74 sources, exit 0); `listStandaloneExamples()` from `examples-staging.cjs` required read-only under node (34 runnable entries); no build, no port, no browser.

Overall: this slice is in good shape. The scripts are correct on every axis the brief named (port collision, clean-stage, manifest, walks, navigation timeouts, Windows paths), both static gates are green, and the README's deep-link claim holds because every example that registers a 2+-segment history route carries `<base href="/">`. What follows is one real packaging seam (finding 1) and four one-sentence documentation drifts; nothing here is a morning's work.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. `dev:example` stages the plain `index.html` for both Story-showcase builds; `stories.index.html` is served by nothing the READMEs name  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: packaging] [size: S]
- Where: `examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs:367` (`htmlSrc = path.join(srcDir, 'index.html')`), consumed by `examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs:425`; readers are sent there by `examples/core/login/README.md:75,91`, `examples/patterns/nine_states/README.md:162,191`, `examples/README.md:165`.
- What: `listStandaloneExamples()` locates a build's host page by the FOLDER of its init-fn namespace and always names `index.html`, so `examples/login-with-stories` (init-fn `login.stories-host/run`, folder `examples/core/login`) stages `examples/core/login/index.html`, and `examples/nine-states-with-stories` stages `examples/patterns/nine_states/index.html`, while the two `stories.index.html` files both READMEs call "host page for the Story-showcase build" are staged by nothing.
- Evidence: `listStandaloneExamples()` run read-only in the frozen tree: `examples/login-with-stories | html=examples/core/login/index.html`, `examples/nine-states-with-stories | html=examples/patterns/nine_states/index.html` (control: `examples/login | html=examples/core/login/index.html`, 34 entries total). `diff` of each `index.html` against its `stories.index.html` differs only in `<title>`, `description`, `og:title`, `og:description`; the bodies are identical (`<div id="app">` + `<script src="main.js">`), so today the showcase still boots and the visible symptom is the plain example's tab title and OG card. The only server that reaches `stories.index.html` at all is a bare `shadow-cljs watch` via `:dev-http` 8040/8041 (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:634-639`, source dir first in `:roots`), and even there `/` resolves the plain `index.html`; the showcase page sits at `/stories.index.html`, a URL no README names. The staging self-test (`implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs:324-329`) asserts only that `htmlSrc` exists, so it pins the current behaviour without noticing which page it is. Meanwhile `check-examples-assets.cjs:357-359` enumerates `*.index.html` and enforces the shared-asset contract on both showcase pages (rf2-x48bp4): a gate on pages the runner never serves. The trap is latent: an edit to `stories.index.html` (an Xray host `<aside>`, a different mount id) would be silently ignored by the documented command while the gate kept it green.
- Action: decide A or B. A (keep the pages): in `listStandaloneExamples`, when the init-fn ns's last segment ends in `-host` (source file `<prefix>_host.cljs`), prefer `<prefix>.index.html` if it exists, else `index.html`; add one assertion to `_examples-staging.test.cjs` that `examples/login-with-stories` resolves `stories.index.html`. B (retire the pages): delete the two `stories.index.html` files and drop the "host page for the Story-showcase build" line from both READMEs; the showcase is already "the same page plus `#/stories`", which is exactly what both READMEs tell the reader to do. B is smaller and removes a file nothing serves; A keeps a distinct title/OG card for the showcase. Either is one PR.

### 2. `examples/README.md` "Advanced" note is false for the three builds whose `:dev-http` entry roots the source folder  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S]
- Where: `examples/README.md:23`; `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:634-654` (`:dev-http` 8040 → `../examples/patterns/nine_states`, 8041 → `../examples/core/login`, 8044 → `../examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite`).
- What: the note says `shadow-cljs watch <build-id>` "stages no host page, copies no `_shared/` assets, and starts no server, so there is no URL to open and the example's own `index.html` cannot find its `main.js`". For `examples/nine-states-with-stories`, `examples/login-with-stories` and `examples/linearlite` a watch DOES start shadow's dev-http (8040/8041/8044) with the source dir first in `:roots`, so `index.html` is served at `/` and `main.js` falls through to the out dir (the "source-dir-first cascade" the edn comments describe). What is true for those three is only that `_shared/` is not staged, so the page comes up unstyled with a broken favicon and OG card.
- Evidence: `:dev-http` map read at `shadow-cljs.edn:628-654`; its own comment advertises `http://localhost:8040/#/stories` and `8041/#/stories`. Control: no other runnable example build has a `:dev-http` entry (keys are 8030-8035, 8040-8045, 8060-8061, 8765; the rest root Xray/Story/top-level testbeds). Neither `examples/README.md` nor the three examples' own READMEs mention the port (grep `804[0-5]|dev-http` over the five pages: 0 hits; the same grep over `shadow-cljs.edn` hits).
- Action: one sentence in the Advanced note: "Three builds also carry a `:dev-http` entry that serves their source folder directly (the login and nine-states showcases on 8040/8041, linearlite on 8044); that page loads without `_shared/`, so it is unstyled. Use `npm run dev:example` for the running app." S.

### 3. `examples/_shared/README.md` §Inline Xray shell names two of the three pages that use the shell  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S]
- Where: `examples/_shared/README.md:53`; `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/index.html:25-33`.
- What: the section says "The `counter` and `flows` examples mount Xray beside the app with the same DOM contract"; `realworld_resources/index.html` carries the identical `.rf2-testbed-shell` + `<aside data-rf-xray-host>` markup, with its own comment saying the dev build mounts Xray into that column.
- Evidence: `git grep -l rf2-testbed-shell -- 'examples/**/*.html'` → 3 files (core/counter, core/flows, real-apps/realworld_resources); `data-rf-xray-host` → the same 3. Control: the two pages the README names are among the hits.
- Action: name the third page, or phrase it as "the pages whose `index.html` carries `.rf2-testbed-shell` (counter, flows and realworld-resources today)". S.

### 4. `examples/TESTING.md` and the `spec-helpers.cjs` header describe the smoke roster as two adapters; the tree has three smokes plus a Fresco spec consuming the helpers  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S]
