Clause 3 blocked it and clause 1 would have too, 17 being nowhere near the band. One tick of waiting took it to 88/0/0 with no action of any kind. That is the second time in this session that a below-band rollup resolved itself by waiting, and both times the tempting alternative was to go hunting for missing coverage that was never missing.

## WHAT LANDED

**F1**: the restore-refusal signal described a `:rf.epoch/*` envelope the tool never emits. Verified at source — the runtime primitive returns a bare `false`, so `restore_epoch.cljs` emits `:restore-rejected` carrying no `:operation` and no `:tags`. The old ownership split therefore filed EVERY refused restore as tool-shaped. The discriminator is now the refusal's own `:hint`, which is the thing that actually distinguishes the cases.

**F2**: the diagnostic ladder is `ensure-runtime!`'s; `resolve-and-preflight!` never calls it and folds everything into `:no-runtime-for-build`.

**F3**: the phantom cite at `:175` — "re-frame2's Tool-Pair surface index (availability legend + production note)", a document that has never existed — repointed to `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Production debugging: what remains, along with its echo at `:178`.

**F4**: both tests named in `design.md`, `authoring-prompt.md`, `README.md` and `evals/README.md`, replacing the "the skill's only test" assertion that stood in five places while two CI-gated tests shipped.

Verified at trunk after merge: the phantom cite reads **0**, `009-Instrumentation` reads **3**, both test names appear in `design.md`, and `known-frictions.md` is still **exactly 250 lines** — the worker's own claim, and the leaf sits at the line ceiling so it mattered.

## THE MAYOR'S "NO GATE WITH TEETH" PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND USEFULLY SO

The brief told this worker its item probably had **no gate with teeth**, on the reasoning that its diff was prose inside one skill's leaves and that the two gates naming the skill both merely record that they skip it. It said plainly that planting nowhere would be an expected and acceptable outcome.

**That was wrong.** `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/tests/eval_corpus_shape_test.clj` **slurps `evals/README.md` and asserts on its content**, so it genuinely grades the F4 edit. The worker found it, planted the false-provenance sentence that test forbids by name into the very paragraph it had rewritten, predicted the match count (0 before, 1 after) and hit it, took the sabotage run to exit **1** naming the assertion, restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, and verified by BLOB hash — default-form `git hash-object` equal to the committed `e893edbacd2656ad01a824039560fbc8276bb5b8`, `git diff --quiet HEAD` exit 0, post-restore re-run exit 0.

**The lesson is about where I looked rather than about being wrong.** I rostered gates by reading `scripts/`, and this gate is not in `scripts/` — it is a `bb` test inside the skill's own `tests/` directory, looped by CI's `skills-structural` job. A skill's own test suite is part of its gate set, and a roster built by searching the gate directory cannot see it. **Brief the skill's own `tests/` as a gate surface, not just `scripts/`.**

## FURTHER CORRECTIONS — THREE MORE, ALL ACCEPTED

1. **The reviewer's own proposed wording for F2 is a false universal.** It said "Every tool other than `discover-app` reports `:no-runtime-for-build`" — but `watch-until` also calls `ensure-runtime!` and takes the ladder path, while `tail-build` and `get-re-frame2-pair-instructions` need no runtime at all. The worker wrote it against the EVAL PATH instead, which is the true scope. The reviewer's COUNT holds exactly, file-for-file: 23 of 50 tool files.
2. **The F3 fix's own suggested replacement cited a SECOND phantom.** The report proposed citing "mcp-transport.md §Fail loud" — which is a **bullet, not a heading**. Writing it verbatim would have planted a fresh phantom cite inside the edit whose entire purpose was to remove one. The worker cited the real heading. This is the sharpest thing on this item: a correction that reproduces the defect it corrects, caught only because the worker checked the replacement as carefully as the original.
3. **F1's evidence was slightly off, in the SAFE direction.** `rf.epoch` reads **1** in the restore-epoch descriptor, not 0 — the descriptor promises "the documented `:rf.epoch/*` failure modes" while the envelope carries none of them. That STRENGTHENS the finding rather than weakening it, and the worker said so rather than quietly adopting the better number.

The brief's two "this gate does NOT grade you" claims were both confirmed at source. The worker also independently re-derived the `check_skill_eval_docs.py:209` NOTE showing `re-frame2-improver` deliberately absent from `TARGETS` — the same finding the `rf2-ikbgk.5` worker made, reached separately.

## GATES

The diff adds no link and no anchor and touches no table. Line endings checked with Python on the bytes, CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0 on all five files.

## HELD, NOT DECIDED — ONE, AND IT BELONGS ELSEWHERE

`skills/README.md:296` records this leaf as `250 L / 17,260 B`. **The line count still holds — verified at trunk, exactly 250 — but the byte figure is now stale.** That file is outside this slice's fence and belongs to the cross-cutting slice `rf2-ikbgk.11`, which is already closed; no gate reads the figure, so nothing is red. It wants folding into whatever pass next touches that roster — and note that the leaf-roster question on those very pages is itself an open operator ruling, so this may be settled for free by that decision.

title: fix(story): promotion drops the terminal expectation that made the source variant fail — artifact->variant-body (promotion.cljc:220) copies neither :assertions nor :expect, so a promoted regression runs :pass with 0 assertions
description:
Found independently by all three Story-parity research passes (ai/findings/Story/{astra,grok,fable}/report.md, 2026-09-14) and reproduced by two of them on the JVM at trunk 98e8ffe9cb; the mayor verified the builder's location at source. Filed under rf2-rln91 (R0a in the fable report).

WHAT: a variant registered with `:assertions [[:rf.assert/path-equals [:v] 42]]` (or any false terminal expectation) runs `:fail` with 1 assertion. Promote its run artifact (`make-run-artifact` -> `materialize-variant-plan` -> `promote-run-artifact!`, the same helpers the Test-mode promotion dialog uses with its default inheritance choice): the registered body carries the keys `(:doc :run-artifact)` plus the script and source link, and NO `:assertions`/`:expect`. The promoted variant then runs `:pass` with `:assertions []` although the expected condition never became true. Builder: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/promotion.cljc:220` `artifact->variant-body`.

THE BOUNDARY, measured (astra's positive control): an expectation that lives INSIDE the retained event program — the assertion dispatched as an event / an `[:assert ...]` step whose event is captured — survives promotion and fails both before and after. What is lost is a declarative expectation authored OUTSIDE the retained event program (`:assertions` / `:expect` on the variant). So promotion is not universally broken; the missing coverage is exactly the declarative case, which is the case the tutorial teaches ("the variant is a test").

WHY IT MATTERS: "generated failures promote to curated variants" is one of the eight surpass items in tools/story/spec/018-Story-UI-North-Star.md section 3.1 and one of the workflows the docs sell (docs/story/06-xray-earned-at-failure.md). A promoted regression that cannot fail is a claimed win that lies; the research re-scored that row from BUILT to SPECIFIED on this defect alone.

FIX (S-M), at the PROMOTION BOUNDARY: `artifact->variant-body` must explicitly carry the applicable declarative expectations of the source variant (its `:assertions` / `:expect`, and the DOM-driven `:script` assertions where the source had them) into the promoted body. Do NOT change ordinary `:extends` inheritance to get there — terminal assertions deliberately do not inherit through `:extends`, which is a coherent reuse rule; promotion is the one transformation that must preserve intent. Add a pinning test.

ACCEPTANCE (the fail/pass/fail the reports ask for): reintroduce the original fault -> the promoted variant runs `:fail` with the same assertion count as its source; fix the app -> `:pass`; restore the fault -> `:fail`. Include one DOM-driven case (clicks/typing/waits/assertions in `:script`) because flat event extraction is not automatically equivalent to retaining them. GATES: tools/story JVM tests (`clojure -M:test` from tools/story) and the CLJS story suite; not a hot zone. Do not add a universal inheritance-removal or merge API.
notes:
== CORRECTION to the description's boundary paragraph (mayor re-frame2-fe, 2026-09-14 11:20 AUSEST) ==
The description says an `[:assert ...]` script step "whose event is captured" survives promotion. It does NOT. The fable pass's probe4 control (ai/findings/Story/fable/evidence.md section P4, JVM at 98e8ffe9cb) put the same assertion as a `[:assert ...]` script step and it was dropped too: `artifact->variant-body` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/promotion.cljc:220-264) builds `:setup`/`:script` from the artifact's `:event-program` via `partition-program` (:200-214) and copies `:network`, `:fx-overrides`, `:extends`, `:tags`, `:args` and the provenance link; it never reads `:assertions` or `:expect`, and an `[:assert ...]` step is a RUNNER step, not a dispatched event, so it is not in the program either. The ONLY expectation that survives today is one dispatched as an `:rf.assert/*` EVENT (astra's positive control: promoted `:script [[:dispatch [:login/flow [:login/dismiss]]] [:dispatch [:rf.assert/path-equals [:missing] 42]]]` still fails). So the acceptance covers THREE source shapes, not two: declarative `:assertions`/`:expect`, an `[:assert ...]` script step, and a DOM-driven `:script` case — each promoted variant must run `:fail` at the fault with the source's assertion count, `:pass` when fixed, `:fail` when restored. Fix stays at the promotion boundary; `:extends` inheritance unchanged; no copying of old result records as if they were new assertions.
== WORKER VERDICT (worker/storypromo-a, PR #9804, 2026-09-14) ==
REPRODUCED at base a34c318c8d on the JVM before any change. A source variant with a false terminal `:assertions` entry ran :fail with 1 assertion. Its promoted twin ran :pass with 0 assertions, both through the Test-mode dialog's helpers (`result->artifact` over `variant-play-events`, default draft with `:extends` = origin, `:setup-count 0`) and through the API route (a `determinism/->artifact` of the plan, promoted with only `:variant/id`).

ON THE CORRECTION NOTE: it is right for the dialog route, not universally. An `[:assert ...]` script step was DROPPED on the dialog route, because Test mode captures only the dispatch-only projection of the program. The same step SURVIVED the API route (:fail, 1 assertion), because `determinism/->artifact` folds the plan's full `:script` into `:event-program`. A dispatched `:rf.assert/*` event survived both routes.

FIX (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/promotion.cljc, promotion boundary only):
- `source-variant-id` reads the variant the ARTIFACT records as its source, `[:source :variant/id]` or `[:result :variant/id]`. An `:extends` parent is never treated as a source.
- `source-expectations` carries that registered variant's own `:assertions` and `:checks` onto the promoted body.
- `retained-program` replaces a dispatch-only capture with the source's full step program (`rf.story.play/variant-play-steps`). It fires only when every artifact step is a dispatch, the source has a non-dispatch step, and the two dispatch sequences are equal, so generated, shrunk and recorded programs are untouched.
- `:extends` inheritance is unchanged. There is no merge or inheritance API, and no result records are copied.
- One line outside promotion.cljc: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/promotion.cljc` `promotion-snippet` now renders `:checks`/`:assertions`, so the copy-to-source snippet matches what is registered. Neither file is held by another worker.
- `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` §Promotion bridge gains a "Source intent" paragraph.

TESTS: fail/pass/fail by both routes for declarative `:assertions`, an `[:assert]` step, and a dispatched `:rf.assert/*` event (regression guard). Also:
- ordinary `:extends` still gives a child no terminal assertions;
- only a recorded, registered source is carried;
- a DOM-driven structural twin;
- a browser suite (`promotion_dom_cljs_test.cljs`) that runs a typing, clicking, waiting and asserting source through the dialog capture under the `:dom` runner, fail/pass/fail;
- the snippet renders carried assertions.
No existing test pinned the old behaviour.

CONTROLS (planted in promotion.cljc; each restore verified by blob hash against HEAD):
- `:assertions` carry disabled: JVM 7 failures (declarative both routes, recorded-source, DOM twin, snippet). The checkpoint and dispatched-event tests stayed green.
- Program restoration disabled: JVM 5 failures (dialog-route checkpoint, DOM twin). The browser suite also went red.

FOLLOW-UP CANDIDATE, not done here: the dialog snippet also omits `:network`/`:fx-overrides`, which rf2-vf8es lifted onto the body.
Merged-PR audit #9804: new open finding rf2-6h2z3 tracks the incomplete promotion verdict-preservation claim for a source using :compose to name a check. Real source fails with one check/assertion; both dialog and API promoted variants pass with zero. Carrying the check restores fail/pass/fail. See rf2-6h2z3 for correction and regression criteria. Original status/closure preserved; no mayor notification or acknowledgment inferred.

title: xstate-parity: a 3-element [:raise ev opts] returned by an action fn is not refused — runtime check at both drains' fx routing (split from rf2-2n6uv.1.6 arm f)
description:
Split out of rf2-2n6uv.1.6, "five registration holes", arm (f). Read that bead's description for the XState-side evidence. The worker on .1.6 (xsval-2n6uv) found that this arm cannot be a registration check, and the mayor deferred it to this bead.

## Defect

An action fn may return a `[:raise ev opts]` tuple with THREE elements, and it is not refused. The bead's arm (f) has the measured behaviour. The shape is returned at RUNTIME by an action fn, so it can only be caught at the fx-routing boundary. There are two sites:
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc`, `split-raise-fx` (~:3672 at filing), in the flat drain;
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/parallel.cljc`, `split-raises` (~:839 at filing), in the parallel drain.

## The design question the worker raised

A throw from inside the drain surfaces as the generic `:rf.error/handler-exception`, which is exactly the unhelpful outcome rf2-2n6uv.1.2 complains about. The loud alternative routes it as a failed macrostep carrying a specific error id.

**Mayor's steer, under the stance:**
1. FIRST check whether the engine already has a runtime path for a MALFORMED ACTION OUTPUT. rf2-2n6uv.1.2 says the engine raises `:rf.error/machine-bad-action-form` at runtime. If an existing error id and surfacing path fit a malformed `:raise` tuple, REUSE them. No new vocabulary.
2. Only if nothing fits, add ONE new id (e.g. `:rf.error/machine-bad-raise`). Surface it the same way the engine surfaces its other runtime action-form errors, and give it a catalogue row in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`.
3. If surfacing it cleanly would need a new failure channel in the drain, stop and report. That is a design ruling, not implementation.

## Sequencing

This lands AFTER the PRs of workers xsval-2n6uv (rf2-2n6uv.1.1 / .1.2 / .1.6 / .4.3) and xseng-2n6uv (rf2-2n6uv.4.2 / .6 / .2.6) merge. Both edit `transition.cljc` and the spec pages this fix touches. Re-derive the line numbers then.

## Gates

- `cd implementation/machines && clojure -M:test`, with a regression for BOTH drains (flat and parallel), each shown red with its fix removed.
- clj-kondo, plain.
- CI's CLJS lanes.
- The `spec/009` catalogue row, if a new id is added.

title: docs(xray spec): truth tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md against the code (review wave rf2-y8doi)
description:
Filed from the senior-developer review wave over Xray (epic rf2-y8doi, tree reviewed at trunk 9555881fe3, 2026-09-17), item S19 of the triage shortlist. Mike's instruction for the wave: "Have an agent with a senior developer persona review the xray codebase. Create beads for any actionable insights. Ensure that the spec is up to date."

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md; paste it into any dispatch preamble unchanged)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

Mike's restatement for this wave (2026-09-17): "The posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece. But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer. We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a minimal, ergonomic API and excellent tools, and low friction. For each review, remember that we don't want to over-engineer. We just want to create a library which has excellent ergonomics for creating SPAs. It presents `:source-paths ["src" "test"]` as why both trees are on the compile classpath and the test build sees test/. Item 1 at line 22 selects `:deps {:aliases [:shadow]}`. In that mode the launcher deliberately ignores shadow-cljs.edn's :source-paths; the effective locations come from deps.edn :paths and the selected alias's :extra-paths. The already-correct conversion paragraph in SKILL.md:82 explains precisely this rule, so the explanatory leaf contradicts its own router.

Concrete trigger/reproducer: start from the documented :deps-mode scaffold and relocate the starter tests to `test-extra`, following item 5 by changing only shadow-cljs.edn's :source-paths to ["src" "test-extra"]. Leave deps.edn's :shadow :extra-paths as ["test"]. Restart the build JVM and run the test build. Expected under the leaf's explanation: test-extra is on the compile classpath and its tests are discovered. Actual launcher behavior: it prints that :source-paths was ignored, passes the :shadow alias to Clojure with no test-extra path, and the relocated test namespace is unavailable for discovery. Likewise an app namespace placed in a directory added only to this key is unavailable to the compiler. This compile consequence follows directly from the inspected launcher path; I did not run a mutating project relocation/build in the shared checkout.

Primary evidence: the exact pinned cache C:/Users/miket/.m2/repository/thheller/shadow-cljs/3.4.10/shadow-cljs-3.4.10-aot.jar contains shadow/cljs/npm/cli.cljs. get-clojure-args at 352-400 reads aliases, injection and JVM options and never includes :source-paths. run-clojure at 424-427 explicitly warns that :source-paths was ignored and must be configured in deps.edn. print-classpath at 838-866 branches the same way: :deps launches clojure -Spath; only the standalone :else branch concatenates :source-paths. The official guide independently describes the deps.edn ownership and explicit :deps activation: https://shadow-cljs.github.io/docs/UsersGuide.html#clj-deps (section 3.2.2).

Impact: the default project works because deps.edn duplicates the advertised paths, which masks the false instruction. This is P3 because the shipped default and SKILL.md's conversion recipe already have the correct active paths; it is not a default-scaffold build failure.

Precise repair: replace item 5 with the actual deps.edn ownership: app directories belong on :paths and test directories belong on :aliases :shadow :extra-paths; shadow-cljs.edn's :source-paths is ignored in this selected mode. ## Target

`rf/project-egress` is the ONLY projection door on the facade. A symbol-level residue check keeps the walker out of `tools/**` and `skills/**/preload`. The spec teaches one name and one sentence about tools.

## Changes

1. NOT namespace-level: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:66` legitimately requires `re-frame.elision` for `classification-effect-defect` / `apply-classification-effects`. Wire it where the composition-vocab check runs (its `docs.yml` job — the workflow's `paths` filter at `docs.yml:71-72, :205` must list the new script and its fixtures, or the job never runs for it — and the fast-PR spine), and prove it against a PLANTED violation in the PR body (exit 1 on the plant, exit 0 on the tree). Build the needle list as a fixed-string pattern FILE, and take the control from that file (CLAUDE.md records the `jq` CRLF join trap).
3. **Prose.** HOT-ZONE `spec/API.md:678-686` (§Size-elision walker rows → an internal-mechanism note under §Record-level egress `:688-696`; the `:690` "layered over" sentence becomes the whole story; `:75` tiering sentence names `elide-wire-value` — drop it from the list; `:572`, `:586` describe the framework-internal emit-time walk — respell as `re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value`, the mechanism, not a door). HOT-ZONE `spec/Tool-Pair.md` — any residual walker mention after stage 1 (`:836` marker table row, `:895`). HOT-ZONE `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:3014` — becomes true as written; reconcile with whatever rf2-kuky.10 did to that line; the other 009 mentions (`:216, :259, :293, :518, :1049, :1220, :1233, :1361`) describe the INTERNAL chokepoint walk and stay, spelled as the home namespace. `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:216-229` — teach the door; delete the profile-to-walker sample at `:223-227`; `:247-251` keep (internal delegation). `spec/Security.md:97, :261-262`; `spec/Privacy.md:82, :277-290`; `docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md:142`; `docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:304`; skills `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/privacy-and-elision.md:175-191`, `api-cheatsheet.md:158`, `production-observability.md:21,77,211,219,227`; `testbeds/large_dispatcher/README.md:134` and `testbeds/large_dispatcher/core.cljs:6` cite "spec/API.md section rf/elide-wire-value" — repoint. The `api-manifest.edn:111` justification "a placement ruling already made against this exact name" settled WHERE the row lived, not whether it must exist — rf2-kuky.9 is the new ruling that retires it.

`spec/API.md`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — one toucher each; this bead is serial behind stage 1 and ahead of the epoch stage for that reason.

title: Consolidate 73 ad-hoc IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT set/restore sites onto one shared fixture
description:
Carried over from rf2-76lhy step 2, which closed on PR #7190 having delivered step 1 (the capture-time profile). This half was never done and should not be lost with the parent.

73 test files set and restore the process-global IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT by hand, with no shared fixture. A test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag into every subsequent namespace in the bundle - a cross-namespace coupling that no assertion can catch and that only shows up as unexplained slowness or flakiness later in the run.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT, so this is not over-sold. rf2-76lhy originally advanced the leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown. The per-namespace profile shipped in PR #7190 dissolved that: 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points all sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.

So this is a HYGIENE bead, not a bug hunt. It retires a real hazard class on its own terms - one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally - and it is worth doing, but nothing is currently known to be broken by it. Size it accordingly and do not let it grow into an audit.

Fenced away from the PR #7190 runner work; this is implementation/**/test/** across many artefacts, so it wants its own dispatch.

INVESTIGATED, NOT DONE (PR #7193 worker, 2026-07-28). Recommendation: leave it, or do it per-artefact later. This is the honest 'not worth doing now'.

CENSUS IS BIGGER THAN THE BEAD SAYS: 78 files, 175 `set!` sites, across NINE trees — freehand 43, ui 15, adapters 7, ssr 6, tools/story 2, tools/machines-viz 2, machines 1, core 1, scripts 1. Not 73, and not one artefact.

THERE IS NO SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION TO ADOPT. The nearest existing shared fixture is `re-frame.ui.test/act-operation!`, which already does exactly the right thing (reads the prior value, sets true, restores the PRIOR value — not `false` — after React settles). But it lives in implementation/ui/SRC, a published and EXPERIMENTAL artefact surface. Adopting it from freehand / ssr / adapters / machines test trees would make those artefacts' tests depend on re-frame.ui. That is an architectural decision, not hygiene, and it is Mike's. The alternative — mint a new shared test-support surface every artefact may require — is also a decision, not a sweep.

WHAT DOES EXIST is per-artefact convergence: freehand already has mount_support.cljs and bench/b6_harness.cljs; ssr has SIX files carrying byte-identical `disable-act-env!`/`restore-act-env!` pairs. So the tractable shape is PER-ARTEFACT, ONE PR EACH — freehand first (43 of the 78 files, landing spot already present), then ssr (6 files, pure duplication), then ui.

WHY NOT NOW. (1) The motivation is gone: PR #7190's profile dissolved the 3-4x CI-slowdown hypothesis this was step 2 of, and PR #7193 confirmed it on a second box — the whole gap was seven benchmark namespaces (71% of the browser lane's wall clock), and the CI factor is a uniform ~1.7x. There is still no observed instance of the leak. (2) A 78-file mechanical edit across nine trees is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open PR touching a mounted test. (3) Every one of those trees was outside PR #7193's fence, so it could not have been done there in any case.

If someone does pick it up: rule FIRST on whether re-frame.ui.test's act door may be the repo-wide answer, because that ruling decides whether this is one shared fixture or nine private ones.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review):

DECISION — leave the sweep undone now; bead DEFERRED. No 78-file mechanical edit during the current mounted-test churn: the motivating CI-slowdown hypothesis was dissolved by measurement (seven benchmark namespaces + a uniform ~1.7x CI factor), and the sweep is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open mounted-test PR. Pick this up only when the high-conflict Freehand work settles AND either a real leak instance bites or an artefact's mounted tests are being reworked anyway — then land it artefact-sized, not repo-wide.

RECORD CORRECTION (from the Codex second opinion; commits verified in this checkout): "no observed instance" is true of the PERFORMANCE theory only. Flag leakage itself has occurred and been repaired — 43ce4cf9f6 and 1fff5b618b (shared-page act-discipline, ~361 warnings) and 0dd432b9ed (un-restored act boundary after a negative-control run, 755 warnings). The hazard class is real and observed; the slowdown attribution is what was disproved. P3 stands.

ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (binding — do not re-litigate):
1. DONOR DEPENDENCY FORBIDDEN. No artefact's tests may require re-frame.ui (src or test): F6e deletes the artefact, and re-frame.ui.test/act-operation! is a private defn- coupled to donor internals in any case. Its invariant is the SHAPE to copy, never the namespace to require: capture the incoming flag value and restore the PRIOR value — not a blanket false — on every exit path (synchronous throw, Promise fulfilment, Promise rejection).
2. ONE repo-private implementation, NOT nine per-artefact copies. Home: the existing lightweight dependency-free shared surface implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs (or a narrowly named sibling in the same core/test root). Verified: it is already required across an artefact boundary today (adapters/uix test) and sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath, so this mints no new architecture and survives F6e. Per-artefact is the DELIVERY boundary — artefact-sized PRs, freehand first (43 files, through its existing mount_support.cljs facade), ssr second (6 byte-identical disable/restore pairs) — not the implementation boundary. Nine permanent copies would reproduce at repo scale exactly the drift ssr's six copies already demonstrate.
3. Design floor for whoever lands it (from Codex, ratified): the helper takes the desired mode — both true (act-disciplined renders) and false (timing discriminators, hydration, deliberate un-acted negative controls) are legitimate, so no runner-wide constant. One save/restore engine with thin sync-wrapping and async-map fixture adapters (cljs.test forbids mixing the two fixture kinds; async tests need the map form) plus a Promise-aware operation bracket for callbacks that reject before done; overlapping async scopes rejected or serialized. Leave re-frame.ui.test self-contained until F6e and skip migrating ui test files the deletion gate removes.

Disposition: deferred (was open P3). Reopen against the conditions above.

RULING 2026-09-02 10:23:48 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-02, dossier review; ai/decisions/rf2-3t2nq.act-environment-fixture-home.md folded here and deleted — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD). Tip at ruling: b26c5ad33e.

HOLD STRUCK — the placement question "held for Mike" in the 2026-08-21 comment is discharged by this ruling.

DECISION — CLOSE AS MINUTIAE. No fixture sweep, no hicasso-only dedupe, no publish on re-frame.test-support, no further deferral. Three findings carry it, each re-measured at tip b26c5ad33e rather than inherited from the bead's earlier numbers:

(1) The hazard the bead is written around — a throw between a set and a restore leaking the flag bundle-wide — has ONE candidate site in the whole repo, and it is not in hicasso. Repo-wide there are exactly two prior-value restores: implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3280/3351 (act-prev, restored under `finally`) and implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:218-223 (prev, restored by `teardown!` at :243, called from the async continuation at :306 — NOT under `finally`; see PREMISE CORRECTIONS). Every one of the 43 `set!` lines under implementation/hicasso sets `false`; zero restore anything. There is no restore in that tree for a throw to skip.

(2) What the flag does makes the residual "hazard" a warning-policy leak, not a scheduler or timing leak (Codex's semantic correction, accepted — see WEIGHING). A `false` left behind suppresses "not wrapped in act" warnings in later tests of the same browser build; it does not defer renders or change what a test measures. The three repaired incidents the 2026-07-28 ruling cited (43ce4cf9f6, 1fff5b618b, 0dd432b9ed) were warning-state repairs of a `true` leaking across the shared page, consistent with that reading.

(3) What is left is a two-line duplicated helper (`leave-act-environment!` at checkpoint_support.cljs:161 and roots_frames_support.cljs:82) whose stated reason for existing twice — the freeze gate forbidding a `:require` of the bench helper — was retired by 8a10915ed8 on 2026-08-29, and whose 35 callers split 22/13 for structural reasons: 34 of the 35 use other functions from the same support namespace, and exactly one (state_dom_cljs_test.cljs) requires checkpoint-support solely for the setter. A dedupe would touch ~35 files in the repo's hottest test tree to remove one redundant require and one redundant defn, retiring no hazard. That is the trade that got the 2026-08-21 lift withdrawn, and the stance (pre-alpha, trust the programmer, do not drown in minutiae) says close it rather than action it.

The placement question that was held for Mike needs no ruling. The repo-private cross-artefact home implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs already exists, is dependency-free (requires only clojure.string), sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath beside hicasso/test (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:34 "core/test", :137 "hicasso/test"), and is required today from three places: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/reg_view_devtools_dom_cljs_test.cljs, implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_source_coord_dom_elision_prod_test.cljs and implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs. "Can hicasso's tests reach a core test-support namespace" is yes, today, without publishing anything. The 2026-07-28 ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (items 1-3: no donor dependency; one repo-private implementation in that home; the save/restore design floor) stands as the SHAPE for any act-environment fixture that is ever genuinely needed; nothing here overturns it. What this ruling adds is that no such fixture is needed now, and the trigger for one is a diagnostic-policy decision, not this bead.

HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED

Dossier author (sections "Summary" through "Evidence"; recommends A, close). Accepted on its main line: the census both ways, the disproven hazard, the drifted docstrings, the dead freeze gate, the existing home, and the rejection of C. Two of its facts are corrected at tip below: "both restore brackets are correct" (the ssr one restores the prior value but is not throw-safe) and "one parameterised on? helper" (there are two, one of them prose in docs). Its option B ("rule the home and dispatch a hicasso-only dedupe") is described as viable and it is, but its own cost line — a wide mechanical diff for zero hazard retired — is why it loses.

Codex ("Codex Recommendation"; also recommends close, and adds "do not dispatch a standalone hicasso dedupe as a substitute"). Weighed heavily on three points, each re-measured here rather than taken on trust. (a) The semantic correction: IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT is React's `isConcurrentActEnvironment()` predicate gating the "not wrapped in act" warnings, while the act queue is `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue`, controlled by `act()` itself. I did not re-read React's source; the citation (ReactFiberAct.js at the v19.2.0 tag, matching the installed react-dom 19.2.0) is specific and consistent with the three repaired incidents, and it changes the disposition in no direction, so it is recorded as Codex's reading, accepted. It DOES sharpen one thing the worker and the mayor both wrote: "a finally-restore would re-enter the act environment and change behaviour" overstates it — a restore would change later WARNING policy, not scheduling — but the conclusion survives, because the hicasso disable is a deliberate lane-wide policy with nothing anyone wants to restore to. (b) The caller split is structural, not arbitrary: verified at tip, 35 callers, 34 use other functions from their chosen support namespace, one (state_dom_cljs_test.cljs, alias `checkpoint`) does not. This overturns the worker's 2026-08-21 claim that native_abi_dom_cljs_test, foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test, imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test and native_hooks_dom_cljs_test require the multi-root harness SOLELY for the setter: the first and fourth no longer exist under any tracked path, and the second and third use cell-keys / make-reset-runtime-fixture / skip! and census / poll-until / released / teardown-census! respectively. The "latent wart in the converted half" is one file, not a class. (c) The freeze-gate residue is wider than the two docstrings — nine lines across nine hicasso test files by `freeze gate|freeze-gate` at tip (Codex counted ten) — and is independent of where the setter bodies live. Codex's reframing of any future work as "warning-state isolation, not scheduler fixture" is adopted below as the reopening condition.

Where the two disagree: the dossier presents B as a live option that a later irritation could justify; Codex says a dedupe would "centralise the spelling of a global write without establishing a correct shared policy for that global" and must not be done as a substitute for the real question. Codex's position is the one recorded, with one preservation of the dossier's view: if somebody is ALREADY refactoring both support namespaces, folding the two defns into one is a free by-product and needs no bead (recipe below). It is not worth a dispatch on its own.

The worker's 2026-08-21 refusal and the mayor's 05:20 acceptance are both upheld in substance; the mayor's "one genuine item" (the arbitrary split) is what this ruling downgrades, on Codex's measurement, from "real wart, held for Mike" to "one file, not worth a ruling". Dissent preserved: the 2026-08-18 comment's case for keeping the bead open ("closing would discard a real hazard on the grounds it has not bitten yet") was written before the value histogram existed; it is answered by (1) and (2) above, not dismissed. The 2026-07-28 RECORD CORRECTION that "flag leakage itself has occurred and been repaired" stays true and is re-characterised as warning-state leakage, not withdrawn.

Bead title and description: the "73 ad-hoc set/restore sites" framing is retired by this ruling. Left as-is on the closed bead for searchability; this note is the correction.
FOR WHOEVER TOUCHES THIS LATER

Recipe if a dedupe is ever wanted (only as a by-product of real work in those two support namespaces, never as a standalone dispatch): keep ONE definition — either roots_frames_support.cljs:82 (13 callers, the fuller docstring) or, if the setter is wanted cross-artefact, a `leave-act-environment!` added to implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs per the 2026-07-28 design item 2; delete the other package copy; re-point its callers (22 files if checkpoint-support's copy goes, 13 if roots-frames-support's); rewrite both docstrings to drop the freeze-gate citation (say instead: set outright because the bench is a separate Shadow project off this classpath, and the disable is lane-wide policy — warnings off, not scheduling). Gate: hicasso's own `npm run test:cljs` from implementation/ (heavyweight, browser), plus the usual CI. Sequence it against any open PR touching implementation/hicasso/test/**.

What would make new act-environment work worth doing — and it would be a NEW bead titled for warning-state isolation, briefed from this note, not a reopening of this one: (i) an observed cross-test act-warning leak that someone has to chase; (ii) a decision to make act warnings uniformly ON by default in the browser runner (today the shared :browser-test runner leaves whatever the last suite set); or (iii) a fixture refactor already touching these suites. Under any of those, first pin the runner default, then provide exact-prior-value brackets for both `true` and deliberately-`false` regions covering sync throw, promise fulfilment and promise rejection — the 2026-07-28 design floor (item 3) is the spec for that helper and it still holds.

Rejected options, one line each. B (rule the home, dispatch a ~35-file hicasso dedupe now): viable, but removes one redundant require and one redundant defn for zero hazard, in the hottest test tree — the trade already refused on 2026-08-21. C (publish on re-frame.test-support): core/src ships in the jar; a CLJS-only React test flag is not a published API, and pre-alpha is when the surface stays small. D (stay deferred with conditions): the bead's premise is disproven and its census has mis-briefed two passes already; a hold with no hazard behind it is a trap for the next backlog reread, not a plan. The original sweep (one fixture with restore-in-finally across all sites): the sites are deliberate lane-wide disables; a restoring fixture is the wrong shape for them and there is nothing to restore to.

FOLLOW-UPS — none filed. The nine-file stale freeze-gate prose is incidental cleanup for whoever next edits those files; the ssr non-finally restore is a one-line change with no observed symptom; neither clears the bar for a bead. Sibling beads under other rulings this pass (rf2-zq34m, rf2-4a0c, rf2-7rzg, rf2-8arzr, rf2-ahjbc, rf2-y8jjk, rf2-lau0u, rf2-kmqx3, rf2-uelji, rf2-y1jkm, rf2-8urba, rf2-hic-063) were not touched.

MAYOR 2026-08-18, BACKLOG REREAD — THIS IS A DEFERRAL WITH NO DATE AND NO STATED RELEASE CONDITION, WHICH IS THE ONE SHAPE THAT NEVER GETS RE-EXAMINED. Giving it a condition rather than a date, so a future tick can test it.

THE STATE I FOUND: status DEFERRED, defer_until NONE, untouched since 2026-07-28. Of ten deferred beads it is one of only two with no date at all; the other (rf2-2hpxo) has a real condition written into it — API-freeze. This one had neither.

THE BEAD IS HONEST ABOUT ITS OWN VALUE AND I AM NOT OVERRIDING THAT. It says so itself: rf2-76lhy originally advanced the flag leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown, and PR #7190's per-namespace profile DISSOLVED that — 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. 'There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.' It is a HYGIENE bead, and it says so.

SO WHY NOT CLOSE IT AS MINUTIAE. Because the hazard class is real and is exactly the kind this project takes seriously: a test that throws between the set and the restore leaks a process-global into every subsequent namespace in the bundle, and NO ASSERTION CAN CATCH IT — it surfaces later as unexplained slowness or flakiness, which is the hardest possible failure to attribute. The remedy is small and correct: one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally. Closing it would discard a real hazard on the grounds that it has not bitten yet.

THE RELEASE CONDITION, which is what was missing: DISPATCH THIS WHEN THE FLEET IS QUIET — no more than one other worker out, and no open PR touching implementation/ test namespaces. NOT because it is risky, but because 73 test files across the tree is the largest merge-conflict surface any single bead in this backlog carries, and a mechanical sweep that has to rebase past several landings will cost more in conflicts than the change is worth. Measured context for that: on 2026-08-18 the fleet ran 6 workers with 5 PRs open and the trunk moved 11 commits inside one worker's run.

SIZE IT WHEN IT GOES OUT: 73 files is above the single-dispatch comfort line here, so expect to split by artefact rather than send one worker at all of them.

NOT A NEW DEFERRAL DATE — deliberately. A date would fire on a day that may be just as busy. The condition is about fleet state, and the backlog-reread loop is the tick that can test it.

comments.text:
WORKER worker/actenv-3t2nq, 2026-08-21 03:30 AUSEST — REFUSAL for the dispatched
artefact, with the measurement. NO code change; no PR. The bead stays open.

The dispatched scope reproduces EXACTLY: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/**
carries 45 files / 51 raw `set!` sites at tip. Nothing below disputes that count. What
the count MEANS is what changed.

FOUR OF THE FIVE PREMISES DO NOT HOLD IN THIS TREE.

1. THERE ARE NO SET/RESTORE PAIRS. All 51 in-scope sites are
   `(set! (.-IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT js/globalThis) false)`. Zero set `true`; zero
   restore anything; zero `finally` within six lines of any site (checked per file by
   awk, and by a value histogram taken two independent ways). So the hazard the bead is
   written around — "a test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag"
   — HAS NO INSTANCE HERE. There is no restore for a throw to skip.

   Repo-wide the pattern is nearly as rare: of 90 raw `set!` lines, 66 set `false`, 22
   set `true`, and exactly TWO restore a captured prior value —
   implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3351 and
   implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:223. Both
   are outside hicasso. The set/restore bracket the bead describes is 2 of 90 sites
   repo-wide, in two files, in two other artefacts.

2. THE PACKAGE ALREADY HAS THE SHARED HELPER, AND MOST OF THE TREE ALREADY USES IT.
   `leave-act-environment!` is defined at checkpoint_support.cljs:161 and
   roots_frames_support.cljs:76, and 34 files / 38 call sites in this very tree already
   call it. Repo-wide there are 98 converted call sites — 59 in the bench tree, 38 in
   the hicasso package, 1 in core. The tree is roughly 43% consolidated already
   (38 converted vs 51 raw), not 0%.

3. THE CENSUS METHOD UNDERCOUNTS BY CONSTRUCTION, and this is the correction that
   reframes the bead. A CONVERTED site does not contain the literal
   `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` — it reads `(support/leave-act-environment!)`. So
   `git grep IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` measures the UNCONVERTED TAIL, never the
   population. The recorded "69 files / 100 sites, nine trees" is a remainder. The real
   population is that remainder plus 98 already-converted call sites, and the shape of
   the remaining work is "finish a migration already 50%+ done", not "introduce a
   fixture into a tree that has none".

4. THE SPECIFIED BAR CANNOT BE MET WITHOUT A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. "One shared fixture with
   the restore in a `finally`" would RE-ENTER the act environment after each test. Every
   docstring in the tree says the disable is deliberate and LANE-WIDE, not a bracket:
   roots_frames_support.cljs:76-85 — "React's `act` queue is not the browser's scheduler,
   and every reading in these suites is taken outside it — a commit measured here is the
   commit a user's page performs." A `finally`-restore would contradict that and would
   violate the dispatch's own "no behaviour change" requirement. The one restoring idiom
   in the repo (ssr) captures the PRIOR value rather than forcing `true`/`false`, which
   is right for a bracketed region and wrong for a lane.

   The fifth premise — that the population might be heterogeneous — is wrong in the safe
   direction: it is perfectly homogeneous. 51 of 51 set `false`.

WHY FINISHING THE MIGRATION IS NOT A SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION.

The two helper definitions are byte-identical and the 34 existing callers split between
them with no principle: 22 files take it from checkpoint-support (THE MICROTASK-CHECKPOINT
INSTRUMENT), 12 from roots-frames-support (THE MULTI-ROOT WITNESS HARNESS). Several
already require a heavyweight, purpose-specific harness namespace SOLELY to reach a
two-line flag setter — native_abi_dom_cljs_test, foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test,
imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test and native_hooks_dom_cljs_test all require the multi-root
witness harness for exactly that. That is a latent wart in the converted half.

Of the 45 raw files, only 8 already require one of the two support namespaces (a free
one-line conversion). The other 37 would each GAIN a `:require` on a namespace whose
stated purpose is unrelated to theirs — deepening that wart 37 more times rather than
fixing it.

Doing it PROPERLY means minting one canonical act-env home, deleting both duplicate
definitions, re-pointing all 34 existing callers AND converting the 45 raw files: ~80
files in the tree, for ZERO hazard retired, against a tree with live peers. That is the
same maximal merge-conflict change with no motivating defect that got this bead deferred
in the first place, merely confined to one artefact. Per the stance — reject
over-engineering, close minutiae rather than actioning it — I am refusing it rather than
landing it.

ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THE DISPATCH ASKED (reusable, or hicasso-specific?)

In SUBSTANCE the helper is not hicasso-specific at all — it is a two-line global setter
with a docstring. In PLACEMENT it is, and that is the whole difficulty. It lives in the
hicasso package TEST tree, which the other eight artefacts have no business importing
(and which the freeze gate already fences in the other direction:
frozen-sources.edn :forbidden-import-prefixes ["re-frame.bench." "re-frame.freehand."]).
A repo-wide answer therefore needs a shared home every test tree can reach. The only
existing candidate is `re-frame.test-support` — but that is
implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc, inside core's `:paths ["src"]`, i.e.
a PUBLISHED surface. Putting a test-only React flag setter there is exactly the
architectural decision PR #7193 flagged and left to Mike, and it is unchanged by the
re-frame.ui / re-frame.freehand retirement. So: NOT reusable as it stands, and making it
reusable is Mike's call, not hygiene.

REMAINING RAW `set!` CENSUS AT TIP (files / sites, .beads excluded)

  implementation/hicasso (package)   45 / 51   <- dispatched scope, refused above
  implementation/adapters             7 / 13
  implementation/core                 2 /  9

  implementation/hicasso (test_kit)   1 /  1
  implementation/hicasso (testbed)    1 /  1

                                     69 / 90

  (90 raw `set!` lines. The recorded "100 sites" counts every LINE mentioning the
  literal, which includes ten that are not `set!` calls — docstring and comment prose
  explaining why the flag is set outright. In the dispatched scope the same split is
  54 mentions / 51 `set!` calls / 3 prose lines.)

RECOMMENDATION

Retire the bead's hazard framing rather than the sites. As written it describes a
set/restore leak that exists in 2 sites repo-wide, neither in hicasso. What actually
remains is a half-finished DRY migration with no defect behind it and no shared home
available without a published-surface ruling. Either close it as minutiae, or re-file the

callers split arbitrarily between them" — which is a genuine wart, but a ~35-file

title: Test-suite pruning, fifth pass: tools/xray panels/
description:
Child of rf2-nvxtm (test-suite pruning, fifth pass). One worktree, one PR.

SURFACE: tools/xray panels/. This is the surface of rf2-txsk5.1 (fourth pass). Read rf2-txsk5.1 first: its description, notes and close reason. Together they give the runners and lanes, the count floors, the surface's cautions, the covers it relied on, and what the fourth pass already pruned. rf2-txsk5.1 gives the exact files in scope, or names the third-pass bead (rf2-n6gq4.1) that does. Confirm the scope and the runners yourself at tip in step 1, and report the delta.

<DIR> in the prompt below means this surface.

REPO MECHANICS: read rf2-nvxtm's description. Its count-floor, CLJS-lane, test-name, cross-surface-cover, hot-zone, plant and one-PR rules apply in full, and they win over anything in the prompt that seems to conflict.

== THE PROMPT (verbatim from Mike's local prompt file, which is not checked in; also in rf2-nvxtm's description)

Simplify the unit tests under tools/xray panels/. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside tools/xray panels/. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
tools/xray panels/ to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in tools/xray panels/; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If tools/xray panels/ plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.

Item 4, same surface, wording only: spec/011 §Payload scope's :rf/frame-id row, and the matching Spec-Schemas comment, call it "the frame the server rendered under". title: day8/re-frame2 ships no clj-kondo export, so downstream lint flags dispatch/subscribe in every reg-view body as unresolved
description:
`day8/re-frame2` ships no clj-kondo export, so in a downstream project clj-kondo flags `dispatch` and `subscribe` in every `reg-view` body as unresolved.

## Where the config lives today

The repo-root config holds all of it, and none of it ships:
- `.clj-kondo/config.edn` declares the `reg-view` hook (which declares the injected `dispatch`/`subscribe` locals), the `with-frame` / `with-new-frame` hooks, and the `:lint-as` / `:unresolved-var` entries for the `defreg-macro` vars.
- `.clj-kondo/hooks/re_frame/core.clj` holds the hook code.

`implementation/core/deps.edn` has `:paths ["src"]`, and its jar alias has `:src-dirs ["src"]`. Core has no `resources/` directory.

Fresco already solved the same problem:
- `implementation/fresco/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2-fresco/`;
- `resources` on its `:paths` and `:src-dirs`;
- the repo consuming that export through `:config-paths`.

## Change

Do the same for core:
- Move the `re-frame.core` entries and hooks into `implementation/core/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2/`.
- Add `resources` to core's `:paths` and the jar `:src-dirs`.
- Point the repo `:config-paths` at the export.

Story's entries stay at the repo root. Export macro shapes only, and add no custom findings.

`implementation/core/deps.edn` is the artefact's own deps file, not the top-level `implementation/deps.edn`, so this touches no hot-zone file.

## Why now

A newcomer's first `reg-view` body is covered in lint warnings. Fixing that is cheapest before the first release.

title: Unit-test pruning: routing
description:
Apply Mike's pruning prompt to implementation/routing/test recursively in an isolated worker worktree. This is a distinct cluster in rf2-0wcq5. Push a test-only draft PR, babysit all checks until green, then mark ready; do not merge. Report no-op with evidence instead of manufacturing changes.

Simplify the unit tests under implementation/routing/test. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside implementation/routing/test. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
implementation/routing/test to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in implementation/routing/test; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If implementation/routing/test plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside implementation/routing/test that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.

title: Rename campaign: all 19 day8/* Maven coordinates -> io.github.day8/* — ONE PR, no prep slice (blocked: rf2-uelji rules the destination group id)
description:
DECIDED 2026-09-09 (dossier + Codex weighed; full reasoning in the DECISION note): this ships as ONE PR. No group-agnostic prep slice exists, none is filed, and none should be created — both candidate prep items were refuted at source (the hardcoded preflight POM paths are a deliberate independent check, not a defect; a derived release matrix is a new mechanism for a one-time rename), and the only two genuinely-stale prose items live in files this campaign already renames, so a prep PR would double-touch them.

BLOCKED on rf2-uelji, and the reason is a DATA DEPENDENCY, not risk appetite: rf2-uelji RULES WHAT THE DESTINATION GROUP ID IS, and this campaign writes that literal string across 429 files. Running first means sweeping to a destination that has not been ruled. The older "work against a dead identity" framing is RETIRED — Clojars' no-yank irreversibility bites at TAG time, not merge time (0 tags on origin; 0 of the 19 present in Clojars' day8 inventory, which returns only lein-cofx, lein-git-inject, re-frame-tracer, shadow-git-inject), so that fence belongs to rf2-kmqx3. Dispatch the tick after Mike's badge lands; never on a defer-date lapse.

THIS IS NOW THE SOLE REMAINING REPOSITORY-SIDE PREREQUISITE FOR THE FIRST TAG. rf2-kmqx3's other named prerequisites — the facade sweep rf2-2hpxo -> rf2-i6kh -> rf2-ar67 — are ALL CLOSED. Everything else in front of the tag is Mike's operator acts. Hence P1.

## STOP FIRST — day8/clein is NOT a coordinate; a blanket sweep breaks every build

NEVER run a blanket day8/ -> io.github.day8/ substitution. There are 31 distinct day8/<name> tokens in tracked deps.edn and ONLY 19 ARE PUBLISHABLE. The clein DEPENDENCY KEY is io.github.noahtheduke/clein (already io.github.*, nothing to rename); the token day8/clein occurs 20 times in 20 tracked files and ALL 20 are inside the URL :git/url "https://github.com/day8/clein.git" (measured both directions; 0 occurrences outside that URL). A blanket sweep rewrites those to github.com/io.github.day8/clein.git, which 404s, and every artefact loses its build tool.

THE DISCRIMINATOR — the only one to use: rename EXACTLY the 19 lines matching  :lib[[:space:]]+day8/  in tracked deps.edn. Every other day8/ spelling is a github.com/day8/ URL (leave), an @day8/ npm scope (leave), a :local/root internal key (leave — see non-scope), or prose. Never drive the census off a bare day8/ token, and never off a re-frame2-* name glob (it silently drops reagent-slim).

## Scope — coordinate work ONLY, one sequenced hot-zone campaign, NOT parallel

Migrate all 19 day8/* :clein/build :lib publication coordinates (14 implementation/ incl. fresco + 5 tools/) to io.github.day8/*. THE COUNT IS 19, NOT 18 — rf2-uelji says 18 in two places and is WRONG; the difference is exactly day8/reagent-slim, the one name outside the re-frame2-* glob. Do not "fix" 19 down to match the ruling. Re-verified 2026-09-09: 19 lines, 19 distinct names, control 43 tracked deps.edn.

day8/reagent-slim -> io.github.day8/reagent-slim. RULED: it keeps its off-pattern name (it advertises what it is; a re-frame2- prefix buys nothing). No longer an open sub-decision.

Surfaces (re-derive the census from source at campaign START; do not trust any list's count):
- :clein/build :lib in every publishable deps.edn, plus the in-repo cross-artefact :local/root coordinate keys the rewrite resolves.
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh — inventories AND its RECOGNITION LOGIC (:186 recognises the old Maven spelling; :683 and :873 pin concrete local dep keys) plus its --self-test fixtures.
- Release workflows + scripts: release.yml (14-coordinate DAG incl. deploy-fresco, the deploy matrix and the release-body roster), release-story.yml, release-machines-viz.yml, release-xray.yml, template-release.yml, rewrite-in-repo-coords.sh (PRESERVE its existing path-based rewrite at :117 — it reads each artefact's own deps.edn rather than a typed roster), rewrite-local-root-coord.sh, preflight-tool-package.sh, preflight-story-package.sh, preflight-xray-package.sh, preflight-reagent-slim-package.sh (:129 spells the old-group POM path; its expected-dependency tuple set is a DELIBERATE independent check — retarget it, do not derive it).

- spec/API.md + spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn hand-edited, THEN spec/api-manifest.edn REGENERATED (it carries the GENERATED / do-NOT-hand-edit header).
- DIRECTORY RENAME: under implementation/fresco/resources/clj-kondo.exports/ the day8/re-frame2-fresco/ directory — clj-kondo resolves exports by group/artifact directory, so this is a MOVE, not a text edit.
- docs/release-process.md (add one sentence: post-campaign io.github.day8 carries both Maven artefacts and the template's GIT coord); CHANGELOG; migration-guide dep edits; consumer-facing usage snippets; the setup skill; the template's emitted coordinates.
- STALE-PROSE TRUE-UPS, corrected to the two that are actually false at trunk: implementation/fresco/deps.edn:42 "PUBLISHED, as of rf2-gra70" (nothing has published) and tools/xray/deps.edn:65 "NOT PUBLISHABLE YET ... carries no :clein/build" (it has since PR #8314). The other two previously parked here are ALREADY HISTORY and must be LEFT ALONE: release-xray.yml:277-279 is past-tense Freehand retirement bookkeeping, and tools/xray/spec/027-Fresco-Evidence.md:515 already reads "Release note — CLOSED". Preserve every consumer-facing "no released coordinate yet" warning until a tag actually lands.

SERIALISATION: this is a board-wide freeze. It touches every hot-zone holding CLAUDE.md names EXCEPT spec/002-Frames.md. Tier A (~73 files) is ATOMIC BY CONSTRUCTION — verify-version-lockstep is an always-on unguarded test.yml job pinning exact coordinate literals, so renaming deps.edn keys without the gate inventory in the SAME commit turns main red. That is why tier-by-tier PRs are rejected.

## Explicit NON-scope

NO repo-wide day8 -> io.github.day8 text replacement. NO Clojure namespace renames. NO GitHub org/URL changes (all 646 github.com/day8/ lines stay). NO @day8 npm scope change. NO edits to ordinary Day8 prose. 2. Any surviving day8/* token is explicitly classified. Do NOT record class (c) as "history" or as a fixture — that would be false.
3. Generated deploy POMs inspected: every in-family GAV uses io.github.day8 at the lockstep version, NO old-group dependency anywhere (a partial migration can publish a valid jar whose POM points at a coordinate that will never exist).
4. verify-version-lockstep.sh --self-test, the lockstep gate, the release-DAG/script-policy tests, and each tool/package preflight ALL green. Package locally in isolation before any publication.
