title: api(observability): key the dev console fallback on nothing-routed-this-record, not on an empty :errors registry
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from observability.md (ref observability.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The untooled-dev console fallback (rf2-fu75) prints a promoted `:rf.error/*` record only while the corpus-wide `:errors` listener registry is EMPTY — `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:221` `(empty? @listeners)`, rationale at `:121-132` ("Registering ANY `:errors` listener takes corpus-wide OWNERSHIP… even if that listener ignores this category or itself throws"). Two consequences the corpus shows:

1. Story registers `(fn [_record] nil)` purely to claim the stream — `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:1149-1161` (`claim-error-ownership!` / `release-error-ownership!`, rf2-8yyd; the comment block at `:1118-1144` explains that the registration IS the payload). That claim silences the console for EVERY frame on the page, including a host app's frames that Story did not mount and does not read — a registration on a door nobody reads, to change behaviour on a door nobody registered. `tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md:190-210` §Error-stream ownership documents the claim as the framework's off-switch.
2. Conversely, a frame whose `:observability :errors` policy already delivered the record to a registered sink (the NORMAL production door, `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:270-300`) still gets a console line, because the sink route is not consulted: `report-unowned-error!` runs before the fan-out and before the sink route at `error_emit.cljc:595` (event-centric) and `:848` (union records), and `route-error!` / `route-error-record!` (`observability.cljc:228-297`, `:299-330`) return nil.

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:280-283` records the same side effect for its one-render `:errors` window.

## Evidence

- `error_emit.cljc:201-230` `report-unowned-error!` (three gates: `debug-enabled?`, DOM host, empty registry); `:595` and `:848` call sites; `:610` and `:852` the `:observability/route-error` / `:observability/route-error-record` hook lookups that follow.
- `observability.cljc:159-170` `deliver-to-sink!` — a sink id with no registered fn is a no-op; a throwing sink is swallowed.
- Pinning tests today: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs` — `an-attached-listener-suppresses-the-fallback` (:318), `ownership-is-implicit-and-corpus-wide` (:346, a listener that ignores the category or throws still owns), `dropping-the-last-listener-resumes-the-fallback` (:366), plus the rollback cases (:406-591) rf2-xpd8 / rf2-vkn8 added; `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/shell_error_ownership_cljs_test.cljs:40-70` (claim/release/idempotent/host-listener-survives).
- rf2-xpd8's ruling (2026-09-04, PR1 on main as `56cd0aa021` / `4b4b104b16`) reasons in "listener, sink, console" vocabulary and names the fallback as firing "when nothing owns the stream" — its producer feeds all three identically and does not move here.

## Target API

No new API, no knob (rf2-fu75's rejections stand: no per-category ownership, no sink discovery, no suppression setting). Only the ownership PREDICATE changes. A record is OWNED when either:

- (a) at least one corpus-wide `:errors` listener is registered — unchanged, including "ignores the category" and "throws" (`ownership-is-implicit-and-corpus-wide` stays green); or
- (b) the record's owning frame declares an `:observability :errors` policy and at least one of its entries resolved to a REGISTERED sink fn, which was invoked. A policy naming a sink the app has not registered does NOT own the record (it went nowhere — codex's "missing sink" caution); a sink that throws DOES own it (the sink author has it — the same posture as a throwing listener).

The fallback fires iff neither holds. Mechanism constraint for the worker: the console decision needs the sink-route result, and today the console fires first at `:595` / `:848`. Have `route-error!` / `route-error-record!` (and `route-stream!`) return the count of registered sinks invoked, and take the console decision after the route. The relative order of listener fan-out and sink route is not contractual (spec 015/009 say "ALONGSIDE") — verify no test pins it (`observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc`, `non_event_observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc`, `capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc`) before reordering, and keep "exactly once per record" (`:590-596` comment).

Story then owns its errors as DATA on the frames it creates: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:811` and `:934` (`rf/make-frame` for variant frames) and `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/artifact.cljc:446` conj `{:sink :rf.story/errors}` onto the config's existing `[:observability :errors]` vector (an author's own entries are kept, never replaced), and the shell registers `(rf/register-observability-sink! :rf.story/errors …)` on mount and `unregister-observability-sink!` on unmount, replacing `claim-error-ownership!` / `release-error-ownership!`. The sink fn may be a no-op with the reason in its docstring (Story's capture path is the trace axis, `shell.cljs:1134-1138`), or feed the assertion strip — worker's call; what matters is that ownership is frame-scoped policy readable off `frame-meta`, and a host app's frames on the same page get their console lines back. Sink resolution happens at delivery time (`deliver-to-sink!`), so mount order between the shell and a variant frame does not matter.

```clojure
;; before (shell.cljs:1153) — page-wide claim through a door nobody reads
(rf/register-listener! :errors ::error-ownership (fn [_record] nil))

;; after — variant frames carry the policy; the shell owns the sink id
(rf/make-frame (-> config-map
                   (assoc :id variant-id)
                   (update-in [:observability :errors] (fnil conj []) {:sink :rf.story/errors})))
(rf/register-observability-sink! :rf.story/errors story-error-sink)   ;; on mount
(rf/unregister-observability-sink! :rf.story/errors)                  ;; on unmount
```

## Corroboration

One-reviewer. Fable: "Key the fallback on 'no entry routed this record'… so Story's frames declare policy and own their errors honestly." Grok: "Key the console fallback on 'no policy routed this record.'" Codex: "real but should remain small… Changing that to 'an entry routed' can hide an error when a named sink is missing or throws; Story also suppresses errors outside a single variant frame… define successful handoff precisely before changing it. Do not invent per-category routing, acknowledgements, or a suppression framework." The predicate above is that precise definition; the Story point is exactly what the change removes.

## Deletion list

- `shell.cljs:1118-1161` — the ownership comment block, `error-ownership-listener-id`, `claim-error-ownership!`, `release-error-ownership!` (replaced by the sink pair); the mount/unmount call sites that invoke them.
- `error_emit.cljc:121-132` comment and `:201-215` docstring — rewritten to the two-arm predicate.

## Consumers to migrate

Story only (above). `hicasso/server.cljs:280-283` docstring stays true under arm (a); no change. `frame.cljc:2810/3909` transient listeners: unchanged (arm (a) — they own for their window, as today).

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1283` (surface #5 paragraph: "an EMPTY `:errors` listener registry", "registering ANY `:errors` listener takes CORPUS-WIDE ownership… that self-suppression IS the off-switch") → nothing owns it = no `:errors` listener AND no frame-policy sink delivery; keep "attach a listener or wire the frame sink before counting on visibility". HOT-ZONE.
- `tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md:190-210` §Error-stream ownership → rewritten to the frame-policy form (scoped to Story's frames; host frames untouched by construction, not by id discipline).
- `git grep -nE "registry is empty|fallback goes quiet|corpus-wide ownership|takes ownership" -- docs skills spec tools/*/spec` and update each line found (measured at drafting: 009:1283, Story 003:197-205, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/production-observability.md` does not mention the fallback).
- Tests to add in `error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs`: (i) a frame with an `:errors` policy whose sink is registered — record reaches the sink, console silent; (ii) same policy, sink NOT registered — console prints; (iii) a sibling frame WITHOUT policy on the same page — console prints for it while (i)'s frame stays silent; (iv) a throwing registered sink — console silent; (v) a frameless (`:frame nil`) record with no listener — console prints (unchanged). Keep :318, :346, :366 as they are.
- `shell_error_ownership_cljs_test.cljs:40-70` rewritten: claim = variant frame carries `{:sink :rf.story/errors}` and the sink is registered → a variant-frame refusal prints nothing; release = sink unregistered → prints; a host frame without policy prints while the shell is mounted; a host app's own `:errors` listener is untouched.
- Gate: `npm run test:story-feature-load` (`examples/scripts/run-story-feature-load-tests.cjs`, console errors fatal) must stay at 0 console errors — that run is the evidence the frame-scoped claim covers everything Story emits. If it does not (a Story-originated record with `:frame nil`), record the category as a finding on this bead; do not reinstate the page-wide claim.
- Manifest: no var changes. Conformance: none.

title: xstate-parity: in PARALLEL regions the reducer and the spawn install write the parent's :rf/spawned mirror under DIFFERENT keys (in-region vs region-prefixed): duplicate entries, cross-region overwrite, and a stale entry after a rejected region spawn
description:
Found by worker xsval2-2n6uv while fixing rf2-2n6uv.2.7 (the parent's :data :rf/spawned mirror cleared on a rejected spawn, draft PR #10373). The worker read this from code; it is outside that fence and was not changed.

## Defect

In PARALLEL regions, the two writers of the parent's `[:data :rf/spawned …]` mirror disagree on the key:
- the reducer (Level 1) writes the mirror under the IN-REGION invoke key;
- the install path (lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc) writes the REGION-PREFIXED key.

Consequences, as reported:
1. A successful region spawn leaves TWO entries in the mirror.
2. Two regions sharing an in-region path OVERWRITE each other's reducer entry.
3. A rejected region spawn clears the prefixed key (after rf2-2n6uv.2.7) but KEEPS its in-region entry, which is the same stale-mirror defect .2.7 fixed for flat machines, surviving in regions.

## Required correction

- Make both writers use ONE key for a region spawn. Which one is decided by what readers of `:rf/spawned` use, including spec/005's §Recording the spawned id user-side and any tool reading the mirror. Settle it against those readers, not by preference.
- Keep the Level-1 reducer surface's documented shape unless spec/005 says otherwise. If the fix would change a documented user-facing shape, stop and report.
- Reproduce all three consequences first, as tests on a parallel machine with a spawn in two regions sharing an in-region path.

## Sequencing

Dispatch AFTER worker xsval2-2n6uv's PR #10373 (rf2-2n6uv.1.3 / .5.2 / .2.7) has MERGED; it edits spawn.cljc's rejection paths and install write. Re-derive line numbers then. It may also interact with rf2-2n6uv.2.2 (reaping tracked children on parent destroy), which reads what a slot tracks, so read that bead's ruling before choosing the key.

## Gates

title: Run the core, routing and SSR production-gate lanes as bare clojure -M:test:prod-gate alias calls and delete their three roster scripts
description:
## Ruling

Run the production-posture (debug-off) JVM lanes for core, routing and SSR as plain alias calls: `clojure -M:test:prod-gate` in the artefact directory, the same command in CI and on a laptop. Delete `scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh`, `scripts/test-routing-prod-gate.sh` and `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh`. Which tests run with debug off is already declared where every invocation reads it, the `:prod-gate` alias. The scripts' selection machinery now computes exactly the set cognitect discovers by default, so it is scaffolding. The calibrated test-count floors go with the scripts. The runner's own nonzero floor and its discovery checks replace them. An elevated floor survives only where it states a specific coverage claim, and then as a runner-owned main-opt, not as an env var exported by a wrapper.

This is the first bead of the tooling dossier's option (C): move each test invariant into the tool that every invocation reads, then trial a JVM lane registry.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

**Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:**

1. **The three rosters are empty or absent.** `scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh:121-236` is a `known_red=( … )` array that holds only comments. `scripts/test-routing-prod-gate.sh:94-165` is the same. `scripts/test-ssr-prod-gate.sh` has no roster and already runs a bare `clojure -M:test:prod-gate` (:126-127). The core script's business end (:381-389) exports `RF2_MIN_TESTS=1043`, passes one `-n` per namespace of an un-narrowed set, and runs `clojure -M:test:prod-gate`.
2. **The posture already lives in the alias.** `implementation/core/deps.edn:200-203` is `:prod-gate {:jvm-opts ["-Dre-frame.debug=false"] :main-opts ["-m" "re-frame.test-quiet.runner" "-e" ":slow" "-e" ":stress" "-e" ":requires-debug"]}`. Routing's is at `implementation/routing/deps.edn:110-112` and SSR's at `implementation/ssr/deps.edn:153-155`.
3. **The floors are hand-edited env vars exported by wrappers:** core 1043 (`test-core-prod-gate.sh:381`), routing 230 (`test-routing-prod-gate.sh:256`) and SSR 332 (`test-ssr-prod-gate.sh:124`). A bare alias call gets the runner default of 1 (`implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/runner.clj:603-655`). The runner already refuses a discovery directory whose files do not readably declare their own namespace (`discovery-defects` and `verify-discovery!`, `runner.clj:940-1007`). That is the structural check the core script's `sed`-based `verify_roster` (:260-300) only approximated.

**Rejected:**

- *Keep the scripts (option A).* They keep a bash roster, an env-var floor and a "do not invoke this alias bare" warning wrapped around a selection that is now empty, so the CI command and the laptop command differ for no reason.
- *Keep calibrated per-lane floors as the default.* Recalibrated suite counts drift: d7ae53df24 lowered epoch's floor by 16, and more than 22 such hand edits were counted. They add no claim beyond detecting a collapse, which the nonzero floor and the discovery checks already catch.
- *Generate the whole CI matrix now (option D).* Rejected at the headline: its size is unmeasured and it means days of hot-zone sequencing. The JVM registry trial is its own bead and follows this one.

**Supersedes:** no standing ruling. This builds on rf2-u4qcq (closed: core's unjudged namespaces became `^:requires-debug` dev-posture tests) and does not reopen it. rf2-7tfz1 (closed, PR #11360, trunk 46ec8b049c) added `scripts/test-epoch-prod-gate.sh` to the classifier's prod-gate arm. This bead removes the three entries for the scripts it deletes.

## Work

- **CI.** In `.github/workflows/test.yml`, the jobs `jvm-core-prod-gate` (:1571, script call at :1608), `jvm-routing-prod-gate` (:2169, :2206) and `jvm-ssr-prod-gate` (:2367, :2405) each run `clojure -M:test:prod-gate` with `working-directory` set to the artefact. Rewrite their comments in the present tense. The stale routing comment at `test.yml:2160-2168` ("Not the whole routing suite: the namespaces excluded are red under the real gate…") goes, and the core and SSR job comments that send the reader to the scripts are rewritten.
- **Delete the three scripts.** Their failure guidance moves to one home, either the lane-pin tests' docstrings (`implementation/{core,routing,ssr}/test/re_frame/*prod_gate_lane_pin_test.clj`) or TESTING.md, not both. The guidance is the "green under `-M:test` and red here is either dev instrumentation or a genuine production defect; decide which before reaching for a posture guard; look for a production-visible witness first" text (for example `test-ssr-prod-gate.sh:127-140`), plus core's tagging rule.
- **Alias comments.** Three comments say the opposite of the truth once the scripts are gone: `implementation/core/deps.edn:158-165` ("NOT THE WHOLE SUITE… Do not invoke this alias bare; run the script"), `implementation/routing/deps.edn:102-109` and `implementation/ssr/deps.edn:145-152`. Rewrite each to say that the alias IS the lane.
- **Floors.** Default to the runner's nonzero floor. Core's roughly 35-test "tagging budget" (`test-core-prod-gate.sh:335-345`) is the one floor that states a coverage claim: an over-broad `^:requires-debug` tag must be noticed. Keep it only if you keep that claim. If you do, make it a runner-owned `--min-tests N` main-opt in core's `:prod-gate` alias, parsed beside `--probe` (`runner.clj:618-638`), and state the claim in the alias comment. Routing's 230 and SSR's 332 go.
- **Classifier.** At current trunk, the prod-gate arm (`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:771`) lists all four scripts. title: Run one bounded spec-only port probe of the conformance corpus and file its gap log as spec-gap beads
description:
## Ruling

Goal 2, "AI-implementable from the spec alone", is ruled **live but measured**. It stays the acceptance test for the spec, under the STRICTER reading: a port may not consult `implementation/`, because a port that reads the CLJS reference is a port of the reference, not of the spec. It is measured by an occasional bounded probe rather than asserted. This bead is the first probe: one fresh AI session writes a minimal foreign harness and runtime from `spec/` alone, for a pure Mode-B slice of the conformance corpus. Its gap log becomes spec-gap beads, and its measured harness size replaces the unmeasured "~300 lines per host" promise. A grammar cannot by itself establish Goal 2; this exercise is how remaining ambiguity is found. The probe follows the closed fixture grammar (`spec/conformance/fixture-file.edn`) and the roster removal, because run before them it would mostly rediscover what a static census already shows.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Decisive facts, at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **Goal 2 is the stated acceptance test, but it has never been executed.** `spec/000-Vision.md:238` calls Goal 2 "the acceptance test for the entire spec effort". The corpus README defines a spec gap as a fixture an AI cannot reproduce without outside sources (`spec/conformance/README.md:4`, and the Checklist at `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:577`). Yet no port, no foreign harness and no probe has ever run. The only non-CLJS reader of the fixtures is the Python bracket scanner `scripts/check_conformance_fixture_edn.py`.
2. **The size promises are unmeasured.** "~300 lines per host" (`spec/conformance/README.md:478`, `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:548`) and "~50 lines" for the DSL interpreter (`spec/conformance/README.md:363`). The reference harness is 5,547 lines, which does not measure a port's minimum either.
3. **There is a wording split on what a port may read.** Vision's own definition forbids only re-frame v1 source and asking the spec authors (`spec/000-Vision.md:290`). The README, the Checklist and the implementor skill forbid `implementation/`. This ruling keeps the stricter reading.

Rejected options:
- **Treat Goal 2 as an aspiration for now.** Rejected, because the corpus would then have no external check on whether the spec is sufficient.
- **Make the probe a CI gate.** Rejected as over-engineering: it is an occasional bounded measurement.
- **Run the probe before the grammar lands.** Rejected: it would mostly rediscover the census.
- **Start the port-facing work now** (shrinking the capability vocabulary, lifting Security.md's hostile cases into fixtures, the HTTP transport seam rf2-mn2ht.71). Deferred until this probe passes stage 1 and Mike wants a real port.

Supersedes: nothing by id. It settles the reading of Goal 2 in favour of `spec/conformance/README.md:4` over the looser `spec/000-Vision.md:290`.

## Work

A **zero-edit research dispatch**: nothing is committed to the repository. The harness the probe writes lives in a scratch directory.

- **Agent:** one fresh AI session, given `spec/` (corpus included) and `skills/re-frame2-implementor/`. It is DENIED `implementation/`, `tools/`, `examples/` and git history. The dispatcher enforces this by handing over a copy of those two trees only.
- **Task:** write a conformance harness plus the minimum runtime, in Python or TypeScript, for a pure Mode-B slice, in two stages:
  - **Stage 1, identity (3 fixtures):** `cedn1-path-algebra-golden.edn`, `sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn`, `sub-cache-key-map-arg-order.edn`.
  - **Stage 1, pure routing (7 fixtures):** `routing-malformed-url-fail-closed.edn`, `routing-match-url.edn`, `routing-pattern-validation.edn`, `routing-plus-decode.edn`, `routing-query-keyword-discipline.edn`, `routing-query-parse-edges.edn`, `routing-query-string-coercion.edn`.
  - **Stage 2, only if stage 1 is clean:** the 66 machine fixtures, against a claimed FSM subset.
  - **How the slices were chosen:** Mode-B-only fixtures (no `:fixture/dispatches`) whose `:call` ops all fall in {CEDN/identity and `:path-*` ops}, {`:match-url`, `:route-url`, `:round-trip`, `:reg-route`} or {`:reg-machine`, `:machine-transition`}. Re-derive the lists at the probe's pin, since fixtures may have been added or renamed.
- **Rule:** every question the agent would have asked an author, every guess, and every point where it would have needed the reference goes into a GAP LOG. Each entry names the spec section and the fixture it was working from.
- **Output:**
  - `passed / claimed-applicable` for each stage;
  - the gap log;
  - the harness's line count, split into harness, DSL interpreter and runtime.
- **Afterwards:** file each gap-log entry as its own spec-gap bead (`discovered-from` this bead). Record the measured line counts in this bead's close reason, inline. If the size claims removed by the roster bead are to come back, they come back as the measured figures.
- **Bounds:** one agent-day. Not a CI gate. Re-run it when the grammar changes materially, or before any public claim of portability.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** none (zero-edit).
- **Depends on:** rf2-nbgqz (the closed fixture grammar) and rf2-s0tzq (the roster removal and prose shrink).
- **Cross-dossier:** none required. The spec-gap beads it files may land on hot-zone spec files, and the coordinator sequences those as usual.

## Evidence

- **Read in source at 89517e8f54:** the `path:line` citations above. The fixture lists come from a read-only EDN parse of all 241 fixtures at that trunk (3 identity, 7 pure routing, 66 machine).
- **Still needs a run:** everything this bead produces. That is the point of it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The probe ran in a fresh AI session given only `spec/` and `skills/re-frame2-implementor/`, with no access to `implementation/`, `tools/`, `examples/` or git history. The dispatch prompt recording this is quoted in the close reason.
2. Stage 1 (the 3 identity and 7 pure-routing Mode-B fixtures, re-derived at the probe's pin) was attempted in Python or TypeScript, and its `passed / claimed-applicable` figure is recorded. Stage 2 (the machine fixtures) was attempted only if stage 1 was clean, and its figure is recorded if it ran.
3. A gap log exists, with each entry naming the spec section and the fixture involved. Each entry is filed as its own spec-gap bead with `discovered-from` this bead, or is explicitly merged into an existing bead that is cited.
4. The harness's measured line counts (harness, DSL interpreter, runtime) are written inline in this bead's close reason.
5. Nothing was committed to the repository by the probe itself.

title: Retire :rf/server-init: the per-request SSR setup event is app-owned (teach :app/server-init; no alias, no diagnostic)
description:
## Ruling

Retire `:rf/server-init` as a framework name. The per-request SSR setup event is APP-OWNED: the app names it, registers it and lists it in `:initial-events`. Docs, examples, skills, spec prose and conformance fixtures teach `:app/server-init` as an example name (any app-namespaced id works; this one keeps the familiar word and pairs with `:app/root`), not as a required id. The `:initial-events` mechanism and every handler body stay as they are; only the keyword changes. `spec/Conventions.md` records the old id as reserved and never recycled, so the `:rf/*` root keeps exactly one app-usable exception (`:rf/default`). No runtime change: no alias, no retirement error id, no warning, and `reserved-event-ids` is not widened.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

Both the original dossier and the Codex review chose option B (retire), with the same scope and the same "no diagnostics, no alias" stance.

Decisive facts (read in source at trunk 89517e8f54):

1. The framework never owns the name. `ssr-handler` requires `:initial-events` and throws `:rf.error/ssr-ring-missing-initial-events` without it (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:355-361`). It runs whatever vector, or `(fn [request] events)`, the caller supplies (`lifecycle.clj:295-344`). Nothing in `implementation/{ssr,ssr-ring,ssr-node}/src` registers, dispatches or reads `:rf/server-init`. The only source hits are the docstring examples at `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:287` and `:377`. The Ring tests already boot through arbitrary app ids `:init/capture` and `:init/uri` (`implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:279-299`).
2. The written contract contradicts itself. `spec/Conventions.md:8` says user code MUST NOT register under `:rf/*`, with one carve-out (`:rf/default`). `Conventions.md:38` and `:46` list `:rf/server-init` as a framework-wide pattern event "emitted or consumed by the framework", which it is not. The core comment at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:884-886` says it is "registered through the public `reg-event` by their owning feature artefacts", and no artefact does. The docs then tell every app to register it (`docs/ssr/tutorial.md:136-151`, `docs/ssr/concepts.md:154-165`).
3. The spec already teaches app-owned setup ids where it matters most: `[:auth/server-init {:user (extract-user request)}]` (`spec/011-SSR.md:774`, `:1357-1358`). Two conventions are taught side by side today.

Rejected options:
- A (keep the name, add a second `:rf/*` carve-out): it makes official a framework name for an event the framework never owns, and gives programmers and AI pairs one more exception to remember for no saved work.
- C (framework-owned server seed that routes from the request itself): it adds routing ownership, a `:url-strategy` decoding seam and setup-order semantics to solve a naming problem; POST form actions would still need an app event. If ever wanted, it would take an `:rf.ssr/*` or `:rf.server/*` name under Conventions rule 3, so retiring the bare id now costs it nothing.
- Retirement diagnostics or an alias: rejected by both reviews. The tombstone rule (`spec/Conventions.md:135-141`) permits a `*-retired` error only for a name that shipped in a released artefact; re-frame2 is pre-alpha and v1 had no SSR (`docs/ssr/concepts.md:117`). The real collision guard is deliberately the closed set of three ids (`events.cljc:889-894`). An app still registering `:rf/server-init` keeps working; trust the programmer.

Supersedes no bead or EP. No bead has ruled on the name; rf2-6zkq8 (closed) fixed the raw-request sites at `spec/011-SSR.md:132` and `:1330`, and rf2-uaah4 / rf2-b7ih8 (closed) shaped the CP-9 server-init recipe that this renames.

## Work

Rename `:rf/server-init` to `:app/server-init` everywhere below, keeping each handler body. At trunk 89517e8f54, `git grep -c -F ":rf/server-init"` outside `ai/` and `.beads/` reports 41 files (about 157 occurrences):

- **Spec.** `spec/011-SSR.md` (6: `:132`, `:1306`, `:1326`, `:1330`, `:1331`, `:1350`), `spec/012-Routing.md:1859`, `spec/002-Frames.md:679`, `spec/Pattern-Boot.md` (`:22`, `:452`, `:511`), `spec/Construction-Prompts.md` (CP-9, `:975-988`, including the handler fn name `handler-rf-server-init`), `spec/Security.md:37`, `spec/README.md:131`, `spec/Pattern-FormAction.md` (14, including the `### :rf/server-init routes GET vs POST, and owns normalisation` heading at `:173`; fix its anchor and every link to it).
- **`spec/API.md:381`.** Delete the `:rf/server-init` row from the SSR events table; setup is a pattern, not a framework event. Neither manifest sidecar names the id (0 hits in `spec/api-manifest.edn` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`), so no regeneration is expected; confirm with the `api-manifest` gate.
- **`spec/Conventions.md`.** Drop `:rf/server-init` from rule 3 (`:38`) and from the `:rf/*` row (`:46`). Add one clause to the `:rf/*` row in house style, matching how `:rf.adapter/helix` and `:rf.optimistic/removed` are recorded: "`:rf/server-init` is reserved and never recycled; a per-request setup event is app-owned and named in `:initial-events`." Do NOT add an error id.
- **Conformance fixtures** (10 files under `spec/conformance/fixtures/`: `cross-spec-route-not-found-ssr-status.edn`, `cross-spec-routing-in-ssr.edn`, `cross-spec-server-error-projection.edn`, `cross-spec-ssr-machine-error.edn`, `ssr-cookie.edn`, `ssr-error-known-mapping.edn`, `ssr-error-sanitisation.edn`, `ssr-head-emits.edn`, `ssr-redirect.edn`, `ssr-set-status.edn`). Rename the registration, the `:initial-events` entry and the trace expectation together (for example `ssr-set-status.edn:27-50` expects `:rf.trace/event-id :rf/server-init`). The computation is unchanged; the recorded event identity changes, deliberately.
- **Code.** Drop `:rf/server-init` from the comment at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:884-886`; it is not a framework event, so it does not belong in that list. Rename it in the `ring.clj:287` and `:377` docstring examples. Rename it in 3 tests: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj` (5), `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_end_to_end_test.clj` (2), `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj` (1).
- **Docs.** `docs/ssr/concepts.md` (14), `docs/ssr/tutorial.md` (7), `docs/ssr/glossary.md` (1; it defines the term, so reword the entry to describe an app-owned setup event, or delete it), `docs/ssr/head.md`, `docs/ssr/response.md`, `docs/ssr/testing.md`, `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md` (10), `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.ring.md` (3), `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` (1). In `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md`, delete the `### :rf/server-init` entry (`:453` onward), reword `:12` and `:433` (the "a name the app registers by convention" sentence goes), and repoint any link to the deleted anchor (one is near `:582`). Delete every "a name the framework reserves and you supply the body for / it does not license registering your own events under `:rf/*`" sentence (`concepts.md:165`, `tutorial.md:136`, `glossary.md:24-25`, `re-frame.ssr.md:433`); under B it has nothing left to explain.

title: Make app-db schemas an ordinary registrar kind keyed by path, inherited by every frame that resolves them
description:
## Ruling

App-db schemas become an ordinary registrar kind, `:app-schema`, whose id is the canonical path vector. `(rf/reg-app-schema [:cart] CartSchema)` is a top-level, frame-agnostic program registration, like `reg-event`. It resolves like every other kind — live for a frame made without `:images`, through the sealed generation for a frame made with them — and every frame validates against the schemas it resolves. A Story variant narrows a schema by shadowing it in a later image. The per-frame side table goes, and `:frame` on `reg-app-schema` / `reg-app-schemas` becomes an error.

This is also the schemas half of B1, the principle both recommendations ruled: every `reg-*` declares a frame-agnostic program member, registration never reads a frame, and anything genuinely per frame instance becomes frame config.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original
> recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then
> remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

This bead is sub-decision C-s1 (with its share of B1) of the dossier "Should every `reg-*` be a top-level program registration in one registration table" (local `one-registry-top-level-reg.md`, now deleted). The same ruling: A1 one registration table (the bead this depends on), C-h2 HTTP interceptors as definitions plus a frame-config chain (the bead after this), D2 facade placement, and E0 — images stay opt-in with no removal date, and gain this job.

**Decisive facts (read in source at trunk 89517e8f54):**

1. Schemas live in a per-frame side table, `schemas-by-frame`, `frame-id → path → schema-meta` (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:32-37`), and Spec 001 says so outright: "App-db schemas are NOT a registry kind" (`spec/001-Registration.md:117`, and the kind table at `:371`). So a test frame, a per-request SSR frame or a Story variant validates against none of the app's schemas unless something re-registers them against that frame's id — and the SSR example does exactly that per request (`examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:369`, `(rf/reg-app-schema [:articles] {:frame fid} ArticlesSchema)`, and again for the client frame at `:574`).
2. The contracts disagree. EP-0023's placement test puts schemas in the image: "If it is a registration, handler, view definition, schema, … it belongs to the **image**" (`docs/EP/EP-0023-image-loaded-frames.md:1772`), while Spec 010 §Per-frame schemas specifies the side table (`spec/010-Schemas.md:449-476`). Spec 010's only stated reason — "a stripped-down schema for a story variant should not bleed into the production frame's contract" (`:474`) — is what image shadowing provides; no non-test call site in `examples/` or `tools/` registers a variant-specific schema (dossier census at that trunk).
3. Inheritance changes behaviour, not just syntax: validation enumerates every schema entry for the frame and reads each path from the candidate app-db (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:941-950`), and an existing test asserts schemas affect only their owning frame (`implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_test.clj:37`, `schema-fires-only-on-the-frame-it-registers-against`). Under this ruling a schema at `[]`, or a required slice absent from a frame's db, applies to every frame that resolves it. That is the intended contract: unrelated programs sharing a process select their own images.

**Rejected:**

- **C-s0, keep the per-frame side table:** test, SSR-request and Story-variant frames keep inheriting nothing, and the `reg-` prefix keeps two meanings.
- **C-s2, inline `:app-schemas {path schema}` on frame config:** loses source coordinates, `clear`, image shadowing, hot reload by re-registration, and frame config as serializable data (`spec/002-Frames.md:2519`); it turns SSR's "register per request" into "pass per request".
- **B0, keep the split and document it:** `reg-` would go on meaning either "program registration" or "per-frame install".

**Supersedes:** Spec 010 §Per-frame schemas (`spec/010-Schemas.md:449-476`), the Spec 001 "not a registry kind" note (`:117`, `:371`), and the schemas half of Conventions §`reg-*` frame-binding convention (`spec/Conventions.md:1594`). It is consistent with rf2-kuky.32's ruling A: `re-frame.schemas/app-schemas {:frame f}` keeps its signature, now answering from the frame's own resolution.

## Work

- **Registrar:** add `:app-schema` to the registrar's `kinds` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:146-147`), with the canonical path as id (paths are already normalized, `storage.cljc:635`). It joins `clear` (`(rf/clear :app-schema path)`) and the hot-reload sweep like any other kind.
- **`schemas/storage.cljc`** (824 lines) loses `schemas-by-frame`, its frame resolution (`resolve-frame`, `:39-64`) and its destroy hook (`on-frame-destroyed!`, `:812`).
- **`:frame`** in `reg-app-schema`'s metadata or `reg-app-schemas`' opts is an error whose message says schemas are program registrations and per-variant schemas come from images.
- **Carry over:**
  - An ambiguous path (two namespaces register it) fails LOUDLY at validation; an enumeration that silently omits ambiguous ids would drop the schema (the rf2-wxyy1 lesson).
  - The reads keep their signatures: `app-schemas`, `app-schema-meta` (still returning source coordinates) and `app-schemas-digest`, each with `{:frame f}`, read that frame's resolution; `registrations {:frame f :kind :app-schema}` answers too.
  - The SSR digest is computed from the frame's resolved schema set, so client and server compare like with like.
  - The hot-reload `:rf.schema/violation` check runs against each live frame that resolves the path.
  - Story's db-seed check (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:951-985`) reads through the same resolution seam.
- **Consumers of `:schemas/frame-schema-entries`** (epoch, elision, Story) and Xray's schemas panel move to the resolved set.
- **Do not** add a second per-frame schema-install API, and do not silently skip inconvenient schemas to hide the inheritance consequence.
- **Tests:** tests asserting per-frame isolation (e.g. `schemas_test.clj:37`) are rewritten to express divergence through images. Add the inheritance cases below.
- **Examples:** delete the `with-frame` / `{:frame …}` wrappers around schema registrations (14 example files carry a `with-frame :rf/default` at trunk, most of them for schemas); the SSR example registers `ArticlesSchema` once at top level.
- **Spec:** Spec 010 §Per-frame schemas rewritten as image-resolved schemas, with the inheritance consequence stated; Spec 001 `:117` and `:371`; the Spec 009 error rows for the schema-registration errors; Conventions §`reg-*` frame-binding convention narrowed (it disappears entirely once HTTP interceptors and flows follow); `spec/API.md` rows and manifest sidecars.
- **Docs and skills sweep** in the style of rf2-sugyt, for every `reg-app-schema` / `reg-app-schemas` teaching site (the dossier counted 20 docs files and 30 skill files at trunk).

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** `spec/Conventions.md`; `spec/API.md` with `spec/api-manifest.edn` (generated — regenerate with `generate!` in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`) and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`; `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (error rows). Possibly `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` if it teaches `reg-app-schema` with `:frame`.
- **Depends on:** rf2-uwsy0, the one-registration-table bead (A1).
- **Followed by:** rf2-sq53g, the HTTP-interceptor bead (C-h2), which touches the registrar `kinds` set and the same hot zones.
- **Cross-dossier:** coordinate with `app-schema-path-presence.md`'s ruling — under this bead every frame that resolves a path checks it, so that ruling decides how a partially seeded test frame or Story variant behaves; land that one first if it is ready, otherwise write this bead's inheritance tests to the presence rule in force. It removes most `with-frame :rf/default` wrappers in the examples, which shrinks `rf-default-conventional-frame-id.md`'s evidence base without deciding it. Precedes the flows work (`flows-static-or-retire.md`).

## Evidence

- Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54: the side table, `resolve-frame`, the destroy hook and path normalization in `storage.cljc`; the validation loop in `validate.cljc:941-950`; the isolation test; the SSR example's two per-frame registrations; Spec 001 `:117`/`:371`; Spec 010 `:449-476`; EP-0023 `:1772`; Story's `db-seed-violations`.
- Taken from the dossier, not re-measured: the caller counts and the "no variant-specific schema in source" census.
- Still needs a run: every acceptance case; performance of resolving schemas per validation is unmeasured.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A top-level `(rf/reg-app-schema [:cart] CartSchema)` at namespace load, with no frame scope, succeeds and registers the registrar kind `:app-schema` keyed by the canonical path.
2. With no extra registration, an SSR request frame, a plain test frame `(make-frame {})` and a Story variant built from the app image all validate against the app's schemas (one test each, plus the app frame).
3. A variant image's narrower schema for a path shadows the app's for that variant's frame only.
4. `app-schema-meta {:frame f :path p}` still returns the schema's source coordinates; `app-schemas` and `app-schemas-digest` keep their signatures and answer from the frame's resolution.
5. A path registered from two namespaces fails loudly at validation; it is never silently skipped.
6. `:frame` on `reg-app-schema` or `reg-app-schemas` raises an error that names the image route; `schemas-by-frame` and the schemas destroy hook are gone.
7. `(rf/clear :app-schema path)` removes a registration, and the hot-reload sweep drops a deleted one.
8. The SSR example registers its schema once at top level, and no example wraps a schema registration in `with-frame` or passes `{:frame …}`.
9. Spec 010, Spec 001, Spec 009's error rows, Conventions and `spec/API.md` (manifest regenerated; api-manifest job green) describe schemas as an image-resolved registrar kind, including that a schema applies to every frame that resolves it; the docs and skills sweep leaves no teaching site registering a schema against a frame.
10. `npm run test:cljs`, `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` and `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` are green, with exit codes quoted in the PR.

PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/11411 (two commits on trunk 5b03e4eaaa)

path; reg-app-schema / reg-app-schemas are frame-agnostic top-level registrations; every frame

title: Machines: :after timer traces carry the raw delay key, not the ms Spec 005 promises; add resolved ms beside the key
description:
Machine `:after` timer traces carry the raw delay key where Spec 005 promises milliseconds. This affects vector, fn and ISO-duration delay keys. Xray's countdown rings assume milliseconds. This was read in source; nothing was run.

## Evidence (trunk 89517e8f54)

- `/scheduled` (the first arm), `/fired` and `/stale-after` report the timer's delay KEY. Only `/cancelled` reports `:resolved-ms` (`implementation/machines/.../timer.cljc:~289, ~300`).
- Spec 005 `:2551-2553` promises `:delay <ms>` on these rows.
- Xray's ring fold reads the delay as milliseconds (`machine_after_rings_helpers.cljc:~126-129, ~233-234`). A static reading suggests two consequences, which only a run would confirm:
  - a timer keyed by a vector, fn or ISO string gets no countdown ring;
  - a `/cancelled` row cannot close the record that a non-ms `/scheduled` opened.

## Change

Keep the timer's identifying key, and add the resolved milliseconds beside it on `/scheduled`, `/fired` and `/stale-after`, as `/cancelled` already does. Then make Spec 005's trace rows and Xray's ring fold read the milliseconds field.

## Scope note

The decision dossier on `:after` delays left one sub-decision open for Mike: whether delay resolution moves into the pure engine. The two reviews split on it.
- The original recommendation's bead 3 would put milliseconds on every timer trace as a side effect.
- The Codex review keeps resolution timing where it is, and asks for a trace repair that "keeps the timer's key separate from the resolved milliseconds".

This bead is that trace repair. It stands whichever way that sub-decision is ruled. Related beads already filed: rf2-m2x7s (remove subscription-vector delays) and rf2-5neb3 (named `:delays`). Sequence this after rf2-m2x7s, because both edit `timer.cljc`.

`spec/005-StateMachines.md` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` are HOT ZONES if the trace-row text changes.

Supporting detail, local to this machine only: `C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\ai\decisions\machine-after-delays-from-subscriptions.md`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. For a fn-keyed or vector-keyed `:after` timer, the `/scheduled`, `/fired` and `/stale-after` trace rows each carry the resolved milliseconds. A test covers this; it fails at base and passes after the change.
2. The timer's key is still present on those rows.
3. Spec 005's trace rows name both fields.
4. Xray draws a countdown ring for a non-literal delay, and a cancel closes it. Prove this with an Xray test, or record it from a browser run.

Design: :delay is the resolved milliseconds on every :rf.machine.timer/* row (/scheduled, /fired, /stale-after, /cancelled, /skipped-on-server), as Spec 005 and Spec-Schemas MachineTimerCancelledTags already promised, and :delay-key carries the :after key as declared beside it (literal, ISO string, :delays name, or the delay fn). title: Align the flow registry and teardown contracts with static activation
description: PR #11426 (de942b8da3) makes reg-flow a top-level registrar registration activated per frame by :flows. Spec 013 Activation now requires definitions only in the registrar, ordinary flow registrations/handler-meta/clear queries, and frame destruction releasing only that frame's evaluation memo. Spec 001:261 agrees, but its normative registry row at :103 still requires an empty reserved :flow slot, a {frame-id {flow-id flow-map}} definition store, frame-divergent definitions and the retired flows/flow-meta/flows-snapshot side doors; :110 still says flow clear accepts {:frame f}. Spec 002:859-861 likewise requires teardown of the authoritative per-frame flow-definition store and calls the registrar kind reserved-empty. A port following these owning registry/lifecycle contracts would rebuild the mechanism the newly settled design removes, and global clear versus frame-specific clear would have conflicting semantics. Complete in-progress follow-up rf2-qgub0 already owns this prose sweep and has been read; this new open audit finding provides independent tracking as requested. Small correction: restate the Spec 001 flow row and clear note as ordinary frame-agnostic registrar registration/clear, and restate Spec 002's flow teardown explanation as releasing per-frame memo and pending-vacation state while leaving all definitions and sibling frames intact. Keep the currently frame-scoped HTTP-interceptor contract unchanged until its own ruling lands. Verify these owning paragraphs agree with Spec 013 Activation and Frame-destroy teardown; no runtime, API, or fixture change belongs to this correction.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (flows-prose-sweep, PR #11433, branch worker/flows-prose-sweep) ==
Fixed in commit 8b9db9bde1, beside rf2-qgub0. Checked against Spec 013 §Activation and §Frame-destroy teardown:
- spec/001-Registration.md ~103: the :flow row says reg-flow writes the kind at the top level and names no frame, and each frame runs the flows its :flows config names, resolved through its own view. Tools read it with registrations / handler-meta like any other kind. Clear routes to unregister!, each running frame vacating the flow's output on its next event, and {:frame f} is rejected. The empty reserved slot, the {frame-id {flow-id flow-map}} store, frame-divergent definitions and the flows / flow-meta / flows-snapshot side doors are gone.
- spec/001 ~110: :http-interceptor is the one frame-scoped clear kind; every registrar kind rejects {:frame f}. The HTTP interceptor half is unchanged until rf2-sq53g.
- spec/002-Frames.md ~859 and ~861: flows' step-6 teardown recipe releases only the destroyed frame's evaluation memo, with its dirty-check rows and pending path vacations together. It leaves every sibling frame's memo and every flow definition in the registrar untouched. Nothing calls the kind reserved-empty.

title: Core: run a destroy requested during a frame's drain at the next event boundary, and delete the in-event continuation fence
acceptance_criteria:
1. A self-destroying handler's `:db` commits, and its `:fx` run, including a `:dispatch` to another, live frame, which that frame then handles. Its epoch record settles `:ok`. Tests pin this on the JVM and on ClojureScript.
2. At the boundary after the destroying event, every still-queued envelope in the internal and external lanes is dropped, including that event's own descendants. They are counted in one `:rf.frame/drain-interrupted` whose `:dropped-count` matches.
3. `:on-destroy` runs exactly once, after the destroying event, on the real router, and sees the committed db.
4. Teardown still cancels host work: timers, `:dispatch-later` and managed HTTP.
5. A same-id `make-frame` attempted while the destroy is pending fails fast with `:rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress`.
6. Captured async operations still compare the exact incarnation at enqueue. A stale timer or HTTP reply for incarnation A that fires after a same-id B is seated never reaches B.
7. A destroy of frame A issued from another frame's handler, reached through a nested cross-frame `dispatch-sync` inside A's event, is deferred to A's event boundary in the same way.
8. A handler that requests its own frame's destroy and then throws still has its frame torn down at the boundary, and the reservation is released. The throw is reported as it is today.
9. A self-destroy inside `:initial-events` has a pinned outcome.
10. A `make-frame` inside the destroying handler meets the reservation before the handler-scope check (`live_frame.cljc:1233` runs before `frame.cljc:3459`). The chosen outcome is pinned by a test: either accept the in-progress error, or move the handler check ahead of the claim.
11. Every terminal record of the destroyed incarnation is attributed to that incarnation, never to a same-id successor:
    - `:rf.frame/destroyed`;
    - `:rf.frame/drain-interrupted`;
    - the `:halted-destroy` epoch record;
    - teardown-failure reports.

    A test pins this. If it cannot be achieved without a fence, the bead stops and reports instead of deleting the fence.
12. No definition or call site remains under `implementation/` of `call-while-exact-owner`, `::stale-incarnation`, `*exact-frame-owner-token*`, `*continuation-predicate*`, `continue-before?`, the fan-out's `continue?` arity, or `:allow-closing?`. This is shown by a census on two token axes. The `frame.cljc:1331-1362` comment no longer calls fence density the design.
13. In machines, one frame owner-token write helper remains, and no recheck that guards stale async work was removed.
14. `frame_destroy_incarnation_jvm_test.clj` is rewritten for boundary semantics. The test at `:177-256` now asserts that the returned `:db` and child dispatches land in A, and that B never sees them.
15. No new executor, thread or lifecycle scheduler is introduced.
16. These are green, each with the runner's own exit code quoted in the PR body: `npm run test:cljs`, `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` (core, machines and epoch JVM suites), and `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`. The PR body reports the measured count of deleted code lines.

description:
## What

rf2-sq53g made HTTP interceptors frame-agnostic definitions (registrar kind `:http-interceptor`) that each frame activates, in order, with the frame-config key `:http-interceptors [ids]`; `(rf/clear :http-interceptor id)` takes no frame opts; the `:rf.http.interceptor/registered` / `cleared` traces carry `:id` only; a `:frame` in the interceptor map, or a malformed `:http-interceptors` at `make-frame`, is `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor`; a chain naming an id nobody registered fails the request at issue with `:rf.error/unregistered-interceptor` (thrown from `re-frame.http.middleware/capture-chain`).

These sites still describe the old per-frame side table. Each was outside that bead's dispatch fence (hot zones held by other workers, or another worker's files), so they were left as they were:

1. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`
   - `#### :rf/http-interceptor-meta` (~602-622): prose says HTTP interceptors live in a per-frame side table keyed by `:frame` and the registrar slot is absent; the schema has a required `[:frame :keyword]`. Now: a registrar row under `:http-interceptor` carrying `:id`, `:before` / `:after` and registration metadata, no `:frame`.
   - `HttpInterceptor` value schema (~2280): `[:frame {:optional true} :keyword]` and "addressable for clear-http-interceptor".
   - `:rf/frame-meta` `FrameMeta` (~4191): add `[:http-interceptors {:optional true} [:vector :keyword]]` beside `:flows`.
2. `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` error/trace catalogue:

   - `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor` (~2250): triggers now include ANY `:frame` key in the interceptor map (message names `:http-interceptors`) and a malformed `:http-interceptors` frame-config value at `make-frame` (`:where 'rf/make-frame`, `:http-interceptors` in ex-data).
   - `:rf.error/registrar-clear-bad-request` (~2249): `:http-interceptor` is a registrar kind, not a per-frame side table, and is not frame-scoped; only `:flow` still accepts opts in code (rf2-s3o2d removes that).
   - `:rf.error/unregistered-interceptor` (~2054) and the emit-site list (~1036 / ~1044): also thrown at request issue by `http/middleware.cljc` `capture-chain` for an `:http-interceptors` id with no definition (ex-data `:ref`, `:id`, `:frame`, `:http-interceptors`).
3. `spec/016-Resources.md` §Request decoration (~1171, ~1186): "a frame-registered `reg-http-interceptor`" / "Registered once per frame" -> registered once at the top level and named in the frame's `:http-interceptors`.
4. `spec/Conventions.md` reserved-namespace row `:rf.http.interceptor/*` (~95): "the per-frame `:before`/`:after` interceptor chain" wording.
5. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` `frame-opts?` docstring (~169): lists `re-frame.http.middleware/clear-http-interceptor` among the users of the `{:frame f}` validator; the http clear no longer takes opts.
6. `spec/002-Frames.md` §Re-registration — surgical update, "What gets replaced" list (~880): could name `:http-interceptors` ("applied to requests issued after re-registration").

## Done when

Each site above describes the definition + `:http-interceptors` chain; the keyword-catalogue and doc-slug gates stay green.

title: Routing: delete :rf.route/url-requested; links and host anchors dispatch navigate {:url <generated href>} (keep route ranking; keep the route-id cofx)
description:
Delete the public `:rf.route/url-requested` event. Links and host anchor interceptors dispatch `[:rf.route/navigate {:url <the generated href> …policy}]` instead. Keep URL-based link resolution, so a link's click lands exactly where its href lands on a reload or in a new tab.

## Ruling

Mike decided on 2026-10-17: "take Codex's side on all five". For this dossier that means option C, narrowed in two ways:

- **Delete the event, but keep the URL payload.** Do NOT switch links to their `{:to … :params …}` address. A named address bypasses route ranking.
  - Example: `/users/me` and `/users/:id` both exist, and a link is authored for `:id` with `id="me"`.
  - Its href is `/users/me`, which ranks to the static route.
  - A named `navigate` would land on `/users/:id`.
  - Click and reload must agree. Evidence: the ranking fixture `spec/conformance/fixtures/route-ranking-precedence.edn`, the link payload in `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc` (~175-201), and named resolution in `navigate.cljc`.
- **Keep the `:rf.route/route-id` cofx (Q3).** An ordinary loader dispatched outside `:on-match` still reads it. `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_nav_token_test.clj` (~99-111) pins that case.
- **Explicit tradeoff:** the `:link` cause attribution goes. Xray detects navigations from allocation traces (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/routing_helpers.cljc` ~343-429), not from the cause. External cause consumers are unknown.

The prerequisites are done:
- option B, one internal `navigate*` pipeline, where a raw `{:url}` gets not-found on a schema miss (rf2-4r50k, closed);
- Q4, the `:on-match` target (rf2-xtkc6, closed).

After B, `url-requested` is a thin wrapper that differs from `navigate {:url}` only by its label.

## Work

`url-requested` appears in about 76 tracked files at trunk 818479f34b. Sweep them all.

1. **`link.cljc`:** `url-requested-payload` becomes `[:rf.route/navigate {:url <generated path-url> + policy}]`. Being the one definition, it reaches both `rf/route-link` and Fresco's `route-link`.
2. **Host `<a>` interceptors** dispatch `navigate {:url (.-href a)}`.
3. **Delete the handler and its registration**, plus the core classification arm and the late-bind directory prose.
4. **Spec:**
   - `spec/012-Routing.md`
   - `spec/Conventions.md`
   - `spec/API.md` with its two manifests (regenerate `api-manifest.edn` with `generate!`)
   - `spec/002-Frames.md`
   - `spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md`
   - `spec/Construction-Prompts.md`

title: PR CI does not run the tenant-switcher scoped-cache smoke on a resources-runtime change, so only the nightly caught #11434's break
description:
PR CI's tenant-switcher scoped-cache smoke (tenant_switcher_smoke) runs only when testbed files change, so a resources-runtime change that breaks it reaches trunk and is caught only by the nightly. #11434 (rf2-v3ory) did exactly that: fed #11434's 44 changed paths, .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh printed tenant_switcher_smoke=false, and the nightly went red for a day (GH #11448, rf2-dh9gl, fixed in #11453).

Change: arm tenant_switcher_smoke for changes under implementation/resources/** (and whatever else the testbed exercises, judged from what testbeds/tenant_switcher requires: resources, the managed-HTTP fx, the Reagent adapter path it mounts through), so a PR that changes the scoped-resource runtime runs the smoke. Keep the arm narrow; do not make it fire on every core change unless the testbed's coverage justifies it, and say why in the PR body.

HOT ZONE: .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and its mirror implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs move together in ONE commit (CLAUDE.md), and both are sequential: no other worker may hold them. Call the classifier with PATHS, never revisions (instrument hazard v), with a control path known to arm the surface. Prove it: #11434's 44 paths print tenant_switcher_smoke=true after and false before; a testbed-only path still arms it; a docs-only path still does not. Run the mirror test (node implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs or its npm entry) red on a planted fault and green after.

title: Core: hold a frame id's reservation until teardown finishes, delete the post-dissoc successor machinery, and make construction claims single-id
description:
## Ruling

Under the "one lifecycle writer per frame id" JVM rule, no same-id successor may coexist with any part of a destroyed incarnation's teardown. A destroy takes the per-id reservation, at the request for a pending destroy or at entry for an immediate one. The reservation is released only after teardown **and its terminal publication** have finished, including on exceptional exits. Spec 002 places terminal publication at step 10, the epoch-listener notify.

That leaves the post-dissoc successor window, and every piece of machinery that defends it, without a job. They are deleted:
- the destroy-claim retry loop;
- its `*destroy-claim-probe*` test seam;
- the structural-delivery special case for the predecessor's terminal facts;
- the stale-marker replacement in `destroying-frames`.

In the same pass, construction claims become single-id (core-frames A2). The set-shaped, all-or-nothing claim API exists only for a multi-id plan preflight that nothing calls.

The normative text is written by the spec bead. This bead follows the core boundary-destroy bead, which introduces the pending destroy that owns the reservation.

Decided 2026-10-16: Mike directed that every dossier recommendation an independent Codex review agreed with be actioned. Mike's instruction, verbatim:

> review all decisions. They now have a "Codex Recomendation" section.  Where the original recomendation matches the Code Recomendation, create a bead to action the decision.  And then remove the file.  Leave behind cases where the two differ materially.

This ruling includes the review's correction. The first draft said "release the reservation when `destroy-frame!` returns", but a pending destroy returns before its teardown runs. Both sides now agree on release after teardown and its terminal publication.

Decisive facts, read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:

1. **Today the reservation is released at the registry dissoc, deliberately before the epoch notify.**
   - The release is at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:4864-4870`, with the comment "so the post-dissoc window may seat a fresh same-id incarnation before stale teardown diagnostics finish". The epoch notify follows it at `:4872`.
   - The epoch-notify step delivers its failure trace under structural delivery because "a same-id successor B may already own the registry key when it fires" (`frame.cljc:4345-4367`).
   - The destroy claim re-spins (`::retry-destroy-claim`, `frame.cljc:4198` and `:4244-4245`) when the candidate token no longer names the frame.
   - `*destroy-claim-probe*` (`frame.cljc:4158-4161`, fired at `:4188-4189`) is a JVM concurrency-test seam that is nil in production.
2. **The set-shaped claim has no production multi-id caller.**
   - `claim-frame-construction!` takes a set and does an all-or-nothing CAS (`frame.cljc:312-341`). `try-claim-frame-transaction!` (`:291-310`) has the same shape.
   - Every core caller passes a singleton (`:421`, `:437`, and the destroy claim's `#{id}` at `:4210`).
   - The only multi-id caller is the test `set-claim-is-atomic-and-its-engine-handoff-is-one-shot` (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_construction_transaction_cljs_test.cljc:93-97`).
3. **The one-shot hand-off is live, and it stays.** Every `make-frame` uses it to put the generation-pool row write inside its own reservation (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:1232-1243`, the hand-off at `frame.cljc:357-425`). It can go only once the generation-pool row moves onto the frame record (core-frames A9).

Rejected options:
- **Release when `destroy-frame!` returns.** For a deferred destroy that reopens the window before teardown has even run.
- **Keep the post-dissoc window (option B).** It defends a same-id cross-thread lifecycle overlap that the one-writer rule takes out of contract.
- **A coarse construction lock instead of the per-id CAS.** It turns fail-fast into waiting and serialises every SSR request's setup.
- **Delete the hand-off now.** It is live (fact 3).

Supersedes: Spec 002's post-dissoc "supported successor window" (`spec/002-Frames.md:731`, `:754`). The spec bead removes the text, and this bead removes the code. No EP or ruling bead is overturned.

**Not decided, and out of scope here.** Two questions stay open for Mike in the dossier `jvm-one-writer-per-frame.md`. Touch neither:
- **Generation publication (core-frames A6).** Change nothing in `set-generation!` (`frame.cljc:1696-1708`) or reprojection publication.
- **Epoch.** `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_concurrency_stress_test.clj` and epoch's monitors stay as they are.

## Work

**Hold the reservation to the end of teardown (`frame.cljc`)**
- Move the `:destruction` release (`:4868-4870`) to after `notify-epoch-listeners!` and the terminal publication.
- The `finally`'s compare-release (`:4900-4902`) remains the exceptional-exit path.
- A pending destroy from the boundary bead holds the reservation until its boundary teardown completes.
- A construction rollback that joined its outer `:construction` owner keeps its current behaviour: it leaves the reservation for the constructor's own `finally`.

**Delete the post-dissoc defences (`frame.cljc`)**
- `*destroy-claim-probe*` and its call.
- The `::retry-destroy-claim` loop, plus anything that only feeds it.
- The structural-delivery wrapper in the epoch-notify step (`:4345-4367`).
- The stale-marker replacement in `destroying-frames` (`:470`, `:4195-4225`, `:4253`).
- `release-frame-destroy-claim!`'s and the `finally`'s defences against a successor that replaced A's claim (`:4890-4903`), which may simplify.
- Sweep the comments that describe a successor seated during teardown.
- The `ssr-ring` comments at `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:298-302` and `:338-342` may be simplified too. The per-request id is a gensym nobody else knows. The destroy-by-value code itself stays.

**A2: single-id construction claims**
- `claim-frame-construction!` and `try-claim-frame-transaction!` take one id, and the set CAS and its set validation go.
- Delete the multi-id test at `frame_construction_transaction_cljs_test.cljc:93` onward, keeping any single-id assertion it carries.
- Update the singleton callers, including `implementation/core/test/re_frame/make_frame_generation_pool_contention_jvm_test.clj:70` and `:181`.

**Tests**
- In `frame_destroy_incarnation_jvm_test.clj`, add the new JVM test:
  - while A's teardown runs, through the epoch notify, T2's same-id `make-frame` fails fast with `:rf.error/frame-construction-in-progress`;
  - T2's retry after teardown has finished succeeds;
  - B never sees A's terminal facts.
- Re-derive each remaining JVM barrier test that pins a same-id cross-thread race against the new rule. A test that pins only now-unsupported overlap is deleted, and the test above replaces it.

**What deliberately stays:**
- the per-id reservation and its fail-fast error;
- the frame value's exact-teardown no-op for a stale value;
- the one-shot hand-off;
- the owner-only visibility of a first construction's provisional row, which is to be re-derived only after A9;
- the enqueue-time token compares.

## Sequencing

- **Hot zones:** none. The changes are in `implementation/core/` and `implementation/ssr-ring/` code and tests only.
- **Bead dependencies:** depends on the core boundary-destroy bead. Both edit the destroy claim and reservation code in `frame.cljc`, and the pending destroy it introduces is what holds the reservation here.
- **Cross-dossier:**
  - **`one-registry-top-level-reg.md`.** Core-frames A9, moving the generation-pool row onto the frame record, is what eventually retires the one-shot hand-off. That is not this bead. If A9 is filed and lands first, rebase.
  - **`epoch-listener-silencing-and-incarnation-storage.md`.** Its incarnation-keyed storage bead deletes core's pre-dissoc epoch hook in the same teardown region of `frame.cljc`. Whichever lands second rebases. That dossier's option 3B, folding the pre-dissoc hook into step 10 under a one-writer ruling, is available to it once this lands.
- **Lane:** the CLJS gates need a shadow-cljs lane grant from the coordinator.

## Evidence

- **Read in source at trunk 89517e8f54:**
  - the release site and its comment;
  - the probe, the retry sentinel and the `destroying-frames` marker logic;
  - the structural-delivery comment;
  - every `claim-frame-construction!` call site, found by a grep across `implementation/`;
  - the live hand-off in `live_frame.cljc`.
- **Not run:** nothing was built or tested. That the epoch stress suite still passes unchanged with the later release point is expected, because its destruction scenario has one lifecycle owner, but it is unmeasured.

Spec 009 §Retention boundary (~825-827) still justifies itself by a same-id successor owning the slot, and describes the structural-delivery special case this bead deletes. When this bead lands, restate that paragraph to match (it is in the HOT ZONE spec/009; sequence with any other holder).

Implemented on draft PR #11469. Commits:

title: Keep same-node :after timers distinct in reply work IDs
description:
Audit of merged PR #11460 (77673c91f26b9472fb10b4cdf9a2b54417d7e99f), following rf2-i5ukz. The regional fix is correct, but a remaining ordinary multi-stage timer case still collapses distinct work attempts. This predates the PR and its body identifies the possibility; the audit now has a focused executable witness.

Spec 005, Delayed :after transitions (lines 2370-2376), explicitly permits several entries on one state and calls each an independent timer. timer.cljc/after-timer-key distinguishes them by {:parent actor :spawn declaring-path :delay delay-key}. reply.cljc/timer-work-id (424-451) still takes only actor, region, path and epoch. after-fired-reply and cancelled-timer-reply both discard the delay when constructing the ID. All timers armed in one visit share the node's epoch.

Evidence: pr-audit-sol-oct11-11460-delay-id-1.clj runs the exact merged after-timer-key and complete pure timer reply functions under Babashka, with no replacement implementations or compiler lane. Two runtime keys for actor :audit/timers, path [:idle], delays 250 and 1000 are unequal, but their fired and cancelled replies both carry [:rf.work/timer [:audit/timers :idle] 1], grouping statuses [:ok :cancelled] into one attempt. The same collision occurs inside :left, with [:audit/timers :left :idle]. Controls confirm different regions and re-entry epochs are distinct. Exit 0; the adjacent .log and .exit capture the result. This is a constructor-level probe, not a full state-machine run.

The impact is incorrect work correlation in the tools: Xray reply_envelope.cljc/races-by-work-id (624-659) groups by the entire work ID and selects one terminal status, so completion of the short timer and cancellation of the still-pending long timer become one work arc. No claim that this changes the machine's actual transition or host timer cancellation.

Small correction: distinguish the declared :after entry inside logical-timer-id, retaining the outer [:rf.work/timer logical-id epoch] tuple, and thread the same discriminator through fired, guard-suppressed, stale and cancelled producers. Use declaration identity rather than resolved milliseconds, since two named delays may resolve to the same duration; keep the ID data-only. Update the few shape pins and contract sentences together.

Acceptance: one state with two numeric :after keys produces two distinct work IDs, with every terminal row joining its own attempt; cover two distinct named keys resolving to equal milliseconds as well. Retain the regional and re-entry controls. No new app-facing API or tracker identity system is needed.

title: Machines: refuse silently ignored inline cofx requirements on spawn completion transitions
description:
Observed while auditing merged PR #11512 at a8d79bd3666ff9cdb860afd627c94d16743296b6. The authored-key diagnostic fix is correct; this is the separate behavior gap reported outside its fence.

Behavior: a parent whose :spawn :on-error is {:target :done :rf.cofx/requires [:rf/time-ms]} registers successfully. The same misplaced declaration on a transition-shaped :spawn :on-done also registers. These declarations are neither refused nor part of the derived ensure-set, so an author can believe the callback's coeffects were declared while the framework silently ignores the declaration. Putting the same map on an ordinary :on transition correctly raises :rf.error/machine-cofx-requires-inline.

Evidence: read the complete rf2-g09gm record, PR body and actual patch. The author's reported branch probe passed each shape through registered-definition and make-machine-handler: both spawn cases registered and the :on control was refused. Source inspection at the merge confirms the cause: cofx_attach.cljc check-inline-restriction! (line 285) visits state :on/:after/:always/:on-done/:entry/:exit and the new state/spawn :on-timeout slots, but neither :spawn :on-error nor :spawn :on-done. Both registration and handler construction use index-ensure-sets (line 482), so the second sweep also misses them. validate-spawn-on-error! and validate-spawn-on-done! accept transition maps (validation.cljc lines 1122 and 1149); normalization only lowers timeout/choice forms. The dispatch-time spawn diets (cofx_attach.cljc lines 612 and 641) read named guard/action diets, not the inline :rf.cofx/requires key.

Contract: Spec 005 Consumer attachment (line 467) permits requirements only on named guard/action entry maps and requires inline declarations to fail registration. Its Final states D2 and child-failure grammar (lines 3341 and 3357) make these spawn completion clauses ordinary transition-shaped slots.

Small correction: extend the existing inline-restriction sweep to these two :spawn slots, reporting the authored slot and retaining the existing error id. Reuse check-no-inline-requires!; add focused registration cases for these transition maps/candidate forms with the ordinary :on refusal and valid named-entry/fn :on-done controls. No new grammar, error category or walker abstraction is needed.

Validation: accepted the PR's reported probe and green machines/CLJS/CI results; this finding follows the actual sweep and ensure-set code and does not claim a new local test run.
close_reason: Already fixed on trunk by 52fc491d12, "fix(machines): an inline :rf.cofx/requires on :spawn :on-error and :on-done is no longer silently ignored" (rf2-4zai4, closed). This bead was filed from the #11512 audit before that fix landed. check-inline-restriction! in cofx_attach.cljc now visits :spawn :on-error and transition-shaped :spawn :on-done, so both shapes in this bead's reproduction are refused at registration with :rf.error/machine-cofx-requires-inline, as an ordinary :on transition already was (Spec 005 Consumer attachment). Nothing remains.

title: late_bind.cljc: measure get-fn against get-fn-cached, then delete fn-cache or correct its comment
description:
## Current

`get-fn-cached` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind.cljc` ~153-178) memoises hook resolution in `fn-cache`, a second atom-backed map (~57-63). That map needs an invalidation generation and race-safe insertion (~65-110), and `implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_cache_test.clj` pins its stale-reinsertion repair.

The comment (~36-56) and docstring (~155) justify the cache as a "per-key dedicated slot" that avoids V8 inline-cache pressure. No such slot exists. A hit is one atom deref and one map lookup, the same work `get-fn` (~142-151) does. About 150 call sites use `get-fn-cached`.

## Change

1. Measure direct `get-fn` against `get-fn-cached` on a representative CLJS dispatch and subscription workload, and on the JVM. A rough benchmark is enough; this is not a benchmark-suite task.
2. Unless the cache materially helps, point the callers at `get-fn`, and delete `get-fn-cached`, `fn-cache`, its generation and `late_bind_cache_test.clj`. Deferred publication and `chain-fn!` replacement must stay visible on the next call.
3. If the cache stays, rewrite its comment and docstring to describe the map it really uses, and the gain measured.

Late binding itself stays.

## Acceptance

The close reason carries the measured numbers. Either the cache is gone and the JVM core suite and `test:cljs` are green, or its comment is truthful.

The deletion touches about 150 call sites across `implementation/`, so dispatch it alone.

Checked at trunk f4e5adad0a.
notes:
== MEASUREMENT (worker core-internals, 2026-10-19 01:45 AUSEST, base 560f3b2829) ==

Verdict: the cache does NOT pay for itself on either host. Whole dispatch and subscription workloads are within noise, and a bare lookup is 23% (JVM) to 40% (V8) FASTER through get-fn. Per this bead's Change step 2 the cache should go. The deletion was NOT done in this dispatch because it crosses files other live workers hold (below), so this bead stays open for a dispatch of the deletion alone.

Method. A throwaway A/B probe, not committed. Arm "cached" is the shipped get-fn-cached; arm "direct" re-points the get-fn-cached var at get-fn (alter-var-root on the JVM, set! in CLJS), so the same ~150 call sites reach get-fn. ABBA-interleaved, 3 warm pairs then 15 measured pairs per workload, medians reported. One frame on the plain-atom adapter. Workloads: 5000x dispatch-sync of a reg-event that bumps app-db; 5000x deref of a two-layer subscription (cache hit); 5000x dispatch-sync then subscribe+deref; 1,000,000 bare get-fn-cached calls cycling over 5 published hot keys.

Census (JVM): get-fn-cached is read 34 times per dispatch-sync and about 9 times per subscribe+deref.
