title: senior review: build and test tooling
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/scripts/** (launchers, lib/shadow.cjs lane, lib/python.cjs, policy tests)
- implementation/test-quiet/**
- implementation/package.json, implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (hot zones: read-only here), implementation/README.md

FOCUS: The machine-wide shadow-cljs lane, npm entry points, the quiet test reporters and the script policy tests — judged as developer ergonomics: is the build easy to run and hard to misuse?

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.

== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 19:13:53 AUSEST, trunk 08872a5db9)

Slice: implementation/scripts/**, implementation/test-quiet/**, implementation/package.json, implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (read-only), implementation/README.md. Focus: the shadow-cljs lane, npm entry points, quiet reporters, script policy tests. 10 findings: 8 S, 2 M. By lens: correctness 1, simplicity 3, ergonomics 2, test rigour 2, docs 2. Two fixes touch hot-zone files (implementation/deps.edn in 3 and 9, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn comments in 1), so sequence those.

1. Remediation messages and comments tell the reader to run bare `shadow-cljs` / `npx shadow-cljs`, which skips the build lane. [lens 3 ergonomics, with a correctness cost] [S] [verified at source]
   Where (runtime messages): scripts/check-elision.cjs:716 `Did you run "shadow-cljs release elision-probe"?`, :726, :848 `Build it:  npx shadow-cljs release elision-probe-control`; scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:1311, :1315, :1326; scripts/check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs:213, :223, :310 `cd implementation && shadow-cljs release examples/login \`; scripts/check-schemas-bundle.cjs:241-242, :249, :267 `shadow-cljs release ${CONTROL} ${PROBE}`. Where (comments): shadow-cljs.edn:749 `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-perf-nightly && \` (an npm script already exists for this: `npm run test:cljs-perf-emit-nightly`); shadow-cljs.edn:582 `One command brings all four up: npx shadow-cljs watch :examples/nine-states-with-stories \` (four builds in one watch, which is the externs.zip race README and dev-testbed.cjs warn about); shadow-cljs.edn:464; scripts/dev-testbed.cjs:39 `Launching npx shadow-cljs watch ... directly also works, apart from the URL printing and the build lane`; :161.
   Why it matters: two shadow-cljs runs at once wedge silently (AGENTS.md), and a bare npx run needs the coordinator's grant. An AI that hits a missing bundle copies the remediation line exactly, so the checker's own error message leads it around the lane and can wedge a peer's build. The policy test allows these strings on purpose, because it only refuses spawns, so nothing would catch it.
   Fix: point every remediation at the npm script that builds and checks (`npm run test:elision`, `npm run test:bundle-isolation`, `npm run test:schemas-bundle`), or at `node scripts/lib/shadow.cjs release <ids>`. Change the comments the same way and delete the "also works" sentence.

2. If a dead holder's pid (or its recorded child pid) is reused by an unrelated live process, the lane stays held forever, and the waiting line does not say which file to delete. [lens 1 correctness] [S] [verified: mechanism; Windows pid reuse is probable]
   Where: scripts/lib/shadow.cjs:112 `return isAlive(holder.pid) || isAlive(holder.child);` and :143-146 `describeHolder` (prints pid, worktree, command and start time, but not the lock path).
   Probe: put a scratch lock (RF2_SHADOW_LANE_LOCK) holding a record whose pid is a live unrelated process, then call acquireLane. After 4s the output was `shadow-lane: waiting for build lane held by 32208 (C:/somewhere, shadow-cljs compile app) since 2026-10-28T01:00:00.000Z`, the lane had not been taken, and the lock was still there. It is never reclaimed.
   Why it matters: Windows reuses pids quickly, and this machine starts node and java processes all the time. A holder that dies hard (a tree kill) frees both pids. If either is reused, every later build waits with no end and no hint. Nothing in AGENTS.md or the code says where the lock lives (os.tmpdir() on Windows, /tmp on POSIX). On Windows os.tmpdir() also follows %TEMP%, so a process with a different TEMP would silently get a separate lane (probable, not seen here).
   Fix: put the lock path in the waiting line, with one clause: "if <pid> is not a shadow-cljs build, delete <path>". Optionally reprint the line every few minutes, so a long wait stays visible in a log.

3. `clojure -M:test` run in implementation/ uses the top-level coordinator alias, runs zero tests, exits 1, and blames the alias for the wrong reason. [lens 3 ergonomics] [S] [verified by simulation]
   Where: implementation/deps.edn:55-114. The `:test` alias has `:main-opts ["-m" "re-frame.test-quiet.runner"]` and no `-d`, so discovery scans `test/`, and implementation/test does not exist. Its comment (:52) says the alias is "convenient for ad-hoc REPL work". No gate invokes it: test-jvm-implementation.sh cds into each artefact.
   Probe: the same runner run from a scratch cwd with no `test/` printed `Running tests in #{"test"}` / `Ran 0 tests containing 0 assertions.` / `[test-quiet] ERROR: this run executed 0 test(s), below the floor of 1 ... a :test alias missing its :extra-paths ["test"]` and exited 1.
   Why it matters: every artefact's lane is `clojure -M:test`, so muscle memory (or an AI) runs it at the coordinator level too, gets a red, and is sent to look for a missing `:extra-paths`.
   Fix: drop `:main-opts` and rename the alias to a classpath alias such as `:dev` (it exists for the REPL), or give it one `-d` per test tree. Hot-zone file.

4. `re-frame.test-quiet-pin-test` cannot go red on the regression it names. [lens 5 test rigour] [S] [verified by JVM REPL]
   Where: test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_pin_test.clj:13 `(is (<= (count non-blank) 5) captured)`, plus its target test_quiet_pin_passing_test.clj.
   Probe: the same body run with the STOCK clojure.test reporter (no quiet reporter loaded) gives 3 non-blank lines (`Testing probe.pin-passing`, `Ran 1 tests ...`, `0 failures, 0 errors.`), and `(<= 3 5)` is true. So the pin passes even with the quiet reporter uninstalled.
   Why it matters: it looks like coverage and isn't. `green-runner-exact-shape` (test_quiet_runner_contract_test.clj:82) already pins the exact green stdout in a subprocess.
   Fix: delete both pin files and the deps.edn alias comment that describes them. Or, if an in-process pin is wanted, assert the exact two summary lines.

5. implementation/README.md misdescribes two lanes. [lens 6 docs] [S] [verified at source]
   Where: README.md:304 `# machines artefact (CLJS-only — JVM run is a classpath probe; 0 tests is normal)`. machines/deps.edn has no `--probe`, and the artefact holds 115 `.clj` and 62 `.cljc` test files under a real `:test` / `:slow-test` split. README.md:110 says "CLJS machine tests" too. README.md:341 `npm run test:adapter-smokes   # example-app browser tests`: the script runs the per-adapter testbeds implementation/adapters/{reagent,uix}/testbed, not example apps.
